With Roy currently running into losses, he hopes to start transactions on the site in the next three years. "People can sell various football related equipment on the site and I will charge them two per cent of the sales proceeds," he claims. Move over cricket, football is here.

For information, contact: 9811725256

Heading: Who you calling chic? - Indian Express
Content:
The Bristol hotel reopens its Chinese specialty diner and tours pan-Asia with its kitchen

The Silk Route at The Bristol has opened shutters after a gap of six months. Walk into the new set up and only the name, it seems, is reminiscent of its previous existence. The diner, now completely revamped, boasts a kitchen that brings popular picks from Chinese, Japanese and Thai to your table. We checked out the restaurant on a Friday evening and most tables were occupied by residents living around the hotel. The menu includes a handful of sushi rolls but if you crave for something specific, Master Chef Sam-Wong can roll out a fresh batch of sticky rice and vinegered fillings on request.

Must try
The menu lists interesting options for appetisers and chef Wong makes a special effort in creating delicious starters. We begin with Larg gai (Rs 375), a speciality from the Esarn region, according to the menu. It turned out to be a bowlful of minced chicken with lime fish sauce garnished with chilli flakes. Yum wunsen pak (Rs 275), a colourful salad with glass noodles and fresh vegetables in a chilli dressing was equally well done. We also tried Yasai tempura (Rs 310), a crispy platter of veggies in paper thin wrapping. Among entrées the menu boasts of Chilean sea bass (Rs 1525) in two interesting flavours. We opted for the Chinese version with steamed fish fillet in a soya ginger sauce. There is also a Thai version of this fish with spicy green curry. Among the various options for noodles and rice, including Japanese sticky rice, we picked stir fry Udon noodles (Rs 300). The kitchen also rolls out a delicious crispy duck recipe. Our order of crispy duck (Rs 950 for eight pieces) had the chef carve the morsels at our table that were rolled with pancakes and duck sauce. In the dessert section try the Tub-tim garob (Rs 275) that is chilled water chestnut in sweet coconut milk. Adventurous and quite lip-smacking.

Give a miss
We did not particularly enjoy Chicken teriyaki (Rs 450) as the squares of chicken were a tad chewy in the centre. Likewise, the vegetarian Miso soup (Rs 150) was quite bland and average.

Meal for two: Rs 1,800
Contact: 95124-4351111
Location: 4th floor, The Bristol hotel, Gurgaon

Heading: Photo Synthesis - Indian Express
Content:
The Chivas Fashion Tours are a hark-back to the Eighties when fashion shows promoted liquor, and trends were few and far-between

In the 1980s and early 90s, fashion shows were parties with an added dose of glamour to promote a brand and for sponsors to make big bucks. The Chivas Fashion Tour 2008, which kicked off in Mumbai a couple of days back, is barely different. Call it the curse of a country that is forever navel-gazing at its past or the imagination brought out by creative heads of Chivas that sees its alcohol as stimulation for imaginative designs, we can now savour the essence of the bygone era.

Chivas, who is a sponsor at all the big fashion events in the country, like the India Fashion Week, Lakme Fashion Week and the India Couture Week, is trying to stamp its brand value in the world of fashion. Bikram Basu, VP-Marketing, Pernod Ricard India, says, "We have been associated with fashion weeks for long. But the fashion tour is different. Unlike the other fashion weeks, the individual consumers can immediately buy off the shelf." Its multi-city format has brought together 15 of India's well-known designers— Ashish Soni, Rohit Gandhi and Rahul Khanna, Deepika Govind, Kiran Uttam Ghosh, Mandira Wirk, Malini Ramani, Raghavendra Rathore, Rohit Bal, Shantanu and Nikhil, Varun Bahl, Vikram Phadnis and Wendell Rodricks-who will be touring across the country. Starting Mumbai, the designers will then head to Bangalore, Kolkata and New Delhi before the finale on November 22 in Dubai.

The three-day long Mumbai leg began with Rohit Bal presenting his Ashta Dhatu collection, with director Karan Johar walking the ramp for him. For Vikram Phadnis who is showing his contemporary collection in Mumbai and Dubai, the tour is going to be kind of a party. "It is the most relaxed fashion events of the lot because of its format and it is not stressful like the other fashion weeks." Dubai-based designer Ayesha Depala who is participating in the event for the first time, too feels that this is a carefree atmosphere to showcase clothes.

But veteran designer Wendell Rodricks who will be showing at Mumbai, Delhi and Dubai has taken this tour in all seriousness. This is the most important outing for him this year. "I am not showing at any of the fashion weeks this year and that's why this one becomes very important to me. I have invited all my buyers here," he says. Rodricks, whose signature style is all about ancient India but with a relaxed Goan attitude has created a range of cocktail dresses and evening lounge wear. "My collection is named Romantica and I have used soft pastels with fewer embellishments and lots of bows, frills and ruffles which is unusual in my collection."

Heading: Busy Bee - Indian Express
Content:
Meet the lady who's got a host of Indian cricketers on her beck and call!

How many of us stay back after a movie's finished and wait for the credits to roll on? Not too many. On the other hand, if you had stayed put for all of director Priyadarshan's films, you would have seen that apart from his, one more name repeats itself each time. And it's an unusual one at that. The name Pony Verma might not yet ring a bell, given the fact that when it comes to choreographers in Bollywood one's more accustomed to hearing names like Saroj Khan, Farah Khan, Vaibhavi Merchant, Shiamak Davar and the likes. But that's just because Pony's just begun her trot. Before you dismiss her as a new kid on the block, you must hear this. "Priyadarshan gave me my first break with his film Yeh Tera Ghar Yeh Mera Ghar that released in the year 2001," tells Verma who has since then done as many as 14 films with the director! "He must like what I do to hire me each time," laughs the choreographer who also has toured the world, performing with mentor and choreographer Ganesh Hegde. "Dance has always been my passion and while I made the most of my performances I wanted to step out of the line and do my own thing," Pony admits. Since then she has to her credit films like 'Nayee Padosan', 'Joggers' Park', 'Hulchul', 'Garam Masala', 'Namastey London', 'Dhol' to the more recent 'Ugly Aur Pagli'.

While her kitty boasts of many more, it's her latest assignment that has Pony truly in the spotlight. After all, she has a pack of Indian cricketers at her beck and call! "It's more like they are dancing to my ishaaras," chuckles the 20-something who is the choreographer for the all-new show 'Ek Khiladi Ek Haseena' on Colors channel that sees cricketers like Harbhajan Singh, Sreesanth, Irfan Pathan, Vinod Kambli, Nikhil Chopra, Dinesh Karthik shake a leg with a bevy of beauties from television. "The channel approached me saying they have a challenge for me. But then I had made the Great Khali shake a leg so I wondered what could be a bigger task," says Verma who said yes the moment she heard the show's concept and the dishy cricketers she had to tutor. "There were many surprises for me. Like I never knew Sreesanth is such a wonderful dancer but it's Bhajji who truly has the rhythm. Even if he falters with a step it looks good," the choreographer lists out. She also found some with two left feet. "Nikhil Chopra was a little difficult. So was Dinesh Karthik but he has drastically improved with each episode. You know I can make them dance like Hrithik or Shah Rukh but that's only when you can have many retakes like in films. Here we are doing a live event and there's just one take to perform," says Pony.

Speaking of Bollywood, Verma's choreographed SRK for his film Billoo Barber. "Akshay is one of my favourites to work with. Though I have made Shahid dance I am looking for a song with him where I can do much more," she wishes. And if you wish to see her work, watch out for 'Chandni Chowk to China' that's slated for a January 2009 release.

Heading: A fortnight after 9/13, it’s miracles versus end of hope - Indian Express
Content: When Bollywood actor Lara Dutta came to the Capital recently to launch Samsung's latest mobile phone Omnia, she obliged the shutter bugs with a graceful smile. Dressed in a creamy coloured top, but was hardly as charitable to the assembled media persons. "She was here only to launch the phone. Since she is not the brand ambassador, it would not be appropriate for her to comment on the phone," a Samsung spokesperson offered by way of explanation. With five releases lined up in the first half of next year, the actor though is quite in the thick of things otherwise. She has just completed the shooting schedule for Anthony D'Souza's action flick, Blue, and is now dubbing for Priyadarshan's Billo Barber. After that, the last shooting schedule for David Dhawan's Do Not Disturb will also commence. Hopefully then there will be lots to talk about for Ms Dutta.

Heading: Impaled by rod, narrow escape for migrant worker - Indian Express
Content:
Two weeks after the horrific serial blasts ripped through the heart of Delhi, leaving 25 people dead, Newsline visited some of the victims who miraculously managed to pull through though with deep emotional scars.

At Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital where most were rushed, most of the staff seem to have developed a deep bond with the victims, "The fact that some like Chama Goel and Satish have managed to come out of their comas is a true miracle. Their injuries could well have been fatal," says S K Sharma, the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) at the hospital. They are not the only ones.

It is a new life for Shibnath Bag, the 25-year-old who happened to be shopping for a mobile phone along with friend Subrato Mandal in Gaffar market. While friend Mandal was declared dead on arrival, Bag fought a long and gruelling battle for his life in the Intensive Care Unit for 12 days before the doctors declared him stable. Bag does not know that his friend Mandal is long gone. Anyone who visits him is advised by the family to say that Mandal is recuperating in another hospital. "Have you met my friend? What is the nature of his injuries? I hope he recovers soon, he is the sole earner for his family," Bag tells Newsline

Bag has vivid memories about the fateful day despite having been in coma for 12 days, "I remember the blast. There was a loud noise, smoke all around and I could not get up from the street. I saw that my stomach was ripped apart, I tried to hold it in place and get up but I just couldn't. I kept calling to Mandal who was also lying on the street but I think he was unconscious," says Bag.

Bag remembers that even in that condition he asked someone to take him to the hospital, "I was talking in Bengali and this other man responded so I gave him my phone and told him to call my family," he says.

Bag's family lives close to Singur in West Bengal and Bag was working in Delhi with a jeweller at Chandni Chowk. His employer Manik Das visits Bag everyday and has promised him his job back as soon as he feels ready to get back to the grind. "Despite everything that happened, I am not scared. I will continue to live and work in Delhi," says Bag.

However, 22-year-old Sajid Khan does not quite believe he will ever be the same again. "I am scared, I can never go back to such crowded places again and I don't ever want to go back to Gaffar market. It was the scariest thing that ever happened to me," says the man who spent five days in the ICU. Khan, who was working as a driver, happened to be parking his car when the blast suddenly changed his life forever. While his employer escaped unhurt, Sajid suffered extensive injuries to his abdomen and had to be operated upon.

"I don't remember much, just that there was a loud noise and then a terribly painful burning sensation in my stomach. It felt like my stomach was on fire," he told Newsline. His employer rushed him to the hospital, where he has been since that fateful day.

"My wife is due to deliver our first child in little less than a month. She is still back home in Sultanpur near Lucknow. I do not know if I will be discharged in time," he says. He also does not think he can go back to being a driver again, "I will have to find some other way to sustain my family," the young man says.

Seventy-three patients were bought to RML Hospital that day, 58 of them have now been discharged. Eleven lost their lives, while the rest still struggle to make it through. Earlier this afternoon, 22-year-old Tahir died due to injuries.

"He was in a coma ever since he was brought to the hospital and while we tried everything to save him, his chances of surviving were small," Sharma says stoically.

Santosh Nadibatt,35, is still in coma but doctors believe that there is a slight chance she will survive, "She has not been responding to any treatment and improvement in her condition is very slow but we hope she survives," says Sharma.

Her father, Rama, also recuperating in the same hospital, has lost his younger daughter Pooja. He has been praying for Santosh's life.

Heading: Mehrauli struggles for normalcy - Indian Express
Content:
A day after a construction worker survived an accident — in which an iron rod pierced several of his vital organs — doctors at Paras Hospital say he is recuperating well.

Mohammed Ahmed, a migrant worker from Kolkata, was driving a truck at a DLF site, when it turned turtle. Ahmed fell and landed on a heap of iron rods lying on the ground.

Dr Minakshi Sharma, who had performed the surgery, said she had never seen such case in her 16-year career. The two-and-half-hour operation at Gurgaon's Paras Hospital was the hardest one the team had undertaken till date.

"The patient was brought to us around 2:30 am," said Dr Sharma, "the 2-metre long, 6 mm thick rod entered the right side of neck and pierced the tongue, the floor of mouth before emerging from near the left eye." It narrowly missed the trachea, left eye, brain and the arteries near the mouth.

"Our first job was to clear the airway so he could breathe. I could not believe that there were no major vascular injuries. Had the rod touched the trachea, it would have been difficult to save him. Now he is stable. But his tongue is damaged, so we have to feed him through a tube," Sharma said.

The doctor praised the good sense of the people who had brought him to the hospital. "No one touched the rod. If they did, it would have led to heavy bleeding," she said.

Heading: Saturday’s blast had Tunda’s signature - Indian Express
Content:
Residents unhappy with suggestions of communal divide from media

The Phool Walon Ki Sair area in Mehrauli, named after the famous annual festival celebrated there, also referred to as Sarai after the older but now non-existent sarai, struggled to get back to normalcy a day after the blast in the busy marketplace.

As shoppers kept away from the market, shopkeepers were jittery and said the "shock" of the incident had not subsided.

Owners took stock of the damage caused by the blast, when the shops opened by the afternoon.

With glass, clothes and broken fragments still littering the area, not many people entered the market today. "It has been unusually decongested today, considering it is a Sunday; most people want to keep away from the market," a shopkeeper said.

Deen Mohammad, who owns a saree shop right next to the spot where the bomb blast occurred, has lost goods worth Rs 40,000 to 50,000. Unhappy about his losses, he recounts the moments after the blast. "I was watching television inside the shop with my brother when the bomb went off; there was instant smoke and a deafening sound as we ducked coughing inside the shop."

Only the screen of the television set is left now; stands with sarees in front of the television and behind it were shredded to pieces by the blast.

Shops on both sides of the road have holes peeping through the shutters — nails and metal pieces pierced through them. Deen Mohammad's brother Aftab Alam said: "We could not hear a thing for at least 20 minutes after the blast and were blinded for at least 10 minutes."

But life has to go on even if it only limps back to normalcy, most people at the market said. Jahaz Mahal was closed today and entry inside was not allowed.

While condemning the blast, almost everyone muttered a word or two against the police and the media.

Criticising a news channel, an old man angrily said: "People in this market have never spoken about a Hindu-Muslim conflict or even a separate identity for as long as I can remember; why should people bring it up now?"

Some shopkeepers had a scuffle with a television anchor on Saturday night when he put forward a "similar question" to a resident.

The festival of Phool Walon Ki Sair is slated for October. Both Hindus and Muslims celebrate it together at the Jahaz Mahal.

The Khattar family, which owns four shops that bore the brunt of the blast, stayed away from the media today, as they cleared the debris from their shops. Sunil Khattar, a family member, said: "We just want our business to get back to normal as soon as possible. There is no problem between communities here."

Heading: Fear of blasts keeps shoppers away - Indian Express
Content:
Saturday's bomb blast in Mehrauli flower market has once again brought the legend of Abdul Karim Tunda back to life. The initial clues about the make of the bomb give it a striking resemblance to the bombs Tunda specialised in.

What strengthens the idea further is that Abdul Halim Shamsullah Khan Pathan (43) — who was arrested by Ahmedabad police soon after the Ahmedabad blasts — had confessed to his links with Tunda.

Pathan was accused of recruiting disgruntled riot-affected youth of Gujarat and sending them for terror training abroad.

An expert in manufacturing bombs, Tunda is wanted in 33 cases under the Explosives Substances Act in Delhi and other states. His standard bomb cocktail consists of potassium chlorate mixed with sugar kept in a tight container packed with nails. In this container, amid the potassium chlorate mix, he packs in tiny bottles of homoeopathic medicines, filled with sulphuric acid. As soon as the container is tilted, the acid begins to seep out into the chlorate-sugar mixture. The package begins to emanate smoke and the blast follows.

This is exactly what happened during Saturday's blast. "Eyewitnesses said smoke emanated from the polythene before it blew up," said a senior police officer. "Also the fact that Pathan was found to be closely involved cannot really be ignored," he added.

Also, according to NSG officials, the bomb was crude and made of chemicals. The Joint Commissioner of the Special Cell, Karnal Singh, however said it was too early to comment.

Abdul Karim got the nickname Tunda, after he lost an arm when one of his own bombs burst in his hand.

Born to a lower middle class family in Delhi, he moved to Pilkhuwa near Ghaziabad.

He briefly ran a homeopathic medicine store. After the business failed, he moved to Mumbai's Mominpura and set up fabric dyeing business.

There, he joined Jamaat Ahl-e-Hadis and later Tanzim Islahul Muslimeen (TIM) or Organisation for the Improvement of Muslims. He also grew close to Laskhar.

Exactly a year after the 1992 Babri Masjid demolition, he executed 43 small bombings in Mumbai and Hyderabad and seven separate explosions on inter-city trains.

His associates were arrested but Tunda escaped to Bangladesh with help of TIM operatives. By 1996, he had established a centre in Dhaka to train Lashkar operatives in bomb-making and rose as a spiritual leader.

In 1999, he was said to have been killed in an encounter in Bangladesh. Then on November 4, 2003, he was reported to be killed in Dhaka in gang warfare.

In 2005, Abdul Razzak Masood, a Lashkar militant arrested by Delhi Police Special Cell, said that he had seen Tunda in Pakistan in December 2003.

Masood had met Tunda in his shop opposite Markaj Taiba main gate at Muridke in Lahore, a place close to the LeT headquarters. He said Tunda has two wives and two sons. The younger one, Shahid, helps him in the perfume business, while the elder son is a LeT activist.

In 2006, he was said to have been arrested in Mombassa in Kenya. Kenyan authorities later said it was not Tunda but a British national.

Heading: Court pulls up DDA for unfair treatment to widow - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the blast at Sarai market in Mehrauli, shopkeepers and shoppers at major markets in South Delhi said the fear of another blast has gripped the city.

Serial blasts in major markets exactly two weeks ago and the blast on Saturday, shopkeepers said, has ensured shoppers stay away. "The police might claim they have stepped up security but the fact that there was another blast in the Capital within two weeks says it all; we are all afraid," Rajesh Kharbanda, a shopkeeper at Saket, said.

Kharbanda was in Mehrauli when the blast took place and claims he saw policemen at the spot shed tears seeing the body of the nine-year-old boy who died on the spot.

"The impact on the boy was such that shredded body parts could be seen littered around," Kharbanda said.

The boy, Santosh Kumar, had picked up the bomb kept in a tiffin box and tried to return it to the motorcyclists who dropped it there.

Vijay Jolly, MLA from Saket, said: "People will lose their sensitivities in such a scenario, when everything lying around seems like a bomb. People are living in constant fear."

Jolly claimed that CCTV cameras installed in Saket by the Delhi Police have not been working for many months now. "Concerned shop owners have even started questioning the visibility of policing in the busy markets," Jolly said.

At the upscale M-Block Market in GK-I, which witnessed two of the five blasts that struck Delhi on September 13, shopkeepers said security has been tightened and that the area had been looking secure till the blast on Saturday. "That all blasts in the past years have taken place on weekends and many blasts having occurred within two weeks has deterred shoppers from venturing out," Rajesh Sharda, president of the M-block Market Traders Welfare Association, said.

"Fear of a blast is visible; crowds at the market have thinned down," he said.

Heading: Driver beaten by traffic cops dies - Indian Express
Content:
If you thought civic bodies are expected to mete "special" treatment to the underprivileged, you are right. The "exceptional" treatment, however, left a woman numb with shock. She was allotted a shop by the DDA under a preferential scheme for widows at a price Rs 1.6 lakh more than those provided with the adjoining shops in the general category.

DDA officials thought that being an instrument of state, no questions could be raised regarding their policy decisions before any judicial forum, unless the same is found beyond the realm of constitutional mandate. The authority felt a citizen could not be allowed to raise contentions against its policies, which fell under the exclusive domain of the government, in a court seeking any kind of recovery or alteration.

It was the intervention of a court that offered respite to the widow, entangled in the legal wrangle for five years. The matter pertained to a civil suit for recovery against the civic body by Parvinder Kaur, mother of a minor, who was allotted a shop in Pitampura under the widow quota at a consideration for Rs 5.66 lakh while a few others were allotted similar shops for Rs 4.04 lakh.

Despite requests and reminders, the DDA asked Kaur to deposit the entire sum. When she approached the court, the DDA argued that others were allotted shops under a different category and she could not compare the two. Also, Kaur's case was considered on compassionate grounds under the "out of turn category" and she should not be permitted to raise questions over the allotment afterwards. The DDA also contended such matters were outside the ambit of the court's jurisdiction.

Additional District Judge Kamini Lau, however, censured the DDA. "This court is under obligation to protect individuals from such institutional bargaining where it appears to be unconscionable, inequitable and unfair," said the judge. The court ordered the DDA to refund Rs 2.30 lakh to Kaur, which included the difference between allotment money and refund of amount charged as interest for delaying the payment.

Heading: AC comfort for Metro workers - Indian Express
Content:
A 35-year-old man who was allegedly beaten up by traffic policemen in Bawana area of Outer Delhi succumbed injuries in hospital. The incident occurred on Thursday when truck driver Jabbar had come to Delhi to deliver a consignment. Traffic cops allegedly beat up Jabbar after he had reportedly jumped the traffic signal on Shahbad red light. The police said he was on his way to Rajasthan after unloading his truck in Swaroop Nagar. "As soon he crossed the signal, he was stopped by the traffic police officials. Traffic officials asked him to show documents of the vehicle and pay the challan amount. Jabbar started arguing and cops started beating him up," sources said. Jabbar was then admitted to Satyam Hospital in a critical condition and after battling for life for three days, succumbed to injuries on Sunday morning. Sources allege the police have not registered a case yet and have not handed over the body to the relatives of Jabbar.

DCP, Outer Delhi, Atul Katiyar denied allegations and said the body will be handed over after the postmortem.

Heading: 10,000 volunteers for Games 2010 - Indian Express
Content: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has installed high-tech cooling plants inside its under-construction tunnels on the Central Secretariat — Badarpur stretch to provide comfortable working conditions for its work force. The imported units will provide air-conditioning for workers operating about 40 feet under the surface operating tunnel-boring machines (TBMs), said DMRC spokesperson Anuj Dayal.

Heading: 12 forest circles in state use wireless connectivity without licence - Indian Express
Content: To ensure safety and security during the Commonwealth Games in 2010, the Centre is finalising a blueprint to impart special training to more than 10,000 volunteers. The training will involve fire-fighting exercises, manning of control rooms, handling wireless equipment, frisking and rescue operation in stadiums and the Games Village.

Heading: Nasir Raziuddin underwent extensive terror training in PoK - Indian Express
Content:
Thanks to the Gujarat Forest Department and the Ministry of Telecommunication failing to coordinate with each other, all 12 forest circles in the state, barring Junagadh, have been cocking a snook at the regulations to operate wireless walkie-talkie sets and base stations without a licence.

This has been going on for the past 25 years. Though the state forest vigilance department has been on an anti-encroachment overdrive and also offered toll free numbers to alert it, hardly anything has been done to regularise the use of wireless sets.

Only Junagadh forest circle, which straddles the Gir National Sanctuary has had a valid licence for operating wireless sets, since 1982, according to Bharat Pathak, Conservator of Forest (CF), Junagadh Forest Circle.

The state Forest Department has around 250 forest ranges and purchases base stations and wireless walkie-talkie sets each year, according to Rajeeva, Chief Conservator of Forest (CCF), Vigilance.

He refused to divulge the exact number of wireless walkie-talkie sets and base stations, but forest officials said their department has around 850 wireless sets and 1,900 base stations in operation in the state.

Interestingly, even as the state Forest Department continues to operate wireless facilities without a licence since 1978, the Ministry of Telecommunication (MoT) has neither raised an objection, nor taken any step against forest officials who have been using the frequency, which is common for all Forest Departments across India.

Ajit Soni, Inspecting officer of Wireless Planning and Coordination (WPC), Western Region, Ajmer, said a mandatory document signed between the WPC and the other party allowed the latter to use a specific frequency. "There are various conditions, including one that specifies the production of the purchase invoice of all wireless sets from time to time," he said.

He added that the state forest department never cared to inform the WPC about the wireless sets being bought and used ever since the frequency was allotted to the state Forest Department.

"It is important to update the WPC about the purchase of all wireless sets, but this has not been done so far," said M C Pandey, Assistant wireless advisor, WPC wing, New Delhi.

Incidentally, the Gujarat Forest Department has not even been paying the royalty and licence fees to WPC, and the arrears would run into a huge sum.

Rajeeva said many attempts were made by his department five years ago in a bid to legalise the process. "We even tried to appoint a nodal officer in the state to decentralise the process, but nothing really worked out," he added.

Pradeep Khanna, Principal Chief Conservator of forest, Wildlife, Gujarat said it was the PCCF administration and the CCF vigilance, which should be looking into the problem. "I am not responsible for it," he said.

Heading: Now, a horror film directed by the differently-abled - Indian Express
Content:
Nasir Raziuddin, who was arrested in connection with the July 26 Ahmedabad serial blasts had taken extensive terror training at Muzaffarnagar in Pakistan occupied Kashmir (PoK) for two years, it has been learnt.

The DCB had arrested Nasir on September 24 from the Belgaum Jail in Karnataka on charge of taking part in SIMI terror camps in Waghamon in Kerala in December 2007.

According to the police, Nasir was assigned the specific task of carrying out terror strikes in India and of targeting American citizens in Goa. Nasir's father, Maulana Naseeruddin is one of the accused in the assassination of former Gujarat Home Minister Haren Pandya.

The DCB said many of the blast accused had taken part in the terror training camp in Kerala and some part of the conspiracy was hatched there. At present, Nasir is in a 12-day police remand.

The DCB said Nasir underwent terror-training in PoK under the supervision of some officers of the Inter Services Intelligence (ISI) and terror groups like the Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT).

"During his training he learnt to use all sorts of automatic weapons. Apart from that he also knows how to make bombs from things such as hydrogen peroxide, ammonium nitrate and other chemicals. After the training he was assigned the task of carrying out terror strikes in India," said a DCB officer.

Nasir was arrested by the Karnataka Police for a vehicle theft from Devangere in January this year. Later, it was found that he is the son of Maulana Naseeruddin and had undergone terror training in PoK. He has been booked under the charge of waging a war against the nation.

Heading: Rtd DSP commits suicide in Surat - Indian Express
Content:
If Ram Gopal Verma has a challenge to send shiver down the spine with his newly released horror flick, here is a better bet. The Mook Badhir Mandal of Vadodara, on the occasion of World Deaf Day on Sunday, released their first-ever horror film.

With no background music or subtitles, the 45-minute movie, titled Home is based on the editing techniques and expressions of the actors to raise the adrenalin of the viewers. The film has been has been scripted, directed and edited by the hearing impaired of the city. Even the actors in the movie are the hearing impaired from the city.

"This is our second film. We have worked a lot on our expressions because that is the most essential thing that binds a movie. With no background music, expressions become very important," said Rajesh Ketkar, the director of the film and a member of the Mook Badhir Mandal.

He said the decision not to use music and subtitles is not an abrupt one. "We didn't use music or subtitles because they are of no use to us. We want the public, who are able to hear and depend so much on sounds, to understand how we feel when we glare at the TV screen without comprehending anything," he said.

He said sign is also a language and their movie is much like a foreign movie with subtitles. "These are small attempts to make us feel a part of society," said Ketkar.

He further said their second bid is just a beginning to their world of sound and action. "I want to make animated films for deaf children and many other such movies which will at least have a comprehensible source of recreation for the deaf," said Ketkar.

A yearly calendar in sign language

The Mook Badhir Mandal has come up with a yearly calendar of its own. The calendar has been formed exquisitely in sign language. "There are so many cultures in India and every state has its unique culture and a different calendar to fit that. Ours is a culture as well — the sign culture, and the calendar has been made using only signs," said Rajesh Ketkar, a member of the Mook Badhir Mandal.

Heading: Robbery complaint lodged against Congress leader - Indian Express
Content:
A 62-year-old retired Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) shot himself on the head with his service revolver at his house in Rander on Sunday afternoon.

Avdhesh Chandrabali Dubey, a resident of Maninagar Society at Palanpur Patia, was at home, with his wife cooking in the kitchen, when he took out his .32 bore service revolver and fired one round from it to his forehead, the police said.

Hearing the gunshots, Dubey's wife rushed to the bedroom where she found him dead. She immediately informed her sons Manish and Rakesh, and neighbours.

Rander police also rushed to the spot after learning about the incident.

The body was later sent to New Civil Hospital for post-mortem, while the revolver was seized by the police.

According to the police, two years ago, Dubey had accidentally shot his jaw while cleaning his rifle.

He had been rushed to the nearby hospital where doctors managed to save his life, but had to install a steel plate in the jaw.

He had been surviving on semi-solid food.

Rander Police Inspector R H Hadiya said: "Dubey may have got fed up of the pain and therefore, decided to take the drastic step."

Hailing from Banaras, Dubey had joined police services as a Sub-Inspector.

He was known as an uncontroversial officer and had a good reputation.

He retired four years ago from Nadiad as DSP.

Heading: Learn from Gujarat: Chiranjeevi tells Andhra - Indian Express
Content:
A complaint of robbery has been lodged against Congress leader and ex-Congress Sewa Dal president Meghna Patel and two others with the Limbayat police station on Saturday.

According to the police, Shailesh Patel, a resident of Dindoli village took a loan of Rs 15 lakh from Meghna two years ago to start an electronics business. Shailesh took help from one Hasmukh Patel, a resident of Limbayat for getting the loan from Mehgna.

The business did not go well and Shailesh failed to repay the loan amount. He requested Meghna for some more time.

A few days ago, Meghna and her husband Devang and four others went to Shailesh's house and demanded the money back. A heated argument ensued during which Meghna and her accomplices beat Shailesh and forcefully took his car keys and left the house along with the car. Meghna warned Shailesh to repay the dues or face dire consequences. On the way back, Meghna and her accomplices also went to Hasmukh Patel's house and beat him up. They also told him to warn Shailesh to repay the dues.

Apparently, the Limbayat Police refused to register a complaint against Meghna and the others — telling them to settle the matter among themselves — following which Shailesh approached the Commissioner of Police. Upon the direction of the Commissioner of Police, Limbayat police registered a complaint.

Limbayat Inspector R L Patel said: "Meghna regularly demanded money from Shailesh, but he gave different reasons for non-payment. We are looking into the matter. We have called both the parties and will record their statements."

Heading: Textile traders livid over harassment by I-T officials during raids - Indian Express
Content:
Actor-turned-politician Chiranjeevi has suggested the Andhra government to take lessons from the Gujarat government's policy for the development of Special Economic Zones (SEZ).

"Let them visit Gujarat and see what the state government there is doing. The Gujarat government is playing the role of a facilitator and not a broker in the promotion of SEZ," Chiranjeevi said.

J Geeta Reddy, Major Industries minister, Govt. of Andhra Pradesh, had on Saturday, criticised the actor and suggested that he should first visit West Bengal to study the SEZ policy. In Gujarat, industrialists directly purchase land from farmers for setting up SEZ, while the state government develops the required infrastructure, Chiranjeevi said.

"It's a peculiar situation in Andhra Pradesh where the government acts as a broker and acquires land for rich industrialists at the cost of poor farmers," he alleged.

The SEZ Act clearly states that farmers, whose land is acquired for setting up trade zones, should be made stake-holders in the respective projects. "The onus is on the govt to ensure that affected farmers get their due. It cannot acquire land at throwaway prices from farmers and sell it at exorbitant rates to industrialists. It should share the profit with the farmers," Chiranjeevi said.

Heading: Now, video conferencing to interlink 6 med colleges - Indian Express
Content:
Representatives of the Federation of Textile Trader Association took out a rally and met the Chief Commissioner of Income-Tax over the issue of harassment faced by them at the hands of I-T officials during raids.

On Friday, the president of the Association, Shree Kishan Banka, along with Federation of South Gujarat Processor Association president Pramod Choudhary, met Chief Commissioner of Income-Tax K P Singh and complained about the I-T officials who harass textile traders during raids.

Singh told the complainants to give a written complaint against the concerned officials and assured them that proper action will be taken.

The Income-Tax department officials conducted raids at the offices, factories, godowns, shops and residential premises of textile traders last week and unearthed unaccountable money to the tune of crores of rupees. Alarmed by the raids, many traders shut down their shops and went to their native places.

The textile traders have alleged that during raids the I-T officials behave in an improper way and force the traders to make disclosure on the spot.

Banka said: "We have requested the Chief Commissioner of Income-Tax to instruct the I-T officials not to harass the textile traders during raids. Even after the spot disclosure, the textile traders have to face many problems from the department. K P Singh has assured us that he will do something about the issue."

Heading: Kachchhi language sees a steady revival - Indian Express
Content:
The six government medical colleges of the state will now be interlinked through video conferencing.

This will benefit the students to learn from the faculty of these colleges. Besides, the project will play a vital role in sorting out the problem of insufficient teaching staff in the medical education system of the state.

While the BJ Medical College in Ahmedabad had already finished the first series of eight lectures organised by the Alumni Association of the college two weeks ago, the other five colleges are yet to follow the model.

Asha Shah, the Additional Dean of the BJ Medical College, said: "The video conferencing lectures are a two way communication wherein the students are able to ask questions to the experts. In the lecture series at BJ, the students are able to see the professors while the professors can only hear the students. Once the other colleges set up the required logistics, the students of all the six medical colleges can ask questions from our experts."

Dr Vitlani, the Director of Medical Education, however, said: "The move is targeted to introduce our students to the variable and outstanding work done by professors and experts across the six medical colleges through advanced information technology."

He added: "The project has been initially started on a trial basis in the BJ Medical College, we plan to make it a permanent feature."

Dean of Medical College Baroda, A T Lehua, said: "The interlinking of the colleges by video conferencing will introduce a provision for an advanced e-learning process as well as act as a virtual library for the students."

Lehua, however, added that before introducing the system in all the departments, the college will have to be taken into confidence.

Heading: 55-year-old killed over trivial issue - Indian Express
Content:
Kachchhi, the language of a small minority in western India, is seeing a steady revival, thanks to a group of dedicated people, who are playing a proactive role to ensure its survival, as also its expansion.

The Kachchhi Sahitya Kala Sangh, a local institution, has been working consistently towards imparting the basics of the language to people who are not acquainted with it.

The Sangh was established in 1999 and has trained more than 9,000 people since then, said Narayan Joshi 'Karayal,' its founder.

Joshi, also a noted short story writer, said: "The next examination will be held in the last week of December. It will be the ninth batch of students learning Kachchhi."

The certificate course offered by the Sangh is popular among non-Kachchhi speaking people, especially students, policemen and government employees, who are transferred to Kutch from other parts of the state.

Joshi has also written a grammar book, the 'Kachchhi Pathavali,' in two parts, for teaching the language. The Gujarat Council of Educational Research and Training (GCERT) has also approved it as the official textbook for teaching Kachchhi to teachers from places other than Rapar and Bhachau.

Joshi said from this year onwards, the Gujarat Kachchhi Sahitya Academy has started giving financial assistance to the Sangh for conducting certificate course exams. "We had requested the Academy to take over the job of conducting exams and awarding certificates. In response, they offered financial help to run the programme," he said.

Heading: World Heart Day: City-based doc talks about congenital heart disease in infants - Indian Express
Content:
A 55-year-old man had to pay with his life on Saturday night when he tried to intervene in a quarrel over a petty custard apple.

According to a complaint by Hasmukh Pagi, his seven-year-old son had plucked a custard apple from a tree belonging to Gordhan Pagi, Shamji Pagi and Raju Pagi. The three started quarreling with Hasmukh over the issue.

Mathurbhai Pagi, their neighbour, and a resident of Godhavata village, intervened with an intention to calm them down. But the angry trio charged at him. One of them attacked him with the scythe, while the other two strangulated him.

Sub-Inspector G P Patel of Barwala police said the victim was rushed to the nearby hospital, but died on the way.

The Barwala police have registered a case of murder. Investigations are on to nab the three.

Heading: GU losing crores as Self-finance colleges fail to pay development funds - Indian Express
Content:
Out of the two lakh babies born with CHD, only 5,000 are diagnosed in time and treated

Three infants joined the league of those extremely rare children who survive congenital heart disease (CHD), when city-based paediatric cardiologist Dr Milan Chag successfully operated upon them last month. Out of the two lakh babies born with CHD, only 5,000 are diagnosed in time and treated.

Giving away an essential message on World Heart Day on Sunday, Dr Chag said that parents and society at large are not aware of the symptoms. One-third of the babies born with CHD die in their first year if not diagnosed in time. Listing out the symptoms, he said, if parents manage to see those signs in their babies, they must consult a doctor immediately.

The symptoms include rapid breathing, inability to feed adequately, dullness, anaemia, excessive coughing or repeated chest infection, excessive perspiration while feeding, excessive crying and slow physical development.

He said there is a very serious misunderstanding about CHD treatment. Parents generally believe that for a baby to undergo a heart operation or a procedure, it is necessary that the child's weight is more than 10 kilograms and he or she is over five years of age, but it is not true, he added.

"Even if the baby is a day old and weighs only two kg, he or she needs to be treated immediately. If treatment is delayed, the disease might become incurable and in some cases, the baby may even die," he said.

In most cases, CHD either occurs in the natural course of foetal development or due to a viral infection during pregnancy. The defect can also develop as a result of the side effects of some drugs, said Dr Chag.

Quoting statistics from the World Health Organization, Dr Chag said that by 2011, of all the adult cardiac patients of the world, 60 per cent would be Indians.

The reasons why Asians, and especially Indians are more prone to heart disease are genetic predisposition, poor handling of fats and metabolic syndrome, diabetes, obesity, high blood pressure and artery disease, besides sudden change in lifestyle and urbanisation, he further said.

Heading: Assaulted Jordanian students write to Embassy, MSU, police for help - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat University (GU) loses a huge amount of money every year, thanks to the GU affiliated self-financed (SF) colleges, which have not been paying the annual Gujarat University Development Funds to the university.

As per the norms, GU makes stamp paper agreements with SF colleges at the time of affiliation about paying a certain amount of money to the university under the GU development funds. But out of the 110 SF colleges, around 70 per cent have not been paying the funds.

Sudhir Nanavati, member of the Executive Council, GU, acknowledged this fact. He said the GU authorities have not taken any steps against these colleges.

He added: "As per the norms, if the SF colleges fail to pay the development funds, then GU authorities can direct them not to take any fresh admissions from the next academic year."

Manish Doshi, member, Executive Council of GU told Newsline: "Since the time SF colleges started getting affiliated to GU, it was made mandatory on stamp papers for these colleges to pay a definite amount of money to GU under the Gujarat University development funds. But these colleges failed to pay the funds. Despite this, the GU has not taken any steps against them."

He said on one hand, the GU is asking for the huge amount of Rs 120.31 crore for the XI UGC Five-Year Plan, but on the other, it is losing crores of rupees by not penalising the SF colleges.

Pradeep Prajapati, member of Academic Council and Dean of Arts faculty, GU, said: "The SF colleges manage to escape from paying the development funds by doing personal favours for some higher authorities at GU."

D G Gohil, Managing Trustee of Vision Education Trust, said: "We don't mind paying an amount of Rs 5 lakh to GU every year. But the problem is that there is a lot of discrimination. GU authorities ask for the development funds as per their requirement. This differs from college to college."

Heading: Escaped jailbird arrested in Madhya Pradesh - Indian Express
Content:
They were hit with sticks and chains and told to stay away from girls

Following the alleged assault on four Jordanian students by a group of MSU students at the Arts Faculty canteen on Thursday, the university on Sunday confirmed that a written appeal had been made to the Jordanian Embassy, the MSU Registrar, the Commissioner of Police and the Dean of the Arts Faculty.

On their part, the police said they are investigating the matter and strict action will be taken against the students who allegedly beat up the foreigners.

One of the four injured Jordanian student said: "On Thursday, my three friends and I were sitting in the Arts Faculty canteen when a group of youths approached us. They hit us with sticks and chains and followed us to the Fatehgunj area where we live. On Friday, we wrote to the Jordanian Embassy, the police and the university authorities."

He said that they are now scared to go out alone. He said the attackers also asked them not to speak to Indian girls.

The Jordanian student told Newsline that 10 students from their country had taken admission in the MSU Arts Faculty about a month ago. He said they had just acquainted themselves with their classmates.

MSU Arts Faculty Dean Nitin Vyas said: "I was not a witness to the entire incident, but I did see that the Jordanian students, who were on motorcycle near the Hansa Mehta Library, were chased on Thursday. The very next day, I took up the matter with the university authorities, who later contacted the police."

Heading: Man kills brother for performing father’s last rites - Indian Express
Content:
A Hardened criminal from Dahod, who had recently escaped from Gharbada, was arrested by the Madhya Pradesh police on Sunday afternoon. Dahod Superintendent of Police Vipul Aggarwal said a team headed by Deputy Superintendent of Police M K Naik will now head for Ranapur in Jhabua district, where Manu Meda was arrested.

With the suspension of two police constables following Meda's escape from the Garbada Sessions Court on September 23, the Dahod police had been conducting raids at all his hideouts. The Dahod police said Meda had been giving them a lot of trouble because of his repeated attempts to escape.

Police said that Meda is the most wanted criminal in Dahod district and was wanted in at least five cases of loot and murder in the district, and Jhabua in Madhya Pradesh.

Initially, Meda was kept at Dahod Jail, but he made an escape bid in which a policeman was severely injured. Although Meda was subsequently nabbed, police said he was always attempting escape. Sources said that police recovered a mobile from him while he was being transferred to Devgadh Baria sub-jail.

On September 23, Meda was brought from Devgadh Baria to Limkheda and later taken on a private bus going towards Madhya Pradesh. Meda and two other criminals were sent to Garbada with two constables and escaped from their custody, as per the complaint registered by the constables at the Gharbada police station.

Meanwhile, the two constables from whose custody Meda escaped in Garbada are under suspension. "We are conducting a detailed inquiry into the matter," Aggarwal said.

Heading: Navratri organisers rush for insurance cover over terror threat - Indian Express
Content:
A man killed his elder brother when he was performing the last rites of his father at Ratanpura village in Naswadi.

Sub-Inspector of Sankheda police station M K Gujjar said Vinod Bhil killed his brother Karsan Bhil, as he was allegedly performing the rituals without informing him.

Gujjar said: "Karsan was performing the rituals when Vinod started shouting at him.

When the elder brother did not pay any heed, Vinod and their uncle Vitthal Bhil attacked Karsan and started hitting him with a rod. He died on the spot".

Both Vitthal and Vinod have been arrested. "The murder took place in front of the entire village. On the statements given by eyewitnesses, we arrested Vinod and Vitthal," Gujjar said.

Police ruled out property dispute to be the cause of the murder. "The incident could have occurred because the family members blamed Vinod for not taking care of his father on his deathbed. He was also ex-communicated from the rest of the community," he added.

Heading: Security stepped up for govt’s Navratri celebration - Indian Express
Content:
Maa Shakti Garba organisers have made an insurance of around Rs 1.5 crore this year

Looking at the threat perception after the recent terror attacks in Gujarat as well as other states, organisers of Garba dance programmes to be held during the Navratri festival are putting extra efforts to insure Garba venues. Vadodara houses Maa Shakti Garba ground, the largest garba ground in Asia, which has made a public insurance of around Rs 1.5 crore this year.

Jayesh Thakkar, the organiser of Maa Shakti Garba said: "Maa Shakti Garba ground is around four lakh square feet. Though we insure the ground every season, this time we have put Rs 1.5 crore in the insurance."

In addition, the Maa Shakti Garba organisers have, for the first time, bought a high-tech camera from the US, which will be installed at the entry and exits, as well as other locations in the ground.

Thakkar said: "Though the Gujaratis have forgotten the bomb blasts, we have decided to insure the venue as a precautionary measure to keep ourselves prepared for any kind of calamity."

The United Way of Baroda (UWB) Garba has announced that CCTV cameras will be installed at the venue along with breath analysers to check for alcohol consumption. "We have installed breath analysers, especially at men's restrooms, venue entry and near the food court," said UWB spokesperson, Dolcy Simon.

Simon added that metal detectors will be installed at the entrance and only those men who have the 'smart cards' in form of a pass will be allowed to enter the venue.

Heading: Striking the perfect note-in miniature - Indian Express
Content:
The state government is leaving no stone unturned to provide foolproof security during the Navratri celebrations, which will be organised by the state government together with Gujarat Industries Navratri Festival Society (GINFS) from September 30 to October 8 at Ahmedabad University Ground (GMDC) near Helmet Circle on the 132-feet Ring Road.

Bharatiya Janata Party's prime ministerial candidate L K Advani is scheduled to inaugurate the event at 7 pm on September 30.

A website www.vibrantnavratri.com was also launched in Ahmedabad on Saturday. The website will contain details about the festival.

Security will be tightened at the venue as the event will involve performances by celebrities and a huge crowd is likely to be present on the occasion.

"The Ahmedabad Police Commissioner is personally looking after the security arrangements at the venue. JCP Traffic and other senior officials have already installed CCTV cameras, metal detectors there," said K D Rao, Gujarat Secretary Industries and Mines.

He added, "Also, private guards of the industrial houses of the state from both the public and the private sector, company volunteers and personnel from Gujarat Industrial Security will man the security." Folk dance and music together with garba will be the main attraction of the event.

Various forms of garba dance from all over the state including Maldhari Raas and Meer Raas will be held during the inaugural function. Also, folk dance forms such as Mevasi folk dance, Rathva Tribal dance, Janvia Dhol will be performed.

Celebrities garba singers like Nayan Pancholi, Aishwariya Majmudar, Abhesinh Rathod, Parthiv Gohil, Shyamal Munshi, Saumil Munshi and Arti Munshi will perform Sheri Garba during the nine nights of festivities.

Heading: Vadodara drools over groovy numbers - Indian Express
Content:
Small is beautiful, and no one knows it perhaps better than 80-year-old Surendra Mehta.

Just a step inside his workshop takes one to a totally new world of music. Instruments from across the country ranging from harmonium, sarod, sitar, tabla and flute are a pleasant sight. What's even more pleasing is the size of each one of them — all none bigger than one's palm.

The fact that all of them are functional makes them exclusive. They have been carved to perfection in this very workshop.

Call it his retiral pass-time or a hobby, but Surendra's obsession to carve out one-fourth the size of the actual instrument has taken him to each part of the country.

"I believe in perfection, not approximation. I am not creating a toy, but a musical instrument. All the instruments are exact miniscule replicas of the original. The same material and the same theory are used to make them. I go to the birthplace of these instruments to get the real essence," said Surendra.

After retiring from railways in the early 80s, he took up to this obsession four years ago. Traveling across cities, villages and jungles, he has replicated some of the most unique instruments.

"Some of the unique musical instruments are with the tribals, which they use in forests. While reading and surfing the Internet, I came across over 340 musical instruments. Out of these, I have made over 240. I now want to go to the villages of south India, especially Andhra Pradesh. They have some of the most fascinating musical instruments," Surendra said.

He has made over 30 instruments from Gujarat and 110 from Rajasthan itself. Finding instruments is not a problem, he said, but hunting down pumpkins and coconuts with the diametre of just an inch takes a lot of time. "Most of the musical instruments have their gourds made out of the shell of coconut and pumpkin. Finding a shell one-fourth of the original is a hunt in itself. I have searched for six months to get the perfect sized shell," he said.

Asked why he has not yet ventured into Western musical instruments, he said: "Our own collection is so vast. There is no point working on Western instruments when I am still left with over a hundred Indian instruments. With this collection, I want to create a museum giving the vivid picture of all the instruments available in India," said Mehta.

Heading: BJP legislator in earthquake relief fund controversy - Indian Express
Content:
Get set to be initiated into the whacky world of Saturday Night Live

Does your only dose of television comedy come in the form of unintentionally funny saas-bahu dramas? Fear not; relief is at hand as Saturday Night Live (SNL), the longest running comedy sketch/variety show on television, is finally in India. The show, which debuted on September 22 in India, airs on VH1, every week, from Monday to Saturday at 9 pm.

Few shows have a richer comic history than SNL. The legendary show launched many successful careers — Eddie Murphy, Adam Sandler, Chris Rock and Ben Stiller, to name a few. In a politically correct world, SNL stands out for its no-holds-barred humour, taking pot-shots at everyone from the Pope to Hillary Clinton to Mel Gibson. The show has also got celebrities to poke fun at themselves such as the famous episode where Britney Spears came on wearing inflatable breasts, in reaction to rumours that she'd had her breasts surgically enhanced.

The typical format of the show features a regular cast of comic actors, joined by a guest host and a musical act. In the past, guest hosts have included Steve Martin, Tom Hanks and Drew Barrymore. The musical acts, both mainstream and breakthrough, have included performers such as Paul Simon, Sting and Jennifer Lopez.

SNL had an audience in India long before VH1 finally decided to bring it here. Says actor and VJ Luke Kenny, "I've been a fan since the '70s. It is not just about comedy; it also brings acting skills to the fore." VJ Cyrus Sahukar agrees. "I've been a fan for at least seven-eight years," he says, "It's like an institution in the west —the Harvard or Oxford of comedy; every established comic actor from Jim Carrey to Chris Rock to Adam Sandler has been on SNL."

Ferzad Palia, Associate GM of VH1 India, says that they picked out SNL episodes that would suit the comic palate of the Indian viewer. "We didn't want to air episodes from the '70s and '80s; we were looking for more current content that had a certain topicality for Indian viewers. Also, we needed episodes with musical acts and celebrity hosts who're known in this country. For instance, on Tuesday, we aired an episode that had Ashton Kutcher as the host and Gwen Stefani as the musical act."

The concept of a comedy sketch combined with live music is not new in India. Movers and Shakers, which was based on the formats of SNL and the Tonight Show with Jay Leno, proved to be very popular with viewers.

But even the peerless mimic Shekhar Suman, known for his spot-on imitations of various political and non-political figures knew where to draw the line.

So will SNL, with its irreverent brand of comedy that combines mimicry, risqué jokes and many, many instances of cross-dressing, ever find an Indian avatar?

"Definitely," says Kenny, "But only for an English-speaking audience. As for a Hindi version of SNL, I don't think that'll happen anytime soon."

Sahukar adds, "I don't see why there can't be an Indian version, since we have some excellent comedians and musicians here. But there are way too many restrictions in our society and people tend to get offended very easily, so it may take many years."

Heading: A clinic exclusively for women, run exclusively by women - Indian Express
Content:
A controversy regarding misappropriation of Rs 60.96 lakh by Radhanpur BJP legislator Shankar Chaudhary from the Prime Minister's relief fund for the 2001 quake victims has reached the Gujarat High Court. Notices have now been sent to the Centre and the National Building Construction Corporation(NBCC) in this regard.

The notices were issued on a petition by a Radhanpur resident, Farsunbhai Mujibhai Goklam, who charged Chaudhary of misappropriating the funds through fraudulent means.

According to the petition, Shri Vivekanand Vikas Mandal, a trust run by the MLA and his family members, ran a number of educational institutions, including the Nalanda Girls School in Radhanpur. Following the devastation in the high intensity quake of January 26, 2001, the Centre came out with a scheme for the reconstruction and repair of school buildings. The said school was run from a rented building belonging to another trust — the Sarvodaya Arogya Nidhi and did not suffer damage in the earthquake. But Chaudhary "connived with the state government officials and fabricated evidence to swindle the amount from the relief fund for his personal benefit."

According to the petition, trustees of the Sarvodaya Arogya Nidhi did not approach the state government for any relief pertaining to the earthquake.

The petition added that Chaudhary used the fund to buy a big plot of land at Radhanpur from one Thakkar Dalsukhram Banaji by executing a sale deed in the name of his own trust. As the land was in the name of the legislator's trust, the district collector of Patan granted permission for construction of buildings for a primary school and a PTC college on the plot. At present, the Nalanda School is being run from its previous rented building as also from the newly constructed building, the petition said.

Incidentally, a government resolution issued on September 19, 2001 regarding the Centre's rehabilitation scheme for the quake victims, specifically states no school or trust will use the fund for any other purpose. The petition further said that the MLA had earlier misappropriated funds meant for members of the state Assembly by diverting it to his own trust. Another petition is still pending against him in the High Court, it said.

Though the state government, its education and finance departments, were issued notices by the High Court in this connection, the state government submitted before the court that the role of the government was limited to sending a report about damage/destruction to the PMO. On the basis of that report, the Centre gave the amount to the NBCC for repair and reconstruction in the quake-hit areas. The state government further said that nothing was given to the district collector or to the legislator.

After the state government's submissions, a division bench comprising Chief Justice K S Radhakrishnan and Justice M S Mehta issued notices to the Centre and the NBCC asking where did the money go?

Heading: As BMC mulls octroi reforms, few takers for Green Channel idea - Indian Express
Content:
The joint venture by 15 doctors, all women, will have on board a general physician, gynaecologist, dietician, psychiatrist and more

For women who believe only the female of the species understands them, this is refreshing news; A women's clinic, a one-stop-shop for all medical dilemmas women have to deal with.

A joint venture by 15 women doctors specializing in various medical fields, the clinic at Dadar will be inaugurated this Dussehra, offering a holistic approach to women's healthcare, for everybody from teenaged girls to senior women citizens.

"Often female patients are hesitant to visit a male doctor. They keep asking their peers about good women doctors. And women from conservative backgrounds would also like to opt for female doctors," said Dr Deepali Prabhat, the founder member of the clinic, explaining its target audience.

The clinic will function as a day care centre, with five beds, three nurses, two attendants, one operation theatre, one lab-technician, along with doctors. "The USP of the clinic is that the clinic has only women — right from nurses, attendants, doctors, and lab technicians. This will help women feel more comfortable," said Prabhat, a gynaecologist attached to Shushrusha Hospital.

The specialties offered will be those of general physicians, a gynaecologist, an obstetrician, a general surgeon, a dermatologist, an opthalmologists, an ENT surgeon and also a psychiatrist. There will also be a panel of other women doctors, available on call, from specialties like gastroenterology, endocrinology, neurology, plastic surgery, orthopedics, urology, laparoscopy. In addition, women can consult a dietician, counsellor and a fitness expert.

"Since these are super-speciality areas, doctors will be working on call. If any major complications are detected, patients will be referred to hospitals, said Prabhat. The clinic will also have a fully functional pathology lab attached.

The clinic will offer various packages like a teen-check package including blood-investigation, sexual counseling and dietary guidance, among other things. "The clinic will be a one-stop solution for women and girls towards a healthy and happy life, based on state-of-the-art sciences," said Prabhat, adding that the clinic would also stress on patient education and host seminars and group discussions for healthcare awareness.

"Even today, women are known to be extremely tolerant, but at the cost of neglecting their own health, and hence are vulnerable to many diseases," said Prabhat.

Heading: State, US to share ideas on mass transport - Indian Express
Content:
Targeted at corporate majors who together account for Rs 1,000 cr in annual octroi collections, facility is now used by only one company

Even as the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) gears up to reform its cash rich octroi department — its annual estimated collection is over Rs 4,500 crore — by way of only cashless transactions from October 2, the earlier much-hyped initiative of e-payments through a 'Green Channel' for corporate majors has had a disappointing response.

After targeting more than 69 big companies for the proposed VIP treatment at octroi check-posts, the BMC now finds itself snubbed by the corporate world. Nine months after the project was launched, only one importer, Hindustan Lever Ltd, has availed itself of the Green Channel, which ensures that vehicles carrying the company's consignments move through a dedicated lane at the Mulund-Airoli Link Road check-post.

Joint Municipal Commissioner (Improvements) V Radha admitted that the initiative, aimed at quick and efficient transactions for 69 companies that had a clean track record of payments and together accounted for Rs 1,000 crore in annual octroi collections, had failed. "We need a lot more strategy to make it successful," she said.

That's why, the BMC has now shifted the target from big corporates to local transporters.

"We will modify and review the whole Green Channel initiative by targeting the transporters. We will be also working out multiple cash options instead of e-payment," Radha said.

While several industry majors including Tata Power, Reliance Energy, Bharti Airtel, Cadbury India Limited, Sony and Toyota had responded positively to the Green Channel idea, only four companies had agreed to be a part of the initiative; Siemens Communication, Godrej, Hindustan Lever Ltd and Pune-based Chitale Co. Later, however, when the much-delayed initiative was finally launched in January, only Hindustan Lever continued to make use of the facility.

"These companies, owing to their huge set-ups and numerous sister concerns, are unable to co-ordinate for the octroi e-payment. The consignments come from across the country and most of the time they are clueless about which goods are coming to Mumbai," said an official.

Once registered with the BMC, these companies would be able to directly make online payments at the BMC portal. Importers could transfer octroi charges from their accounts via four bank — State Bank of India (SBI), Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI), Axis Bank and Union Bank of India. On producing the receipt at the check-post, their trucks can pass through the Green Channel.

Meanwhile, the civic administration will soon kickstart cashless transaction for trucks carrying construction material like stone, bricks, sand and cement by way of 'silver cards'. Vehicle operators will have to swipe these cards at the check-posts, reducing cash payment time from 10-15 minutes per truck to 10 seconds per truck.

Heading: Disabled by bridge collapse 16 yrs ago, couple see fresh hope for claim - Indian Express
Content:
The Federal Transit Administration (FTA) of the United States of America and the Maharashtra Government will on Monday enter into a Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) for sharing knowledge on mass public transport systems in the state.

A delegation from the FTA will hold detailed discussions with officials of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) to extend assistance on how to strengthen public transportation systems in Mumbai and other major cities in the state.

"The Maharashtra government will be signing an MoC with the FTA on Monday, to facilitate sharing of technical know-how between USA and the state government. A team of FTA officials is scheduled to meet MMRDA officials to discuss the issue," said Dilip Kawathkar, Joint Project Director (public relations) at MMRDA.

Last year, a memorandum of cooperation had been signed between the Ministry of Urban Development of the Union Government and the FTA for cooperation in areas like public transport, inter-modal transportation, safety in transport, transportation for persons with disabilities, intelligent transportation systems, traffic information centres and training in public transportation and other allied fields.

This MoC is seen as a step forward for the state, which is currently exploring all possible options to upgrade transportation facilities in the financial capital and in the other big cities.

It is expected that this MoC will be a precursor to a more specific project which will tap the FTA's experience in running state-of-the-art transportation networks. There would also be an exchange of specialists, alongside joint seminars, training programmes and also joint research urban transportation.

Officials felt that sharing of such technical know-how will help the state consider more options in mass transportation projects and also in transportation best practices.

Earlier, the FTA delegation met senior officials of the Urban Development ministry in New Delhi and were also briefed on various mass transit projects underway across the country, including the Metro Rail projects, Bus Rapid Transit projects and major expressways and highways.

Heading: Inside Marathi cinema’s turnaround, a modest suburb finds its feet - Indian Express
Content:
Following a recent decision by the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, a city-based couple, who had suffered injuries rendering them partially disabled in an accident, have fresh reason to hope for justice.

Sixteen years after Vinaya and Vilas Sawant were severely injured when a railway foot overbridge collapsed, the national commission has referred their case back to the state commission, which had rejected their claim 10 years back.

On September 29, 1992, while returning from a family function in Ghatkopar, the Sawants took the foot overbridge at Jogeshwari. Minutes after they climbed the staircase, the pedestrian bridge collapsed, leaving a handful of people dead and many more injured. Both Vinaya and Vilas suffered multiple fractures and spinal injury. Vinaya also suffered partial blindness.

Vinaya, a telephone operator at MTNL, had then moved a complaint at the district-level consumer forum in 1995, seeking compensation from the Railways stating that since they had purchased railway tickets, they were eligible consumers. However, the district forum rejected the application stating that the railways did not fall within the purview of the forum.

The family had then approached the state commission, without success.

Last week, a national commission joint bench presided over by Justice M B Shah and Justice Rajyalakshmi Rao observed that "a railway passenger who purchases a ticket to travel by rail would undoubtedly be a consumer because he pays for availing of the services to be rendered by the Railway. And hence discomfort caused due to any of the services means the Railway is directly responsible. Along with the rails, the Railway is also liable to ensure a consumer's safety at ingress and egress from the train."

Referring the case back to the State Commission, the forum has also observed that the commission should keep in mind the inquiry report prepared after the accident.

The report, commissioned by the railway, had found that there had been negligence on the part of railway officials who were responsible for maintaining the foot overbridge. The report also pointed to "corrosion of cross girders connected to the beam of the foot overbridge" that led to the mishap.

The matter will now be heard in the first week of October by the State Commission. As per the direction from the National Commission, the case is expected to be settled within a week's time.

Heading: Shooting the Offenders - Indian Express
Content:
Dombivli, in Thane district, gets a first: A Marathi feature film shot entirely in this township

The urban sprawl of Dombivli, a suburban city 50 km from Mumbai, will soon be the backdrop for the entire shooting of a forthcoming suspense Marathi film, a unique distinction for the township that is known as a cultural hub and also shot to cinematic fame earlier with the critically-acclaimed Marathi film Dombivli Fast.

For the otherwise modest suburb, a densely populated township with a population of nearly 12 lakh, this film will hold another first: A mahurat shot.

Paul Khuna (Footprints), a suspense feature film by debutant director Sandip Salgaonkar and produced by Samir Bapardekar, was clapped to a start on Friday morning at the Dombivli Gymkhana. No less than the mayor of the Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation Ramesh Jadhav of the Shiv Sena made it to the mahurat, along with KDMC Standing Committee chairman Ravindra Chavan, who belongs to the Bharatiya Janata Party.

While Dombivli Fast had few scenes shot in Dombivli, Paul Khuna will be shot here entirely over a ten-day schedule.

Why shoot an entire film in Dombivli? "The city is a virgin landscape for film shooting. Some of the locations in Dombivli have never been touched before for any other film," pointed out Ajay Nikte, executive producer of film. Besides, he adds, he and the other executive producer Sachin Chitnis hail from Dombivli themselves.

"The 13-minute film is expected to be completed by October 5. The locations selected for the shooting are Dombivli Gymkhana, Regency Garden, Savitribai Phule Auditorium, Retibunder and Madhuban Cinema, among other locations," said Nikte.

The suspense movie will feature Mangesh Kulkarni, Pankaj Vishnu, Trupti Bhoir and Nikte in the lead roles. "The story is about a newly married couple coming to Dombivli and residing in an old vacant house belonging to the bride's parents. The suspense is built with the wife fearing always that she is being stalked by an unidentified person," said Nikte.

Suspense is itself an uncommon theme for Marathi films and cinegoers believe the revival of Marathi cinema will see more experimentation with genres in the coming years.

The few noted suspense films in Marathi have been Patlag (1964) directed by Raja Paranjpe, Ya Khel Sawlyancha (1976) directed by Vasant Joglekar and Ek Ratra Mantarlei (1989) directed by Kumar Sohoni.

"In the last two decades, it is comedy that has been the leading trend in Marathi films. Maybe the filmmakers believe that comedy films are more economically viable. We have tried to give something different to the audience," said Nikte.

The film features three songs based on the lyrics by Kedar Parulekar and music director Bagwant Narvekar. The recording of all three songs has been completed. "Vaishali Samant, popular for singing racy numbers, has sung a sober song for the first time," said Chitnis.

Heading: A World Around Earth - Indian Express
Content:
Eighteen schoolchildren spent the summer chronicling the city's traffic misdemeanours, part of an international programme on road safety in seven cities

The camera-work of these 18 school kids may be amateurish, but they certainly bring out the lack of awareness on road safety amongst pedestrians and motorists in the city.

Eighteen youngsters, between the age group of nine to 14 years and belonging to different schools in the city were part of Photovoice, a photojournalism programme to make children safer pedestrians and motorists. The programme also included children from six other nations.

For this bunch of enthusiastic kids, the opportunity to head out to the city's streets, armed with cameras, to shoot their perspectives of road safety was a great learning experience, they say. Globally, 1,676 child participants photographed pedestrian environments, including the behaviour of pedestrians and motorists.

During their field trips earlier in April, each of these children clicked over 200 photographs per head, of various things on the city's roads that they felt posed a risk to pedestrian safety. These photographs, along with those clicked by students from Sao Paolo, Toronto, Beijing, Seoul, Manila and Washington D C are being displayed at venues across these cities, with the objective of promoting pedestrian safety. In Mumbai, an exhibition was held at the Scouts & Guides Pavilion at Shivaji Park over the weekend, with images captured by children from the seven cities.

Of the photos displayed at the exhibition, a large number depicted the dismal condition of the city's streets, congested with hawkers on both sides, unruly pedestrians jaywalking, with complete disregard for vehicles speeding their way, etc.

Quite candidly, these kids admit that at first they were quite hesitant to take part in the programme, mainly because the vacations were on and most didn't know how to handle the camera.
