Heading: New swanky bus stop blocks shop - Indian Express
Content:
Life convicts seeking an early release have been in the news ever since Rajiv Gandhi's assassin Nalini sought to be freed from a jail in Tamil Nadu. She didn't succeed, but Rajaram Kashinath Charoskar has.

Charoskar, lodged at the Nashik central prison, managed to prove in court that he had overstayed his prison tenure.

A recent amendment to the laws redefined life sentences so that such convicts would have to spend their lifetimes in prison. But Charoskar had been awarded his life sentence in 1993, years before the amendment.

The Bombay High Court said as far as the judiciary was concerned, "a sentence of imprisonment for life must prima facie be treated as imprisonment for the whole of the remaining period of the convicted person's natural life". However, the court directed the authorities to release Charoshkar.

Arrested in February 1992, senetenced in October 1993, Charoskar had stated in his original plea that he had undergone 14 years of actual imprisonment. He said the total time he spent in custody was not being considered as a set-off period against the total years he spent in jail.

Nitin Pradhan, appointed as amicus curie in the case, pointed out that the trial court which convicted the accused had stated that no set-off should be given under Section 428 of the Criminal Procedure Code. This was later confirmed by a division bench of the High Court without looking into the sessions court order of 2006, Pradhan said.

The division bench of Justice Bilal Nazki and A A Kumbhakoni said: "Any decisions regarding remission of a life sentence of a convict rested solely with the state government and not the judiciary. It's exclusively a judicial function to award appropriate punishment to a person who is found guilty of an offence, but once such a punishment is awarded, the judicial function comes to an end."

However, considering the facts put forth by Pradhan, the court observed that set-off could not have been denied to the petitioner on the ground that the sessions judge had also ordered accordingly. The order said it's open for the state government to grant a set-off to the petitioner.

Heading: Timeless Tunes - Indian Express
Content:
When Ramesh Jain, owner of Chanel, a Kids and Teenage apparels store, went to open his shop in the Harkishandas building on Friday (September 26) located on the Raja Ram Mohan Roy road, he was stunned to see his shop completely blocked by the Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) new swanky bus stop.

The footpath on which Jain runs his shop since 1990 also has a 'Prathana Samaj' bus stop—a halt for bus route no 65 and 69. "Things were fine when we closed the shop on Friday night, but next day when I came, I was stunned to see that it was blocked by the BEST bus stop. We immediately filed a non-cognizable complaint with the police who instructed us to contact the BEST. I tried contacting the BEST officials, but Saturday and Sunday being non-working days, nothing was done," said Jain who couldn't open the shop since last two days.

"Our officers will visit the site and ascertain the problem on Monday. We will see what type of relief can be given to him and if there is no solution of for this, then we will remove the bus stop from the spot," said BEST chairman Pravin Chedda.

Interestingly, this is not the first time the BEST has received complaints from the shopkeepers against the new swanky bus stops for blocking the shop's way. The swanky bus stops which are being installed across the city since last year, also earn revenue for BEST through advertisements.

Heading: The New Poet’s Society - Indian Express
Content:
While we don't mind waking up to Birendra Krishna Bhadra's baritone for several Mahalayas to come, is Mahishasur Mardini never to see new voices?

Before you picked up today's paper, you have probably experienced the magic— some rousing Sanskrit recitation, music and a dash of acoustic melodrama — thanks to the reverberating baritone of Birendra Krishna Bhadra. It goes without saying that this show at All India Radio, is what whole of Bengal rises to in the chilly predawn hours of 4 am, to be precise, on the Mahalaya.

Since the early 1930s, Mahalaya has become synonymous with Mahishasur Mardini recited by orator Birendra Krishna Bhadra. But in the Mahalaya morn of 1976, Bengal woke up to what can be called a jolt. "AIR decided to experiment and planned a special show. Uttam Kumar, was roped in to do the chandi path for us. He obliged, but the response we got was far from favourable," says Ratna Sen, radio presenter with AIR.

The Akashvani Bhavan was flooded with angry phone calls demanding the return of Bhadra to the airwaves. "Some phone calls were so caustic that we had to slam the phone down," remembers Sen.

Bhadra has long passed away, but his recorded voice still forms the core of the Mahalaya programme. What is it about the original show that makes it such an integral part of our lives? "Mahishasur Mardini is a remarkable piece of audio drama matchless in Indian culture. Look at the people associated with it. It was scripted by Bani Kumar, and narrated by Bhadra. The enchanting music is composed by none other than the immortal Pankaj Mullick, and the songs were rendered by famous singers of yesteryears, including Hemant Kumar and Arati Mukherjee," says percussionist Bickram Ghosh.

The bad taste of the 1976 fiasco has been long washed away. Bhadra continues to rule airwaves. But in this age of jazzed-up Devdas and Parineeta, are we still that hostile to the idea of a new version of Mahishasur Mardini? "I have my doubts. The original version of the show has become a part of the Bengali psyche. It will be very hard to reconcile to anything new. Bhadra's mellifluous voice is a part of Bengali milieu," says music director Debjyoti Mishra.

However, there was a time when Bhadra himself was prevented from participating in the programme as he was considered "too old". "Sanjay Gandhi had said that older people like Bhadra should not be a part of the cast and so he was prevented from singing. There were even people who went and stoned Bhadra's house. However after the programme, when younger singers went on air, the listeners were so angry that they started stoning All India Radio," recalls Supriti Ghosh, one of the members of the original voice cast that made the show.

Ghosh anticipates such a scenario if we end up putting together a newer version of the programme, without "proper dedication". "Why meddle with a work of art when you can't better it. I am not saying that we can't better the enterprise, am sure we have enough talent to do so. But one thing I am sure of, we cant do it just for the sake of doing so," says Bickram Ghosh.

Mishra agrees. "Bhadra has achieved the status of an icon, so there is no question of bettering him. What people can aspire for is to emulate the success story of the dream team that made the show."

Heading: Jay Talking - Indian Express
Content:
International Music Day is observed on October 1. What do our home-grown musicians have to say about it?

NILADRI KUMAR

sitar player

I'm performing in a concert to celebrate the International Music Day. For me, as a musician, everyday is special, but it's great that we have such a day, especially since it falls in the beginning of the concert season in India. July to September is a dry period in the India musical scene with fewer concerts and very low audience attendance. So I'm very glad that this particular day is celebrated at the beginning of October.

SHAAN

singer

I didn't know October 1 is celebrated as International Music Day. But now that I know, I'll take the day off and use the opportunity to go through all my old music. I've just shifted to a new house, so I'm still filtering out all my CDs. This will be a great time to catch on all the music from the 80s that I've collected.

NANDU BHENDE

singer

I had no idea that October 1 is celebrated as International Music Day. For a musician, everyday is like International Music Day. We don't need a specific day to celebrate music. The importance pf music in my life is the utmost. But it makes sense for other people to celebrate it as a special day, because then it can draw attention to the fact that music is important.

SOPHIE CHAUDHARY

singer and VJ

I don't know about International Music Day and personally, it doesn't matter, because I celebrate music every day of my life whether it is singing or listening to music or discovering new music. But I think it's wonderful that other people celebrate it and I think they should use it as an opportunity to explore new kinds of music and discover music from other cultures.

SUNEETA RAO

singer

I am not aware of a special day being celebrated as International Music Day. But for me everyday is special as far as music is concerned. I don't know if celebrating this day will help the cause of music. If it's just some commercial stunt to make more money then I don't support it. But if it genuinely gives an opportunity to talented people and if efforts are being made to explore music more deeply, then I think it's a great idea.

Heading: Kolkata Knight Riders routed - Indian Express
Content:
While his single Ride it climbs up the charts and wins awards in London, singer Jay Sean travels to Delhi to belt out some rhythm 'n' blues

Londoners might not know Kamaljit Singh Jhooti, but mention Jay Sean and everyone with a little bit of rhythm and some blues in the soul will hum Ride it, the hit single that is riding up the charts and winning awards. At his recent Mumbai act, the British-Asian singer, however, nonchalantly threw in a bit of rap in his otherwise melodic pop R&B. Oh, that was just for fun, he laughed. Expect something similar when the 27-year-old performs today at Elevate in Noida, as part of Ray-Ban VH1 Global Music Xpress.

"The set list is a mix of my old songs and new ones. But what I love doing is to add something that people have not seen me do before, like rapping," smiles Jay Sean, who debuted with Rishi Rich and Juggy D in Dance with you in 2003 and went on to belt out hits such as Eyes on you. "Rishi Rich and Juggy D are good friends and it was a wonderful experience, but we all have moved onto our solo projects and are happy for each other's accomplishments," he says.

So when Jay Sean released his latest album, My Own Way, whose track Ride it has won the 2008 UK Asian Music Awards for Best Video and Best Urban Act, he did it under his own label 2Point9/Jayded. "When someone else is putting money on you, it gets frustrating after a point when a lot of what you do is decided by them. So I trusted my instincts and 2Point9/Jayded was born," he says. He is the only artist his label has signed on till now, but he says with relief that he is flooded with demos.

After a brief interaction with Bollywood — his track Dil mera was part of Kya Kool Hai Hum while actor Bipasha Basu appeared for his song Stolen — he is ready for more and is in talks with Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy. "I'm a huge Bollywood fan. I love the way the films offer everything — emotions and comedy and music. I am really look forward to working with the SEL trio," says Jay Sean, who wants to bring here his experience of the West.

But how did Kamaljit Singh Jhooti become Jay Sean? "Well Jay comes from my last name Jhooti and my grandmother used to call me shaan which is where Sean comes from," he laughs. That is a little bit of West in his name as well.

Heading: Dasmunsi gets his turn on Singur stage - Indian Express
Content:
Out-of-favour Australian all-rounder Andrew Symonds made very little impact as Queensland defeated Kolkata Knight Riders by seven wickets in the Twenty20 double header in Brisbane today.

Making a comeback yesterday after the infamous "gone fishing" episode, Symonds had figures of (0/8) off four overs with the ball, but failed miserably with the bat, scoring just two.

Meanwhile, in the match, batting first the Knight Riders were restricted to 8-79 off their 20 overs, with the Kolkata side's coach John Buchanan's son, Michael top scoring with 16. Disappointingly, only four Knight Riders batsmen managed to score double figures. Queensland skipper Chris Simpson (2/11) and Ben Laughlin (2-15) were the pick of the bowlers for the Australian side.

Chasing the target, Queensland had no hiccups as Clinton Perren cracked an unbeaten 50 to see his side through by the 8th over without losing any wicket.

Heading: Cash & Carry to get licence, Bloc relents after CM apology - Indian Express
Content:
Congress leader will meet Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi to discuss the imbroglio

After Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee and Opposition leader Mamata Banerjee, it is now the turn of Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi who will hold talks with Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi on the contentious Tata Motors Nano car plant in Singur.

Dasmunsi, who addressed a rally in Singur on Sunday, criticised the state government for messing up the situation and failing to provide a proper compensation package to the dispossessed farmers.

The Congress leader said: "We must find out a solution to the Singur problem and it is time that we take an initiative. I will meet the Governor on Monday and discuss the matter with him. There should be no more politics over Singur."

"I will also talk with the Tatas to resolve the issue," he added.

He said the Tatas should also show more patience regarding the project. They should not be stubborn in their attitude, nor should they insist on pulling out of Singur, he said.

"Is it a child's play to suddenly abandon the project? One thousand acres have been acquired and even if the land is returned, it will not be cultivable for a long time after all the construction work that has been done over there," he said. If the October deadline could not be met for rolling out the Nano car, it could be done in November, he added.

The minister was addressing a rally at Sahanapara near the Tata Motors small car factory. Around 3,000 people, mostly outsiders, attended the rally. In response to Bhattacharjee terming the Opposition as traitors, Dasmunsi hit back, saying: "It is the state government that has breached the trust of the people and farmers of Singur. The compensation package offered by the state government is not adequate."

Dasmunsi also urged the agitators and farmers to show restraint. "It is also not right to oppose every development," he said.

He said the farmers should be provided with alternative land even outside the plant area.

"Some land can be provided from inside the plant. The rest may come from outside. The farmers should have the alternative land as part of the compensation," he added.

Dasmunsi further said an all-party meeting should be called to discuss the impasse where attempt should be made to find a solution on the basis of three formulae — land for land, adequate compensation and employment.

He said the Tatas should have been involved in the discussions at the Raj Bhavan and Industries Minister Nirupam Sen should explain why Tata was kept out of the crucial meeting.

Heading: N-deal passage a diplomatic feat: Congress - Indian Express
Content: It was a poor start to the BJP's campaign for Lok Sabha elections in Doaba, with party president Rajnath Singh's Vijay Sankalp rally, coinciding with Bhagat Singh's death anniversary, drawing less than 5,000 people against the tall claims of 50,000. The crowd — apparently rustled up from nearby factory workers — comprised mainly the elderly. Singh accused the UPA Government of being soft on terror, and reiterated the demand for a strict law to counter it.

Heading: CM gets industry support to prevent ‘Carry’ fiasco - Indian Express
Content:
Left says nothing to celebrate

While the Congress on Sunday termed the passage of the nuclear deal in the US House of Representatives as the "highest feat" of diplomacy sculptured by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, the Left said there was hardly anything to celebrate for the UPA Government even as it chalked out its strategy to fight Government on the issue.

Congress spokesperson M Veerappa Moily said the country was also "grateful" to US President George W Bush who made it possible to happen due to his "untiring" efforts. "This is the highest feat of diplomacy chiselled and sculptured by our great statesman Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, guided and inspired by our visionary party president Sonia Gandhi," he said in a statement.

Congratulating the team of diplomats and nuclear scientists, he said "proud" India presented itself to the entire world "victory after victory" from the day the MoU on 123 agreement to the trust vote and from the clearance of the IAEA to the passage of the deal in the House.

In Kolkata, CPI(M) Politburo member Sitaram Yechury said the party would oppose the Indo-US nuclear deal when the Prime Minister comes back to India and places the bill in Parliament for discussion.

Claiming that apprehensions of the Left parties would come true, Yechury told the media that "this will only lead to India's surrender to American dictates and will have implications and bearing beyond the nuclear deal". "It is not surprising that the Senate will also approve it," he added.

CPI(M) State Committee secretary in West Bengal Biman Bose called for a "jihad" against the deal by uniting all sections of people. "It will endanger India's sovereignty and independent foreign policy," he said.

In the national Capital, CPI national secretary D Raja told The Indian Express, "There is nothing to celebrate. There is a wide gap between what the Prime Minister had told the Indian Parliament and what the Americans are saying now. This deal is not in India's interests. Our apprehensions have come true."

He said contrary to the Indian Government's claim, the 123 agreement was bound by the Hyde Act and other national laws of the US which is against the fundamental interests of India and would reduce New Delhi into a subordinate ally of US imperialism.

Heading: Kolkata police among the best: CM - Indian Express
Content:
Amid the uncertainty over the fate of Tata's small car factory, all the business chambers in the city are unanimous in their support of Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee in his efforts to renew licence of German wholesale giant Metro Cash & Carry.

"The chief minister's move is very much pro-industrialisation and investment-friendly," said Sandipan Chakraborty, Chairman of the Confederation of Indian Industry.

"We cannot have one more Singur. The stalemate over Tata Motors' plant is already sending a wrong message to the investors all over the world. We are often asked about the investment scenario in the state when we go abroad. So we can understand the condition. It is the time to act," he added.

"After Tata Motors, we cannot afford Metro Cash & Carry to leave the state and lose the scope of huge employment," added Chakraborty.

The same opinion is echoed by the Indian Chamber of Commerce (ICC).

"There must be a political will that can work for the state by not politicising things. Any kind of difference can be sorted out through discussions," said Sanjay Budhia, president, ICC.

"As far as the issue of using the discretion power is concerned, we support the chief minister . If he does not use his special powers during a crisis, then what is the use of the governance," asked Budhia.

"We praise the CM's move as it is investor-friendly. His decision will encourage the investors and attract more investment in the state. We are with the CM in every possible way. If this step had not been taken then the state might have lost all hopes of industrialisation in future," said P R Agarwala, president, Bharat Chamber of Commerce (BCC).

Heading: Buddha defers handing over of Technicians Studio till October 15 - Indian Express
Content:
Speaking at a ceremony to felicitate Police Award winners at the Shishir Mancha on Sunday, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee shied away from speaking on the recent string of controversies that have dogged his government.

Instead, he chose to spread awareness on the need to enhance security in the light of the recent terror attacks in the country.

"It seems that terror attacks are spilling over from our neighbouring countries. Kolkata is very much within the radius of terror attacks. Every once in a while, there are bomb blasts in major cities. Security needs to be enhanced in this regard," Buddha said.

His remarks are significant, given that the Centre is now looking at speeding up the Megacity Policing project, according to agency reports. Following two blasts within a fortnight in the national Capital, the Centre has decided to give impetus to the project in metro cities.

As part of the Megacity Policing Project, police forces in metros are to be equipped with more patrolling vehicles, latest surveillance gadgets and wireless sets to beat constables. To enhance surveillance, each city is to have helicopters.

The project extends to cities with population over 10 lakh, which brings 35 such cities under its scope.

Commending the 78 Kolkata Police officers who were awarded medals for outstanding service, Buddha said the city's police force was one of the best.

He said: "It is very necessary for the police to have a social face and be approachable."

Apart from police officers, six civilians were also conferred bravery awards.

The "Best Police Station" award went to Alipore Police Station.

Heading: Assam culture to come alive at Suruchi Sangha - Indian Express
Content:
Bogged down by the crisis involving the Tatas and German wholesale major Metro Cash & Carry, the state government seems to be in two minds on the handing over of the Technicians Studio to Zee Telefilms.

A month after announcing — much to the chagrin of the leading artistes and technicians of Tollygunj — that Technicians would be handed over to Zee for an amount of Rs 41 crore, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee last week told the information and culture department of his government not to go ahead with the process of handing over till October 15.

The state government had served eviction notices to 33 organisations including Artistes Forum and Technicians Forum, who have offices in the Studio premises. The deadline was supposed to expire on September 30.

On September 23, artistes and technicians including actor Saumitra Chatterjee, Prasenjit, and film makers Rituparno Ghosh and Gautam Ghose among others, met the chief minister at Nandan, and told him that they had some plans about the Studio, which they wanted to submit in writing.

Dilip Chakrabarty, principal secretary, department of information and culture, told The Indian Express: "The chief minister told me not to do anything now and wait till October 15. He said that by that time the artistes would let us know what they wanted to do there. Let us see what plan they send us".

Zee is planning to build a state-of-the art studio with facilities for the shooting of both telefilms and feature films.

Earlier this month, a group artistes and technicians led by Saumitra Chatterjee met Chakrabarty at Writers' Buildings and protested against the eviction of the offices. They also protested against the manner in which the 100-year old Studio was handed over to Zee.

Zee Telefilms officials, meanwhile, are waiting for the decision of the government. "We believe things will be sorted out amicably between the government and the artistes and technicians, and the Studio will be handed over to us. We are committed to the growth of the state and we will keep on doing everything in that direction," Rajib Chaterjee, head of Zee operations in Kolkata, said.

Heading: Flights resume with unchanged fares - Indian Express
Content:
From battlefields to Puja pandals, Kamalakanta Kaman (61), a former Border Security Force personnel, has come a long way. Kaman is busy carving bamboo and wood for deuri (a house-like structure of the Missing tribe of Assam) that will form a part of the Suruchi Sangha Puja pandal at New Alipore.

The organisers made several trips to Assam to source materials for Puja pandals and during one such trip they came to know about Majuli village, nearly 400 km from Guwahati. "Assam is a confluence of Shaiva, Shakti and Vaishnav sects of Hinduism. Cultural activities in Majuli village are being promoted by the Vasihnav sect," said Raja Sarkar, who has conceptualised this year's Puja along with Subodh Roy.

A team of 30 artisans from Navalgiri and Goalpara villages in Assam have been working for the last three months to recreate a temple that faintly resembles the famous Kamakhya temple of Assam.

The 70 feet structure is a riot of colours with splashes of red, green, yellow, brown, gold and black bamboo engravings, mats and artworks of cane. At least six types of bamboo, typical to Assam, are being used to create the pandal.

The idea to recreate Assam, said Sarkar, came due to practical reasons. "Over the last few years, rains have been spoiling Puja preparations. So, it made sense to use wood and bamboo, and the best theme was Assam," said Sarkar.

"We have to first burnish the bamboos so that they last long. It is difficult, they tend to attract bugs," said an artist.

Apart from aesthetic elements, the culture of Assam will come alive through live performances in the Puja pandal. Part of the entire structure is devoted to a workshop of the artisans where artisans will display their works throughout the Puja.

Moreover, artistes from various parts of Assam will perform Bihu, Assamese, Jumai and Rashlila dances and sing their traditional songs in a space devoted to them. In fact, the performances will be organised in a structure that resembles rang ghar, an integral part of royal structures in Assam. Six monks from the Shankardeb Ashram have also consented to be present at the Puja pandal. They are expected to preach about their sect and world peace through musical compositions, recitals and poetry.

Heading: Kolkata on Wheels arrives to reduce your traffic woes - Indian Express
Content:
With a slash in Air Turbine fuel (ATF) prices, most Airlines that had withdrawn flights from various sectors in July citing less passenger traffic have resumed their services.

The ATF contributes nearly 40 per cent of airlines' operating costs. The current reduction in its prices comes after two straight hikes during July and August. Domestic carriers are expected to lose $2 billion in the current financial year mainly on account of soaring fuel prices.

For consumers, however, it is not celebration time yet. Leading domestic airlines, including national carrier Air India, have ruled out any revision in fares at the moment.

"No fare cuts are being planned at the moment," said an Air India official. Air India that had temporarily withdrawn its flight to Bagdogra has already resumed the service from September. It also plans to operate its daily flight to Port Blair after September 30.

Delhi-based SpiceJet that had temporarily withdrawn flights to Bangalore, Delhi and Hyderabad, has decided to operate the Delhi flight from September. "The Hyderabad flight still remains suspended," said a SpiceJet official.

"We are not looking at any fare cuts now. ATF prices are volatile. We need at least 2-3 months of stable ATF prices before we go back and review current prices," said Samyukth Sridharan, Chief Commercial Officer, SpiceJet Limited.

Naresh Goyal-owned Jet Airways had raised base fares by 10 per cent in August.

The airline is planning to operate its early morning flight to Delhi from the last week of September, but has no plans for any fare cuts at the moment.

Heading: Defeating death, miracle baby to arrive home today - Indian Express
Content:
Wondering where to head for a long drive on the weekend? Or how to navigate your way through the chaotic traffic snarls in the city? Or even the best places to savour "rosogollas" from? There is good news for the explorers in Kolkata: The first automobile-centric lifestyle magazine dedicated exclusively to the city has been launched.

The monthly magazine, aptly christened Kolkata on Wheels, promises to be a complete handbook on the city. The first issue of the magazine, for instance, has one whole section describing the terrible condition of median dividers on city streets and how they pose a threat to motorists.

A Guide India publication, the magazine is supported by the Kolkata Traffic Police, Automobile Association of Eastern India, Rotary International District 3291 and Bengal Motor Sports Club.

In each issue, the magazine will trace the history behind each of the streets in Kolkata, with Park Street (now Mother Teresa Sarani) being in the spotlight in the first issue.

The magazine, which claims to be the first-of-its kind to fill a huge void in motoring in and around the city for the new generation car owners, will also dedicate a section to the "one-ways" in Kolkata.

"When you are caught in a traffic jam and not familiar with the streets and alleys of that locality, the section will help you to find a way out of the chaotic traffic maze," said Shyamashree Sen, managing editor of Kolkata on Wheels.

She added, "This is where the Kolkata Traffic Police has chipped in with its technical support, without which the venture could not have been possible".

It also has sections dedicated to places of interest in the city and destinations close to the city ideal for short trips. The first issue features Mandarmoni, a sea-side locale where motorists can drive-in during their weekends.

The magazine will also contain sections on food and columns where celebrities speak of their favourite car models. It will also have car care tips and a discussion forum for car owners to brainstorm on the myriad problems centred around motoring in the city.

Heading: Students to judge pandals - Indian Express
Content:
Holding her three-month-old infant in her arms in the neonatal intensive care unit of the Calcutta Medical Research Institute (CMRI), Sangita Das could not conceal her tears of joy.

Her baby is now ready to go home on Monday after a long battle for survival.

Das still shudders at the recollection of the sad sequence of events on July 1, when her newborn was declared dead by the doctors of a private nursing home where the baby was delivered. It was only when the death certificate of the baby was being prepared that the hospital staff found him alive.

"This is one feeling which cannot be described in words," she said. The baby, fondly called "Rik", was born after 24 weeks of gestation and weighed only 700 grams. In medical parlance such condition is described as "extremely premature and low birth weight baby".

"When I saw the baby, he was only 11 hours old. His heart beat was irregular and faint and he appeared blue due to poor blood circulation. The lungs and kidney were not functional either," recalled Dr Kakoli Acharya under whose supervision the baby was kept. "We admitted him to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit where he was put on an artificial life support for more than a month," she added.

Doctors of Belle Vue nursing home had declared the baby dead and later clarified that it was a case of "suspended animation" —- a term used to describe the condition of a patient who does not respond to medical treatment. The newborn was then admitted to CMRI.

Dr Parag Pal of RG Kar Medical College and Hospital, who is conducting a research on suspended animation, said: "In medical history, there is no recorded case of a patient in suspended animation for more than 30 minutes. This baby remained in this state for nearly 10 hours." It was a proud moment for the doctors of the CMRI who battled all odds to ensure the miraculous survival of the infant.

"The challenge was taken up not only by the team from paediatrics department, but by all the departments together to ensure the speedy recovery of the baby," said Rupak Barua, Chief Operating Officer of CMRI. The baby required round-the-clock monitoring and was given doses of "surfactants" and "ionotropes" to stabilize his lungs and heart respectively.

Dr Sougata Acharya, a member of the medical team, said: "It is a miracle. In case of extremely premature babies, the survival rate is only five per cent in the best paediatric centres in the country".

Weighing a little over a kilogram now, the baby is fast gaining weight. He is, however, still on doses of iron and vitamin supplements along with breast milk, Acharya said.

He added that the last four months had witnessed only three such similar cases across the world — in Isreal, Mumbai and Kolkata. In the first two cases the babies could not survive.

The baby's father, Manas Das, has meanwhile christened his child "Arjun". "He is no less than a fighter and no name could be more apt than this ," said Das.

Heading: Student dies, kin blames Apollo - Indian Express
Content:
Pandal committees will not only face competition from big brands but will also be scrutinised by schoolchildren who will judge them for this year's M P Birla Foundation Puja Utkarsh Samman.

Twenty four students of Class IX and XI from South Point High School and MP Birla Foundation Higher Secondary School will visit nearly 100 pandals in and around Kolkata to judge them for the award.

"For me, the criteria to judge pandals will be safety measures and art display," said Poulami Lahiri, a Class XI student of South Point.

"Every year I go out with my parents. It will be exciting to visit pandals as a judge. It is a matter of pride and responsibility," said Rishav Mitra, a Class IX student of MP Birla Foundation. Each student will study art work, idol designs, clothes, illumination and also find out whether the pandals have adopted adequate safety norms.

"They will see whether the pandals have taken all the precautionary measures to control fire as per our specified guidelines. Being young, these students will be fair in their judgment," State Fire and Emergency Services Minister Pratim Chaterjee said.

The students will be split into eight teams and will visit nearly 100 shortlisted pandals for two days on Sasthi and Saptami from 3 pm onwards.

The students will be escorted by teachers and individual evaluation sheets filled up by them will be tabulated to come to the final verdict.

Although the names of the winners will be announced on October 7, the awards will be presented during the prize distribution function of South Point High School on July 4 next year. The awards will comprise of a gold chain, an angavastra, a certificate and a trophy.

Heading: Kolkata confidential - Indian Express
Content:
Students of Jadavpur University's engineering department tried to enter Apollo Gleneagles Hospital on Sunday after they came to know that their classmate Mayuk Ghosh, who had been admitted earlier this month, had died allegedly under questionable circumstances. A pandemonium was, however, averted by the timely intervention of police.

Phoolbagan police station OC Nimroz Khan said around 100 students had tried to enter the hospital at around 6 pm.

"They were agitated but we stopped them from entering the building. No arrests were made. Mrinalkanti Ghosh, father of the deceased, has lodged a complaint alleging negligence on the part of the hospital," Khan said.

Mayuk (19), a first year student of civil engineering, had fallen off a running train on September 4. They added that his left hand had been amputated and he was recuperating with the support of a ventilator.

Ghosh said when he reached the hospital on Sunday morning, he found the ventilator was taken off. Shortly afterwards, Mayuk died. Apollo Hospital's director of medical services Saibal Chakraborty said, "We are looking into the matter seriously."

Heading: On high notes - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Express showcases news from the City of Joy that was off camera and outside inverted commas

Mood swing at Writers' Buildings
With the chances of the Tatas staying in Singur becoming slim, the mood in the bureaucratic circles at Writers' Buildings has become grim. A definite streak of despair and frustration is evident in their words whenever they talk of Singur. "It will be a tragedy if the Tatas leave the state," is their common refrain. Many officials are not happy the way Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee signed the compensation package agreement with the Trinamool Congress. "Had Minister for Commerce and Industries Nirupam Sen handled the issue, he would have never signed the agreement," an official said.
Police deal with threat on home front With the beginning of festive season, it seems that Kolkata police personnel are more vulnerable on home front rather than anywhere else. Almost all police officers, irrespective of their ranks, have a duty schedule stretched to its limit. But their family members, especially wives, are a furious lot. Many officers were heard pacifying their wives on telephones. "Our wives want us to take them shopping during Pujas. They do not understand that we cannot afford to go as we have a very tight schedule," said a senior police officer at Lalbazar. "My wife is staying at her parents' house with our two children. She said she will spend the festival there. She does not even pick up my calls now," said an inspector at a central Kolkata police station.

Anti-Dalmiya? Come to BCCI
There's good news for critics of Jagmohan Dalmiya. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has appointed former Bengal player Raja Venkat for the coveted post of national selector. Venkat, a former Ranji Trophy player, not associated with the Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB), but he was picked up for the coveted Rs 25-lakh-a-year job because he is the only Dalmiya critic available at the moment among the former cricketers of Bengal. The Dalmiya-led CAB had forwarded several names for the high-profile post, but all of them were rejected. The lesson: Don't lose heart if you can't beat Dalmiya in Maidan politics, BCCI will look after you if you are stamped as anti-Dalmiya.

French curiosity over Singur
Singur has aroused curiosity even among the overseas visitors to the state. Following a meeting between a seven-member delegation of French Senate and Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee at Writers' Buildings, when the mediapersons pounced on the delegation in the conference room, its leader Pierre Fauchon started explaining in French on what the Chief Minister told them about the farmers' resistance in the state. At first, the interpreter started translating his words in English, but soon she realised that not everything that was discussed between the delegation and the CM should come to light. Little did the leader realise that he was addressing the media. The interpreter cut Fauchon short, but the word "media" was overheard and the delegation leader switched the topic.

Embarrassed on traffic chaos
"Despite your tall claims of streamlining the city's traffic, the major arterial roads are jammed. What is wrong?" This question saw a police officer turning red, when asked by his senior at Lalbazar. The reason: the officer had come to invite mediapersons assembled in the senior police officer's room for a press conference on traffic arrangements during Pujas.

Heading: Euphoric beats - Indian Express
Content:
Soniya Jain, a Puneite, will be competing aginst 69 countries at Miss Intercontinental beauty pageant in October

After having walked the ramp for designer Nivedita Saboo at the Pune central mall and chosen as the finalist at the NDA Queen Pageant this year, Pune girl Soniya Jain is all set to give her best shot at the Miss Intercontinental pageant held by the World Beauty Organisation (WBO), next moth in Zebraze, Poland.

A second year student of Ness Wadia College, pursuing her Bachelors degree in Business Administration, Jain is the only contestant representing India this year and will be competing participants from 69 countries across the globe, "The pageant training, for me, has been a transformation from a reluctant teenager to a responsible woman who will be shouldering the responsibility to represent my nation on an international platform. And I promise to give my best shot," says Jain. While talking of her studies she adds, "The crown does means a lot to me, but my studies remain of prime importance. Education would give me a broader dimension to look at things. One day I want to set up my own business. I want to be an independent woman and even after I get married I would love to work."

Apart from these Jain has keep interest in adventure sports and acting. She says, "After the Pagent I would be working towards making a mark in Bollywood."

Says the bubbly teenager who loves to munch on burger, chips and pizzas, "I have been missing all of it for long, My fitness and diet sessions have been very strict and I have followed them very obediently as I wanted to give in my hundred per cent," says Jain who admits that beauty does not come easily and there is a lot of grinding to it.

British singer Jay Sean shares his list of favourite Hindi movies and songs

He has always had a huge female following and he is immensely talented and known as one of UK's major Asian talents. Jay Sean the British singer and songwriter from London, who started his career in 2003 with his first single Dance with you—Nachna Tere Naal with Juggy D and Rishi Rich "It was a great experience working with both of them. They are immensely talented and know the music very well," says Sean. His video Stolen featuring the Bong beauty Bipasha Basu sizzled the UK charts for many weeks.

Talking about Bollywood films and Indian music Sean says, "I have grown up seeing Hindi films and I am very fond of them. I have always loved the melodious numbers from films like Saajan and Aashiqui and I specially like the title track of Aashiqui," says Sean who has been nominated for two awards—best R&B soul Act and Best UK Male Solo Act—for the Mobo Awards to be held in October this year, one of UK's premier music awards. Sean was in the city for a show.

He is the winner of the 2008 UK Asian Music Awards for the best video and Best Urban Act for the song Ride It. "When I was making the song I had gone to this club called Movida. That's when I decided to shoot it. I liked the place so much that I also mentioned the name of the club in the lyrics of Ride It," says Sean.

Sean has released two albums — Me against myself and My Own Way— along with five top 20 hits in the UK Singles Chart. Best known for his hit numbers Stolen, Eyes On You and the latest Ride it, Sean is tipped to be the first British Asian to make the cross over into mainstream Rhythm and blues, music genre combining jazz, gospel, and blues influences. "I have been doing R&B for over six years now, but I enjoy other music forms too," says the 25-year-old singer.

Talking about his trip to India he says, "Although I was born and brought up in UK, I have always felt like a part of me is in India. I feel immensely proud to be a native Indian and I feel privileged to be associated to its name and to see people living here expecting so much from me. I'm very excited about this tour to India, especially places like Hyderabad where I haven't been in a while. I look forward to meeting all my fans and friends here and playing some of my new music from my new album My Own Way and I also look forward to having fun here."

Heading: chatter box - Indian Express
Content:
Get set to be initiated into the whacky world of Saturday Night Live

Does your only dose of television comedy come in the form of unintentionally funny saas-bahu dramas? Fear not; relief is at hand as Saturday Night Live (SNL), the longest running comedy sketch/variety show on television, is finally in India. The show, which debuted on September 22 in India, airs on VH1, every week, from Monday to Saturday at 9 pm.

Few shows have a richer comic history than SNL. The legendary show launched many successful careers — Eddie Murphy, Adam Sandler, Chris Rock and Ben Stiller, to name a few. In a politically correct world, SNL stands out for its no-holds-barred humour, taking pot-shots at everyone from the Pope to Hillary Clinton to Mel Gibson. The show has also got celebrities to poke fun at themselves such as the famous episode where Britney Spears came on wearing inflatable breasts, in reaction to rumours that she'd had her breasts surgically enhanced.

The typical format of the show features a regular cast of comic actors, joined by a guest host and a musical act. In the past, guest hosts have included Steve Martin, Tom Hanks and Drew Barrymore. The musical acts, both mainstream and breakthrough, have included performers such as Paul Simon, Sting and Jennifer Lopez.

SNL had an audience in India long before VH1 finally decided to bring it here. Says actor and VJ Luke Kenny, "I've been a fan since the '70s. It is not just about comedy; it also brings acting skills to the fore." VJ Cyrus Sahukar agrees. "I've been a fan for at least seven-eight years," he says, "It's like an institution in the west —the Harvard or Oxford of comedy; every established comic actor from Jim Carrey to Chris Rock to Adam Sandler has been on SNL."

Ferzad Palia, Associate GM of VH1 India, says that they picked out SNL episodes that would suit the comic palate of the Indian viewer. "We didn't want to air episodes from the '70s and '80s; we were looking for more current content that had a certain topicality for Indian viewers. Also, we needed episodes with musical acts and celebrity hosts who're known in this country. For instance, on Tuesday, we aired an episode that had Ashton Kutcher as the host and Gwen Stefani as the musical act."

The concept of a comedy sketch combined with live music is not new in India. Movers and Shakers, which was based on the formats of SNL and the Tonight Show with Jay Leno, proved to be very popular with viewers. But even the peerless mimic Shekhar Suman, known for his spot-on imitations of various political and non-political figures knew where to draw the line. So will SNL, with its irreverent brand of comedy that combines mimicry, risqué jokes and many,

Many instances of cross-dressing, ever find an Indian avatar?

"Definitely," says Kenny, "But only for an English-speaking audience. As for a Hindi version of SNL, I don't think that'll happen anytime soon." Sahukar adds, "I don't see why there can't be an Indian version, since we have some excellent comedians and musicians here. But there are way too many restrictions in our society and people tend to get offended very easily, so it may take many years."

SNL who?

* Sting is the only non-American performer to appear as a musical guest at least five times; he has also performed in at least one sketch during each of his performances.

* The movies The Blues Brothers, Wayne's World and Wayne's World 2 are film spin-offs of SNL sketches.

* Sinead O'Connor's October 2, 1992, live performance in which she destroyed a picture of Pope John Paul II was substituted by her dress rehearsal performance from earlier that evening when she held up a picture of a starving African child.

* Britney Spears was 18 when she first appeared on the show on May 13, 2000, which makes her the youngest person in SNL history to act as a host and a musical guest at the same time.

Heading: Defeating destiny - Indian Express
Content:
Best fit

For Amit Tandon, playing the character of the NRI Abhay Singh in Saath Saath Banayenge Ek Ashiyaan on Zee TV was an easy task, because of his Canadian origin and the firang accent he sports. But after a successful run, Tandon has decided to call it quits. The channel has subsequently roped in Salil Acharya as a substitute in the show. Salil who has been a part of popular shows like Yeh Meri Life Hai, Kasauti Zindagi Ki, Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Thi, Kittu Sab Janti Hai and Kasturi, is very excited about the role he has bagged. But matching Tandon's American twang is going to be difficult.

Home grown

Neena Gupta has her plate full these days. After her much talked about wedding with Vivek Mehra, Neena is now resurrecting her career. She will make a comeback with her character of Manno Bhabhi in Saath Phere. She has been given the liberty to design her costumes, jewellery and hairstyle. Interestingly, the lehenga- cum -saree that she plans to drape in the show has been inspired by her costume that she had worn in her mehndi-sangeet ceremonies. We'll keep our fingers crossed.

Heading: Match this - Indian Express
Content:
Two individuals from two different countries find strength not in their analogous misfortune but their common will to survive and reach out to others

Jonathan Sigworth is a US citizen who came to India in 2006 to study world history. Studies, change of climate and new surroundings, everything seemed just perfect until September 2006 when taking a steep turn on the mountaneous Mussourie roads on his bicycle, Sigworth met with an accident that changed everything forever.

"I do not remember how I met with the accident. But what came as a shock was that when I opened my eyes in the hospital, I realized that I was no more a normal human being. The accident had made me a quadriplegic," says Jonathan.

Quadriplegia made Jonathan paralytic, taking away all sensation chest downwards. Jonathan's incapability to move his hands and legs meant nothing but dependability. "That year I went back to the US to be with my parents, friends and relatives. The initial sympathy and concern was there but I realized that no one is going to be with me permanently, despite all their love for me."

Jonathan was left with only one solution- doing everything on his own. And that was the real challenge. Quadriplegic patients not only lose the strength but also the senses from below the chest, which means that not only the activities like walking, running and writing but also routine activities like bathing, getting up, wearing clothes are affected. "I had no other option but to become self dependant to regain my lost confidence. It was during this time that I came across rugby, a sports played by quadriplegics in the USA. I played it and started enjoying it. The game gave me a confidence that there are people like me in the world and it boosted my morale," adds Sigworth.

Today, Jonathan in his own words is 99 percent independent. He says, "You will be surprised to know that it takes me 45 minutes to get up. One hour to have bath, 45 minutes to go to the loo. It is time consuming but yes I am on my own. I am proud of the fact that I am quadriplegic yet self dependent."

And now, the passion has entered his blood. He's realized that efforts pay and Jonathan is on a new venture. Today he dreams of opening the largest quadriplegia surgery center in the world. "I had come to India after that and I realised that the condition of quadriplegics in India is not the same as ours. The kind of facilities that we get in US are much more advanced that what we have here. For instance, the chairs here are heavier than the ones in US. Also, we get a yearly compensation in America. The roads and elevators there are much more user-friendly for people like us than the ones here. I cannot change the conditions in India. So I am here to strengthen the quadriplegics so that they like me can face life with confidence," says Jonatahn who is currently at the Paraplegic Rehabilitation Center in Pune to teach the patients rugby.

Destiny can sometimes be synonymous with injustice. What else can explain the turn of events that led to Amit Saroha, a national level hockey player, becoming wheel chair bound. The 25-year-old resident of Sonipat in Haryana still vividly remembers that day in February 2007 when Saroha along with his four friends was traveling in a car that met with an accident. The irony is that while the four friends who were under the influence of alcohols survived with minor injuries, Saroha the only was who had not consumed had his life altered forever.

A year since the accident his family is yet to get over the shock. But they have rallied around the young man like only close families are capable of doing. His brother Sumit Saroha left his media job in New Delhi to take care of Amit Saroha, who since the accident has become a quadriplegic. Saroha says, "I look at the positive side of life. The good part of my story is that I met Jonathan during my surgery in Delhi. It is a difficult life as a quadriplegic. But since one year, I have also been traveling with Jonathan helping him in his noble cause."

A year with Jonathan has made Saroha partly independent. He is learning not only to do his routine activities but is also helping Jonathan promote rugby. "In fact I myself am surprised over the fact that I learnt swimming from Jonathan in just a few hours," he smiles.

The duo is undoubtedly a living example of how determination overpowers destiny.

Heading: Dissolving boundaries - Indian Express
Content:
Constable Smita Pawar on being the first woman in the city to win the highest-grade sports award in handball

Making the force and her city proud is Smita Pawar, a constable with the Wanowrie Police Station, who has just bagged the Shiv Chhatrapati Award for the game of handball. In real life, the otherwise tough looking constable, is traditional and a soft-natured person.

"I have been playing this game since my school days. Our coach always encouraged the girls to participate in such sports. At that time I played handball with my batchmates, later, I was selected to represent our school at the state level," says Pawar, an alumni of Bhekrai Mata Madhyamik Vidyalaya, Phursungi.

Smita has graduated with Bsc. Honours in chemistry after which she joined the police force three years back. "My aim is to become the deputy superintendent of police for which I am pursuing my education now. My parents advised that if I want to be in this department then I must know it from the core, so I started off as a constable after passing the police exams," says 25-year-old Pawar, who loves to read literary books in her leisure time.

Striking a balance between her duty and the game, Pawar says, "Although, these days I do not get much time to read, I make sure not to miss on my early morning sessions of handball, after which I start off for my duty." So how does she cope up with the tiring work hours and her sports, "Well, it's not really tough. Infact my game is like a workout for me, these daily sessions not only help me be fit but also build my stamina and endurance," says Pawar who is currently studying to attain a higher position in the police department and also preparing for admission to an MBA in human resources. "Being a cop is my first choice. Besides, one must have good management skills and they are also very important to be in the police force," says Pawar who looks up to Meeran Borwankar as her role model.

Talking of the increasing number of women in the police department these days Pawar says, "It is good to see the increasing strength of women. I hope some day women will equal men in the police force in terms of numbers." And while speaking on the role and responsibility of a cop she adds, "This is an honourable job. I am proud to be a part of a department that serves for the people and the nation. I would just like to say that whatever may come your way, you must fulfill your duties with complete loyalty and keep up the trust that people have imposed on you," she concludes.

Heading: Mistimed, misplaced, mismanaged - Indian Express
Content:
Vishwa Jagriti Mission Trust has set an example for the society by visiting flood hit areas of Bihar and helping the flood victims with basic things

While some leave no stone unturned in dividing the country on the basis of regionalism and language, there are few bravehearts, who make all efforts to save human life irrespective of the political boundaries and other differences.

Setting one such example for the world to follow, a Pune based organisation, Vishwa Jagriti Mission Trust (VJMT), had set out to help people of Bihar, who were stuck in flood.

"In past we have participated in rescue operations during tsunami in Andaman and earthquake in Gujarat. People of Pune have been an excellent support as we could manage to get four wagons full of food, clothes and other necessities for the flood victims within two days," says Narendra Pal Singh, who was in the rescue team of VJMT and who is a financial consultant by profession.

Sharing his experience with the Bihar administration, Singh says that they had to struggle a lot to get their stuff cleared from the administration. "We nearly had to fight to get a permission to get directly involved in rescue operation and reach out to victims. We were asked to hand over the material to Red Cross to which we did not agree. As I myself saw that heavy amount of food grains and other materials were lying unused but were not distributed among the needy. So we decided that we would ourselves distribute things among the flood victims," shares Singh.

Singh says that they were a bit apprehensive regarding the response that they might get from the victims but all turned out be better than expected. They had heard of the anti-social activities that go on in the deserted villages and also heard that the victims might get violent. But they were surprised to see that when they very humbly explained the situation to the villagers and asked for their cooperation, they got more than expected.

"It was height of honesty when flood hit families returned the extra food to us after taking their required share. I was touched by this gesture. The youth their helped us in unloading and distributing the stuff among the victims. Media has so wrongly portrayed people of Bihar, who are hardworking and honest," shares Singh.

Singh says locals point out that even in such adverse conditions politicians do not sink their differences and come together to help the flood-affected. The existence of Lalu camp, Nitish camp and Paswan camp corroborates the fact that politicians merely look upon this as an ideal opportunity to further their cause by influencing the voters.

For further assistance, Singh says that they are committed to send mats to arrange for bedding for the victims.

Heading: Students to welcome baton team - Indian Express
Content:
The Commonwealth Youth Games' special superfast airconditioned train chugged into utter chaos on Sunday. The train, on its maiden run from Delhi, was late by more than an hour and the authorities sent passengers scrambling in confusion over the platform slotted for the train.

"First they said platform number 3; when we took our bags there to wait, they announced it would arrive on platform number 1. The departure was scheduled for 3.30 pm; we have been waiting for more than an hour. If this is the case on the first day, then what are they going to do during the CYG," said Parinder Singh, a passenger.

Passengers were also upset by poor amenities. Karlok Singh and three other businessmen had reserved tickets to Delhi via the Mumbai Rajdhani. "We cancelled those after we read about the Games train in the newspapers. But there is no water in the toilets, the air-conditioner is not working and the train is late," Singh complained.

Railway authorities said all this was nothing more than teething problems. "The train arrived late from Delhi. It ought to have arrived by 10.30 am, but it came after 1.30 pm," Senior Divisional Commissioner Ashok Malhotra admitted, after postponing the departure by an hour.

On the confusion over platforms, he said, "We had scheduled it for platform number 3 but there were many petitions from the public asking us to put it for platform 1. The slot between 2 pm to 6.30 pm is very hectic but we rescheduled it because this is an important train for the city."

Rail authorities were also criticised for the lack of publicity for the train. On its maiden run, the train ran nearly empty with only 74 passengers - 64 in the third AC and 10 in the second AC. Most passengers had heard about the train only through newspapers. "We were not sure that the train would start today. The bookings opened only at 8 am in the morning, because of which the reservations are few," said Malhotra.

The train was finally flagged off from platform number 1 at around 4.30 pm by former Indian hockey team captain Dhanraj Pillai. It will run twice a week till the CYG ends and w ill depart from Pune at 15:20 hours and reach Nizamuddin at 12.40 hours. The journey will last for 21 hours and would cost less than trips on other trains plying between Pune and Delhi.

Heading: Sewage, once paid for, will now pay - Indian Express
Content:
Thousands of students from various schools and colleges of the city are getting ready to give a warm reception to the Youth Baton Relay, on the run up to the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) starting on October 12 at the Balewadi Sports Complex here.

Rehearsals are on in full swing, not only to welcome the relay team, but also to perform cultural events for the CYG show. The relay, flagged off from New Delhi on August 1, has already crossed around 200 cities in nine states and will reach Pune on October 6. On October 6-7, cultural events and street plays will be staged at various points on the roads to welcome the participants.

Thousands of children will be there to welcome the baton relay team that has a green theme and is spreading the 'Save the Tiger' campaign of the central government.

"At 3 pm on October 6, the relay will start from Bhakti Shakti Chowk in Nigdi and pass through Bhel chowk, Bijalinagar, Chapekar chowk, Pimpri overbridge, Morwadi Road and then head towards the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation office. It will end for the day at Telco guest house," said assistant police inspector Arvind Gokule.

The next day, it will start at 7 am from the guest house and pass through Magar Stadium, Mhada Colony, Morwadi chowk, Mumbai Pune highway, Chinchwad railway flyover, Chapekar chowk, Walhekarwadi Phata, Dange chowk, Sai chowk, Shagun chowk and pass in front of the Hindustan Antiobiotics factory on the Mumbai-Pune highway. The team will then proceed to Nashik Phata, Kasarwadi, Phugewadi, Dapodi and Khadki.

Students all over the city are rehearsing every day to participate in the CYG. They are not competing in the events but will be cheering the participants of 71 countries. They will also stage various cultural events. Jigrr, the mascot of the Games, has been put up at schools where students are rehearsing.

Heading: Delimitation headache: Same voters, different lists, 3.4 lakh times - Indian Express
Content:
Civic admin turns expense into earning

For years, the Pune Municipal Corporation has been paying for the disposal of sewage and effluent, but it is now all set to generate revenue from it. The civic administration has floated expression of interest for selling treated sludge and effluent from its sewage treatment plants (STPs) for use in agriculture and construction activity.

"The PMC has been so far giving money to dispose of the sewage to private parties. It also supplied effluent to its own gardens department. But the augmentation and upgradation of the STPs under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) has changed it all and now the good quality treated sludge and effluent would be sold," V G Kulkarni, development engineer (STP projects), said on Sunday.

He said PMC has floated expression of interest for selling treated sludge and effluent to parties that can make proper use of it.

"This is the first time that the PMC has decided to sell the treated products from the STPs. The civic administration is not expecting much revenue from it initially, but is hopeful of its demand increasing once interested parties get to know about the quality of treated sludge and effluent," he said, adding, the high nitrogen, phosphate and potassium content makes the sludge good for agriculture.

The PMC would initially sell the treated sludge from Erandwane, Tanajiwadi, Bopodi, Naidu and Bhairoba STPs. "Even if the treated sludge is sold at Rs 2,000 per day per STP, the PMC would earn Rs 30 lakh annually from the four plants. This will increase as the treated sludge is sold from other plants too," Kulkarni said. However, the additional cost of the construction of STP under JNNURM is under scrutiny.

"This will reduce the load on STPs daily and generate revenue for the PMC," he said. The PMC has asked potential bidders to visit the STPs and check the characteristics and quantity of treated sludge generated to ensure the quality and quantity. "The interested parties can select any of the STPs and collect the sludge every day from it," he said. "The bidders have to make suitable arrangements for lifting the sludge at their own cost for limited time period as per the contract."

Similarly, a good quality of effluent is being generated from the STP and it can be used for flushing, washing floors, gardening and construction purposes, Kulkarni said. "In no case should the treated effluent be used for potable purposes."

The treated effluent from the five STPs will be around 305 million litre per day. "The effluent from other STPs too will be sold as per demand. The proper use of effluent can help in reducing the load on the water supply system of the city," he said.

"The water supply department offers the service of water supply from tankers at Rs 350, but the same can be made available at Rs 25 per tanker for those assuring proper use of it either for gardening, construction or cleaning," Kulkarni said.

Heading: Cheated at 50, case won at 60, money lost forever? - Indian Express
Content:
With over 3.41 lakh voters from 21 assembly constituencies in the district figuring twice in the voters application list after delimitation, the election branch of the district collectorate is all set to issue notices, as per procedure, to those individuals after the final list for the district is declared on October 7.

Pune has 21 assembly constituencies after the delimitation exercise, up from 18. The district has 54,82,085 voters according to the data available till July 31.

Around 3.47 lakh additional applications came for revision after till August 22, after the delimitation process. These applications are being scrutinised by the election branch. The final list after checking additions, deletions, corrections and transfer from one constituency to the other will be put up on October 7, according to the deputy election officer, Varsha Untwal.

With many instances of repetitions, Untwal said a software developed by the department is targeting to identify at least 10,000 repeated names in each constituency. "It is a voluminous work and we will have to issue separate notices to these individuals as per procedure. This would take time and we would deal with it separately after the list is put up," she said.

Untwal said that the July 31-August 21 period saw a good number of fresh applications. The final list will be displayed in each constituency, she said. Chinchwad, Kasba Peth, Vadgaon Sheri, Baramati, Pune Cantonment, Hadapsar, Parvati, Khadakvasla, Kothrud, Bhosari, Pimpri, Maval, Bhor, and Shirur constituencies have more than 2,50,000 voters each. Chinchwad leads with 2,92,928 voters. The lowest number is in Daund with 2,33,634 voters.

The department is also gearing up to issue voter I-cards starting October 15.

In Pune city, the number of constituencies has gone up from six to eight after delimitation. These are Vadgaonsheri, Kothrud, Shivajinagar, Parvati, Kasba Peth, Hadapsar, Pune Cantonment and Khadakvasla.

The others in the district are Junnar, Ambegaon, Khed Alandi, Shirur, Daund, Indapur, Baramati and Purandar.

Heading: Media should not conduct parallel trial: SC judge - Indian Express
Content:
The press should not conduct its own parallel trial or give their evaluation of evidence and foretell the decision of the court, said Justice Dalveer Bhandari, Supreme Court Judge, while addressing the students during a lecture series organised by Symbiosis International University at Symbiosis Vishwabhawan on Saturday.

Bhandari said, "In the Arushi murder case, before the investigations were over the media interviewed the officers. Though what they spoke to the media is not admissible in court, people believed it and her father became the most hated man in the world, a criminal before the verdict was out."

Bhandari said, "In a free democracy, even the person who had assassinated the Father of the Nation also has right to a fair trial. The media is expected to not invade the rights of an individual or obstruct a fair trial. Their obligation of fair reporting becomes even more important when they know that the judiciary does not respond or the judges by and large do not respond because of the longstanding convention that the Judges speak only through their Judgements."

He said that the time has come that every court should have a senior person who should assist the press in getting them the certified and other copies of the orders passed by the court, particularly in areas of larger public interest.

Speaking on the occasion Swatanter Kumar, Chief Justice of Bombay High Court said, "Undue stress on employment-oriented studies and result-oriented examination has its adverse effect on the overall quality of education. Assessment of teachers on the basis of pass per centage of their students compels a teacher to be exam-oriented resulting in mass production of mediocres."

'Don't treat a witness like an accused'

* At the state conference on criminal Justice system organised by the Maharashtra Law Academy on Saturday, Bhandari said that witnesses should not be treated like accused as they assist in the delivery of justice. "A witness hesitates to depose before the court as he as to take leave from work and come to the court at 10 am and wait till 5 pm, only to know that his case has been adjourned. So the best the judges can do is if the case if going to come up for hearing at 3 pm, then call the witness at that time." Bhandari pointed out that every court in India violates right to speedy trial, even the Supreme court is no exception. We should ensure that the trial should be completed in two years.

Heading: Pimpri Cong launches website - Indian Express
Content:
A man was hacked to death by three people on Baner Road around 1 am on Sunday. The police have identified the man as Dharampal Munnilal Verma (26), who was doing road construction work. The police have arrested the accused Navnath Tamhane (25), Sagar Chakankar (22) and Rahul Chakankar (22) in connection with the case on the basis of a complaint filed by Rambabu Verma.

"No reason could be found for the killing. The three people who are accused for the murder of Verma were drunk at the time," said assistant police inspector BI Kamble.

Police officials said that Rambabu and Dharampal accompanied by a surveyor were working on Baner road near Balewadi phata on Sunday morning, when suddenly a group of boys came to the spot they were standing and hit Dharampal on the head with a crowbar and a wooden club. Dharampal sustained serious injuries. He was taken to Aundh Chest Hospital where he was proclaimed dead on arrival.

Heading: IDBI Fortis opens its branch - Indian Express
Content:
The Pimpri Chinchwad unit of the Congress is launching a website of its own which has been christened www.pimprichinchwadcongress.com . The website will be inaugurated on October 2.

"On October 2, we are going to take out a prabhat pheri spreading the message of ahimsa (non violence) from Bhoirnagar in Chinchwad to Congress party's office in Pimpri. The rally on its way will pass through Chapekar Chowk and Link Road. At the Congress party office members will take a pledge of non-violence and a common prayer meeting for people belonging to all religions will be held," said Congress leader Babu Nair.

"On October 2 we will also start a membership drive which will go on till November 14. We hope to register around 50,000 members till that time," he added.

Heading: ATS surges ahead - Indian Express
Content:
As a part of its aggressive 100-branch plan, IDBI Fortis Life Insurance Co Ltd on Friday formally opened its branch in the city. The branch is located at Erandwane.

The company has launched operations in March this year, leading with its innovative product Wealthsurance. It has already collected premium over Rs 100 crore in five months. The company plans to have 13 branches in the State, out of the 30 branches in the western region in total, stated a release.

"With changing lifestyles, more and more people want to invest their money for long term wealth building. We hope to target this segment with our unique wealth-building products that will help their investments grow by protecting it from unforeseen circumstances," said G V Nageswara Rao, MD & CEO, IDBI Fortis Life Insurance Co Ltd.

IDBI Fortis Life Insurance is a joint-venture of IDBI, India's premier development and commercial bank, Federal Bank, a leading private sector bank and Fortis, Europe's banking and insurance giant.

Wealthsurance aims to provide people with protected growth. The product is designed to ensure that the hard-earned money that is invested is not susceptible to unforeseen circumstances. WealthsuranceTM offers investment choices such as Guaranteed Return Fund, Capital Guaranteed Fund, Monthly Interest Account, Equity Funds, Debt Funds. "The powerful insurance benefits of WealthsuranceTM ensure that a customer's wealth plan is not affected by unforeseen events that may strike them," Rao added.

Murali Iyer, national head, Agency & Alliances, IDBI Fortis, said, "Pune is the most industrialised district in western Maharashtra and a famous IT hub in the country, all this makes the city more attractive in terms of economic development. We at IDBI Fortis see a major opportunity in Maharashtra not only to expand our business but to harness the state's talent pool."

Heading: How to file RTI plea? Few know... - Indian Express
Content:
ATS Conveyors India has increased its automobile market participation by collecting orders from Mahindra International, Ashok Leyland and Tata Motors.

In first quarter of fiscal 2008, ATS India bagged orders worth around Rs 25 crore. ATS India is in position to meet the growing customer demand with well-developed and expanded manufacturing facility in Pune, stated a press release. Over the years, European ATS Group has combined expertise, technology, a commitment to quality and advanced manufacturing skills to become a major supplier to provide the solution to complex material handling needs on turnkey basis.

Within a short span of two and half years, ATS India has more than 25 installations across the country comprising mainly of electric monorail sysytem, P&F overhead conveyors and floor conveyors, the release added.

Heading: 8 villages of Itaunja district submerged again - Indian Express
Content:
Despite three years of enactment of the Right To Information (RTI) Act, "most visitors who visited RTI on wheels, a mobile van for giving information about the act, did not know the basics of filing an RTI application," said Major General S C N Jatar, advisory council member of Public Concern for Governance Trust (PCGT).

According to Jatar, about 750 persons visited the mobile van stationed at Salunke Vihar Community Hall on Saturday and at Pune Vidyarthi Griha and S P College on Sunday. "Many defence personnel and students visited the van. Although not many students questioned us, they keenly watched our presentations and sought information on fine details of the act," Jatar said. While in Pune, the volunteers not only gave presentations, but also helped many in filing RTI applications.

The van, developed in Ahmedabad by Gujarat-based Mahiti Adhikar Gujarat Pahel (MAGP) was in Pune in coordination with PCGT. The main focus of this van is to take RTI to grassroots. It is well equipped with audio visual aids like television, multimedia projector and public awareness system and volunteers to disseminate the information, said Pankti Jog, MAGP coordinator. It was developed six months back and has covered various tribal areas, market places and housing societies. "In Gujarat, we have been able to reach about 80,000 persons from 16 districts," Jog said. The van left for Mumbai on Sunday evening, where it will be stationed for two days before returning to Gujarat.

After seeing the response to this mobile van, PCGT, Mumbai is planning to develop a similar project. Speaking about it, Jatar said, "PCGT shall chalk out a similar plan, where the vehicle can shuttle between Pune, Mumbai and nearby rural areas giving information about this act. We are trying to get funds for the same, as the cost of developing this van is about Rs 5 lakh."

The PCGT runs a RTI helpline in Pune at its centre in Sancheti hospital. Those interested may call on 64005613 during office hours.

Heading: India’s health insurance for poor set for global stage - Indian Express
Content:
For the third time in two months, the people of eight villages of Itaunja district have been displaced due to the rising levels of Gomti.

"Once again, the area has been flooded. For how long are we supposed to bear this? Until and unless the administration decides to do something about the problem, we will continue to suffer," said Daulatram, gram pradhan of Sultanpur and Bahadurpur village.

The villagers of the eight affected villages — Sultanpur, Bahadurpur, Lhasa, Akhariyakala, Akhariyakhurd, Dughra, Jamkhurwa and Heerapurwa — are living in makeshift tents. The floods have once again destroyed houses and property in these areas.

"This is the third time that the place has been flooded. My house has been submerged. Whatever belongings I could save, I did. But for how long will this go on? We have no home and hardly any belongings left now?" said Sanjhili, a resident of Dughra.

The administration has started rolling out boats for the villagers so that they can salvage whatever they can from their houses. They have also been given a week's relief cheques, calculated at Rs 20 for each adult and Rs 15 for each child per day.

"Instead of providing them with the ration supplies, we have given them relief cheques. For a long-term relief, the irrigation department is deliberating on the issue of solving the problem," said Pawan Kumar Gangwar, Sub Divisional Magistrate.

The water has entered the Gomti Nagar Extension area. It has, however, not yet reached the residential areas. "If the situation is not brought under control, then the area will be flooded and once again we will be forced out of our homes," said Devesh, a resident.

The level of Gomti is rising steadily — from 106.60 metre on Saturday to 107.25 on Sunday.

Heading: Terror maligned Sanjarpur lures politicians - Indian Express
Content:
The innovative scheme of Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojna (RSBY) — cashless and paperless health insurance for BPL families — launched by the Central government across the nation is all set to go global.

After getting accolades in the Wall Street Journal that carried a detailed article on RSBY titled "India's poor get health card to fund medical treatment", the World Bank has now invited the Indian officials to make a presentation of the scheme before other countries at the World Bank headquarters in Washington.

The presentation is scheduled for November during the annual meeting of the World Bank on "most innovative ideas". At the meeting, countries selected for their innovative ideas, share their plans with other nations.
