2. Manali—Rohtang—Gramphoo
3. Kaza—Kaza Gate
4. Kaza—Rong Tong—Losar
5. Patseo—Nakeela
6. Leh—Khaltse
7. Kargil—Panikher
8. Kargil—Leh

Heading: Sachika, Karun bag honours - Indian Express
Content:
Rwandan Dieudonne Disi and Ethiopian Deriba Alemu, the defending champions in the men and women's sections, respectively, have confirmed their entry for the Delhi Half Marathon, the fourth edition of the race to be held here on November 9.

Disi, a world class half-marathoner with a personal best of 59 minutes, had clocked 60.43 minutes in the 2007 edition, breaking the then existing record of 61.36, set by Kenyan Francis Kibiwott in 2006.

Deriba Alemu was not among the pre-event favourites in 2007, but the Ehtiopian put behind a star-studded field with her strong run to come home in 70.30 minutes, also breaking the course record of 70.40 set Kenya's Lineth Chepkirui in 2006.

According to Ian Ladbrooke, the elite athlete co-ordinator, besides the defending champions the Delhi event is expected to attract a strong field of elite athletes thanks to the stature of the event, which has been awarded the Gold Label by the IAAF and the $50,000 increase in prize money.

Race Director Hugh Jones is of the opinion that the expected strong field and the cool weather prevalent in Delhi during the time of the race should see even quicker times being clocked. The half-marathon route will be the same as last year's and the race will start from the Central Secretariat ground.

Heading: 2 held for bid to kidnap CEO of US firm in Noida - Indian Express
Content:
Sachika Ingale won the girls u-15 and u-19 titles of Delhi-NCR Junior Squash Championship 2008 to prove her undisputed dominance.

She defeated Pankhuri Malhotra 3-0 in u-15 category and Vishruthi Sahni 3-0 in u-19 category.

In u-13 category, Pankhuri defeated Adya Advani 3-0 while in Girls u-11, Adya defeated Harshit Kaur 3-0 .

In the boys section, Karm Kumar dominated beating Kush Kumar 3-0 in u-17 and Gunaraj Singh 3-0 in u-19 categories. Kush Kumar defeated Deepak Mishra 3-2 in u-15 while Abhishek Kumar defeated Junaid 3-2 in u-13. In u-11 cap, Robin Mann beat Divyanshu Sharma 3-2 while Pawan Jaini defeated Kunal Oak 3-2 in u-19.

Heading: Traffic cops beat trucker to death, allege kin - Indian Express
Content:
The Noida Police has arrested two persons, including the son of a Ghaziabad sub-inspector, for allegedly attempting the abduction of Ashish Dwivedi, CEO and director of Expedien Solutions, a US software firm operating from Noida.

Two co-conspirators of the alleged kidnap attempt are still on the run, the police said.

According to police, Ghaziabad resident Saurabh Yadav and Ashok Sharma of Hoshiarpur had tried to abduct Dwivedi when he was returning from office on Friday night. They had plans to seek a ransom of Rs 60 lakh, the police said. They said Yadav was the mastermind as he needed the ransom money — he purportedly nursed an ambition of contesting the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections from Madhya Pradesh.

Yadav, in his early twenties, is son of Sub-Inspector Balbir Singh Yadav, posted at Vyapar Kar in Ghaziabad's Mohan Nagar police station.

The four tried to pull in Dwivedi in their Tavera, the police said, but had to abandon the plan and speed off when passersby and a security guard gathered on the spot on hearing Dwivedi's cries for help. "Sharma owns the Tavera; he also runs a transport business," Noida SP (City) Ashok Tripathi said.

From the arrested duo the police have learnt that the four were hatching the abduction plot for the past at least one month, a senior officer said. "They trailed Dwivedi at all hours to know his daily routine and the route from home to office. They tried to put their plan into action on Friday night as Dwivedi was returning late, following a video-conferencing with the company's US counterparts; he was also driving back himself," the officer said.

The officer said a company employee close to Dwivedi probably passed on the information about his schedule to the alleged kidnappers.

Expressing hope that the co-conspirators would be held soon, Gautam Budh Nagar SSP R K Chaturvedi said, "The case against the two has been lodged in Noida Sector 24 police station, and we have got crucial information about the two absconding."

Ashish Dwivedi, 37, said, "I hope the two absconding would soon be arrested but I am unaware of the involvement of anyone close to me in the abduction bid."

Heading: Week after CEO’s lynching, it’s back to work at Graziano - Indian Express
Content:
The circumstances under which a truck driver died in the city over the weekend have become a matter of dispute between his relatives and the police. It is now being alleged by the victim's family that Mohammed Jabbar, from Mewat (Rajasthan), had died after traffic policemen beat him up in Bawana area on Saturday.

Jabbar was declared dead by doctors at Babu Jagjiven Ram Hospital on Sunday, as reported by Newsline in its Monday edition.

Family members alleged that the police "delayed" conducting the postmortem despite assuring them on the weekend that the autopsy would be done today.

A relative, Mohammed Umar, said: "We have visited the police station several times since this morning but we did not get any satisfactory reply. After giving us excuses since morning, policemen told us that postmortem would be conducted on Tuesday."

The family had claimed on Sunday that the police did not hand over the body on the pretext that the autopsy would be conducted on Monday.

According to Umar, following lack of cooperation from the local police they took their case to the Police Headquarters and began demanding that the post-mortem be conducted at the earliest. "Senior officers at the Police Headquarters then assured us that the postmortem would be conducted tomorrow (Tuesday)," Umar said. 

According to sources, Jabbar was stopped by traffic policemen near Karnal Chowk bypass — he was reportedly driving from Swaroop Nagar towards Haiderpur at the time — on Saturday night and penalised for jumping a red light. "The cops asked him to pay up Rs 100," Umar said, "but he was carrying only Rs 50 at the time.

"When he said this, the policemen beat him up — he died as a result of severe beating." He alleged that the traffic policemen on duty asked a rickshaw-puller to admit Jabbar to hospital.

Jabbar's father Deen Mohammed said, "He hadn't eaten anything since he had kept a roza (fast). We don't know where the cops hit him but we believe he died on the spot. The police told us about his death on Sunday."

Mohammed Umar, a student of MA (Arabic) in Delhi University and lives in Sadar Bazar area of the Capital, said he reached the hospital immediately after getting to know about the mishap on Sunday.

Jabbar's family members — father Deen Mohammed, mother Ramzano, wife Shakila and brothers Jamshed and Zubair — were at the hospital. Jabbar was driving a truck owned by a company called "BGR" (Bombay Gujarat Roadways). Umar claimed locals have told the family that the traffic policeman who hit Jabbar is known as "Pehlwan" in the area and is absconding since the incident.

DCP (Outer district) Atul Katiyar said, "We have written for his postmortem. It will be conducted tomorrow. The next step will be taken once the reports are out." About the family's allegations, he said no has come out till now to prove that aspect. Further investigations are on, he added.

Heading: Water woes at MAMC: typhoid hits 15 docs - Indian Express
Content:
A week after the chief executive officer-cum-managing director of Italian multinational Graziano Transmissioni India Lalit K Choudhary's was lynched on September 22, the company resumed work under heavy police cover. Around 200 workers reported for work today.

The company was provided with one Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) company along with local police personnel. Entry for outsiders has been restricted.

The company's personnel manager and spokesperson, L K Gupta, said there is still danger to the lives of employees. "Not many are happy with the circumstances in which they've had to work," he said.

Newly appointed Greater Noida SP (Rural) Surendra Verma said, "Fifteen PAC personnel, four sub-inspectors and 15 constables have been deployed at Graziano. No extra security personnel have been provided to senior executives," said Verma.

A senior executive with the Human Resource department of the company alleged the production manager, Ajay Tyagi, had received an anonymous threat call.

"Tyagi received the threat call around 11.37 am yesterday," the company official said. However, according to Verma, such calls are not new and were discussed in a meeting held on September 25.

"As the company is located in an isolated place, employees feel insecure. The dismissed workers could attack us for resuming work," said an employee. The company said it has engaged private security personnel as well. The company is yet to select its new CEO. "The segment CEO Marcello Lamberto along with senior executives will decide on the issue soon," Gupta said.

Heading: Blast killed teen, mother unaware: How will I get her married? - Indian Express
Content:
Doctors staying on the Maulana Azad Medical College (MAMC) campus have an additional task to perform these days — boil water every morning. Fifteen doctors staying on campus are suffering from typhoid. Residents say the Public Works Department (PWD) has been supplying impure and smelly water.

"There is definitely some problem with the water. It stinks and is discoloured. We have made several representations to the PWD. My mother, father and I all had typhoid. While, the PWD has been taking the problem lightly, we have started boiling water every day," said Dr M S Chopra, Medical Superintendent (MS), Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital. Dr Chopra has been staying on campus for the last seven years.

While there are around 50 apartments for doctors on MAMC campus, including Type 4, 5 and 6, the problem seems to have struck mainly Type 5, which has 16 apartments.

The PWD supplies water every morning and evening that gets collected in cement overhead tanks. These tanks, doctors say, have not been cleaned for years.

"The tanks are very old, many without lids. They were installed when the apartments came up and lack maintenance. We have written to the PWD to change the tanks," added Dr Chopra.

Like Dr Chopra's family, Dr Satish Aggarwal, professor of paediatrics surgery, his wife and son also suffered from fever. This is not the first time that doctors staying on MAMC campus are falling ill due to the callous attitude of the PWD. Last year, the boys hostel also faced the same problem.

"Despite several representations to the PWD, the problem of contaminated water crops up every few days," said a doctor.

Dr Tulika, professor of dentistry, and her children also suffered from typhoid. She said since June this year contaminated water is being supplied to their homes. She and many others have either got an RO system installed or boil water every day. MAMC dean, Dr Arun Aggarwal said he is aware of the complaints and PWD officials have been alerted.

Sukhdev Singh, executive engineer said, "We have just got to know that untreated water got mixed with drinking water, which led to the contamination. Chlorine tablets have been put in water and samples have been sent for testing."

Heading: Poll tricks? Govt subsidy ready as BSES wants more money for power - Indian Express
Content:
Having won a tough battle with death after the September 13 serial blasts, Krishna Nadibatt, 44, is now recuperating in Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital thinking about her two daughters.

"Doctors say my elder daughter Santosh is in a very serious condition," says Nadibatt, in the hospital with almost the whole face bandaged and multiple splinter injuries all over her body. "My younger daughter Pooja is admitted in some other hospital — we have to marry her now, but I don't know how I will manage that in such a condition."

Only, Nadibatt still does not know her younger daughter was declared dead on arrival at the Lady Hardinge Medical College on September 13.

Hospital sources, meanwhile, say improvement in Nadibatt's condition has come as a miracle in itself. Just a week ago, doctors had informed that both she and Santosh were in coma and were not responding to treatment. "Krishna Nadibatt has now miraculously shown tremendous improvement. But she has lost her right eye forever," says Dr S K Sharma, Casualty Medical Officer at RLM Hospital.

Her husband Rama Nadibatt, 48, is also recuperating in the same hospital with a broken arm. Hospital authorities broke the news of Pooja's death to Rama sometime last week, and he is yet to come to terms with the fact. "My dearest daughter is gone; now I only wish Santosh survives," he says, fighting in vain to hold back tears. "What will I do if anything happens to her?

"Doctors say she is still very serious — I just keep praying all the time for her to get well."

Asked about the terrible Saturday evening, when the family had gone to gaffer market in Karol Bagh, Krishna Nadibatt says she remembers nothing much — only that she was eating with Santosh and Krishna. "That's all I remember," she says. "We do not have a house and slept on the pavement in Gaffar Market, where we set up our shop during the day. But now we will never go back to that market. We will go anywhere Rama takes us.

"We will probably make ourselves a jhopdi somewhere in Raghubir Nagar."

Krishna's stomach was also ripped open in the blast and the wound is still green. "It hurts," she winces, and then gets back to that most important question of her life now: "I am in such bad shape; how will I get my Pooja married now?"

Heading: Play for a cause - Indian Express
Content:
Gaurav Gupta on designing costume for an Indian superman and bringing Gaudi on to the ramp

When an Indian superman takes on the evils of the world, what should he ideally wear? He can't be wearing a jumpsuit, or can he? That was what troubled Anaita Shroff Adajaina, the stylist of Goldie Behl's soon-to-be released film Drona, who finally put the question to designer Gaurav Gupta sometime last year.

Intrigued, Gupta began to toy with antique brocades from Varanasi and rich silks, sketched metal embroideries and jewelled headgear. "Since it's the story of an Indian superhero, we had to have an oriental look. We worked with traditional fabrics, using the reverse side of silks for added sheen and then crafted a metallic embroidery on it that would look like a sheath or armour of sorts," says Gupta. Adajania was impressed and Gupta's sketches turned into the costume for Abhishek Bachchan.

"He loved the shirts that we had designed for him and even commissioned me to do some for his personal wardrobe," says Gupta, who had also made the futuristic costume for Priyanka Chopra in Love Story 2050.

However, Bachchan has been replaced by Antoni Gaudi in Gupta's scheme of things now. Busy giving the final touches to his spring-summer collection to be showcased at the Delhi Fashion Week and the Tranoi Fair in Paris, Gupta confesses to being influenced by the maverick artist who led the Spanish Art Nouveau movement. "I was vacationing in Barcelona recently and I was impressed with Gaudi's work. I took a lot of photos and used them as an inspiration for my collection," he says.

So, Gupta has ditched his usual pastel palette and gone in for brighter tones like teal, red and orange. "I have tried playing up the colours and working on panelling techniques. The effect is quite different from my usual work," he says. Wait and watch if it is Gaudi or not.

Heading: Is that too Gaudi? - Indian Express
Content:
These days, the probasi Bengali does not fret if he cannot be in Kolkata for pujo. Neither does he necessarily want to. While the zealous charm of visiting a puja pandal down every block can only be experienced in Bengal, Bengalis in different part of the world celebrate Maa Durga's homecoming in their own distinctive styles. Starting today, a probasi Bengali will tell us what puja means in their corners of the world

Today Arjun Daga, student of Singapore Management University tells us about puja in Singapore

While most of Singapore is absorbed in a daily monotonous routine of getting back home and grabbing a bite at the local delicacy Kopitiam, a small hall at the far end of the posh Tessensohn Road comes alive with the beats of the dhak (minus the plumes). It was Mahashatami, the 3rd day of Durga Puja, and no Bengali would pass up a chance to partake in the festivities marking this day, be it in Kolkata or Singapore.

The only puja in the city is organised by the Bengali Association of Singapore and is among the largest events in their annual calendar. There is no pandal, no bright electric lighting and no thronging crowd, but there is a fervour with which people look forward to this event. The idols are shipped all the way from Bengal and festival is celebrated in all its glory over four days.

Though the pratima is much smaller compared to humongous ones back home, it ignites a spark of devotion along and some nostalgia with its intricate daker saaj and karigari, transporting the probasi Bengali back to his puja days in Kolkata.

The function hall is rented for the occasion and a week of cultural extravaganza is organised which is enhanced by the various singing and talent competitions.

The one thing that most die-hard Kolkatan will not miss is the crowd (since the hall is quite small compared to the size of the Bengali community in Singapore). Serpentine queues lead to the food stalls where a mouth watering fare consisting of luchi, aloor dum, pulao with chicken and fish curries is laid out for the crowd.

However, the area outside the hall is starkly quiet with no intricately decorated pandal or electric lights from Chandernagore to announce the presence of a puja. There is no crowd of pandal hopper jostling to catch a glimpse of the Goddess. Just a load of people piling into their Merc's and Audii's to get back home. I guess this is the way the Bengali out of the country lives, a dual life, that of Durgotsav and the Corporate.

Heading: Cities Lost and Found - Indian Express
Content:
Sonagachi goes Bollywood in Sanjay Gupta's new film

As a volunteer with Durbar Mahila Samannay Committee, a collective of sex workers in Sonagachi, Sudipto Chattopadhyay, would be mesmerised by the day-to-day lives of prostitutes working the maze of back alleys scattered around the city's red light district. "I had decided that I will make a film on their lives someday," says Chattopadhyay, whose yet-to-be-released film Pankh is creating ripples in Bollywood because of its sensitive treatment of gender and identity.

Years later, Chattopadhyay, is back to the familiar lanes of Kolkata's notorious red light district to shoot his dream project— a film on the lives of prostitutes. "The film will be called Sonagachi and will star a mainstream Bollywood actor in the lead. I plan to shoot the film during puja," informs Chattopadhyay.

Sonagachi will be produced by Sanjay Gupta, who has made films like Kaante, Zinda, Plan, Musafir and Dus Kahaniyaan in the past. "We plan to capture the puja spirit in Kolkata. Sonagachi will be produced under the White Feather Arthouse Film banner like Sudipto's last film Pankh," informs Gupta.

While Pankh, which stars Bipasha Basu and Lilette Dubey, is being readied for a November release, Chattopadhyay is busy with the new film. "I have decided to cast plenty of local talents. There are many talented actors here who are just waiting to be discovered," says the filmmaker who completed his graduation from Presidency College. Tollywood veterans like Indrani Haldar and Rupa Ganguly will be cast in supporting roles in the film. "I have always admired the body of work of these actors. They are so versatile," he says.

Will the lead star of Pankh, Bipasha Basu, also star in Sonagachi? "It is too early to comment on that, but we have a big star in mind," is all Chattopadhyay is willing to divulge.

Heading: Little Big Men - Indian Express
Content:
What happens when two people who met with similar fates come together? They relive history. That is what journalists Kuldip Nayar and Asif Noorani did at the launch of their book Tales of Two Cities (Roli) at the India International Centre: they went back to a moment in 1947 when two nations were born in blood, forcing them to leave their land, cross a new, hastily drawn-up border and find homes in unaccustomed earth.

Karachi-based Noorani, associated with the Dawn Group, was in Bombay and all of five when Partition happened. "I vividly recall shouting 'Up, Up the National Flag, Down, Down the Union Jack' as a schoolboy. When someone asked me why I wanted the Union Jack down, in all my innocence, I replied that since Jack fell down and broke his crown, the Union Jack must also come down," laughed Noorani, offering a light moment.

Noorani's family left Bombay for Pakistan only in 1950 when the wounds were not so raw, but Nayar was not so fortunate. He was 24 when he left his hometown of Sialkot, exactly a month after the city became part of Pakistan, and saw first-hand the trauma of migration.

"Circumstances no longer sheltered us in our hometown. Our patience had exhausted in a month, though we came over to Delhi with the idea of returning when things got better. But they only worsened," says Nayar, who started the annual candlelight vigil at Wagah on the night of August 14. The mood is reflected on the pages where personal stories intertwine with history: if Nayar's "From Sialkot to Delhi" is grim, Noorani's "From Bombay to Karachi' carries twists of humour.

Heading: Gomti Nagar Extension flooded yet again - Indian Express
Content:
Sculptor Ved Gupta's little men wear wicked smiles and have sparkling eyes. Look again, and in the contours of their caricatured figures, you will find biting satire. After receiving accolades at the Asia Pacific Contemporary Art Fair in Shanghai, Gupta has brought his fibreglass figurines before Delhi's complacent art public. "Arrested Moment" is also Gupta's first solo show in the Capital.

"The so-called bada aadmi is not a man of enormous size. He is the one with power, though, one that is attained at the cost of the ordinary, lower-class citizen," says Gupta, 32. He would know — his own life has been an extraordinary journey of a labourer becoming one of India's brightest talents. When he came to Delhi 13 years ago, it was not as an artist. He had arrived from Bihar with a shirt on his back and a rupee to his name.

And he worked as a labourer till commercial artist Mathuram Verma hired him. "That was my first art education. I honed my skills while being deployed at various sites in Delhi," smiles Gupta. Then he went to Baroda, discovered fibreglass and delighted in satire. His little men — politicians, corporate fat cats and multinational honchos — are cut to size. But they are lethal and keep bouncing back, as Gupta portrays them in Motion in Paralysis. In Love Chair, the businessman promises sweet nothings to the naked man sitting on the other side.

There are bronze figurines, too, with distorted faces, accentuated by scaffolds, a reminder of his days as a labourer. "My visual language is meant to attack class structures," he says. Take a look, he says. And you'll keep looking.

The show at the Visual Arts Gallery, India Habitat Centre, is on till September 30 and then moves to Gallery Threshold, F-213 A, Lado Sarai.

Heading: UP Police also see IM hand now, arrest one named by Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
The increasing water level of the Gomti river has once again seeped into the Gomti Nagar Extension area.

For the second time in two months, residents of Sector 1 and Sector 4 have started vacating their homes, which are lying submerged in knee-deep water.

"Given the pace with which the water is flowing in, it seems the entire area will be flooded once again. The flow of the water has increased since morning, and it has already become difficult to move out," said Shikhar Chandra, a resident of the area.

On Monday, the water level at Gomti Barrage was recorded at 107.85 metres. The danger level is 109.50 metres.

"Sector 1 was flooded in the morning and the water is now spreading. But the administration is yet to come forward to help us," said Devesh Yadav, gram pradhan of the Makhdoompur village, which is part of the Gomti Nagar Extension.

Lucknow Development Authority Vice- Chairman M K Meshram said: "The stay on the construction of a 5.95-km embankment on the river has been lifted by the Supreme Court. We have written a letter to Irrigation Department, asking them to begin the construction work."

Heading: Raj Babbar will join Congress on October 5 - Indian Express
Content:
Naming the Indian Mujahideen (IM) for the first time in terror acts in the state, the Uttar Pradesh Police on Monday arrested an alleged operative of the outfit, Arif alias Abdul Qadir, who was preparing for his pre-medical entrance test in Lucknow.

Arif had been one of the men named by the Delhi Police, and their UP counterparts today said he had a hand in the blasts that took place in the Lucknow, Varanasi and Faizabad courts on November 23 last year and the July 2008 Ahmedabad attacks.

So far, the UP Police had claimed that the court blasts had been carried out by the Harkat-ul-Jehadi-Islami (HuJI). Today it said they were a joint operation of the HuJI and IM. Arif has apparently revealed that IM men were not supposed to disclose their identities to HuJI operatives, and so he had assumed the name Abdul Qadir.

Arif is a native of Azamgarh's Sanjarpur village, the same as the men now being blamed for the serial blasts across the country.

UP DGP Vikram said Arif, who was arrested from Natha Tiraha in Lucknow and lives in Daliganj, had disclosed names of four other persons involved in the UP court blasts. They include Shadab Malik, Saif, Sajid and Ariz alias Junaid. Saif was arrested after the Delhi Jamia Nagar encounter, while the three others are absconding.

Arif is the fifth person to be arrested in connection with the UP court blasts. On December 22, the UP Police had arrested Khalid and Tariq and described them as members of the HuJI. Two more persons, Sajjad and Akhtar, also allegedly associated with the HuJI, were arrested from Jammu and Kashmir on December 28. "During preliminary investigation, Arif confessed to his involvement in the court blasts of UP and the Ahemadabad blasts," the DGP told the media.

Arif is believed to have planted the bomb on the Lucknow court premises. According to the UP Police, he met Sajjad and Khalid at the Charbagh Railway Station at 8 am on the day of the blast carrying two bags of explosives.

Ariz alias Junaid reportedly purchased the bicycles used in the operation. They all met up in the Tile Wali Masjid area, and then went to Nimbu Park. Finally they hired a rickshaw for Lucknow court. Ariz reportedly went to LaTouche Road to buy two bicycles, the bombs were kept on them, these were parked on the court premises and they dispersed.

The police claimed Shadab Malik and his associates placed bombs on the Faizabad court premises while the bombs at the Varanasi court were kept by Saif, Sajid and others.

Heading: Varanasi blast: After 3 years, victim yet to recover, govt turns a deaf ear - Indian Express
Content:
Actor and rebel Samajwadi Party parliamentarian from Agra Raj Babbar will formally join the Congress on October 5.

In a rally planned in Agra that day, he has invited AICC general secretary Digvijay Singh and state Congress president Rita Bahuguna Joshi.

After turning against the Samajwadi Party, Babbar had worked with the Jan Morcha, led by former Prime Minister V P Singh.

He had snapped his ties with Jan Morcha after the state Assembly elections in May 2007. In the trust vote on July 22, he had voted in favour of the UPA government.

Upendra Singh, spokesman of the Agra MP, confirmed that senior Congress leaders are expected to participate in the rally, which will be held in Targhar Maidan. Over 50,000 supporters of the MP are expected to participate. "Thousands of Jan Morcha activists will also join the Congress on the occasion," he said.

Raj Babbar is likely to contest the next Lok Sabha election from the adjoining Fatehpur Sikri constituency. In the recent delimitation exercise, Agra has been declared a reserved seat for Scheduled Castes and a new constituency of Fatehpur Sikri has been carved out.

Congress sources said it is certain that the Fatehpur Sikri seat would be given to Congress as part of the electoral tie-up with the Samajwadi Party. But SP general secretary Amar Singh has expressed his reservation against leaving the seat for Raj Babbar.

Samajwadi Party spokesman Rajendra Chowdhary said the negotiations with Congress are still on and so far no decision had been taken on Fatehpur Sikiri.

After last week's unscheduled meeting of Sonia Gandhi and Mulayam Singh Yadav at the Lucknow airport, leaders of both parties are confident that the seat sharing issue will soon be sorted out.

Babbar had raised the banner of revolt against Amar Singh in 2006 when the SP was in power in the state. Describing Amar Singh as a political broker, he had spearheaded a campaign against the all-powerful party general secretary.

Heading: Govt rolls back VAT on computers - Indian Express
Content:
Three years on, Raj Kumar Shahani is yet to recover from the blast that shook the temple town. Bed-ridden, paralysed below waist by two nails that penetrated into his spine from the blast that occurred on a fateful Wednesday — February 23, 2005 — at Varanasi's Dasashwamedh Ghat.

The shrapnels were taken out by the doctors the very next day. But the damage inflicted on his spinal chord was permanent. The government although gave him a compensation of Rs 25,000, which was spent in no time.

After undergoing medical treatment from six different hospitals in Varanasi, 25-year-old Shahani has reconciled to spending the rest of his life in bed, swallowing pills to fight the pain. His four brothers have spend their meagre earnings hoping that one day he would walk, but to no avail.     

Dr Ashish Dutta of Shri Ram Laxman Narain Marwari Hindu Hospital, who treated Shahani, said: "His MRI report showed that his spinal cord was badly damaged and there was no chance of his recovery. The government should arrange for his rehabilitation."

Asked as to how he remembers Shahani, Dr Dutta said, "I discussed his case with other doctors after seeing his MRI report."

Shahani belongs to a family of boatmen who earn their living by taking tourists on river cruises. The black Wednesday is etched in his memory as though it occurred yesterday. "My mother asked me to wait at the house as some guests were coming. I did not listen to her and went to the ghat. My friends had told me that several tourists had arrived. I thought I will earn some money," said Shahani.

As he reached the ghat, a shopowner, Manoj called him. "We were talking when this deafening sound occurred. After that I fell unconscious. When I opened my eyes, I found myself in the hospital," said Shahani. Twenty days later, he was discharged.

Seven people, including Manoj, died and 13 people were injured in the blast. Initially, the police dismissed it as a gas cylinder blast. Later, forensic evidence indicated that the blast was caused by ammonium nitrate. Till date, the case remains unsolved.

The tragedy for Shahani did not end here. "There was a marriage proposal at that time. But after I got in this condition, the girl's family backed out," said Shahani. Shahani's younger brother Nand Lal said he had met the district officials several times and told them about the condition of his brother.

As for the authorities, Shahani's case came as a surprise. Varanasi District Magistrate A K Upadhyay said: "No one informed me about this victim. I will definitely pass his request to the state government," he said.

Heading: Now, quality check for LDA to be done by engineering institutes - Indian Express
Content:
Traders not pacified as tax rates on more than 40 items remain unchanged

Following protests from traders, the state government decided to rollback the hike in VAT on commodities like computers, peripherals and cellphones on Monday. The entry tax of two per cent on computers and peripherals remains unchanged.

Among edible items, the government has decided to exempt dates from VAT, perhaps in view of the month of Ramzan, as it is a part of the meal of devout Muslims. 

"The government, following the representation from several organisation of trade and industry, reconsidered the tax rates on different goods and decided against the hike in VAT on computers and cellphones," said Govindan Nair, Principal Secretary for Tax and Registration.

The rollback has, however, failed to pacify the traders because tax rates on more than 40 items remain unchanged. Trader's organisations have announced to launch a protest, demanding a complete rollback.

With the rollback, the tax rate on computers, peripherals, LCD monitors and cellphones was restored to the original four per cent. The tax rate on other items remains unchanged. The new rates will be effective from October 1.

In a bid to make up for the loss of revenue due to the rollback, the government decided to hike VAT on molasses from 4 to 12.5 per cent.

Following an objection raised by the Excise Department, the revised rate is going to be effective from April 1, 2009.

The department argued that a revision of tax rate on molasses in the middle of the year will lead to litigation from the distilleries.

On September 19, the Cabinet had decided to hike the VAT on computers along with 44 other items from four per cent to 12.5 percent and entry tax was also imposed on seven categories of goods.

Among all the northern states, UP had imposed the highest rate of tax on these items. The necessary notification was, however, had not been issued.

Heading: Hacking threat forces institutes to postpone Wi-Fi plans - Indian Express
Content:
Failing to monitor the quality of construction and facing repeated complaints of use of substandard material, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) has now decided to involve Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur (IIT-K) and Harcourt Butler Technological Institute, Kanpur (HBTI).

The two reputed engineering institutes have been roped in to test the quality of construction before the LDA makes the payments to the contractors.

"The step had become necessary because of repeated reports of the poor quality construction in various schemes. It will also motivate the contractors to ensure the quality of the work," said Mukesh Kumar Meshram, LDA Vice-Chairman.

"In all the upcoming schemes, an expert panel from IIT-K or HBTI will regularly visit the sites to collect the samples of material being used in the construction and test these in their laboratories," said LDA Secretary Mani Prasad Mishra.  

A fee will be paid to these institutes for this work. "I have spoken to the respective authorities of these institutes and they will hopefully start working with us very soon," Mishra said.

The LDA vice-chairman has already issued an order stating, "specification of development works, rate analysis and estimates given by the contractors and engineers will be checked by the civil engineering department of these institutes and payment will be made only when the panel verifies all the details."

The order also states that if required, help of other engineering institutions could also be taken for quality testing.

It is learnt that Chief Minister Mayawati had noticed some irregularities in constructions inside Ramabai Rally Maidan and Smriti Upvan at Bangla Bazaar.

Earlier, in June 2006, an executive engineer was suspended and a few construction firms were blacklisted when Housing Minister Naseemuddin Siddiqui inspected the Gomti Nagar Extension and found poor quality constructions.

Last week, Meshram had instituted an inquiry in the poor quality of houses in Vastu and Vinamra Khand, Gomti Nagar. Joint Secretary Atal Kumar Rai confirmed that most of the houses were totally dilapidated.

Heading: Health programme in school to tackle malnutrition - Indian Express
Content:
The reports of hacking into Wi-Fi networks of Mumbai to send terror mails in the recent serial blasts cases have exposed the vulnerability of the network.

The IT institutions across the state are now hastening to shelve their plans to go in for Wi-Fi connections. Those who already have a network have decided to restrict its services in certain areas.

A Wi-Fi system works without wire and all communications in a given area are connected with a centralised hub. The system enables anyone who enters the campus to link their computer with the Wi-Fi system. Which, however, lays the system open to hackers who can find their way into the institute's database and use its server for any purpose.

Premier institutes like Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT-A), Motilal Nehru National Institute of Technology (MNNIT), IIT-Kanpur, Banaras Hindu University, Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences, Lucknow and IIT-Roorkee have been using Wi-Fi network in their campuses.

The IIIT-A has now decided to shelf its project to connect the entire campus with Wi-Fi. The institute's director Dr M D Tiwari said: "Following the threat of hacking, we have decided to rely on USB wireless system. It will make it impossible for any miscreant to hack our network because the USB system is being allotted to individuals who have been made accountable for their gadgets." He further added that the project could be re-launched once a hacking-proof technology is developed.

MNNIT director Prof A B Samaddar said: "Earlier, we had an ambitious plan to connect our entire campus with a Wi-Fi network but we are now forced us to reconsider our plans."

The MNNIT has already made half of its campus including the director's office, seminar hall, executive development centre and computer centre Wi-Fi enabled.

"We will not extend the facility to the remaining areas of our campus as it will lead to unmanageable flow of networking links," said a professor.

"We have also asked experts to develop a spherical air-link jammer for preventing any hacking. So far the country does not have any system to check air-links hacking," he added.

Heading: Man shoots at sister - Indian Express
Content:
To address the problem of malnutrition among the children, the state government is all set to launch a school health programme on September 30, targeting around 50 lakh children in 32,000 government schools across the state. 

The programme — Ashirvad School Health Programme — is a part of the Centre's National Rural Health Scheme and will also be funded by it. 

It will be officially launched by Health Minister Anant Kumar Mishra at Juggaur Primary School.

The programme will be operational in all districts from October 1. Gradually, it will be extended to cover around 1 lakh primary schools.

"The programme is being launched with high hopes. It will be our direct attack on malnutrition among the children of the state," said Rajiv Kapoor, Director of National Rural Health Mission.

"It will also act as an important tool in sensitising parents, as the students would be asked to get their health cards signed by the parents," he added.

Along with eradication of malnutrition, the programme intends to increase community involvement and make people aware of the importance of personal hygiene. 

Under it, 40 government primary schools will be selected in each block. 

A team of consultants formed at the block level comprising specialists as well as local accredited social health workers will implement the programme.

The children will be given de-worming tablets. Teachers will be given stocks of iron and folic acid tablets to be given to the students at regular interval.

Every six months, the students will get a free health check-up monitoring their height, weight and vision.

"At a later stage, we plan to provide free spectacles to children who are found to have a weak eyesight," said Kapoor.

All information about a child's health parameters will be mentioned in his or her health card.

Why it is necessary
According to the National Family Health Survey — III:

* 46 per cent children are too short for their age
* 47 per cent are underweight 
* 85 per cent children between the age of six months and one-and-a-half years are anaemic

Heading: Nanavati report makes room for BJP-Cong spat in House - Indian Express
Content:
A businessman, itendera Keswani, shot at his sister on Monday in Sector H of Aliganj police circle, for her alleged involvement in a relationship.

According to Ashok Prashad, ASP Transgomti, "At 8.30 pm, Keswani shot at his sister Kanchan Karamchandani after a heated argument between them over Kanchan's relationship with one Krishan Pal Singh."

The bullet hit her leg and she was admitted to a hospital. Police said her condition is now stable.

According to the police, Kanchan got married to Jagdish Karamchandani in 1992 and settled in Ghana, Africa. The ASP, however, said, "She came back in 1996 from Africa and got involved in a relationship with Singh."

Police said Kanchan was involved with Singh even before her marriage, and had started living with him after she came back from Africa.

Heading: Of cursed cradle and fanged death - Indian Express
Content:
Leader of Opposition calls it an eyewash; Home Minister accuses Congress of protecting POTA accused

The ruling BJP and the Opposition Congress traded charges and counter-charges in the Assembly on Monday during an hour-long debate on the first part of the controversial Nanavati Commission report on the Godhra train burning incident.

During the discussion, Leader of Opposition in the Assembly Shaktisinh Gohil dubbed the report as a "mere eyewash". He challenged the ruling BJP to approach the Supreme Court for fresh investigations into the burning of the S-6 coach of the Sabarmati Express at Godhra on February 27, 2002.

In his reply, Minister of State for Home Amit Shah threw a gauntlet at the Congress to make the Godhra carnage its poll plank in the coming Lok Sabha elections. Shah said: "The people of Gujarat will once again ensure a total rout of the Congress at the elections." The minister alleged that the Opposition was attempting to "protect the POTA detainees of the Godhra train burning incident" by raising a hue and cry over the report.

Initiating the debate in the House, Gohil referred the name of Justice J S Verma, the former Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission. He said Justice Verma had observed that investigations into the Godhra and post-Godhra riots were not being conducted properly. "It was the BJP-led NDA regime that had appointed Justice Verma as the NHRC chairman who had made these observations," Gohil told the House.

Debunking the "pre-planned conspiracy" theory, Gohil said the Sabarmati Express was late by five hours that fateful day, and that even the Forensic Sciences Laboratory (FSL) had pointed out that petrol had not been poured into the coach from the outside. This suggests that the "conspiracy" theory has been cooked up, he said.

The Congress leader further said that while the Chief Minister and other BJP leaders had sought to justify the post-Godhra riots by citing the "action-reaction" theory, the Nanavati Commission has in its report clearly de-linked the Godhra train incident from the ensuing riots. Gohil also criticised the Inquiry Commission for ignoring a spate of applications demanding that Chief Minister Narendra Modi, his ministers and senior officials be called upon to depose before the Commission.

Meanwhile, Shah intervened that there was no question to approach the apex court for a re-investigation into the Godhra carnage. It was the Supreme Court only that had appointed Justice (retired) Nanavati to the Inquiry Commission, he said.

This prompted Gohil to ask the minister, through a point of order, if the state government had suggested the name of Nanavati to appoint him to the Commission.

The Opposition MLAs resorted to full-throated slogans like "jhooth bolvanu bandh karo (stop telling lies)," and "give justice to the Opposition party," even as the BJP members started shouting counter-slogans, plunging the House in disorder. The assertive intervention by Speaker Ashok Bhatt cooled the frayed tempers on both sides after a few minutes of ruckus in the House.

Shah said the Nanavati Commission had brought out the truth (about the Godhra incident) after over six years of judicial exercise, and that there was nothing wrong in the report.

Earlier participating in the debate, Pradeepsinh Jadeja of the BJP came down heavily on the Tehelka sting operation on the Godhra and post-Godhra incidents. "This news channel is known for blackmailing others. If the channel has had evidences, why did it not produce the same before the Nanavati Commission," the BJP member said. Countering this, Arjun Modhwadia of the Congress argued that since the sting operation by Tehelka was shown on several TV channels across the country, it was the responsibility of the Commission to call for the tapes and examine them.

Heading: Exodus of IAS officers on, one more puts in papers - Indian Express
Content:
With one of the country's worst female to male ratio, Gujarat has made female feoticide into a thriving industry — on the fringes of law.

Seventeen new born infants, averaging one every fortnight, have been recovered from rubbish heaps in the city in just the last eight months. A few rescued before the street dogs found them first, some partly eaten but still alive, a few packed live in rubbish cans and thrown into trash heaps for municipal workers to cart away.

Sixteen out of the 17 abandoned infants recovered so far this year are girls — there is no count of others likely to have been completely devoured by the dogs or quietly buried under piling garbage. A rare exception was two days ago, when Vijay Sonavne of Pandesara, a textile mill worker, found an infant wrapped in a white sheet in a roadside garbage container and called the police. The baby was rushed to the New Civil Hospital, but it did not survive. It was a boy.

In this case too, the police did the expectable: They "registered a case against an unknown woman as the accused" at the local police station. These cases pile up in many parts of the city, Pandesara, Rander, Varachha and Kapdoara. Not one of these have been detected. The cops claim to be helpless : "People abandon the infants in the wee hours, so they are never spotted. Street dogs prey on them, so most are found dead. Our investigations usually cover the government and private hospitals in our limits, to check on new born babies and their parents,"said Varachha Inspector V B Patel.

The few who survive the dogs, hunger and the hot sun or cold usually reach the New Civil Hospital in the city. But, at the hospital's Neonatology department, Dr Sandeep Chug says survivors aren't many.

"We do everything to treat the surviving recovered babies. We keep them in the nursery for some days till they get fully cured and then hand them over to police. But not many of those first found by the dogs survive. Many die during treatment, either from their severe injuries or infection."

District Social Welfare officer A H Rabari claims that the lucky few who live on are looked after well. "We pay a great deal of attention to these baby girls from the day the police brings them to the hospital. They are looked after and supported for years, even until they are married away. Some are handed over early on, under our supervision, to those wanting to adopt them. We have, in fact, married away many girls of the Nari Gruh. No one would imagine that these girls, now housewives, were all found from garbage heaps or trash containers."

At the Nari Sanrakshan Gruh, Superintendent P G Trivedi says the trained staff in the attached Shishu Grih take over these infants once they are out of the hospital. "Many couples apply to us wanting to adopt these infants, but some are never adopted. We look after them, give them an education and marry them off — we even monitor their married lives for years," according to him.

But the dogs in the garbage bins still don't need to wait long.

Heading: Junior Bachchan promises an unforgettable tryst with people of Ahmedabad - Indian Express
Content:
G P Joshi is the 11th officer to quit ever since Narendra Modi first became the Chief Minister

One more IAS officer, G P Joshi, the Principal Secretary (Expenditure) in the state Finance Department, has put in his papers. Since 2001, when Narendra Modi took over as the chief minister, as many as 10 IAS officers had resigned from the services. Apparently, two of them were later persuaded by Modi to withdraw their resignations.

Sources in the Chief Minister's Office told Newsline that Joshi, a 1978 batch IAS officer, sent a mandatory three-month notice to the General Administration Department (GAD) with a request to relieve him from the civil services after the expiry of the notice period.

When approached this evening, Joshi refused to comment. He said, "I have to go for an urgent meeting."

Sources, however, confirmed that the senior IAS officer had been contemplating for long to quit the civil services. They said Joshi is likely to join a corporate house, as had been done by some of his colleagues in the recent past. "He is close to at least a couple of big industrial houses, and his joining one of them cannot be ruled out," they said.

A senior IAS officer Sanjay Gupta, who is being credited for turning the state-run Gujarat State Petroleum Corporation (GSPC) into a blue chip company, was the first to put in his papers and join the Adani Group during Modi's first stint as chief minister in 2001. This was followed by the resignation of Roads and Building Secretary H P Jamdar.

In the last five years or so, several other IAS officers have put in their papers. They include Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Ltd (SSNNL) Managing Director S K Mahapatra; Gujarat State Fertilisers and Chemicals (GSFC) Managing Director A K Luke; Principal Secretary (Energy) Vijay Ranchan; Gujarat Infrastructure Development Board (GIDB) CEO Jayant Parimal and Principal Secretary (Social Justice and Empowerment) J S Rana.

Parimal, a 1989 batch IAS officer, has already joined Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries at its main corporate office in Mumbai.

Two other IAS officers, who had resigned last year, but were later persuaded by Modi to withdraw their resignations, are R K Tripathy and Vipul Mitra. While Tripathy, a 1977 batch IAS officer, is at present the Joint MD of SSNNL, Mitra, a 1986 batch officer is the Development Commissioner.

A senior IAS officer who resigned from the civil services recently, said: "It is not possible for a sensible and hardworking IAS officer to work in the hostile environment created by Modi's autocratic style of functioning. IAS officers are being treated as clerks under the present dispensation."

The bureaucrat said that one should not be surprised if several more IAS officers put in their papers in the days to come, particularly after the implementation of the Sixth Pay Commission recommendations. "IAS officers will start receiving a hefty pension after the Commission's recommendations are accepted by the government. This may prompt even junior IAS officers, who have already put in 20 years of their services in the government, to seek voluntary retirement, and find some good assignment in corporate houses to earn extra money," said a former IAS officer.

Heading: Festive fervour and crass commercialisation - Indian Express
Content:
He came here asking Amdavadis to fall in love with Drona and went with a promise that he'll talk to his father about bringing 'The Unforgettable Tour' to Ahmedabad. Bollywood actor Abhishek Bachchan landed here on Monday afternoon and sent a cheer among the people. But it was his humility that stole hearts. "When you live with Amitabh and Jaya Bachchan, you learn how to remain down-to-earth," he told one of his fans who asked as to how he maintained such a down-to-earth image.

Humble he may be, but he is assertive enough while expressing his opinion on the controversy sparked off by Jaya Bachchan's alleged 'anti-Marathi' statement. He says, "I'm a law-abiding citizen and I don't believe that anyone can stifle you or your freedom in any way." So, does he find it justified that Bachchan senior had to apologise on her behalf? "It was an off-the-cuff remark and never intended the way it was taken. But, if anybody's feeling was hurt, there is nothing wrong in saying sorry. Maafi maangne se koi chhota nahi ho jata," came the reply.

Going back to his October 2 release, Drona, Abhishek said it's a fantasy-adventure story about an ordinary boy with extraordinary power. "Drona's mission is to protect a secret. The idea of the film, directed by childhood friend Goldie Behl, goes back to our childhood days when we broke all the fake swords while playing on the sets of the Big B movie Pukar. We were thrown out of the sets and that very day Goldie and I decided that one day we will make a film with lots of sword-fighting scenes and it'll be all ours," said Abhishek.

The actor has surely come of age, but quiz him if he still feels overshadowed by Amitabh Bachchan while working with him, and he says: "Not just me, there is not one actor who wouldn't feel overshadowed by Amitabh Bachchan. He was, he is and he will always be there."

Abhishek's interaction with his fans was equally interesting. While he readily hugged a kid on the latter's insistence, he also promised to start blogging if and only if his fans wanted so. The suave actor, who has already dabbled in singing (Bluffmaster), surprised his fans when he said that as a singer, he rated himself (–) 20. When asked what he rated his father, he said, "well… +20."

On serious issues like terrorism, Abhishek said that in today's world, there is not one person who can be looked upon as a saviour. "We need to look within ourselves just as Drona does," he said. Before bidding goodbye to his fans who had gathered at Big Baazar and Cinemax on the SG Highway, he thanked the Amdavadis time and again for their love and said adieu with the punchline: "Spread love and peace."

Heading: Civic feat: Chorwad municipality holds a people’s congress to discuss woes - Indian Express
Content:
Paid entry into garbas banned in Mehsana, Surendranagar districts

The nine day Navratri festivities, wherein Bhakti-ras melds with the trademark Gujarati folksy dandiya raas – invoking the leela of Gopis, begins from September 30, culminating on Dusshera. Newsline joins in the festive fervour in these nine days, catching the nuances, the trends and the metamorphosis of the festival that has become the catchphrase for the Gujarati identity. On the first day, Newsline reports the notification issued by two district collectors of Surendranagar and Mehsana banning paid entry in garba venues — the correction mechanism that comes in response to the rapid commercialisation of the traditional festivities. Parimal Dabhi reports…

Navratri will be a shade different this year in the two districts of Mehsana and Surendranagar. In an unprecedented move to check the rapid commercialisation of the festivities associated with Navratri, the district collectors of Surendranagar and Mehsana have banned the paid entry into garba venues in the areas under their jurisdiction.

With corporate houses, politicians and real estate builders in the fray in organising garba festivities across the state, expensive entry tickets and passes have become the norm in cities like Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Rajkot, with smaller towns following suit.

Surendranagar District Collector J D Bhad and his Mehsana counterpart Ajay Bhadoo have issued a notification banning the ticket shows of garbas. Violators will be prosecuted under the provisions of the Indian Penal Code, it has been learnt. Bhad said: "This is a religious festival, but some people are trying to get financial gain out of it by commercialising it, which is a deviation from the religious fervour. So, I have taken this step to check the ticket entries at the garba venues in Surendranagar district."

In Ahmedabad, Maninagar, SG Highway and the 132 Ring Road are the hot spots where the commercial garbas are organised.

Heading: Rs 41 cr lost in police dept’s lethargy - Indian Express
Content:
Chorwad, just about 70 kilometre from Junagadh, created history of sorts with its civic body convening a general body meeting in presence of hundreds of people.

The meeting was also attended by 21 elected municipal members who passed resolutions regarding the town's development.

The town, which has a population of around 30,000 people, is riddled with innumerable civic problems.

The public meeting began on a positive note with the common people also attending it. They put forward their questions, made suggestions and welcomed the civic chief's move to hold the meeting in public.

"The people of Chorwad used to repeatedly accuse the civic body of being corrupt. The allegations made me upset. I therefore, decided to convene the meeting so that everyone could attend it," said Chorwad municipality president Hirabhai Chudasama. "We have taken serious note of people's suggestions. Action will be taken to solve the problems forwarded during the meeting," he said.

It was also unanimously decided that stern action will be taken against those involved in encroachment cases.

Nearly 700 people took part in the meeting. Resolutions were passed regarding resurfacing of roads, making adequate water supply arrangements, improving education facilities, beautification and so on.

Incidentally, Chudasama (54) has been leading the civic body since his college days.

"To lead the civic body for such a long period is perhaps, a world record. Once official of the world record's book had approached me in this regard," he said.

Heading: Flood of contradictions: Tale of two inquiry reports - Indian Express
Content:
CAG report states the police department did not collect the amount due to them before deploying police personnel and that's why lost money in crores

The state police department has incurred a loss of Rs 41.94 crore for failing to recover dues for providing security to various government departments, local and private bodies, commercial institutions and the railways, in and outside the state.

This was pointed out in a report of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India for the year March 31, 2007, which was tabled in the State Assembly on Monday.

According to the report, the police department did not follow rules with regard to the recovery of dues while deploying forces in government and private departments.

According to the report, the Gujarat Police Manual 1975, amended in 1999, stipulates that police charges should be collected in advance at double the rate of pay and allowance from banks, public sector undertakings and private institutions.

The Bombay Police Act, 1951, adapted by the state government, also lays down that the cost of additional police force deployed at any place of amusement or entertainment must be borne by the concerned party or organisation.

According to the state police department rules, other states borrowing police personnel from Gujarat should deposit Rs 50 lakh per quarter, which must be adjusted against the final bill.

But according to CAG report, the records available with the offices of the Director General of Police, four commissionerates of Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Surat and Rajkot, and in

the offices of superintendents

of police of Ahmedabad, Bharuch, Gandhinagar, Rajkot and Western Railway (Vadodara) indicate that police personnel were deployed for various periods between April 2001 and March 2006 even though the concerned departments did not make advance payments.

The CAG report states that the biggest amount — of Rs 17.65 crore — is to be recovered from the Western Railway. Another amount of Rs 9.94 crore is to be recovered from a state government for deploying forces there. Rs 7.54 crore from commercial institutions, Rs 1.26 crore from private institutions and another sum of Rs 3 crore from the government departments is also yet to be

recovered.

The report states that while dues from the Western Railway police could not be recovered due to non-settlement of disputes between the state police department and the railway police between 2001 and 2003, it blames police for failing to recover dues in other cases.

According to the report, the matter was brought to the notice of the police department as well as the state government between July 2006 and April 2007, but there was no reply from them till the final compilation of the report.

The CAG report also states that the police department also lost a total of Rs 23.57 crore by short recovery of police charges from 100 police units between April 2001 and March 2006. Of this, Rs 18.96 crore was short recovered for providing 99 police units to commercial institutions and Rs 4.61 crore to the Western Railway police.

According to the report, the police charge was recovered at single rate, instead of double the rate in case of commercial institutions. Pension charges were also not included in police charges, claimed from the Western Railway police.

Heading: ..but people’s panel unleashes damnation, says they’re guilty of criminal negligence - Indian Express
Content:
Surat flood, 2006: Official commission gives clean chit to dam authorities…

The Commission of Inquiry to probe the August 2006 deluge in Surat following excessive release of water from the Ukai dam — has given a clean chit to the dam authorities — asserting that "appropriate steps" had been taken by the people concerned for the protection and safety of the dam during the 2006 monsoon.

Back then, the state government had faced serious flak for the alleged mismanagement of the Ukai reservoir and its idea of conserving water without taking into account heavy floods in the area. A large number of people had died in the floods and there had been widespread destruction with damage to both houses and industries. While suggesting measures to prevent floods in Surat and the nearby industrial areas like Hajira, the report instead, blames unplanned development in the flood plain area and largescale encroachment along the river.

It had said that the reduced water-carrying capacity — with water levels going higher and discharges getting lower — was the reason for the flood-like situation almost every year. The report of the Commission headed by Justice Sugnya Bhatt underlines an urgent need to restrict further development in Surat along the riverbanks, flood plains and Hajira area. Stating that the smooth water flow in Tapi riverbed should not be obstructed to check floods in Surat city and Hajira, no construction in the water escape route of Tapi should be allowed under any circumstances. "If construction in the escape route of the river is not checked, the future of the city will be in dark as far as floods are concerned," the report points out, and suggests proper coordination between Surat Municipal Corproation, Surat Urban Development Authority, district collectorate and Hajira Urban Development Authority to ensure that drainage and storm water routes are not blocked.

The reports also asks the SMC to be very firm with those not conforming to building by-laws, apart from ensuring that the city's sewage line does not directly lead to Tapi river, which makes the riverbed shallow with a reduced capacity.

It also suggests that the sewage pipeline be diverted to the sea. The report also recommends that the person in charge of the dam during monsoon should have a technical background with experience in managing dams during crisis. The report recommends that no single individual should be entrusted with taking decisions for managing the crisis and instead, it should be given to a committee of experts available at the dam site. The report has advised that the manual system of data collection with regard to rainfall and discharge measurement be replaced with Real Time Data Acquisition System (RTDAS) for "efficient, accurate and timely forecasting of floods". Stressing the need for setting up a few rain gauge stations in the catchment area in the 107-km long route between Sarankheda and Ukai, the report wants the existing wireless communication system to be replaced with satellite telephone during monsoon for better communication, which would give more time for alerting people during the release of water from the dam.

Heading: Groundswell of protest: Groundnut yards to go for an indefinite strike from Oct 1 - Indian Express
Content: The official report on the August 2006 Surat floods may have absolved the State Government of negligence and laxity, but the 'Report of the People's Committee on Gujarat Floods of August 2006', released last July, had, however, come to a different conclusion. The nine-member committee set up by Narmada Abhiyan and Gujarat Sarvodaya Mandal under the chairmanship of former acting chief justice of Gujarat High Court Justice R A Mehta, which was formed to investigate the cause of the floods, had pointed out that those who took and implemented the decision of holding the water back "are guilty of criminal negligence and liable to be prosecuted for culpable homicide not amounting to murder". It had argued that the Surat floods were a manmade disaster. The committee, which came up with its report in July 2007, had severely indicted the state government for the sudden release of a huge amount of water from the Ukai dam that led to over 80 per cent of Surat going under water. More than two million people had become incommunicado — trapped in their houses without food and drinking water for four days and four nights. It had held the Narmada Water Resources and Water Supply Department responsible for the mismanagement in the operation of the Ukai Dam.The report notes: "The water level in the reservoir had crossed the prescribed level of 333.60 ft on the morning of August 3 ...and [the] water level in the reservoir was raised up to 335.5 ft by the end of August 5, which was 1.5 ft higher than the prescribed rule level of 334 ft for the day. Thereafter too, the water level in the reservoir was continuously raised and brought up to 337 ft by the end of August 6 and then up to 339.5 ft by 8 am on the morning of August 7… By that time, the reservoir was already 90 per cent full with very little empty space (flood cushion) left for storing additional water. And the inflow was still increasing…The outflow was then sharply increased in a short span of a few hours from 5 lakh (500,000) cusecs at 9 am to…8 lakh (800,000) cusecs by 3 pm in the afternoon (of August 7, 2006). The outflow was then increased further to about 9 lakh (900,000) cusecs at 11 am on August 8 and kept at that level up to 8 am on August 9." Digant Oza, a member of the committee said it is frustrating that the official report has not answered the points put forth by the committee. "Experts in our committee reported whatever they felt and saw. The official report does not give the correct picture, which the people of Surat have a right to know," he said. The committee, in its report, had said that the state government had worked against the forecast of the Central Water Commission. The district collector and the municipal commissioner had sounded the alarm bells, but were ignored, it noted.

Heading: Crossover kings: 60 lions venture out of Gir, may pick conflict with humans - Indian Express
Content:
Centre's decision to ban export of edible oil evokes sharp reaction in Saurashtra, Kutch

More than 53 major marketing yards of Saurashtra and Kutch would go in for an indefinite closure from October 1. The agitation is in protest against the Centre's policy to ban the export of edible oil, which came into effect in March 2008.

Hardevsinh Jadeja, chairman of the Rajkot Marketing Yard, said: "Saurashtra is a major producer of groundnut and 30 per cent of country's total groundnut production is from Saurashtra only. Due to this ban, the prevailing price of groundnut has plummeted to Rs 400 for every 20 kg, whereas it should be between Rs 500 and 600."

A meeting of the elected body members of the major yards of Saurashtra and Kutch have now met under the banner of Marketing Yard Federations at Rajkot to discuss the further programmes to intensify their agitation.

Jadeja said: "All the activities including buying, selling and auction will be stopped from October 1 at all the 53 yards of the region. Only the vegetable and fruit section of the yard will operate during the strikes. We have also decided to meet ministers Kamal Nath, Sharad Pawar and Pranab Mukherjee in New Delhi on October 3 or 4 with our representation, which will comprise chairmen of all the marketing yards and Members of Parliament from Saurashtra and Kutch."

He added: "The fresh crop of groundnut has just start coming in at the yards. At present, 30,000 bags of groundnut reach the yards. The peak season will start around Diwali and around one lakh bags will reach here per day."

Jentibhai Dhol, chairman of the Gondal Marketing Yard, said: "At present, only small farmers are coming to sell their crops at the yard because they cannot hold ready crops for long. They are facing a cash crunch. Due to the ban on exports, the prevailing price of Rs 400 (per 20 kg) is also less than the support price of Rs 480, declared by the state government. If the ban is not withdrawn, the price will reach something between Rs 500 and 600 per 20 kg, which will save the farmers.

He added, if the ban is removed after two to three months, only oil millers and big farmers will reap the benefit, which will be an injustice to the small farmers.

"We have decided to form a permanent committee to fight against injustice to the farming community. Our fight is not against any particular political party, but we will fight against whosoever is responsible for this."

Dineshbhai Patel, another member of the Marketing Yard Federation, said: "We will conduct awareness programmes during the strikes and advise the farmers not to sell their crops to the oil millers directly. This agitation is for their benefit only. We will also take this agitation to every taluka and take out rallies at every centre and submit a memorandum to their respective authorities."

Hardevsinh Jadeja further said that the elected bodies of oil millers have not come forward to support them. "Informally, some oil millers have given their support, but we know they will not come forward to support us. They are busy stocking up groundnut, as it is available at a low price now. After a few months, when the ban is withdrawn, they will sell the export oil at a high price and make money," he said.

Jadeja, however, added that the Bharatiya Kisan Sangh has declared their support in the agitation.

Heading: So near, yet so far: Dalits get deity’s blessing, but not prasad - Indian Express
Content:
WII report shows that Asiatic lions are looking for new habitat along grasslands

With more than 60 lions roaming outside the Gir Sanctuary area, fears have been expressed on potential man-animal conflicts in the region.

A study by the state Forest Department and the Wildlife Institute of India (WII), Dehradun has found that Asiatic lions from Gir are now looking for a new habitat along the grasslands of Palitana, Mahuva and Sabartundla adjoining the sanctuary.

It has also been observed that lions moving out of the sanctuary area cover approximately 800 sq km as opposed to the ones within the park, who restrict their movement within 100 sq. km. This came to light after tracking the movement of five lions, who have been radio collared by WII.

"With 60 out of 350 lions out of the protected area, the potential for the man-animal conflict is very high. This is astounding and very unusual. This indicates that the existing lion population will need about 10,000 sq. km use," said Dr Y V Jhala from WII, Dehradun.

Forest Department officials have, however, said that despite such movement of lions outside the protected area, cases of man-lion conflict have not really gone very high. Generally conflicts are reported between humans and leopards around the Gir Forest area, they said.

Bharat Pathak, Conservator of Forest (Wildlife) Junagadh, said: "Looking at the kind of dispersal of the lions, we cannot really say that incidents of lion-human conflicts have really gone up in the region. In the last four years, we had registered only one human death due to a lion attack and that too in 2005-06."

He said they are still studying the lions and intend to radio collar some more of the big cats. But one thing that has come to light is that the lions are now increasingly looking for new habitat, he added.

"Once we get the required amount of data, we'll be in a far better position to understand the social dynamics of the lions and their movement patterns, but for now, one thing is certain. The lions in Gir are looking for new homes," he said.

Jhala said the lions mostly live on dead animals surrounding the numerous Panjrapoles in the area and on the live-stocks of the farmers. "The lions occasionally kill wild boars and nilgais, which are a menace to the farmers," he said.

Pathak said most incidents of man-lion conflict arise due to wrong handling of the big cats. "Only recently, an old man was injured by a lioness near Lalpur village near the sanctuary area, when the villagers disturbed the big cat who was feeding on a kill. While the department promptly pays compensation for such kills, there is no need to disturb them. The irritated lion retreated to the forest and on the way came across the man and attacked him," he said.

Pradeep Khanna, Principal Chief Forest Conservator, said that lions are moving out of the protected area but cases of lion-human conflict have not really gone up. On the other hand, Instances of leopards straying into human habitation has become a cause of concern. "We are working with the different communities in forest and trying to sensitise them and also help them in village development. As a measure to reduce conflict, we are now paying compensation within 40 days of a killing," Khanna said.

Khanna further added that while the state forest department has already declared Girnar Forest as a sanctuary, it is also treating about 200 sq. km across Amreli and Bhanvnagar districts as protected forest.

Heading: 17 bombs recovered from garbage dump - Indian Express
Content:
Police protection ensures entry of Dalits at biennial Shikotar Mata puja for the first time

The age-old tradition of encircling a village with a cotton thread for protection from the evil eye had to be stopped at Targara village of Botad block of Bhavnagar District on Sunday, simply because the Dalits wanted their houses to be included in the 'safety net' as well.

Despite stiff resistance, the Dalits managed to get entry into the temple in the presence of the local police, which too had been denied to them since long.

The village deity, Shikotar Mata, is worshipped in the village every alternate year in a grand manner. A cotton thread is taken out from the temple and the entire village is encircled within its fold in an attempt to ward off the evil spirits and keep the people and the livestock free from ailments. The Dalits of the village have traditionally been kept out of this 'safety net'. Besides, they are also denied the prasad of the puja performed in the temple.

Village sarpanch Babu Koli said: "The practice has been going on for many years, but this year the Dalits demanded that they too be included in the "Suraksha Kavach. We could not allow that to happen." He also admitted that until Sunday, the Dalits were not even allowed to enter the village temple.

"Woh log door se pranaam karke chale jaate the" (They used to pay their obeisance from a distance and go away)," he said, adding that their demand to be included in the whole process led to a confrontation. Later, the Dalits were admitted into the temple. However, Mataji declined to permit the Surakhsha Kavach through the bhuva (the worshippers who get into a trance and apparently spell the will of the deity) and we had to postpone the ceremony," he added.

Harji Bala, a member of the Targara village Panchayat and the Chairman of Social Justice Centre, said: "Shikotari Mata was the family deity of some Dalit families from a nearby village, but the people from the higher caste laid their hands on the deity and barred our entry into the temple. We have been traditionally kept out of the Suraksha Kavach and also denied prasad."

He added that on Saturday, the Dalits requested the higher caste people to include them in this year's ceremony, which was flatly refused. "Later, we got in touch with Navsarjan, a Dalit organisation and informed the police about this. On Sunday morning, we went to the temple in the presence of the local police and for the first time got an entry into the temple. While they could not refuse us entry in front of the police, they later announced that the bhuva has made it clear that mataji doesn't want the Suraksha Kavach to be tied around the village this time," he said.

Sub-Inspector Nayak from the Paliyad police station, said: "There was some tension in the village as the Dalits tried to defy the tradition and get included in the Suraksh Kavach. We had a strong bandobast there and the Dalits performed their puja in the temple. Later the Bhuva postponed the contentious Suraksha Kavach."

Heading: GU plans on ‘knowledge kiosks’ for students from humble families - Indian Express
Content:
Kalupur police recovered 17 'desi' bombs from a garbage dump in Kalupur area on Monday morning.

Cops suspect unidentified persons may have left the bombs in the garbage dump, fearing arrests after increased police checks in the wake of the July 26 serial blasts.

The incident was reported around 8.30 am when a passer-by informed the city police control room about the bombs in the garbage dump on the footpath near the G A Latif Building in Kalupur area. The bombs were wrapped in a piece of cloth and made of normal fire-crackers sealed in an iron box, used to keep pan-masala. The iron boxes, wrapped with sutlis (jute strings) were filled with nails.

"We rushed to the spot and called the Bomb Disposal Squad and the FSL officers. The bombs were taken to a safe place and then defused," said Kalupur police inspector N B Nagori.

"The bombs seem old. Someone may have kept it at home, but due to increased police vigilance after the July 26 blasts, may have dumped it in the garbage dump," he said.

Nagori refused to call it an act to create terror in the wake of the upcoming festive season.

Heading: Urja Nigam ready to bear the cost for power-packed festivals - Indian Express
Content:
he Gujarat University (GU) is planning to set up 10 Knowledge Extension Centres (KEC)-cum-libraries in the economically backward areas to help the students get all the information related to the university near their residence.

"We are approaching the Municipal Corporations and NGOs as they can play a major role in helping us get buildings and arrange for the infrastructure for setting up these centres. Moreover, such centres would help in the development of society and students," said Parimal Trivedi, Vice Chancellor (V-C) of GU.
