He further said, "Keeping the needs of the 21st century in mind, GU is planning ahead and providing books, journals, newspapers at the KEC in order to help students who are not able to afford such things."

"At KEC, the students will able to get all the updates related to admission, examination, results and other important announcements. With GU making arrangement for computers and Internet services at these centres, students will be able to download forms. This will also help in cutting down on travelling expenses," said Trivedi

Elaborating further, the V-C told Newsline, "The proposal will be put in front of the Executive Council and as soon as the budget is passed we will begin work on the same. Once we begin the project and get feedback from the students, we will think about expanding the project further."

Heading: Talk the walk - Indian Express
Content:
Bowing to 'religious sentiments', the nigam decides to forgo temporary meter charges for garba venues

Once again, the Gujarat Vikas Urja Nigam Limited is all set to incur losses in the name of religious festivals. Succumbing to collective pressure from the Congress as well as the saffron brigade, the electricity department has decided to bend the rules that it had once set.

As per the rule, all organisers of functions during festivals must procure a temporary electricity connection, get a metre installed, and deposit an amount of Rs 10,000. But the department has now decided to press for it. Reason: It may hurt the religious sentiments of small non-profit groups that cannot foot the bill.

The department took this step when the Congress and the saffron brigade organised aggressive protests in Rajkot on Monday.

In Rajkot, Congress members barged into the office of Paschim Gujarat Vij Company Limited (PGVCL) asking them to scrap the rule. The BJP leaders, some of who are also garba organisers, threatened them of dire consequences if they implemented the rule. The electricity department gave in to their demands. This however, means increased chances of accidents. Several thousand garbas across the state will now have tubelights, decorative lightings and sound systems running on wires pulled from nearby houses, commercial establishments and even the nearest electricity pole. In Rajkot alone, the number of garba venues will touch the 1,500 mark.

Out of this, 1,000 are big garba mandals. The situation would be no different in places like Ahmedabad, Vadodara and other central Gujarat centres that fall under Madhya Gujarat Vij Company Limited.

"Aa vi Hitlersahi na chale. Ame eva fatwa natho manta (We will not accept Hitler's rule. We will not adhere to it)," said Janak Kotak, deputy mayor of Rajkot Municipal Corporation and organiser of Junction Society Garba, a 44-year-old garba group in Rajkot.

On Monday, Kotak led the Hindu Dharma Raksha Samiti Rajkot, a group jointly formed by the BJP, Shiv Sena, VHP and Bajrang Dal. It met the PGVCL authority.

The Congress too, submitted a memorandum with the city party president Jaswant Sinh Bhatti stating: "The rule has hurt people's religious sentiments."

While PGVCL authorities said that it has already announced the relaxation, MGVCL officers maintained it has always gone soft on this issue. "Organisers have promised us that they will not take the connection directly from electricity poles, but from houses or commercial establishments," said PGVCL chief engineer J Rajyaguru.

Heading: Song & dance - Indian Express
Content:
The runway sets the pulse racing for the older of the tantalising model twins

It isn't often that we read Tupur Chatterjee's name separated from her sister Tapur. But during the just concluded India Couture Week, Tupur tells us that it was a conscious decision on their part to not do the same shows. "Once in a way, it is nice to see us separately. Only then probably people see the difference between us," she says, as the make-up artiste does a good job of making her eyes look dramatic for Pallavi Jaikishan's show. But do people confuse between the two? "All the time. But now we are used to it. If you spend a couple of days with us, you will know the difference in our facial structure and also our personalities," she says, as she enters the green room.

The backstage seems to be the centre of all activity right now with make-up artistes and hairstylists getting their act right, caterers serving some diet food, event organisers running helter-skelter to get the stage ready, choreographers doling out instructions, models dabbing on some rouge and gloss and an in-house photographer capturing these moments. Tupur, who is older by 12 minutes, feels the backstage is a quintessential part of their life because it is here that they spend most of their time dressing up, making friends, practicing their walk and, sometimes, thinking of innovative ways of killing time. Other models, who are doing similar stuff, hover around graciously as Tupur fields simple questions. "In our profession, the waiting period is the biggest drawback. Models make it to the venue at least seven hours in advance. If we could cut down on the waiting period, we would look so much fresher," she says sipping on water.

In spite of being in the profession for eight years, her enthusiasm is still in place. Even today she looks excited about wearing yet another designer ensemble and sauntering down the ramp. "I get very excited but I am never nervous of walking the ramp. If the ramp is slippery or has paper bits, it does get a little scary," says the 28-year-old, while practicing her sequence of steps. And with the couture week being more elaborate in terms of settings, choreography and clothes, the anxiety becomes two-fold.

The sisters have had a firm finger on the fashion pulse of the city. But Tupur, a graduate in Biology, feels that the industry has grown massively over the last couple of years. "Today there are more international designs in the market. There is a Western feel to Indian wear," she says as she points to the outfit she wears. "Also the fashion shows are more organised now, unlike earlier when you did not know what was happening."

But for this granddaughter of Hrishikesh Mukherjee, one of the most revered filmmakers of the industry, Bollywood is still a distant calling. "It is those two minutes on the ramp that make me feel like a queen. Also, most of your dreams of wearing the best clothes available in the country get fulfilled." No wonder then, that between shouts of 'Hurry Up' and 'Find the damn hair pin' in the green room, Tupur manages to hold on to her nerve.

Heading: MS University V-C adjourns stormy syndicate meet - Indian Express
Content:
Parents' day out

High on getting a nod from the court for its release, Hari Puttar-A Comedy of Terrors makers organised a preview for parents and their little ones. Suchitra Krishnamurthy came with daughter Kaveri, Nasir with kids Insirah and Aisha, Jatin with Kainaz Pandit and Adesh Shrivastava with family. Sarika, Ken Ghosh, Neha Bhasin, Suresh Wadkar too reached Cinemax, Andheri, to catch the show. The film's young actors Zain Khan and Swini Khare got loads of compliments.

Showstopper Sarika was thrilled to find a life-size Hari Puttar mascot.

Heading: District administration gears up to help the differently abled - Indian Express
Content:
Vice-ChanCellor (V-C) of the Maharaja Sayajirao University (MSU), Prof Ramesh Goyal adjourned the syndicate meeting on Monday over an issue where syndicate members differed on his decision on the selection of lecturers in Performing Arts.

At the previous syndicate meeting convened last week, the members allegedly altered the lists of lecturers for the faculty of Performing Arts preferred by the selection committee. The panel is appointed by the university authorities. Even as the syndicate's resolution was passed last month, the V-C put his foot down and overruled the syndicate decision by using MSU Section 11 (4).

On a query, Prof Goyal said: "As chairman of the syndicate, I had shown my opposition to the syndicate's selection. However, the lecturers' lists were altered. My opposition is recorded by the university registrar… I found the decision wrong. But the syndicate continued arguing on the selection. Therefore, the meeting was adjourned."

Commenting on Monday's syndicate meeting on the two issues discussed last month, syndicate member I I Pandya said: "A few months ago, M S Patel, an engineer from Sujalam Sufalam Yojana Gandhinagar, was given a PhD degree by the varsity. While objections were made by the external committee to scrutinise the PhD thesis, the matter was finally sorted out. On Monday, I demanded the number of leaves taken by Patel."

He said according to the university rules, around 200 days' leave can be taken while working on the thesis, but the chairman of the syndicate could not produce this.

The selection committee had recommended Sirsagar for the Dance Department of the Performing Arts faculty and Shruti Vaghela for the Vocal Department in the same faculty. But the syndicate selected Ami Pandya for dance and Hemant Kothari for vocal. On September 22, MSU V-C Prof Ramesh Goyal re-appointed Sirsager and Shruti Vaghela using MSU Section 11( 4).

Heading: From Oct, VMC to don a transparent look - Indian Express
Content:
Realising the lack of awareness on the various Central and state government schemes, the district administration has decided to undertake the ambitious Swanirbhar project on Gandhi Jayanti, and reach out to all the differently abled people in Vadodara.

According to information furnished by the district administration, there are over 75,000 differently abled people in Vadodara, but only 11,621 are registered. While only 1,800 people sought for the pension scheme, 5,000 requested for bus pass concessions.

"Most of the disabled people either don't know or do not take the advantage of the schemes available. So now, instead of them coming to us, we will go to their doors to give them the facility," said District Collector Vijay Nehra.

The one-year project, which will start from Thursday, aims to achieve success by the next Gandhi Jayanti. The district administration aims to do a door-to-door survey across the city and the talukas to identify the differently- abled and get them registered.

Nehra said the details will be entered in a specially formulated software, which will ensure a reliable source of reference. With the comprehensive details in place, camps will be organised to fulfil the requisite official formalities to avail the various schemes, he said.

"We have seen that most of the disabled don't even have identity cards or medical certificates because of convoluted the system," he said. During the camps, each one can complete paper work and formalities and get the papers.

"We will have a medical team, which will give the certificates. They can get their identity cards and avail bus passes and various pension schemes. We will also look into their requirements and help them with employment facilities," he said.

Heading: Driver shoots dead dacoit; employer lodges complaint under Article 302 - Indian Express
Content:
Accounts of the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) will become transparent from October.

Under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM), every municipal corporation will have to function under the accrual system. With the system in place, every possession with the VMC will be accounted for and work under the double entry accounting system. "At present, the VMC has over 6,992 crore immovable articles under its property. From September 30, the accounting system in the VMC will change to accrual system," said VMC Commissioner M K Das.

The corporation was recently assessed by Mumbai-based Crisil, after which the VMC received an 'A' grade, the Commissioner said.

"With the accrual system, the VMC will be graded with a double 'A.' We will also be more credible and it will help us get loans easily from nationalised or private banks," Das said.

Heading: 7/11 challenge for police: Matching new claims with old chargesheet - Indian Express
Content:
In A bid to stop three dacoits from robbing his employer's house, a driver shot one of the criminals dead with a .22 bore rifle at Dharapur in Anand District. "But the owner of the Giriraj Bungalows had to file a complaint under Article 302 as the driver, Indra Vadan Patel, was not using an authorised rifle," said sub-Inspector V S Jadav.

The police said that the incident took place around 1:30 am on Monday, when three unidentified people tried to break the main entrance to the bungalow. "It was Patel, who spotted the criminals trying to barge in and that was when he ran towards them with a .22 bore rifle licensed to Thakker. He shot one of the criminals, while the other two fled from the spot," said Jadav.

Patel belongs to Moraj village and was working under Thakker for a long time, the police said. Meanwhile, the police have seized the rifle. "We are yet to find out how the rifle got into Patel's hands," said Jadav. The slain dacoit is yet to be identified and the post-mortem report is awaited. Thakker is a Dharapur-based businessman. The police said he owns three petrol pumps in the district.

Heading: Crawford Market: Heritage restoration yes, redevelopment no - Indian Express
Content:
Chargesheet names Pakistani infiltrators who planted bombs, will now have to match those alleged aliases with arrested IM men
ATS said RDX came from outside country; Crime Branch now says explosives were sourced from Karnataka through Roshan Khan

With the Mumbai Police Crime Branch's fresh claims that five of the 12 Pakistani terrorists involved in the 7/11 serial blasts are actually the local Indian Mujahideen (IM) members arrested last Wednesday, the police might have unwittingly complicated matters for themselves as the heat will now be on to bridge the gap between the original and altered versions of the 7/11 story.

While the police top-brass maintains that their new revelations would have no adverse bearing on their case, several important parts of the chargesheet will come under close scrutiny.

In the chargesheet submitted by the state Anti-Terrorism Squad on November 29, 2006, a total of 12 Pakistanis were shown to be involved. Of this dozen, one Salim died in the blasts and another Pakistani identified as Abu Osama was killed in an encounter. The ten others have been identified as — Abdul Razak, Abu Umed, Sabir, Abu Bakr, Kasam Ali, Ammu Jan, Ehsanullah, Abu Hasan, Aslam and Hafizulla.

The police will now have to match some of these alleged aliases to the five Indian Mujahideen members arrested.

The chargesheet also mentions that the Pakistanis infiltrated into the country through the Indo-Nepal, Indo-Bangladesh and the Gujarat borders. It also pinpoints two of the 13 arrested accused — Kolkata-resident Majid Mohammed Shafi and Madhubani-resident Kamal Ansari — as crossers who facilitated the Pakistanis' passage into the country. While Shafi allegedly helped Sabir, Abu Bakr, Kasam Ali, Ammu Jan, Ehsanullah, Abu Hasan cross into India from Bangladesh, Ansari helped Aslam and Hafizullah's entry through Nepal.

Having mentioned these infiltrations in the chargesheet, the police will now have to specifically connect the IM members to either Shafi or Ansari.

Similarly the police will also have to link the IM members to Faisal Shaikh, Sajid Margub Ansari, Ehteshaam Siddiqui or Abdul Wahid Din Shaikh who allegedly harboured the Pakistanis.

The ATS had also claimed that seven groups — each comprising an Indian and a Pakistani — planted the bombs aboard the trains. The police will now have to connect each IM member with a specific blast.

"The arrested accused have already given us information on what trains they travelled on and which of the bombs they planted. This information will be passed on to the ATS, who will investigate further once we hand over the accused to them. Since the ATS is the investigating agency of the 7/11 case, they will file a supplementary chargesheet," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria. Maria sought to downplay the disparities too. "There are no loopholes in the chargesheet filed. It is just that the accused arrested in the 7/11 case were misled by the IM members arrested now," he added.

Additional Director General, Railways, K P Raghuvanshi, who was the ATS chief when the chargesheet was filed, also claimed the new revelations would not affect the chargesheet. "We have solid evidence to prove the involvement of all the arrested accused chargesheeted in the case. It is quite plausible that they were given misleading information by the Indian Mujahideen members arrested now, and that is why they told the police that Pakistanis planted bombs along with them."

Following the arrest of the IM members, the police stated that the explosives used by the group to carry out attacks was sourced from Karnataka through absconding accused Roshan Khan alias Riyaz Bhatkal. However, in the 7/11 chargesheet, the ATS claims that the RDX used in the train blasts was brought from outside the country by Ehsanullah, one of the Pakistani accused. Further, while the 7/11 chargesheet states that the arrested accused conspired with LeT commander Azam Cheema, the police are now stating that the IM members arrested have not mentioned any association with Cheema. Rather, they are controlled by Pakistan based Ameer Razaq, the police claim.

Heading: State to drop MCOCA charges against Salem - Indian Express
Content:
The 139-year-old Crawford Market, mired in controversy over its redevelopment for more than two years, is now gearing up for restoration of its heritage structure. With dents in its tin roof, a dysfunctional mechanical clock tower and huge cavities in its slabs, the Grade I heritage building will finally get a restoration and strengthening by a consevation architect. The redevelopment plan, which envisaged multi-storey towers next to the heritage structure which were to be constructed by utilising the special FSI of 4, will effectively lie in cold storage for now. The proposal has been tabled with the Mumbai Heritage Conservation Committee (MHCC) and is expected to be on the agenda at the October meeting.

In April the panel had refused to consider the restoration plan over the confusion of two architects: re-development by architect G D Sambhare and associates and the heritage restoration plan by Abha Narain Lambah, who was appointed a consultant for the heritage part by the civic body.

Civic officials from the Heritage Department have now said that the confusion over restoration and redevelopment has been sorted out. "We are going ahead with the restoration and strengthening of the heritage structure of the market," said an official. "We have drafted a new proposal with Lambah as a consultant for the project, asking for restoration, strengthening and beautification of the Crawford Market. There is no reference to the redevelopment part and there should, therefore, be no objection from the committee members," the official pointed out. During the restoration work, shops and stalls inside the market area, too, will be realigned. "The arrangement of shops is haphazard at present. Without disturbing the shop area, they will be realigned," the official informed.

The restoration, whose cost has been pegged at Rs 28 crore, will turn the heritage market back to its original glory. Crawford Market is spread over an area of 72,000 sq yard and is famous for its architecture, a blend of Norman and Flemish architectural styles designed by Lockwood Kipling, father of writer Rudyard Kipling. One of the main features of the building is the Clock Tower, which is adorned with beautiful Victorian carvings and two fountains and a pyau which form an integral part of the market. Named after the then Bombay's first municipal commissioner, Arthur Crawford, the market is divided into sections for fruits, vegetables and meat, while another section sells livestock and pets.

Civic officials from the Heritage Department said that the market in its existing state is dilapidated at many places and is in dire need of repairs and structural strengthening. Once restored, the building will have its roof — which is at many places tin shade — restored with a Manglorean-style roof. When contacted, Lambah described the scope of her work as "full restoration of Crawford Market". "I am awaiting the MHCC clearance," she said.

Heading: Young man with Abhishek’s face threatens Big B, demands Rs 25 cr - Indian Express
Content:
Charges under MCOCA, against extradited gangster Abu Salem, in the Ajit Dewani murder case will be dropped. The state government has given an undertaking to the Bombay High Court that it would drop the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) charges against Salem within two weeks, as it breached the extradition conditions.

Dewani, the former secretary of actor Manisha Koirala who had later turned a film producer, was killed in 2002, allegedly at Salem's behest. After Salem was extradited from Portugal in 2005, MCOCA charges were slapped on him. Salem filed a petition in the High Court saying he was not supposed to be tried for charges other than those for which he had been extradited.

Salem's advocate Sudeep Pasbola and Chief Public Prosecutor Satish Borulkar confirmed the government's willingness to drop the MCOCA charges.

In another petition by Salem, the government had informed the court that it was ready to allow Salem's trials before a single judge. As for his trials in other states, the government submitted that the designated TADA judge should pass necessary orders for producing him in other states. Salem has three trials pending in Mumbai, the Dewani murder case, the murder of builder Pradeep Jain and the 1993 serial blasts.

Heading: Hope I can still party at 65, says India Inc’s first lady - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Police Crime Branch on Sunday arrested a 25-year-old youth from Rajasthan for allegedly issuing a death threat to actor Amitabh Bachchan and demanding Rs 25 crore from him through an SMS. According to the police, the youth bears a resemblance to actor Abhishek Bachchan and came to the city hoping to land a role after being used as a body double for the actor during the shooting of Drona in Jaisalmer.

The arrested accused has been identified as Devisingh Kadamsingh Rajpurohit, a resident of Jalor district of Rajasthan who originally hails from Pokhran. He was brought to the city by a team of Crime Branch officials on Monday, and will be produced at the Esplanade Court on Tuesday.

"On the morning of September 26, Amitabh Bachchan received a threatening SMS which stated that he would be killed and had just three days to live unless he paid Rs 25 crore. The actor lodged a complaint with the Anti-Extortion Cell on the same day. We tracked the message to Rajpurohit's number and arrested him yesterday," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Crime) Rakesh Maria.

According to the Crime Branch, the accused resembles Abhishek Bachchan. When the actor was shooting for Drona in Jaisalmer a year and a half ago, Rajpurohit's neighbours told the actor of this likeness following which Rajpurohit was called in and asked to double up for the actor for some shots.

"That is when he came in touch with Abhishek Bachchan. Following this, he came to Mumbai seeking roles in movies. When Amitabh Bachchan's mother passed away and on his birthday, he sent a message to the actor and received a reply out of courtesy. When Abhishek was getting married, a newspaper used him in a sting operation to pose as the actor and breach security to reach Aishwarya Rai's apartment with a bouquet of flowers. When he failed to land any roles, he decided to extort money from the Bachchans," said Maria, who said that the accused had taken the actor's mobile phone number from a popular cine-magazine.

Heading: Hari Masjid case: Why is CBI running away, asks High Court - Indian Express
Content:
Tina Ambani reminds us that 'age ain't nothing but a number', shares her passion to help elders live productive lives

It's a nondescript shamble at Thakurdwar, where a hundred odd citizens are playing carrom, reading magazines or practicing yoga. But Tina Ambani, wife of India's richest man Anil Ambani, seems to be absolutely at ease. "Age ain't nothing but a number," she chortles to a 70-year-old gent even as she strikes a cookie in.

"Our elders are not a liability; we can turn them into our strengths," says the fabulous-at-50 lady, speaking about the Harmony Silver Awards scheduled for October 7 at Rabindra Natya Mandir. The awards — which carry Rs 51,000 in cash and a citation for each awardee — instituted by her five-year-old Harmony Silver Foundation are in their second edition.

The jury comprises MP Priya Dutt, actors Om Puri and Victor Banerjee, Justice Leila Seth and The Indian Express Group Editor-in-Chief Shekhar Gupta, and is presented to "silvers" who've achieved something remarkable considering their age. Last year's winners include Chelekkodan Ayesha, an 80-year-old woman who sat for her 10th standard exams along with her great-granddaughter and is now the face of education in her home state Kerala.

"The numbers of our seniors are boggling; from the current 80 million, we will have 137 million seniors by 2012," she says, "And I'm not scared of their growing numbers."

The Harmony Interactive Centre, which we visited today, is a three-storey community centre where Ambani's initiative functions as a flagship. There are other spaces in Mumbai, Delhi and soon Bangalore, where elders collect to make friends, train in computers and yoga, learn about investments and the like. "They don't need care; they need interaction," she adds.

Ambani says that even though her parents are no more, she came from a "very secure and loved childhood, the youngest of nine siblings", who recently collected and toured the Ashta Vinayak. "It was fantastic. We drove all over, that too in the rains," she says excitedly.

Her mother-in-law, she says, is as close it can get to being her mother. "I just love her; she's the most caring and giving person ever."

It's probably for the same reason that she has dedicated her soon-to-open hospital to her. It will be called Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital and Medical Research Centre and will house a Geriatric centre too. "There are only one or two hospitals in the country offering geriatric care," Ambani explains.

The lady, her chic rose-pink tunic and ice cube-size diamonds showing off her movie-star good looks, is also particular to bequeath the values she has learned to her sons, Anmol, 17, and Anshul, 13. Family time is where she finds her stress-buster.

"My husband and I take the kids for African safaris twice a year," she says, citing a week as a long vacation. "It's fabulous; we're completely disconnected; there's no stress and no shopping to worry about," she laughs, adding that she's saturated with her purchases. "I can wear Abu-Sandeep with the same joy as my own designs made by my tailor."

Ambani hopes to have the same energy when she's "a silver" as she does today. "I hope to have achieved something and make a small difference by then. And I hope to be able to party as hard," she laughs.

Heading: Woman manages to avert robbery - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Monday asked the Centre why the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is reluctant in investigating the Hari Masjid police firing case in which seven people had died 15 years back. "Why is the agency running away from the case? You rush to investigate other cases. Here seven persons died but you are aloof," a Division Bench of Justice F I Rebello and Justice Ashutosh Kumbhakoni said.

The case pertains to the death of seven persons in police firing outside the mosque during the 1992-93 riots. Farooq Mapkar who was chargesheeted for murder and rioting in 1992-93 had urged the court to initiate action against the then assistant police inspector Nikhil Kapse, who was held "guilty of unjustified firing" and "inhuman and brutal behaviour" in the Srikrishna Commission report.

Mapkar had moved the High Court seeking a CBI inquiry. Although the Maharashtra government is ready to hand over the case, the CBI is not willing to take it up. The state government issued a notification last year, handing over the case to CBI. But the agency told the High Court that its hands were full and it cannot investigate a 15-year-old case in which a Special Task Force had already given the police a clean chit.

Although the Commission report had indicted Kapse's team for opening fire without any provocation, a departmental inquiry found that the police were not at fault. The police had filed a case of rioting against Mapkar. The court today said it would examine whether the CBI can refuse to take over a case despite a request from the state government and adjourned the hearing to October 7.

Heading: Four acquitted in 2002 murder case - Indian Express
Content:
An accident averted a robbery at Marine Drive on Saturday. The incident occurred at 8:35 pm when two men tried to rob 69- year-old Amina Ahmed who stays in Kasturi Building at Marine Drive with her brother Faisal Ahmed.

On Saturday, two men who posed as courier boys came to Ahmed's residence. They were carrying a parcel. They said the parcel was for one Razmi Ahmed. They entered the house by force and shut Amina Ahmed's mouth when she protested. They also put a gun to her head. Ahmed accidentally knocked the gun on the floor and immediately picked it up. She then pointed it at the two men and pulled the trigger. Met by Ahmed's unexpected resistance the two thieves fled.

Surprised by the light weight of the gun, Ahmed opened the parcel. There was a box for this 'gun' which turned out to be a harmless lighter. Ahmed filed a case of attempted robbery at the Marine Drive police station the next day. She has furnished the police with the description of the criminals. Ahmed has been living in the place for the past 52 years.

Senior Police Inspector of Marine Drive police station, Sanjay Amrute said, "The woman has shown immense courage by standing up to her probable robbers." He added, "The thieves seem to be first time offenders as according to Amina Ahmed, they must have been between 17 to 20 years. Also, they had got the wrong name of the person who lived there. Finally the fact that they ran away even though they knew the gun was fake proves that they may have thought someone was in the house."

Heading: State told to reply on hysterectomy on mentally challenged girls - Indian Express
Content:
The Thane Sessions court on Monday acquitted four persons including Saquib Nachan in a 2002 murder case for lack of evidence. The others acquitted are Mohammed Ansari, Farhan Khot and Adnan Mulla. Nachan is a prime accused in the 2003 Mulund-Vile Parle and Ghatkopar blasts.

Suresh Sherekar, a reputed lawyer from Thane was shot by a person on a motorcycle on the Bhiwandi highway while he was on his way from the Thane court to his residence in Padga in January 2002. He was in a Santro car. A pillion driver allegedly opened fire at Sherekar who died on the spot.

The Padga police which was handling the case, handed it over to the Thane rural crime branch. Ansari, Khot and Mulla were arrested only after Nachan was arrested in Mulund blast case. Ansari was allegedly the shooter. All four were charged with murder, conspiracy and various sections of the Indian Penal Code.

According to the prosecution, Nachan had political enmity with one Tariq Duzar who was supporting the Shiv Sena and the RSS faction. Duzar was hugely supported by Sherekar, who was also a prominent RSS figure in Padga.

Nachan's lawyer, Mubin Solkar said, "None of the eyewitnesses identified the accused. Of 23 witnesses examined by the prosecution, nearly 18 turned hostile. There was no evidence to prove either of the accused guilty."

Heading: Court acquits six charged with extortion, attempt to murder - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Monday directed the state government to reply on the issue regarding performing hysterectomy— surgical removal of uterus and ovaries— on mentally challenged girls and women.

The court had earlier observed that the government was not taking the issue seriously and sought a magisterial report on the matter. Though the report was submitted on Monday, the court said that it was not satisfied with the condition of the institutions and directed the state government to file a reply within four weeks. While hearing the case, a division bench led by Chief Justice Swatanter Kumar and Justice S A Bobde reiterated the previous orders that had stated that none of the mentally retarded girls should be subjected to the surgery.

The court directed the government pleader Madhubala Kajle to reply regarding the conditions under which the mentally retarded girls were subjected to the surgery prior to the previous court orders and also the steps taken to correct the problems after the court's direction. "Mentally challenged girls should not be subjected to surgical process without following the due process of law," Chief Justice Kumar said.

The court was hearing two public interest litigations (PILs), one suo-motu and another filed by a Pune-based doctor. The PIL filed by the doctor stated that performing hysterectomy without a woman's consent — even if she's mentally retarded— is a violation of her fundamental rights.

PIL filed by Dr Anant Phadke in 1994 had raised the issue of hysterectomy performed on a 17-year-old woman at a state-run institution.

The government counsel had earlier contended that these women could not take care of proper hygiene during menstruation period, and they have to face unwanted pregnancy, if sexually exploited.

The court had earlier stated that as you (state) have opened these five institutions, it's your duty to take care of these women.

However, the state government had argued that authorities concerned had taken permission from girls' parents, and also obtained medical experts' opinion before performing the surgeries. The case will come up for hearing on November 17.

Heading: ‘RTI on wheels’ to educate people about utility of act - Indian Express
Content:
Just a week after the evidence was recorded, a special Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) Court on Monday acquitted six men charged with extortion and attempt to murder.

Special Judge MP Kukde acquitted all six men after the police failed to produce any material evidence against them in the court.

The accused- Abdul Latif, Yusuf Khaniya, Akbar Dhosani, Raju Rehman, Mohammad Asgar Khanwere and Nasir Pochi -were booked under MCOCA and charged with extortion and attempt to murder.

According to the prosecution, in November, 2004, a businessman working at the Abdul Rehman Street had received a phone call from a gangster Ejaz Lakdawala demanding a huge amount of money as extortion.

However, when he refused to cough up the amount, on January 17, 2005, the six accused allegedly conspired and opened fire on his shop which left the businessman injured.

But after scanning through all the evidence and listening to the testimony of the witnesses, the court observed that, "no connection could be made to prove that they were members of the Lakdawala gang."The court considered that there was no material evidence such as recovery of firearms to link the accused to the actual shooting.

"There was no eye-witness to identify any of the six accused. Nearly seven witnesses were examined. Three of them were salesmen from the shop that was attacked, but none of them could identify the accused," said defence advocate Sushan Kunjuraman.

All the six accused were on bail since 2005 as the police failed to file chargesheet within the stipulated period of 90 days. At the time of granting them bail, the MCOCA Court had observed that even the investigating officer was absent from court and the remand plea for an extension of their custody was a "stereotypical" one.

Heading: Bid to teach tiny tots about modes of transport - Indian Express
Content:
After successfully touring the districts and villages of Gujarat and educating the citizens about the RTI Act, Mahiti Adhikar Gujarat Pahel (MAGP) along with the Public Concern for Governance Trust (PCGT) and Western India Regional Council of Institute of Chartered Accounts of India (WIRC-ICAI) are all set to bring the RTI mobile van in the city. 'RTI-on-wheels' was launched in the city on Monday. The van will be operational from October 2.

Pankti Jog of MAGP said, "The van is created to educate the common man to use the RTI Act effectively. Most people though know about the Act, have no idea how to use it. In rural area, the challenge is double as most people are still unaware of the Act. The van is designed for these purposes." The van is equipped with a LCD projector, television, computer with an internet connection, scanner, printer and a small library. Two volunteers will be manning the van to help applicants with any information. According to Jog, the vehicle was a huge success in Gujarat. "We launched the vehicle in Gujarat in March this year and visited inaccessible villages and tribal belts. We covered areas like Ahmedabad, Patan, Surendranagar, Rajkot and Sabarkhanta. Seeing the success there we decided to launch this vehicle in the financial capital too," said Jog.

The PCGT, which has been sensitizing the public about the Act and its various aspects, also decided to lend a hand to this initiative. Founder trustee of PCGT, Narayan Verma said, "Since its inception in 2005, the RTI Act has come a long way. Though more and more people are using the act now to get public information, many still do not know the necessary procedures. This van will help in making the whole procedure less cumbersome. Basically, the purpose of the vehicle is to tutor people on how to effectively use the Act." The group is using a modified Tata Sumo which they used in Gujarat in the city as well.

"We purchased the vehicle at market rate and additionally shelled out Rs 3 lakh for all the equipment," said Verma. In Mumbai, students of WIRC-ICAI are also pitching in the initiative. "This year we are celebrating the diamond jubilee, and as part of our social initiative programme we thought of spreading awareness about the RTI Act, and this van is good ground for the purpose. People at large, especially the youngsters are not very much aware of the various aspects of the act. So we tried to be a part of this initiative," said Chairman of WIRC-ICAI, BM Agarwal. Starting tomorrow the van will be touring various city colleges to spread awareness about the act. "We will first be sensitising the youth about the act and officially operate the van from October 2," said Verma.

Heading: Positive Health Awards - Indian Express
Content:
Pre-primary kids of the South Indian Education Society (SIES) School in Matunga were initiated rather early into travails of urban public transport, with their annual exhibition this year themed around mass transit systems titled 'Chalti Ka Naam Gaadi'.

The children along with their parents and teachers have organised the exhibition on different modes of transport, with models, charts and informative banners.

The exhibition saw students from lower and upper kindergarten depict various modes of transport in the form of models. The exhibition has models right from man's wonder creation of the wheel to space flights . "There are models of the wheel, elephants carrying logs, and cars on roads, upto space travel," says SIES trustee KA Vishwanathan.

"Last year the theme was seasons, before that it was birds and earlier than that it was plant life. This is the fifth exhibition," says Parvathi Ramachandran who is in-charge of the pre-primary section of the school. Around 400 students along with their parents have participated in the exhibition. "Though the parents and teachers have done the major work on making the models, the children learn a lot from it, " says Veena Venugopal, another teacher. "We have also shown the modes of transport used by the army along with cable cars ," says Anamika Chowdhury, an ex-student.

Heading: Beer factor - Indian Express
Content:
The Dr Batra's Positive Health Clinic has called for nationwide nominations from individuals who have overcome physical disease and disability, for the Annual Positive Health Awards.

In its third year, Dr Batra's Annual Positive Health Award is an attempt to recognise medical miracles and individuals who have demonstrated enormous fighting spirit to beat the odds to recover from seemingly hopeless medical conditions.

The Positive Health Awards 2008 will be presented at a grand ceremony on October 15, 2008.

Nominations should be sent with the details of the person and case history to: positivehealthawards08@drbatras.com

Heading: Cong to take part in all-party meet: Dasmunsi - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai brews its own watered-down version of the world famous Oktoberfest

Back in Nordrhein Westfalen, Germany, Oktoberfest is a mammoth affair. "It's very big - thousands come each day. It's about eating, drinking and having good conversations," says Chef Maurice de Boer of Germany. De Boer is visiting chef at Shamiana,Taj Mahal Palace and Tower, Apollo Bunder, for what can be called Oktoberfest celebrations in Mumbai.

A quick précis: Oktoberfest is an annual 16-day festival held in Munich every year, starting late September. The festival is synonymous with beer (called Oktoberfestbiers) served at the event in Munich since 1818. The event is special to pop cultural forces and attracts a lot of young adults. The amazing quantity of alcohol at the event sees thousands of Beer Corpses every year. It is a term invented for young people who pass out after excessive drinking. This year the festival is celebrating its 175th anniversary.

Beer, yes. But the other things people flock for to the festival are Pig leg with Sauerkraut (red cabbage), Apple Spatzle (tiny egg and flour dumpling), Weisswurst with Brezel (white sausage with Pretzel) and Sweet Mustard Schnitzel (traditional German cutlet) with cabbage salad. "These are some of the things that I am preparing for the Deutschefest too." When people the world over are eager to catch up on Oktoberfest, De Boer has caught a plane to India. Why? "I see it every year. So for me, being in Mumbai is a different experience. I like the attitude of the people. They are curious to know more. The markets and ingredients here are delightful." Although Oktoberfest in Mumbai is not even remotely like what it is in Germany, De Boer is happy to do his bit.

At the ITC Maratha, Chef Nikhil Merchant has created quite a spread of German delicacies. The hotel gets a lot of German guests who are only too happy to see Oktoberfest being celebrated here. One such person

Albrecht Becker likes the tap beer and the Apple-potato au gratin the best. "It's my first visit to Mumbai and I am surprised by the number of people celebrating the festival, however small-scale it may be. In fact, here they add their own touch to it and to tell you the truth, I am amused as well as impressed by it." Other German delicacies include Spit roasted chicken, German sausages, Asparagus Baden-Baden, Asparagus spears, Rote Rubensalat (pickled beetroot salad), Sauerkraut soup with German bread rolls, Sauerbraten (marinated pot roast in a sweet sour sauce) and Schokoladenpudding (Steamed chocolate pudding) and Apple strudel.

For most Indians who aren't guzzling lager in Munich right now, celebrations mean drinking tap beer till they drop. So whether it is Sports Bar, Toto's, Ghetto,

Geoffrey's, Pause or Café Mondegar, beer and sausage combos are selling like hot cakes. Manager Huxley Pimenta of Café Mondegar says, "We always sell barrels of beer. During Oktoberfest time, we sell some more."

However, original Oktoberfest frequenter Yogi Shah of backpacker.co.in feels that in our city, celebrations are merely a watered-down version. "Once you have been to the Mecca of beer festivals all the others pale in comparison. Oktoberfest is all about beer gardens and enjoying your beer and food outdoors. Now, where in Mumbai can one replicate all that? Besides, we do not have the secret anti-hangover formula that the Germans have."

Heading: To discuss Singur, Mamata to meet Sonia today - Indian Express
Content:
Chief minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee willconvene an all-party meeting on the Singur issue on Tuesday afternoon at the Writers' Buildings.

Sources in the chief minister's secretariat said all political parties represented in the state legislative assembly have been invited.

Except for Trinamool Congress, all the parties, including the Congress, will attend the meeting.

Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting and state Congress chief Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi, meanwhile, sided with Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee in finding a solution to the Singur impasse.

After a meeting with Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi, Dasmunsi said Congress will take part in the all-party meeting, scheduled to be called by the chief minister shortly on the issue.

It was Dasmunsi who floated the idea of an all-party meeting on Sunday to resolve the crisis in Singur. Party sources said Dasmunsi also had a talk with the chief minister over the issue recently.

"We want a solution to the Singur problem. Therefore, the Congress will participate in the all-party meeting on the issue," said Dasmunsi at a press conference at Bidhan Bhavan, party headquarters in Kolkata.

"The problem regarding Tata's Nano factory can be resolved through dialogue. What happened in Singur and what is happening in Singur is most unwanted."

On Monday evening, Dasmunsi had an hour-long meeting with the Governor in Raj Bhavan to discuss the Singur issue. He said his party wants the Governor to continue the mediation and call the Tatas to participate in the meeting.

"The Tatas should not leave Bengal¿ they should find out themselves how much land can be given to the affected farmers from inside the plant. The rest can be arranged from outside. The Tatas should build up the industry, keeping in mind the human factor," said Dasmunsi.

He also added that it was wrong on part of the state government to announce a fresh rehabilitation package for Singur while an agreement was signed with the Opposition. "The government is to blame. The Opposition is not responsible for the Singur problem," he added.

Heading: Tata agrees to meet Buddha - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee has said that she would meet Congress president Sonia Gandhi in New Delhi on Tuesday to thrash out the Singur issue.

Announcing this at her Kalighat home on Monday afternoon, Banerjee said: "We believe this government has no right to remain in power because it flouted the agreement signed in front of the Governor. We have taken up the matter with the Governor and will take it up with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and President Pratibha Patil. But since the PM is abroad and will take around five days to come back, I will meet Sonia Gandhi and demand Central intervention."

But speculations are rife on the real purpose of the meeting. In face of the coming Lok Sabha polls, Gandhi is reportedly keen to have an alliance with the Trinamool. According to TMC insiders, she had even called Banerjee a few times, expressing a desire to meet her.

According to TMC sources, Banerjee herself is in favour of an understanding with the Congress, as one of the reasons for her party's doing well in the last panchayat elections was her distance from the BJP.

"If there is no alliance between the Congress and the TMC, the Congress will put up its own candidates and that will divide the votes. In the panchayat elections, we got a lot of Muslim votes because we kept away from the BJP," said a leader.

The last time Mamata met Gandhi was in the first week of December 2007.

That Singur alone is not on agenda was hinted at by the party's former parliamentarian Dinesh Trivedi, who is going to accompany the Trinamool leader to 10, Janpath. "When two political leaders meet, so many issues can crop up. Who knows whether other issues will not come up or not. Let us see," Trivedi told The Indian Express.

The meeting also assumes importance in face of the recent developments in the state Congress. On Saturday, Pradesh Congress Committee president Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi said at a rally in Singur that the land inside the project area is no longer cultivable but still, the government may try to give as much land as possible to farmers who did not take the compensation package. The rest can be given from outside the project area.

On Monday, without naming Dasmunsi, Banerjee said: "Some leaders, the agents of CPM, who have come to fish in troubled water have now come forward. People should know them and keep away from them."

Dasmunsi, however, reacted mildly. "She has not named any name. I won't say anything on this. She is going to Delhi to meet our leader. I won't comment on that either," he said.

Heading: Singur crisis may affect Japanese investment - Indian Express
Content:
The much awaited meeting between Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee and Ratan Tata is likely to be held on next Friday.

According to sources in chief minister's secretariat, Ratan Tata will be meeting the chief minister to explain the problems his company is facing to resume work at its Nano factory in Singur.

"We have not yet got any signal that Tata Motors would resume work immediately. The government is looking forward to the meeting and its outcome," said a senior official in the chief minister's secretariat.

Bhattacharjee wrote a letter to Ratan Tata last Friday, asking him to meet the state government so it can explain its stand on the situation. He had also requested the Tatas to resume work at the Nano site and not move out of Bengal.

On Sunday, Bhattacharjee announced that he has received a reply from Tata who has accepted the invitation. The date and venue of the meeting is yet to be decided.

"On October 3, Ratan Tata will be in Kolkata. He will meet chief minister on that day. However, the venue is yet to be finalised," the official added. The CPM sources, meanwhile, said the situation in Singur has boiled down to a question of law and order, with Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee sticking to her stand.

"Maintaining law and order in and around the Nano factory means police action against any attempt at lawlessness by the protestors. One has to see if Tata favours strong steps, though the party and the government may opt for it," said a senior CPM leader.

The state committee of the CPM, meanwhile, discussed the Singur deadlock on Monday. The party's state secretary Biman Bose, during his address to the 83-member committee, blamed Banerjee for her agitation which prompted Tata Motors to suspend work at the Singur site.

Heading: Subrata Mukherjee back in Congress good books - Indian Express
Content:
Japanese investors are closely watching the Singur imbroglio and if Tata Motors pulls out of West Bengal, that will have an adverse impact on them, said Fujio Samukawa, consul general of Japan in Kolkata.

"Japanese people are interested in Nano car as it is a unique product. The problem (in Singur) needs to be solved amicably, as early as possible," he added.

Samukawa was speaking on the sidelines of a seminar on Monday. He is the third consul general in Kolkata to express concern over the recent troubles faced by the industry in the state. Earlier, US consul general Beth Payne had said the political tussle over the Tata Motors project had made the US investors wary of doing business in the state. German consul general

Günter Wehrmann had also expressed his disappointment over the non-renewal of licence to Metro Cash & Carry.

So far, Mitsubishi Chemicals and Kubota Corp are the two Japanese investors in the state. Kubota Corp's joint venture with Tata Metaliks at Kharagpur for manufacturing of iron ductile pipes will be operational from March next year. "There is a scope for further Japanese investment in West Bengal though nothing is in the pipeline at present," said Samukawa. He added, "We cannot force Japanese companies to come to West Bengal, but we can try to explain them the advantages of investment in the state."

While Samukawa refused to comment on the land acquisition process in the state, he said: "In Japan, private companies buy land directly from the farmers. Companies negotiate with the landowners and it has nothing to do with the government."

Heading: No Third Front but quest on for Third alternative - Indian Express
Content:
With the Congress busy making the most of the Singur crisis, the controversy in the state Congress over Subrata Mukherjee seems to have taken a backseat.

West Bengal PCC chief Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi held a meeting with Mukherjee on Monday and nominated him as one of the leaders to represent the Congress at the all-party meeting to resolve Singur crisis. Mukherjee also accompanied Dasmunsi when the latter went to meet the Governor at Raj Bhavan.

Mukherjee said, "We had a long discussion. He (Dasmunsi) explained me the work. I will attend the all-party meet." Whether he has been reinstated as the chief spokesperson of the party, Mukherjee said, "No, the issue was not discussed."

On September 16, Mukherjee had defied the party line and joined Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee's protest rally in Singur. While Mukherjee said he went there as a Congress leader to support the people's movement, Dasmunsi said Mukherjee had not obtained the permission of the party.

Congress sources said the party is trying to make a comeback in the state using the Singur issue and matters such as actions on Mukherjee will be dealt with later. "With Singur impasse continuing, this is not the time for inner-party bickering and take actions against party leaders. Moreover, we need seasoned politicians like Mukherjee," said a senior party leader.

Heading: German giant says its model will benefit farmers - Indian Express
Content:
There is no 'Third Front' but the Left parties are engaged in the quest for a 'Third Alternative', said CPM general secretary Prakash Karat on Monday during an interaction at the Indian Women's Press Club in the capital.

"The party has decided that we will not be hustled into any front or alliance but will take our time to get together with those we can work with on common policies," he said. At the same time, this long-term search for a Third Alternative was not to be confused with "effective electoral intervention — adjustments and understandings with parties that can help us and those we can help".

Speaking on the recent and ongoing violence against minorities in Karnataka and Orissa, Karat drew another distinction.

"The problem of the deep communalisation of society is here to stay but given the present political alignment, it is very difficult for all secular parties to come together on a common platform against it." At the same time, a "broader unity" is needed to "fight the danger". So let there be "broad platforms", said the CPM general secretary, "in Karnataka, Orissa and Uttar Pradesh, where secular forces can come together alongwith a range of non-party people".

On such a "broad platform", Karat drew a line between the Congress and the BJP. He recounted how, when asked whether the Congress could be equated with the BJP at a gathering last week, he had replied that the two parties could not be clubbed together.

The Congress could be part of the anti-communal platform that is so worked out, he said.

Mayawati has "a party and a possibility of getting a large number of seats in the Lok Sabha elections", and in a non-Congress and non-BJP government, she has a "good claim and a chance", said Karat. But the BSP's common understanding with the Left on issues beyond their shared opposition to the Indo-US nuclear deal is "still in the works", he said.

In the coming Lok Sabha elections, the Left's slogan would be two-pronged, said Karat: One, to defeat the BJP and "communal forces". And two, "It is inconceivable for us to support a government that forges a strategic alliance with the US" he said, without naming the Congress.

The CPM general secretary reiterated his party's well known opposition to the Indo-US nuclear deal. The bill passed by the US House of Representatives and pending before the US Senate is a "new Hyde Act with attachments" he said.

Karat was combative on Singur — "there isn't much hope, the way it is going, the Tatas don't want to resume work in the current situation" — holding the Congress answerable alongwith the Trinamool Congress. But "Nandigram was different — we made political and administrative mistakes".

Karat said that the UPA government "has not been able to get its act together"on terror. "There are genuine grounds to be concerned about why since the Delhi blasts in October 2005 a number of cities have come under attack and yet the security and intelligence agencies have been unable to uncover the network behind these attacks". At the same time, Karat ruled out tougher anti-terror laws as a solution, urging the revamp of intelligence gathering and better policing.

On the lynching of Graziano's CEO L.K. Chaudhury in Greater Noida a few days ago, Karat was brief: "No serious trade union will support such acts. We don't yet have an industrial culture — it will come," he said.

Heading: Yechury concerned over FDI in retail - Indian Express
Content:
While the Forward Bloc opposes the issuance of a trade licence to Metro Cash & Carry claiming that it will hurt the interests of farmers and small shopkeepers, the German major claims that these communities will be hugely benefited by its Business to Business model.

The model is quite unlike the marketing system prevailing in Burrabazar, the largest wholesale market in the city, and other markets.

In Burrabazar, anyone can buy commodities in a large quantity, whereas the consumers of the Metro Cash & Carry must have a proper trade licence issued by the company itself. People without a proper business establishment like hotels, restaurants and kirana shops, cannot purchase commodities from the distribution centres of the company.

The German giant will issue identity cards to its customers who run business establishments. The company has constituted several teams to verify credentials of the applicants.

The unique business model, a first in the state, will streamline the entire supply chain between the farm producers and customers. It will bypass several middlemen, who have been taking away the profits of agricultural produce by duping farmers.

Under the model, the German company will procure its agricultural commodities and other food items from several cooperatives and marketing committees registered under the Agricultural Marketing Board. The company's spokesperson, Vishal Shegal said, "We have already tied up with some local cooperatives for procuring the farm produce."

He further added: "Farmers will be hugely benefited by this model as it will eliminate the wastage of commodities. We have our special trucks for carrying agricultural produce that will reduce the logistic cost for farmers and small shopkeepers, besides keeping the produce fresh. We will also train farmers and shopkeepers on how to preserve agriculture products."

To ensure that no retail business is undertaken by the company in future, the authorities have also limited the quantum of sale by fixing certain quantity below which commodities cannot be sold off.

President of Aloo Byabsayi Samiti, Sanatan Santra said: "Cooperatives and registered marketing committees will benefit from this because the farmers will be able to sell at a higher price than they presently do."

The Forward Bloc, meanwhile, is yet to decide on the conditions that will be imposed on Metro Cash & Carry for issuing the APMC licence. "We have not yet decided the rules for the company. We will certainly protect the interests of poor farmers and small shopkeepers, "said Naren Chatterjee, a Bloc leader.

Hawkers protest Cash & Carry licence
Kolkata: To protest against the issuance of the Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee trade licence to Metro Cash & Carry, the Hawkers Sangram Samity staged a demonstration at the company's office on the Eastern Metropolitan Bypass on Monday and burnt the effigy of the comapany's managing director. "We will continue our protest if the government issues a licence. This kind of organised wholesale trade will destroy the livelihood of poor farmers and small shopkeepers," said Shaktiman Ghosh, general secretary of the samity. The company's spokesperson Vishal Sehgal said: "I really do not understand why the hawkers are protesting because our business does not affect their businesses."
— ENS

Heading: On Mahalaya, man swept away in Howrah ghat - Indian Express
Content:
While the crisis over the renewal of the licence of Metro Cash & Carry is over, the CPM is still skeptical about foreign direct investment in retail. Politburo member Sitaram Yechuri said the German giant was given the permission only for conducting wholesale business. He was speaking at an interactive session organised by a chamber of commerce on Monday where the members expressed their concern over the industrialisation scenario in West Bengal.

For FDI in India, Yechuri laid down a few conditions. "FDI should provide employment and ensure technological advancement," Yechuri said, adding that FDI in retail will adversely affect employment opportunities. He said one should be careful that the FDI does not enter the retail market through the backdoor.

"The companies begin by selling only single brand items," he said, hinting that they later enter into other segments.

Talking about the Singur crisis, Yechuri said it was imperative for the state government to acquire farmland in the area as there is only one per cent fallow land in West Bengal. "Land acquisition laws must be amended and the amount of compensation should be incorporated in the Act," he said, referring to the party's efforts to change the 1894 Land Acquisition Act.

"Had the Act been amended, the crisis in Singur would not have occurred," said the CPM leader.

"The issue will be settled at the meeting between the CM and Tata," he said.

Heading: Bus runs over woman, set ablaze by mob in Behala - Indian Express
Content:
A 41-year-old man drowned while offering tarpan in Shibpur on Monday morning. Barun Pal, a resident of Rajaballav Para Lane in central Howrah, had gone to the Ramakrishnapur Ghat with his brother Bijon Pal to offer tarpan in memory of their parents.

The incident occurred around 11 am when Barun went to take a second dip. In spite of being warned by the locals about the high tide, he decided to go ahead and was swept away as he did not know how to swim.

Apart from the solitary incident, people who went to perform the rituals in various ghats during Mahalaya on Monday claimed that the rush was a lot lesser than other years.

Eighty-five-year-old S P Bose, a resident of Shyambazar, who went to perform the ritual at Belur Ghat, said: "Since the timings for offering Tarpan had began on Sunday afternoon, most people preferred to finish it off yesterday. Today it was easier to offer tarpan since the ghats were less crowded".

He added, "Even Baghbazar ghat, which is always bustling with people, was relatively desolate in the morning than previous years. I felt there were more policemen this year manning the ghats".

Tarpan, which is performed on the day of Mahalaya, is a ritual to commemorate the ancestors. It is performed over a period of 15 days which culminates on the day of the Mahalaya with Teel Darpan.

Pritam Mukherjee, a Panihati resident and an employee of a private company, who went to offer tarpan at 7 am, said: "There is usually a scuffle on the ghats with so many people standing on the steps performing the ritual. It was, however, much better today".

Heading: Shopping frenzy turns New Market plastic - Indian Express
Content:
An unidentified woman was run over by a speeding minibus on Diamond Harbour Road on Monday afternoon. After the accident, angry mob set the vehicle on fire.

The accident took place at 3 pm, when the bus driver, in a bid to overtake another private bus of route 235, lost control and hit an auto-rickshaw. Noticing that the auto-rickshaw passengers were hurt, the driver tried to get away, only to crush the woman who was crossing the road.

Locals rushed to the rescue of the injured passengers and the woman who was bleeding profusely.

The driver of the minibus, meanwhile, managed to escape, leaving the vehicle. The bus was set ablaze by the mob, and two fire tenders had to struggle for over one-and-a-half hours to douse the flames.

All the injured were taken to the Vidyasagar Hospital where the woman was declared dead on arrival, while the others were admitted for treatment.

The police, meanwhile, are on the lookout for the driver. "We are trying to determine the identity of the woman and book the driver of the bus," said SP South 24 Parganas, Ajay Ranade.

Heading: Mayor in a ‘road rage’, will write to Centre - Indian Express
Content:
With more disposable income in the hands of middle class people, shopkeepers of New Market are witnessing a rise in the number of shoppers using plastic money.

Rekha Hathiramani, proprietor of a children's store in New Market, said in the last three years there has been a substantial rise in the number of people using their credit cards for shopping.

"Earlier, people used to carry cash for shopping and plastic money was used only by the rich. But now, most middle class families have credit cards — in fact, it has become a status symbol. Of course, people still pay in cash, however, this Puja there has been a definite rise in the number of people using credit cards," Hathiramani said.

Most of the big shops in the market have swipe machines for their customers. Rajesh Bathija, owner of a sari shop, said nearly 40 per cent of his customers prefer paying through credit cards.

"Out of 10 customers, four prefer credit cards. In a place like New Market that is considered as the shopping hub for middle class families, it is quite surprising to see so many people using credit cards," said Bathija.

A spokesperson for Sanskriti, another shop in the market, claimed the equal number of shoppers are using credit cards and cash for purchases. In fact, a rise in the number of customers with credit cards left them no choice but to keep a swiping machine in the shop.

Gita Gurbani, proprietor of a toyshop, said that in comparison to the 20 per cent customers who use credit cards during non-festive season, nearly 50 per cent of people who walk into her store for Puja shopping use credit cards.

"There is a lot more rush during Pujas and most of the middle class shoppers prefer credit cards over cash as cards are handy and hassle free," said Gurbani.

It's not only the big shops who are adapting to the new system of payment.

Many of the smaller shopkeepers admitted that those who do not possess swipe machines have to go to bigger shops to get the cards swiped.

Heading: To light up the nights, two pockets get a sunny inspiration - Indian Express
Content:
As you get mesmerised by the beautiful illumination during your visit to the pandals in Manicktala Chaltabagan and Salt Lake BD Block, don't miss out on the message these pandals want to convey through the glittering lights.

The two famous pandals of Kolkata have decided to go solar this year, and are bent on spreading the message on keeping the environment clean and green. While the Chaltabagan pandal will have its insides decked up with solar lights, the BD Block pandal will keep its exteriors illuminated with solar panels.

"Puja is a time when one has the opportunity to spread a socially-relevant message. We came up with the idea of making people aware of the solar energy appliances that one can use to protect environmental degradation," said Ashok Jaiswal, vice-president, Manicktala Chaltabagan Durga puja committee.

The mounting concern to arrest environmental degradation resulting from traditional dependence on fossil fuel has led to the importance of shifting focus to harness renewable energy resources.

Both Manicktala Chaltabagan and Salt Lake BD Block have approached the West Bengal Renewable Energy Development Agency (WBREDA), a state-level nodal agency under the department of Science and Technology and Non-Conventional Energy Sources, to help them out in their attempt to popularise green energy concept. With the help from WBREDA, the committees have tied up with private companies to hire energy lighting devices.

"This month we were approached by two Puja organisers who have shown interest in using energy saving lighting equipment to promote and make people aware of need to use non-conventional energy devices," said S P Gon Chaudhuri, former director, WBREDA.

While the interiors of Manicktala Chaltabagan pandal will be adorned with 15-20 solar energy bulbs, the committee members are also planning to put up 10-15 solar lighting pillars on the street leading to the pandal. Though their theme budget this year is Rs 10 lakh, the cost incurred for the solar lightings will be an additional one.

Salt Lake BD block, on the other hand, will have cubical chains of solar panels and LED bulbs displayed outside their pandals to create awareness and curiosity among the pandal hoppers.

"The message that we want to send out is that when there is an acute problem of pollution and severe dearth of electricity supply, the people of West Bengal have the option of using energy saving devices like solar lighting systems, solar fans and other solar and wind appliances to save the cost of energy," said Jaiswal.

Heading: After Bagan surprise, Mumbai FC eyeing another upset - Indian Express
Content:
Mohammedan Sporting and Air India played out a 1-1 draw in the I-League match at the Barasat Stadium here today.

Surojit Roy put the visitors in front in the 23rd minute, which was cancelled by Theodore Sunday in the 59th minute. In the end, both teams looked happy to share the spoils.

The conditions were demanding. Excessive humidity and heavy underfoot conditions made things difficult for the players, and the match never rose above mediocrity. Basically, it was a game of sloppy defending, miss passes and poor technique intertwined with some flashes of brilliance.

Air India enjoyed a greater ball possession in the first half and tried to play a good passing game. Surprisingly, their coach Bimal Ghosh preferred to defend deep after the breather and surrendered the initiative. Md Sporting, led by Man of the Match Adebayo Adewusi took control of the middle-third and finished stronger.

Both goals, however, were courtesy defensive lapses. In the 23rd minute, Air India caught the opposition defence napping with a fast counter attack and Michael Tayo set it up for Roy with a lovely flick. Roy's right-footer was too good for Naseem Akhtar.

The airmen had quite a few chances in the first half. They were controlling the midfield and were playing incisive passes upfront. Md Sporting's only chance in that half came in the 14th minute when Mike Okoro dropped his markers and sent a cross inside the box only to see Theo hitting it straight at goalkeeper Arup Debnath.

Things changed in the second half, especially after Theo converted a Jothi Kumar free-kick from a goal-mouth melee. The Air India defence was too slow to react and paid for it.

The goal helped Md Sporting gather momentum and they went into attack mode. Air India started to defend with eight players inside the box. Actually they were looking for a point from this away tie. They, however, must rue the lost opportunity in the 77th minute when substitute Subhas Singh's header was acrobatically saved by Akhtar.

The hosts upped the ante in last 10 minutes but there were not many real chances. That Okoro was a little off colour today didn't help Md Sporting's cause.

Going by the statistics, draw was a fair result. Both teams had four corners, Air India took a crack at goal 10 times compared to Md Sporting's nine, ball possession too was on an even keel. But today's game was not a good advertisement for Indian football.

Heading: Against all odds Dempo march on - Indian Express
Content:
It may sound weird. But the fact is, India's No 1 football club is plagued by the lack of infrastructure.

Last week, Dempo Sports Club created history by becoming the first Indian club to reach the AFC Cup semifinal. They won the National League thrice in last four years. Clearly, they are the team to beat as far as Indian football is concerned.

But all's not well back in the ranch. Their request to the state government for a piece of land has so far fallen on deaf ears. The club management and coach Armando Colaco hope that the AFC Cup achievement may now bring on some good news.

Dempo generally train at the University ground that barely meets the required standards. The conditions have deteriorated due to rains. The team had a hard time finding a suitable ground for training ahead of their AFC Cup semifinal. The club doesn't have a gymnasium let alone modern equipments like Jacuzzi.

Players, however, are not complaining. Rather they are interested in talking about the team spirit and Colaco's contribution that has helped them reach the top.

Said goalkeeper Abhijit Mondal: "Colaco's selection of overseas players and his method of handling them have been a key factor. The foreigners have gelled well with the local boys and that is our strength."

He elaborated: "Ranty Martins and Roberto Silva Beto lead from the front. Beto gives us quotes of some world greatest philosophers before every match. It's a real motivating factor. Martins takes up the cudgel when we are under pressure and shows us the way."

After the AFC Cup win over Home United, Singapore the team returned to a cold reception. The players were not upset though. The club president has already announced incentives that will be presented after he returns from Japan.

Coach prefers to keep a low profile and gives credit to his boys. "That I didn't make a single change in our last two AFC Cup matches speaks volumes for the way the players performed," he told The Indian Express.

Dempo, however, stumbled in the I-League opener against JCT. But Colaco doesn't want to read too much into that loss. "Right now I have set my sights on the AFC Cup semifinal against Safa FC of Lebanon," he said.

Dempo will play host to the first-leg tie on October 7, while the return-leg match will be played on October 21.

Heading: Golden Dreams - Indian Express
Content:
The stage is a medium for many messages — from RTI to nature conservation

A few months ago, WWF-India was discussing a not-so-wild problem — how to drive home the message of conservation among children? Prashant Narang of Prabodh, an NGO that works on the issue of good governance, was meanwhile racking his brains about something else — how to make the Right to Information Act less boring for college students? At CanSupport, the debate was about an effective fundraiser. All three hit on the same solution — why not say it through an entertaining play? Indeed, a play! Not rock concerts, not movies, not a celeb circus, but good old play.

Prabodh tied up with Five Elementz to present the wackily titled Gabbar Singh Files RTI at NSIT College, of the Capital, and landed a runaway hit. The story of the Sholay villain exposing bureaucratic corruption was peppered with oneliners and witticisms that had the young audience rollicking even as they learnt a lesson or two about the nitty-gritty of the RTI Act. "We now plan to hold a theatre competition on good governance before the general elections next year," says Narang.

Coming up next month is Snap, a play jointly produced by the Poddar and Nanda foundations for an aid fund for cancer patients. The play is being directed by Vivek Mansukhani of Scene Stealers, who for the past three years has also been involved in making plays for the organisation Kids for Kids.

For theatrewallahs, the support of an organisation means they don't have to scour for funds, permit, place or PR. "It also helps as a branding exercise. Working for a cause like the RTI Act is special," says Rakhi Mehta of Five Elementz.

For the NGOs, it means a relatively cheaper but powerful medium to get the message across. "Theatre means a captive audience," says Narang. Talk about stage-managing issues.

Heading: 1 arrested, hunt on for other five accused - Indian Express
Content:
What happens when two people who met with similar fates come together? They relive history. That is what journalists Kuldip Nayar and Asif Noorani did at the launch of their book Tales of Two Cities (Roli) in the Capital: they went back to a moment in 1947 when two nations were born in blood, forcing them to leave their land, cross a new, hastily drawn-up border and find homes in unaccustomed earth.

Karachi-based Noorani, associated with the Dawn Group, was in Bombay and all of five when Partition happened. "I vividly recall shouting 'Up, Up the National Flag, Down, Down the Union Jack' as a schoolboy. When someone asked me why I wanted the Union Jack down, in all my innocence, I replied that since Jack fell down and broke his crown, the Union Jack must also come down," laughed Noorani, offering a light moment.

Noorani's family left Bombay for Pakistan only in 1950 when the wounds were not so raw, but Nayar was not so fortunate. He was 24 when he left his hometown of Sialkot, exactly a month after the city became part of Pakistan, and saw first-hand the trauma of migration.

"Circumstances no longer sheltered us in our hometown. Our patience had exhausted in a month, though we came over to Delhi with the idea of returning when things got better. But they only worsened," says Nayar, who started the annual candlelight vigil at Wagah on the night of August 14. The mood is reflected on the pages where personal stories intertwine with history: if Nayar's "From Sialkot to Delhi" is grim, Noorani's "From Bombay to Karachi' carries twists of humour.

Heading: Increase in retirement age of teachers: HC tells Home ministry to decide by Oct - Indian Express
Content:
Accused asked victim to help park the Mahindra Scorpio, overpowered her inside the vehicle

A day after six youth allegedly kidnapped a German national from Hotel Taj GVK and molested her, one of the accused was arrested by the Chandigarh Police today. The accused, identified as Pankaj, a resident of Jindali village near Naraingarh (about 40 kilometres from Chandigarh), was arrested from his native village.

The victim has also identified the other five accused as well as the Maruti 800 car (HR-01-S-8489), in which she was dropped at Sector 20, Chandigarh, on Sunday afternoon. Pankaj is reportedly one of the two accused who escorted her back.

Assistant Superintendent of Police Madhur Verma said the victim had come out to the hotel's parking lot to smoke when she was approached by one of the accused. He asked her to help him out in parking the black Scorpio properly. She accepted the request and sat in the driving seat.

"Before she knew it, five youths sat in the car and asked her to take the vehicle out of the exit and enter the parking lot from the other side. The girl agreed and drove out of the hotel, taking a left turn towards Matka Chowk. The accused then asked her to turn the vehicle towards the Sector 9-10 dividing road.
