When the girl protested, the accused overpowered her and pushed her to the rear seat. Then they drove away," said Verma addressing a press meet.

This was also confirmed by the hotel's CCTV footage.

"The footage shows the girl going out of the hotel on her own," said general manager of Hotel Taj GVK, Anil Malhotra.

During investigation, the police also found that reported registration number of the black Mahindra Scorpio was allotted to an auto-rickshaw.

"After collecting information from various quarters, including the Taj's security guards, guests and the victim, we have dispatched our teams to Panipat, Yamunanagar and Ambala. In Ambala, our team managed to intercept a Maruti 800, which matched the suspected car's description. The victim has identified the vehicle," said a senior police officer.

Sources said the Maruti car was registered in the name of one Sube Singh, who told the police that Pankaj had borrowed the vehicle from him on Sunday afternoon around 12.30 pm and returned around 4 pm.

A senior police officer said they had the names and addresses of all the accused and will arrest them soon.

Ques:Who are accused?

All the accused are in their early 20s and come from villages in Haryana and Punjab. Sources said the youth had come to Chandigarh for drinks and went to the Taj to merely hang around.

During preliminary interrogation, Pankaj told the police the names and addresses of all the accused, out of whom one is reportedly the son of a police officer and another is the son of a Zila Parishad president in Haryana.

Heading: Cash at judge’s door: Bansal, justice examined by special committee - Indian Express
Content:
If the Ministry of Home Affairs allows, the entire teaching staff of Panjab University will have a happier Diwali this year. For, on the anvil is a resolution by the Ministry of Human Resources and Development, which if implemented will permit the retirement age of teachers to be increased from 60 to 65 years.

Today, the Punjab and Haryana High Court directed the Ministry of Home Affairs to decide the issue by October 20. The orders were passed after advocate Anupam Gupta, appearing on behalf of Panjab University, requested the court to resolve the issue.

A bunch of petitions, filed by several PU professors, demanding directions to the university to increase the retirement age from 60 to 62 years are pending in the High Court. The professors' stand is that since PU is a "central university" (in central universities, the retirement age of teachers has been extended to 62 years), the same shall apply in PU.

Contesting this plea, Gupta stated that the orders do not apply to PU as it is not a central university — it's a centrally-funded institution.

He further apprised the court that PU is under the purview of Ministry of Home Affairs, which is yet to decide on the issue. The counsel, however, requested the court to intervene and direct the MHA to decide the issue with immediate effect.

Accepting the request, the division bench directed the MHA to decide the issue by October 20 and file an affidavit to this effect.

Heading: Bone of contention at MC meet-Sector 17 projects - Indian Express
Content:
Several witnesses and accused in the 'cash at judge's door' scandal were examined today by the three-judge committee, constituted by Chief Justice of India K G Balakrishnan to investigate the case.

The committee comprises Allahabad High Court Chief Justice Hemant Laxman Gokhale, Jammu and Kashmir High Court Chief Justice K S Radhakrishnan and Delhi High Court Justice Madan B Lokur.

The day started with Justice Nirmaljit Kaur recording her statement at the UT guesthouse. Her examination lasted for nearly two hours.

On August 13, Rs 15 lakh was "wrongly" delivered at her residence allegedly on the directions of former Additional Advocate General, Haryana, Sanjeev Bansal.

Later, the statements of Sanjeev Bansal and his wife were also recorded by the committee.

The statements of co-accused in the case — Rajiv Gupta, Nirmal Singh and Parkash Ram — and several witnesses, including advocate Pankaj Bhardwaj, ASP Madhur Verma and a few UT police officers who had earlier investigated the case, were also recorded.

The process of examination began at 9 am and continued till 5 pm.

On Tuesday, the committee will record the statements of Delhi-based hotelier Ravinder Singh and his wife.

Ravinder Singh's counsel, meanwhile, moved an application demanding permission that his client's examination be postponed.

"Ravinder is in CBI custody for the last ten days and is not mentally or physically fit to make a statement," said advocate Y S Dhillon.

On the other hand, Bansal's counsel has withdrawn a bail application filed in the court of special CBI judge Jagdeep Jain.

"As Ravinder is still in CBI custody, we have moved an application demanding permission to withdraw the earlier bail application and the liberty to file the application afresh," said advocate N K Nanda.

Heading: You can find many working women in Pakistan now - Indian Express
Content:
The Municipal Corporation has earmarked Rs 1.42 crore for shifting electricity cables from the site of the proposed multi-level parking in Sector 17. At the House Meet held today, the MC also passed the scheme of setting up a new amusement park in the sector. And both issues have become an apple of discord among the councillors.

Amusement park

As reported earlier, councillors are at loggerheads on the issue of the amusement park. Former Mayor Harjinder Kaur opposed the project stating that the southern sectors are being neglected even though the majority of the city's population is concentrated there.

"If an amusement park has to come up, it should be built on a larger area," she added.

Echoing Kaur's views, councillor Amrit Bolaria said an amusement park is not required in the sector as it would increase traffic chaos.

Mayor Pardeep Chhabra assured the councillors that the southern sectors were on the path to development as the MC had taken over the community centres and green belts for maintenance.

"The amusement park will be built on a lease-hold basis and land will be vacated only if the need arises. Anyways, it will house only a few swings which may prove to be an attraction for children," he added.

Multi-level parking

Objections were also raised in the House over the release of Rs 1.42 crore for shifting cables for the parking lot to come up at the site of the Sahib Singh parking lot. Union Minister of State for Finance Pawan Kumar Bansal questioned why 24 per cent of the departmental budget was needed to fund the project.

Other issues

The MC plans to purchase another 100 garbage containers at a cost of Rs 39 lakh. A survey found that only 836 bins were kept across the city. The House also cleared the renovation of existing community centres in Sector 16 and Sector 39. The estimate (Rs 85.28 lakh) for widening and strengthening of the road from the District Industries Centre to the Phase II Industrial Area fire station was passed.

A process for a complete city-level assessment of managing e-waste will also be initiated. The study will identify potentially harmful substances and test them for adverse health and environmental effects. Chairman of the e-waste management committee, Arshad Khan, said occupational health safety norms for recycling should be devised.

Heading: Hyderabadi artist on a mission to spread ‘Ahimsaism’ - Indian Express
Content:
Students from Pakistan are on a visit to the city. Talking to Newsline, they spoke about the changing education scenario in their country.

"Breaking away from the conventional mode, parents are becoming increasingly aware and are allowing their daughters to pursue higher education," said Resham, a student from our neighbouring country.

While the students felt that rote learning is still prevalent in their schools, they were glad that higher education back home includes holistic knowledge.

The emphasis, they said is more on the practical aspect of the subject.

Speaking further on education of girls in Pakistan, Resham said that the parents' outlook towards education has changed.

"They have realised the significance of making their daughters independent. Due to this, girls have become more career-oriented. You can find many working women in Pakistan now," she added.

The guests also shared various initiatives taken by the government to promote education in Pakistan.

"In Punjab, education is free of cost in rural areas. The government provides children with free uniform and stationery so as to further support this cause.

Underprivileged students are also offered scholarships," explained Mariam Khaled.

Interestingly, the fad of engineering and medicine is pursued as relentlessly in their country as well, they said.

"Though students have started exploring other career options after 10+2, these two subjects continue to rule the roost. But of late, the media is also being preferred as a new vocation," said Shabbir.

"Many colleges are offering courses in Journalism and many women too are opting for them," added her friend Shayan.

Talking about higher education, Zikra said, "It is a blend of practical and theoretical knowledge and teachers try to maintain a perfect balance between the two. In fact, interning with different organisations has become mandatory so that we get hands-on experience."

Pakistani students also seem to be increasingly looking for greener pastures and moving to international shores.

"Brain drain is on the rise. Many students are moving to European countries for academics as well as work," said Resham.

Heading: Admn gears up for Navaratra mela: special security arrangements in place - Indian Express
Content:
Ahimsa has been his inspiration, which has kept him going for more than two decades now on his mission to spread the message of universal brotherhood. Ignatuis Xavier Joseph, a senior artist and painter, was in the city to be a part of the International Students' Peace Festival.

This artist from Hyderabad, who is on a peace mission, started painting only to communicate the message of world peace.

Colours, he says, are the best way to draw attention towards a cause.

"Words do have an impact but sometimes a picture speaks a thousand words. When red is splashed all over the canvas to show blood, the intensity of the colour hits you," feels Joseph.

A self-taught painter, Joseph is credited with developing a new form of art, India's Ahimsaism.

"I have always believed in the doctrine of non-violence, which was the main catalyst in our freedom struggle. My paintings are a way to further the message of Mahatma Gandhi," says Joseph.

Elaborating on this new art form, Joseph says that Ahimsaism follows the five principles of Jainism. "Anybody who takes up this form of painting has to follow certain rules like having complete vegetarian food. Working on the same doctrine, instead of using a brush for painting, we use a Pilate knife. This is to promote vegetarianism," he says.

A remarkable feature of his paintings is that he uses both oil as well as acrylic paints. "While the oil paint takes about two months to dry up, acrylic paints take five minutes. The concept behind this is that when two different colours can form part of a painting, various societies too can exist under one roof," explains Joseph.

Heading: ‘Credit crunch in America has also hit other economies because - Indian Express
Content:
With the Navratra mela all set to begin at the Mansa Devi shrine from Tuesday, the Panchkula Administration has made intensive arrangements to ensure that the mela carries on smoothly.

While around 14 checkpoints would be put up in the entire area, police in plain clothes would also be keeping a close watch on the law and order situation of the area. This was told by DC, Panchkula Rajender Kataria and SP, Sandeep Khirwar who were addressing a press conference at the shrine on Monday.

"All arrangements for the mela have been made. Besides the law and order situation, around 15 acres of land near the shrine premises have been made available for the parking of vehicles. Also, 6 CCTV cameras have been put up near the parking lot besides the 16 cameras that have been put up within the premises of the temple for intensive surveillance during the mela," said DC Kataria. He also added that around 10 duty magistrates would be pressed into service during the mela.

It was said that the transport authorities of different areas also have been contacted so that the devotees coming from the far-off places do not face a problem. "Besides the 24-hour medical facilities, a special laboratory is being set up so that a quality check on the prashad being distributed could also be kept," said Kataria. Sandep Khirwar, meanwhile, said that special arrangements have been made to face any eventuality.

"A special police post and a police helpline have been set up so that people do not face any problem during the mela," added Khirwar.

Heading: ‘Bunking helps one bond with friends over endless cups of tea’ - Indian Express
Content:
"To understand the current financial crisis, we need to clear the cloud of verbal confusion and understand the basics. Words like stagnation, recession stagflation and economic slowdown have been used interchangeably by economists and the press leaving the general public quite stunned," said Satindra Singh Ahluwalia, faculty member, ICFAI Business School, Chandigarh in a seminar organised by the Chandigarh CFA Association on Monday.

The seminar was based on the most discussed topic these days, "World Financial Crisis: Is the worst over". Anil Katia (CFA), State Head, HDFC Bank Ltd and Satindra Singh Ahluwalia, a faculty member of ICFAI Business School, Chandigarh, shared their views on the subject.

Ahluwalia explained how the ripple effect of the American credit crunch is being felt by most of the countries of the world because of their inter-dependent economic ties and financial involvement.

"Countries like UK, Russia, Japan, and Germany have suffered huge losses because of the massive amount of money coming from America," said Ahluwalia.

He added: "There is a group of countries that have experienced what can be called the 'participatory impact', while another group of nations is experiencing what can be called the 'ripple effect'. India is mainly affected by the ripple effect despite direct exposure by companies like the Tata AIG and ICICI Bank."

Heading: HC summons state Food dept secy for delaying selection of four district forum presidents - Indian Express
Content:
The word 'bunk' rings in so many emotions. Feelings of happiness, enjoyment and most of all, the thrill associated with it. Bunking classes is one of the most loved activities of college students. I wonder if there is any student who has not missed classes at least once during his college days.

The sheer pleasure of bunking a lecture when other students are busy listening to the teacher is an experience in itself.

The fear of getting caught by a faculty member, which lurks somewhere in the mind, adds to the excitement.

Bunking not only helps students escape a boring lecture, but it also helps them bond with friends over endless cups of tea and coffee.

Canteen, the favourite haunt of students like me, offers a good refuge from torturous academic sessions. Not a harmful habit, if I may say so, but missing classes is just an excuse for us to enjoy what I believe is the golden period of a youngsters' life. For those lecturers who view bunking with a scorn, I want to tell them that if they see students sitting in the canteen or under that Banyan tree outside the department, they should not think that the students are indulging in just idle talk.

Students are so much aware these days that I have seen and experienced heated debates on the 123 Agreement, the Singur issue etc. We do 'utilise' our time even while not attending classes.

Come winter and there will be numerous sights of students sitting in the sun, enjoying themselves with cups of tea and peanuts, their staple diet during the season. Blame it on the season, but winter acts as a catalyst for even the 'non-regular bunkers' to sacrifice classes and bask in the sun.

Summing up, I feel that the days of graduating from school to college would had been dull and unexciting had there not been the concept of 'bunking classes'.

Heading: Punjab, PCA get HC notices for waiving entertainment duty - Indian Express
Content:
THe Punjab and Haryana High Court has asked the secretary of the state Food and Supplies department to appear in the court regarding the appointment of presidents of four district forums.

The directions have been passed in the wake of a PIL filed by Advocate H C Arora. The petitioner has sought directions from the Punjab Government to clear appointments for the post of presidents.

Though the recommendations for appointment of these candidates were made by the Selection Committee on May 15, 2008, these were hanging fire in the Consumer Affairs Department.

In a startling development, the Department of Consumer Affairs and Food & Supplies Department has conveyed it to the president of the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission that the state government cannot make appointments of these candidates, which were recommended by the Statutory Selection Committee.

The Statutory Selection Committee comprised Justice S N Aggarwal (retired) as its chairman, who is also the president of the State Commission; R PS Pawar, secretary of the Food & Supplies and Consumer Affairs Department, and Rekha Mittal (Legal Remebrancer) as member.

The secretary has objected to the appointments as there were certain complaints against them in the past. Some of them were also pending in the High Court.

The petitioner brought this development to the notice of the court. The petitioner also produced the copy of the proceedings of the Selection Committee (obtained by him under RTI Act), which revealed that the objections raised by Pawar, Secretary, Food & Supplies, were duly explained to him by the chairman and the other member.

Ultimately, of the 24 candidates, all retired district judges, on the basis of marks allotted to the candidates by the members of the Selection Committee, four persons were recommended on the basis of merit.

Taking a serious note of the stand (now taken by the secretary of the Food department), the court observed that the attitude of the department is dissatisfactory.

"The state government should not interfere in the recommendations made by the Selection Committee, unless there is something very drastic against a particular candidate," the High Court observed.

Heading: Illegal mining still on in Panchkula: CJM report - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has issued notices to the Punjab Cricket Association (PCA), Mohali, and the Punjab government on a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by Sarabjit Singh Kahlon, a resident of Ludhiana.

The petitioner has challenged the exemption granted by the Punjab government to the PCA for the payment of entertain duty on the sale of tickets for cricket matches organised between April 1, 1995, and December 2005.

The petitioner had stated that an entertainment duty on the sale of tickets at the PCA Stadium since April 1,1995, comes out to be a whopping Rs 3.02 crore. But the state Cabinet waived off the duty against stiff objection from the Finance ministry and the adverse legal opinion given by the then Legal Remebrancer.

The Legal Rememberancer had, in a note dated May 30, 2005, categorically stated that the exemption orders cannot be issued by the state government with retrospective effect and that it can be issued only with prospective effect.

He had also opined that if the Administrative department considers that issuance of an exemption order with retrospective effect is necessary in public interest and it is not likely to be challenged in a court of law, then the department may issue the same, but if such an order is challenged in the court of law, then it would be for the administrative department to defend the same. The Cabinet, however, went ahead with proposal to waive the entertainment duty payable by the PCA.

The petitioner submitted in the PIL that the Punjab government had no jurisdiction or even justification to waive off the entertainment duty payable by a commercial organisation like PCA, as the tax-payers' money should not be wasted on dolling out relief to commercial organisations, and that too with a retrospective effect, when the law does not permit it.

The petitioner has also asked the court that the state government should be directed to recover the entertain duty, with further interest and penalty from the PCA.

Heading: SC reinstates Chahal’s relief - Indian Express
Content:
The Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) of Panchkula today, in an interim report submitted to the Punjab and Haryana High Court, stated that illegal mining is still on in Panchkula without any check.

Taking strong note of the allegations of illegal mining, the High Court has directed the mining officer to appear before the court on the next date of hearing. The CJM has also been directed to submit the final report in this regard.

It might be recalled that taking strong note of the illegal mining continuing in Panchkula, the High Court had appointed a local commissioner to look into the matter.

The directions were passed in the wake of a petition filed by Advocate Vijay Bansal and two others residents of Panchkula. The petitioners had submitted that the former Chief Minister Om Parkash Chautala in September 2004 had made a statement with regard to the alleged illegal mining going in the adjoining areas of Panchkula.

Chautala had also pointed out to one of his senior party leaders without naming him involved in illegal mining.

The petitioners had demanded that since Chautala had not named any senior party leader, a

CBI inquiry shall be conducted into the illegal mining and the guilty shall be booked.

They have also alleged that those involved in the illegal mining have political patronage as a result of which they are yet to be caught.

Taking note of the accusations, a division bench of the High Court had directed the CJM, Panchkula to get an inquiry conducted.

Heading: Shraadh ‘outbids’ transport dept as car numbers’ auction draws cold response - Indian Express
Content:
In a major sigh of reprieve for ex-media advisor B I S Chahal to former Punjab CM Amarinder Singh, the Supreme Court has stayed the operation of the order passed by the Punjab and Haryana High Court on September 10.

Through the order, the High Court had recalled the interim relief given to Chahal wherein the Punjab government had been directed to issue three days notice before arresting Chahal in any fresh case. However, this order was later withdrawn by the High Court. Chahal moved the Supreme Court, which today issued notices to the Punjab govt and reinstated the relief given to Chahal.

Chahal had alleged that he might well yet again be made a victim of political vendetta for his close association with Captain Amarinder Singh.

Heading: Tortured for her brother’s ‘sin’, woman attempts suicide - Indian Express
Content:
Owing to the poor response received during Shraadh, the Registering and Licensing Authority (RLA) fetched an unimpressive total of Rs 9.86 lakh as against the Rs 26.91 lakh fetched during the auction in June.

The VIP registration number CH-04-F-0001 went for Rs 2.11 lakh to Satish Kumar Saini, a resident of Sector 32-D. Interestingly, the registration number CH-04-E-0001 had fetched an impressive Rs. 5.15 lakh in June earlier this year when a local businessman Kanwar Deep Singh had purchased the number for his Bentley.

The RLA officials credited the poor response received by the auction to the ongoing Shraadh. "With the period considered inauspicious for purchasing new things, particularly vehicles, many people did not partcipate in the auction. The next auction, expected after about four months, would attract a better response," added a senior RLA official.

The registration number '0108' was auctioned at a paltry sum of Rs 5,300 while number '0009' was taken for Rs. 1.5 lakh.

The registration number '0002' and '0005' were auctioned at Rs 30,000 each; while '0003', '0007' and '0010' were auctioned at Rs 16,000 each. Registration numbers '0004' and '0008' were auctioned at Rs 15,000. The registration number '0006' was not bid upon in the auction, as there was only one taker for the same, who bagged the registration number at the reserve price of Rs 15,000.

Interestingly, in the last auction in June, the registration number '0003' fetched Rs 2.65 lakh, while the registration number '0004' was also auctioned at Rs 2.25 lakh. In all, the RLA received 162 applications from vehicle-owners, who expressed their interest to book registration numbers of their choice, by paying the requisite reserved price.

Heading: Nokia to replace cellphone for deficiency in service - Indian Express
Content:
"They would again kidnap and rape me". It was this level of paranoia that prompted Suman, the 28-year-old resident of village Pasena Khurd, Panipat, to attempt suicide outside the Haryana Police headquarters, Sector 6, Panchkula, on Saturday.

"My brother Nitesh Kumar was booked on charges of kidnapping a minor, but despite the local court acquitting him in the case, the family members of the minor girl wanted to take revenge," said Suman after being discharged from the General Hospital, Sector 6.

She added, "It was on May 31 that my father Chain Singh was brutally murdered by a group of 11 persons of the girl's family in front of my eyes. But the police declared it as a case of suicide."

She alleged that being the only eyewitness in the murder of her father, three men of the same group kidnapped her on April 8 and then gangraped her.

Suman added that while an FIR was lodged in the gangrape case against Roshan, Brijpal and Balbir Singh of the area, no significant action was taken in the case till date.

"I visited the DGP office three times and every time I was assured that I would be given justice, but then nothing happened. The threats from the other party continued and it was then on September 21 that they picked up my brother and murdered him on September 23," added Suman.

For Suman, the worst came on the night of September 26 when she was again followed by some men from the same gang.

"I had gone to the market to buy vegetables around 8 pm, when I saw two men of the same gang stalking me. They wanted me to withdraw the case of my father's murder," said Suman.

She recalled, "Without any second thought, I boarded the bus to Panchkula. I reached here late in the night and stayed with my relatives. As I was fed up of the entire system, I went to Zirakpur in the morning and consumed some unknown medicines at one of the chemist shops."

After consuming the medicines, Suman reached the DGP office in Sector 6, Panchkula, where the officials asked her to come on Monday.

"I had no place to go. They told me to sit at the park outside the office till Monday if I had no other place to go. It was then that my condition deteriorated and I was rushed to the hospital," said Suman.

The IG, Ambala range KK Sindhu visited the hospital on Monday and assured Suman that stern action will be taken against all the accused in the case.

Suman was later discharged from the hospital after which she left for her village with her husband Kaka.

Talking on the developments in the gangrape case, the spokesperson of police headquarters, meanwhile, said, "As there were insufficient evidences to prove that she was raped, the case was dismissed. Also, the DNA report for the same did not confirm rape."

Ques:What she went through

May 31: Father of Suman allegedly killed

April 8: Suman kidnapped and gangraped

September 21: Brother Nitesh kidnapped

September 23: Body of Nitesh found near the village drain

Heading: ICICI Lombard to pay up Rs 50,000 for misleading forum - Indian Express
Content:
The Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed Nokia to repair the handset of a complainant without charging anything towards repair or replacement of its component. The forum also said that if the set is found to be non-repairable, the complainant shall be given a brand new cellphone of the same model and configuration free of cost.

Devinder Kumar Sharma had purchased a Nokia 5300 handset for Rs 7150 on July 20, 2007. It was alleged that within 20 days of its purchase, the handset developed problems in its normal functioning. It was given to the company for repair and was to be collected after some days.

It was averred that the handset was returned after an inordinate delay of 25 days. A few months later, when it again developed the same problems, the company refused to replace the handset.

In its reply, Nokia pleaded that when the handset was brought to them, they repaired the same and handed it over to the complainant. After the set was repaired, he never visited their office for his alleged complaint. The forum held that as the defect was recurring, proper service should have been provided to the complainant.

Heading: Mullanpur masterplan published, suggestions sought from public - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed ICICI Lombard General Insurance to pay Rs 50,000 as punitive damages for producing a false document to mislead the forum. The company has also been directed to pay Rs 40,074 as the insurance claim.

The complainant, Vinod Kumar, had got his Tavera car insured with the company in 2007. After the vehicle was badly damaged in an accident and sent to a workshop in Industrial Area, the insurance company was also informed. The estimate for repairs, including denting and painting, came out to be Rs 60,000 to Rs 70,000.

The complainant alleged that despite repeated requests, the company did not pay the amount (Rs 65,312) to Motorways garage where the vehicle was repaired. Finally, Kumar made the payment himself.

In its reply, ICICI pleaded that the car was insured as a private vehicle but was being plied as a commercial vehicle. The company said upon intimation of the claim, a surveyor was duly deputed for assessing the loss which was fixed at Rs 40,074. But as discrepancies were pointed out by the surveyor in ascertaining the exact loss, the company got the matter investigated by a licensed investigator. The detective found that the vehicle in question was being used as a taxi at the time of accident. Only then, was the complainant's claim repudiated.

The forum, however, found that the opinion that the vehicle was being used for commercial purposes was based on a statement allegedly given by the complainant himself. Kumar admitted that the investigator had recorded his statement as to how the accident occurred but contended that the first six lines and the last two lines were subsequently added.

In a copy of the statement, the forum also observed that there was an inordinately huge distance between the fifth and sixth line, as compared to the rest of the report. "The line which states that the complainant drives the vehicle as a taxi has been crowded into a small space and the font is also very small. Similarly, the distance in the last two lines is quite small showing that the writer tried to adjust them above the complainant's signatures. And these are the only lines in the report that state the vehicle was being used as a taxi," the forum found.

"We are, therefore, of the opinion that if the disputed lines are ignored, there is no evidence to suggest the vehicle was being used as a taxi. The company has tried to introduce false facts by tampering with the document, which was filed before this forum to be considered as evidence," opined the forum

Heading: ‘As time goes by, Corbusier’s works appear more meaningful & ageless’ - Indian Express
Content:
The department of Town and Country Planning, Punjab, on Monday published the much-awaited masterplan of Mullanpur Local Planning Area, which has envisaged developing 6,109 hectares spread across 33 villages in the Chandigarh periphery, as Punjab's first "eco-town".

For inviting objections in writing from general public, the copy of masterplan and existing land use plan was displayed at the offices of Chief Administrator, Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA), and Deputy Commissioner in Mohali besides Chief Town Planner (CTP) of Punjab.

The objections can be sent to the CTP within 30 days, after which the state government will examine and consider the appropriate objections before formally notifying the masterplan for its implementation.

The experts from the Jurong Consultants Private Limited of Singapore, in the masterplan submitted to the Punjab government, have proposed Mullanpur as low density, country living, resort centre and northern gateway to Greater Mohali.

The masterplan presents opportunity for a well-managed "eco-town" environment with a variety of new and exciting developments to encourage diversified growth in tourism that balances economic growth with environmental, cultural and community values.

Heading: Hundreds of trees face the axe on NH-21 - Indian Express
Content:
Following each new chapter in the history of architecture, a few architects endure for posterity as the ones who created the epoch. As the spirit of era changes, they lose their topicality and as time goes by, the majority is only of historical interest.

Every now and then, however, there are some who prove to have created something that goes beyond what is characteristic of the period, something that continues to have something to say to us in spite of the march of time.

Since the advent of modern architecture, in the early twentieth century, Le Corbusier has been considered one of its founding fathers, and today he must be regarded as the one who endures as this century's greatest architect. What is fascinating about Le Corbusier is that, as time goes by his works appear more meaningful and ageless.

He was a keen observer of life and events — present and past — that influenced his inquisitive mind. Le Corbusier's creative endeavours emanated from a passionately attentive painstaking study of the world, including contemporary reality, the heritage of tradition and laws of nature.

Le Corbusier was not unaware of his place in history. By self training, he was an environmentalist, painter, sculptor architect, planner, poet, philosopher and writer.

Even though he influenced the world-thought on contemporary planning and architecture, he had to face many setbacks in his early years. Even during the most disappointing period of life, he relied on his convictions and wrote in 1934 : "The defeats of the past three years represent as many victories. Public opinion, when aroused, will force the same officials to change their attitudes."

His predictions came true and all his sketches and drawn proposals are today published and held in high esteem.

Corbusier made his statements in diverse materials - distinctively his own — nnovative, dynamic and having timeless quality. However, hard we may try, it is difficult not to be inspired or influenced by the works of great masters.

Le Corbusier was way ahead of his time and yet with his feet firmly rooted in the past culture. He learnt from history and, in turn, made architectural history rich and inspiring.

The Legislative Assembly is one of the best examples.

Space, light and volume serve as the basic elements in Le Corbusier's creations. He remains a great sculptor in his paintings as well as architecture. He did not work for financial gains. His efforts are borne out of belief in objective beauty and not out of any political or religious convictions.

Le Corbusier's philosophy and ideals are becoming increasingly valid and have stood the test of time. Corbusier is revered much more after his death and his views are backed by world bodies and professionals alike. Architects around the world hold in great reverence everything Le Corbusier had said or done, almost like any prophet.

Speaking purely in the context of Chandigarh - with the passage of time-we have lost our bearings and are struggling to keep pace with the changing conditions.

Hypothetically speaking if Corbusier came alive or was resurrected, there would be much greater appreciation of his works and ideals in India also. His very presence would have removed most misunderstandings. Also, his voice would carry the backing of great minds and world bodies like the UNESCO. Le Corbusier, however great, can only be relevant in today's context if we make his ideas work and make suitable changes as he would have himself done. This could truly be the golden era in Chandigarh's history and perhaps, the most meaningful homage to Le Corbusier.

Heading: Courtesy inflation, Mohali civic body hikes cremation charges to Rs 600 - Indian Express
Content:
Hundreds of trees along the Mohali-Kharar stretch of National Highway-21 are being axed these days to pave way for the much-awaited four-laning of the highway stretch, ill-famed as the "killer highway".

The large scale deforestation was being carried out by the Punjab State Forest Development Corporation under the project to four-lane NH-21 from Desumajra to Ludhiana T-point and Kurali to Kiratpur Sahib, confirmed Ropar Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) Amit Mishra.

He said the felling of almost 200-250 trees was permitted under the four-laning project after completing the formalities and receipt of requisite charges.

The DFO disclosed that the concerned department has also deposited the requisite money for double plantation to compensate the loss of trees. "Almost 4 hectares of land, along the highway, owned by PWD and maintained by the Forest Department has been diverted to undertake the four-laning," added Mishra.

Tracing the idea behind four-laning

In May 2007, the Union Minister for Shipping, Road Transport and National Highways T R Baalu had permitted the Punjab government to execute construction work on the four-laning of the 17-km stretch from Desumajra to Kurali via Kharar township at an estimated cost of Rs15 crore.

The funds for the project would be provided by the Union Ministry for Road Transport and Highways, Baalu had announced at a high-level meeting with Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal in New Delhi.

Pained over the loss of several precious lives in fatal mishaps on the "killer stretch", Badal had become instrumental in fulfilling the long-pending demand of area residents.

The development assumes significance in view of increasing volume of traffic on the NH-21 stretch, which is a vital link between Chandigarh and most parts of Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, J&K.

While the 3 km stretch on NH-21 between Desumajra and Mohali bridge had been four-laned sometime back, the remaining 4-km stretch in Kharar was not four-laned and instead, a bypass was mooted to divert the long-route traffic from Desumajra to Khanpur. With the bypass project costing over Rs 30 crore, the project was shelved after former Kharar MLA Bir Devinder Singh had objected to the acquisition of land required for the project.

Ques: Why the 'killer stretch'?

Data reveals that the stretch of NH-21 between SAS Nagar and Kharar bridges claims a life every alternate day with a major accident reported everyday on an average.

This highway lacks dividers, indicators, lights, speed breakers and road symbols. Accident-prone points have been identified as Daon, Desumajra, Mundi Kharar, Bansan Wali Chungi chowk, Quila Chungi chowk and Khanpur T-point.

Officials say the highway was constructed in 1940 with a speed limit of 60-kmph. Traffic volume has increased manifold over the past 66 years, say officials adding that the width of the road has remained the same.

Heading: Uproar in House over delay in clearing encroachments - Indian Express
Content:
With inflation spiralling northwards, even cremation in Mohali will become costlier.

At its General House meeting, chaired by its president Rajinder Singh Rana, Mohali Municipal Council (MC) hiked the charges of wood procured to cremate bodies at the local cremation ground from the existing Rs 320 to Rs 600.

Taking up the agenda item moved by the MC engineering wing, the MC House, however, turned down the proposal to increase the charges to Rs 1,200 at par with Chandigarh. The civic body, however, resolved to charge Rs 600 for the wood supplied for cremation of a single body, MC Executive Officer (EO) Amana Kumar Goel told Newsline.

The MC House also approved the estimates amounting to almost Rs 5.65 crore pertaining to development works, including construction and repair of roads, streets, pavements, water supply and sanitation works in different parts of the city.

On the plea of the striking MC employees, a table item was moved and approved to recommend the cancellation of FIR against the stray animal catching employees of the MC, who were charged with causing death of a stray bull in Phase VIII on September 17.

Heading: Security stepped up in Ambala after threatening letter and e-mail - Indian Express
Content:
Municipal Councillor Kuljit Singh Bedi questioned MC Estate Officer on the progress of work to remove rehris and temporary encroachments in the city, which the latter had promised to remove within 15 days during the last MC meeting in August. As the EO reasoned that the work could not be accomplished due to the MC employees' strike, Bedi, supported by a majority of the councillors, both from the opposition and ruling groups, accused an MC clerk of "accepting bribe" to promote encroachments.

There was pandemonium all around following which the EO assured to shift the said MC clerk, for which he had earlier asked the MC House to adopt a resolution, which Bedi strongly opposed on "technical" grounds. "If a transfer of an MC clerk requires the MC resolution, you undertake that no transfers will be done in future without our recommendation," Bedi told the EO who finally budged when a majority of the councillors threatened to boycott the meeting on the issue.

Heading: Jaffar’s ton steers Indian Oil into final - Indian Express
Content:
Under the red alert being sounded in the district, sensitive parts of the city including public places like railway station, air force station, general bus stands, the Indian Oil Company terminus, Military Hospital and other vital points of the city are under tight security cover in the wake of threatening letters and e-mail received here.

These letters and e-mails had warned of a blast in the railway station and Air Force Station on September 29.

According to sources, the time limit has been extended to October 2, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.

The Administration, under orders from the state government, is leaving no stone unturned and every place mentioned in the threatening letters have been brought under tight security.

Earlier, these places were being manned by the police, GRP, RPF and other security personnel.

Now, additional forces comprising of commandos, Haryana Armed Police and Central Railway Forces have been deployed at these places.

Round-the-clock vigilance has been ordered to protect the places under threat.

Although the railway station was already provided with CCTVs, metal detectors on entry gates and more equipments have been installed at each platform.

According to a railway official: "Metal detectors have been installed at all entry points."

He added, "The CCTVs, some of which were not in working condition, have been repaired now and are in working condition. Every person entering the platforms now has to go through the metal detector."

Bomb-diffusing squads with sniffer dogs have also been on search duty and every incoming and outgoing train is being scanned on arrival at the Ambala Cantonment railway station.

But despite the high alert, anti-social elements seem to be active as incidents of looting, snatching and pick-pocketing are still occurring in different parts of the city.

Crime on the rise in Ambala

Rs 1.5 lakh was stolen from a paddy grower at the

Ambala Cantonment general bus stand on Monday. The victim identified as Mohinder Kumar was returning after selling his crop at the Ladwa grain market and was waiting to board a bus to his village, Raipur Rani, when he fell victim to pickpockets. In another incident, a petrol pump owner was reportedly robbed of Rs 2.73 lakh in the past 3 days. Also, a woman was robbed of cash in a garment shop on the busy Sadar Bazaar by allegedly putting chilli powder in her eyes. — ENS

Heading: Eight foreign teams for A K Misra C’ship - Indian Express
Content:
Bolstered by a brilliant ton by Wasim Jaffer (108 runs off 120 balls), Indian Oil defeated defending champions MRF Chennai by 46 runs to enter the final of J P Atray Memorial Cricket Tournament being held at Sector 16 Cricket Stadium on Monday.

MRF Chennai won the toss and invited Indian Oil to bat first. After losing two quick wickets, Test player Wasim Jaffer came to bat and enthralled the audience with some scintillating strokes. His century included eight fours and one towering six. Ravikant Shukla (68 off 96 balls) gave able support to Jaffer and the duo took Indian Oil to safety. Jaffer was dropped on 64 when Mahesh failed to hold onto a catch at mid-wicket off the bowling of Venu Gopal. With some contributions from the lower order, Indian Oil made 279 runs for the loss of nine wickets in 50 overs. Rahul Shukla grabbed three wickets while N Mohammad claimed two wickets.

Chasing the target, MRF started on a bad note as they lost three quick wickets for just 28 runs. Skipper Venugopal Rao tried to increase the run-rate and hit a flurry of strokes in his innings of 88 runs off 72 balls that included eight boundaries and five towering sixes.

U Shushil tried to build a decent partnership with the tailenders but his effort was brought to an end by Gaurav Jathar who had him caught by A Rahene for a well compiled 41 runs of 51 balls. MRF fell short by 46 runs. Gaurav Jathan (3 for 51) and R Raje (2 for 29) were the main wicket taker for Indian Oil.

Brief Scores:

Indian Oil: 279 for 6 in 50 overs (W Jaffar 108, R. Shukla 68, Aditya Tare 29 no, Rahul Shukla 3 for 54, Niyas Mohammad 2 for 51); beats MRF: 233 all out in 44.2 overs (V Gopal Rao 88, U Shushil 41, Gnaneshwar Rao 27, G Jathar 3 for 51, Rohan Raje 2 for 29).

CCA-Chandigarh to honour players

The Chandigarh Cricket Association (CCA) affiliated to Punjab Cricket Association will honour the Chandigarh men's team and women's Under-19 team who were declared joint winners in the recently held Katoch Shield and Under-19 district tournament on October 4.

Heading: Anjali rallies to beat Nikita - Indian Express
Content:
Amateur Boxing Association has decided to organise the 16th A K Misra Championship as an international meet from February 11 to 15, 2009 in the General Council Meeting (GMC) held in PML SD Public School, Sector 32 on Sunday.

The A K Misra championship was previously played at all India level with participation of national and international boxers from India. Boxers from Mauritius and Nepal had earlier participated in the event three times. In the GMC, it was decided that 16 teams will be invited out of which eight should be foreign. The teams will be selected on the basis of results of the last senior Nationals and one host team from Chandigarh will also be selected. Olympian Vijender, Akhil and Jatinder will also be invited for the event.

Heading: Deepak shines for Little Flower - Indian Express
Content:
Talented Anjali rallied to outplay Nikita by 5-7, 7-6, 6-2 in the girls Under-14 singles first-round match of the AITA Championship Series Tennis Tournament at the Sector 10 Tennis Stadium here today.

In another hard fought encounter Samriti defeated Shivya 7-6, 7-5. Bhavtaranpreet Singh was given a good fight by M. Sai Nikhil before winning by 6-3, 4-6, 6-2 in the boys under-14 singles match. Mandeep Kumar rallied to prevail over Sean Yip 1-6, 6-0, 6-3 in another first round encounter. Fatehdeep Singh ended the challenge of Ishaque Eqbal 6-0, 6-0. Nishchay Rawal also had a smooth railing against Ranjot whom he beat by 6-0, 6-1.

Results:

Boys under-14 singles (Ist round): Nishchay Rawal bt Ranjot 6-0, 6-1,Fatehdeep Singh bt Ishaque Eqbal 6-0, 6-0, S.K. Girls under-14 singles (Ist round): Samriti bt Shivya 7-6, 7-5, Ashwini bt Arshpreet 6-1, 6-1, Anjali bt Nikita 5-7, 7-6, 6-2.

Heading: Cycle Polo C’hip from today - Indian Express
Content: Deepak Kathait's blazing knock of 53 runs enabled Little Flower Convent School, Panchkula to register 8-wicket win over Moti Ram School, Panchkula in the ongoing U-16 inter-school district cricket tournament.  Batting first, Moti Ram School compiled paltry 93 runs losing all wickets. In reply, Little Flower Convent achieved the target in just 7 overs.

Heading: Creative call - Indian Express
Content: Punjab Cycle Polo Association will organise the 29th Junior National Cycle Polo Championship for boys and girls from September 30 to October 5 at the Polo Ground in Patiala.

Heading: Full spin - Indian Express
Content:
These women are discovering a brand-new dimension to their work and their self

Her mode of self-expression shines bright. With basic tools, and on her kitchen table, Namita Sharma finds inspiration from life's minutest details and casts them in silver. Her creations, like fingerprints, can't be replicated and so her studio which was launched last month is called Fingerprints. The jewellery designer has a varied work experience, having taught jewellery design in institutes, executing extensive projects for leading companies, designing for jewellery houses, travelling extensively for research till she decided to unleash her creative instincts at home, at her own pace, as per her mood. The freedom to fashion what's in her head and heart makes up for the jitters of not getting a secure pay-check on the first of every month. "You're your own chief and what you do is aesthetic and superlative, for there are not any conciliations to carry,'' Namita does everything from scratch. And it's this exclusive self-dependency that makes the process so precious and self-liberating and her pieces original, with attractive use of precious and semi-precious stones. "Silver is such a versatile metal to work with and I prefer enhancing it with colour. Working with my bare hands and without any pressure is pure joy. This is my inner calling,'' Namita looks for more ideas around her.

The energies in the city are just right for attempts that are not superficial, but have a soul, philosophizes Kanchan Raina, a product and textile designer, whose heart is set on reviving traditional crafts. Kanchan has launched her own design pad recently and apart from designing cards, logos, custom-made things for people and companies according to their personality, she's working on ways to help craftspersons earn a living. Giving up a full-time job, agrees Kanchan, made her a wee bit nervous initially, "But now Do, my studio seems to be just perfect,'' Raina believes in work that's simple, which does not defy aesthetics and creativity. When effort becomes a pain, she believes, it should be stopped and in her case, this was just the perfect time to follow her instincts. "Do gives me time to work on craft revival, make it functional by teaching craftspersons finishing techniques and how to sell their products and in the process, I feel complete.''

Back to the basics, Paramjeet at her design den, strives to create eco-friendly products like pin-boards, pots, lamps, earthy decoratives that not only appeal to the outside world, but her first. "That's the beauty of being your own boss,'' the lady who runs Manthan Creations gave up her job to follow her heart. Paramjeet conceptualizes each of the designs herself and take weeks to give it the feel and finish she has in her head, and as there's no pressure of following ideas and time frame of someone, it all translates into a labour of love.

Exactly why Sonia Singh has taken a break from her strenuous job as a graphic designer and is now working on launching a website for children, "one that will give them a chance to explore and have fun and me, the freedom to improvise and time to think what I want from life."

Heading: Jump cut - Indian Express
Content: When Bollywood actor Lara Dutta launched Samsung's latest mobile phone Omnia, she obliged the shutter bugs with a graceful smile. Dressed in a creamy coloured top, but was hardly as charitable to the assembled media persons. "She was here only to launch the phone. Since she is not the brand ambassador, it would not be appropriate for her to comment on the phone," a Samsung spokesperson offered by way of explanation. With five releases lined up in the first half of next year, the actor though is quite in the thick of things otherwise. She has just completed the shooting schedule for Anthony D'Souza's action flick, Blue, and is now dubbing for Priyadarshan's Billo Barber. After that, the last shooting schedule for David Dhawan's Do Not Disturb will also commence. Hopefully then there will be lots to talk about for Ms Dutta.

Heading: Bride side - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Fashion Week announces the designers for its maiden edition

It seems Delhi is gearing up for an active fashion season this October. Jostling beside the customary Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week Spring-Summer by the Fashion Design Council of India (FDCI) will be the newly floated Delhi Fashion Week (DFW), backed by Sumeet Nair, former executive director of the FDCI, who set up the Fashion Foundation of India.

As he hosted a packed lunch at Ai, the Japanese restaurant at MGF Metropolitan mall, Saket, Nair, looking dapper in a chic pink shirt, announced the names of the designers at the DFW. "Going by Paris, Milan and New York standards, fashion weeks pack in a lot of events, solo shows and studio shows. Our endeavour promises more options to buyers and benefits designers as well. It wouldn't create any confusion," said Nair, who confirmed the presence of 33 designers and 35 buyers for the Week.

From the look of it, DFW promises some big moments for fledgling designers. There are six debutant designers. Delhi-based designer Rajvi Mohan, known for her exclusive menswear, will be presenting a grunge collection for the first time on the ramp. Mohan, 27, will send down a pack in long, dapper jackets with kurtas in a muted palette. "The collection is inspired by the rag-pack gang of the 1940s and '50s endorsed by personalities such as Frank Sinatra, Dean Martin and Sammy Davis Jr," said Mohan, who has worked for British designer Vivienne Westwood.

There is also Smita Singh Rathore, owner of Celldsgn store at Hauz Khas, who will be launching her label 11.11. The alumna of the prestigious Domus Academy in Milan promises "a real masculine look to womenswear with cheery voluminous skirts and drape jackets".

Greco-Lebanese Alecca Carrano, who has been working out of Delhi for the past two years, too has finally managed to put herself on the Indian fashion map. "I was trying to participate for the last couple of years but couldn't because FDCI only allows designers of Indian nationality. I have a stall this time and will showcase a very feminine collection for mature women," smiles Carrano, who is heading for the Dubai fashion week next. Besides the punk vibes, Vineet Bahl, showcasing for the first time in Delhi, will crank out a cocktail collection aptly called Mojito. Watch out for a heady cocktail.

Heading: Fabindia goes to Patiala - Indian Express
Content: They are a girl's best friend and if you ladies are planning on making some new friends, step in at Sant Ram Mangat Ram Jain Jewellers (SRMRJJ) in Sector 17 that's rolled out a 'Volcanic Wedding Collection' exhibition'. The five-day exhibition (September 30 to October 4) showcases over 250 jewellery pieces designed especially for the coming wedding season by SRMRJJ. The exhibition includes sets, bangles, bracelets, pendant sets, chandelier earrings, cocktail rings with prices ranging from Rs 50,000 to Rs 25,00,000. A unique feature of this exhibition is that it's a "talking exhibition" where every piece pronounces its complete details like cut, colour, clarity, weight, hours of production, metal used and the cost. Another attraction of the show is the exquisite Christie's Copy. One of the rare masterpieces, the lovely piece is adorned with pure white diamonds of very high clarity and F colour, accompanied with golden marquise cut diamonds and boasts of a man hour production time of over 625 hours. Says Samir Jain, Director, SRMRJJ, "The Volcanic Wedding Collection Exhibition is a one of its kind event in the city. The collection has been specially designed with different pieces coming from different parts of the country. We have handpicked and included individual specialities of various states in the collection. The designs are especially suited to the sensibilities of the modern bride."

Heading: Filth on campus: V-C pulls up PAU bigwigs - Indian Express
Content: They are spreading wings. Fabindia, the retail handloom chain, has launched its exclusive store in Patiala. Tucked away in the New Leela Bhavan market, on offer is a product range comprising of a vast collection of fine textile merchandise in clothing, accessories, home linen, home furnishings and floor coverings. On the occasion of the store launch, a Fabindia official remarked, "Keeping in mind an increased demand for hand crafted handloom products in the region, Patiala is an ideal destination for us. The brand caters to the ever-changing lifestyle trends of its customers through its exclusive product categories and is sure to catch the attention of fashion conscious people of Patiala.

Heading: Sexual abuse: College of Home Sciences Dean to conduct probe - Indian Express
Content:
Shows film to deans,directors on problems plaguing university

The Deans and the Directors of Punjab Agricultural University were taken by surprise today.

Irked with the filth on the campus, V-C Dr MS Kang used a novel way to make the university dons cudgel their brains.

At a meeting held this afternoon, the V-C showed a film to the university authorities on the problems plaguing the university. At the end of the show the message from the top was clear — act now!

Dr Kang had shot scenes of garbage strewn at various places across the campus including the Botanical Garden. Dr V K Sehgal, chief engineer-cum-estate officer, PAU, said, "See the clippings. We will shortly formulate a policy on how to handle garbage on the campus."

Disposing of garbage is a major problem in the university as the institute does not permit the burning of garbage. Though a huge area had been earmarked on the campus for converting garbage into manure, the practice is rarely followed.

Dr Kang also showed clippings on the conditions prevailing in the labs and research fields in the university. Dr P S Minhas, Director Research, PAU, denies that labs are being neglected. "Our research fields and labs are very meticulous as we handle a lot of work. We cannot afford to neglect them."

Confirming that the film was screened, Dr Minhas said, "All this was primarily about cleanliness of the campus. Garbage was the major issue taken up at the meeting. Our farms and all were not a part of the film."

Heading: One tiffin box, 30 mins of paranoia - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Agricultural University Vice-Chancellor Dr Manjit Singh Kang has asked Dean College of Home Science Dr Neelam Grewal to conduct an inquiry into the alleged sexual harassment case. He has sought the report on the matter at the earliest.

Though Dr Kang could not be contacted, Dr Grewal confirmed the development but refused to divulge the details.

A woman employee of the university had levelled charges of sexual harassment against Dr Dulcha Singh Brar, Director Students Welfare. Though the matter became public last month, till date no formal inquiry has been initiated on the grounds that the university was preparing a new sexual harassment policy.

It has been learnt that when Dr R K Mahey, Registrar, PAU, brought it to the notice of the V-C that the university had standing committee on such issues, Dr Kang decided to stick to the old draft.

Dr Kang had explained, "We had compared the new and the old draft and found that both the policies were almost similar. Thus, for now we have decided to stick to the old draft as the new draft will first have to be approved by the PAU Board of Management before it can be implemented."

Meanwhile, Dr Brar maintained that there is no such issue against him. Dr Brar is considered to be very close to the Badals and was given a state award at the Independence Day function this year.

Heading: Forest dept sends legal notices to 100 businessmen - Indian Express
Content:
Abandoned lunch box creates panic in the city

Panic spread for the second consecutive day today about suspected bombs in the city. While yesterday there was a hoax call that some miscreants were going to blow up a train at the city railway station, an abandoned tiffin box

created terror on the Gill Road today.

Some shopkeepers spotted a tiffin box lying on the road divider on the Gill Road this afternoon. This created panic among the shopkeepers and they informed the police. A police party led by SHO Surinder Mohan from Division Number 2 police station reached the spot. An anti-sabotage team of the police was also summoned to defuse the bomb, if any.

SHO Surinder Mohan said, "When the tiffin box was opened - kheer and other eatables were found." He said that the entire operation took about half an hour.

On Sunday evening too, the police received hoax call that some miscreants were going to blow up a train near Ludhiana. Ludhiana SSP RK Jaiswal along with the police force reached the railway station and thoroughly checked a train which was on way to Banaras from Jammu. Nothing was found on the train.

Meanwhile, Khanna railway station too was inspected on Sunday evening in the view of the coming festive season.

Heading: Dengue on the rise, malaria on the decline - Indian Express
Content:
Acting tough on violators, the Forest department has initiated legal action against more than 100 marriage palace owners, industrial houses, dharam kanda owners, colonisers and showroom owners for encroaching upon the forest land.

These violators have their establishments on the Chandigarh Road, Ferozepur Road, Samrala Road, Jagraon, Riakot and Khanna.

District Forest Officer (DFO) Mahavir Singh said, "Before using the forest land for access purposes, a formal application needs to be filed with the department to get a no-objection certificate. This way the Forest department earns revenue from its land."

DFO adds, "We have written to various departments such as Municipal Corporation, Town Planning, Ludhiana Improvement Trust and Greater Ludhiana Area Development Authority (GLADA) asking them not to give any NoC to colonisers or private building owners till the time the Forest department clears the case."

He added, "Any construction near the forest area gets a green signal after the owner gets an NoC from various departments. But they don't bother to write to the Forest department."

Though the court will soon decide on the penalty to be levied on violators, the forest department has asked residents to refrain from using its land.

On the wrong side of law

Sartaj Palace, 4 Aces Farm, White Rock, Spring Field Resorts, Maharaja Farms, Pearl Plaza, Rhythm, Regency Garden, Harkaran Palace, Karan Palace, HK Computer Dharam Kanda, Sokhi Dhrama Kanda, Kewal Krishan Bricks, Namdhari Private Limited, Ganesh Overseas, Shiva Glass House, Akme Colony, Jindal Agro, GK City Colony, Sunrise Wrought, Noble Steel, Osho Forge, Friends Colony, Ajit Mills, Kalra Industries, Ginni Exports, Gurdeep Timber, Kulwant Timber, Gurbax Timber, Royal Industries.

khanna: Sonia Goyal and Company, MS Dhanpat rai and Dera Baba Mastana.

Heading: Woman, two sons get life term for killing cop - Indian Express
Content:
While the worst damage caused by dengue was reported in the year 2006 when over 1,000 dengue cases were reported from the district alone, this year too, it has been showing an increasing trend with the total number of dengue cases having shot up to nearly 250.

However, on the other hand, the figures for malaria cases in the last four years suggest a declining trend, from 623 in 2004 to 47 in 2008 so far.

District Health Officer Dr S.S. Dhir said that the malaria cases were sharply declining over the years while the dengue has again shown a sharp rise from 28 cases last year to over 200 so far this year.

The number of cases of malaria reported in the district in 2005 were 267 and in 2006 and 2007, the number of cases were pegged at 192 and 75 respectively.

As for dengue cases, the total number of cases in the state has gone up to 405, with the most number of cases - 246 - from Ludhiana, according to the latest data provided by the state unit of Integrated Disease Surveillance Project.

Meanwhile, the flow of patients of dengue in the city hospitals continued as Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH) reported 35 cases, SPS Apollo Hospitals recorded five and Christian Medical College and Hospital (CMCH) and MD Oswal Cancer Hospital recorded one each.

IDSP project coordinator visits city

Project coordinator of Integrated Disease Surveillance Project (ISDP), Dr Deepak Bhatia who visited the city on Monday, said, "We are closely watching the increasing trend of the disease and the daily report is being sent to the Government of India for providing feedback on the same." A health team from Delhi was also expected to arrive in the city on Monday in regard to the current situation, but the visit was cancelled at the last moment.

Schools told to make full-sleeve shirts mandatory for students

Realising the gravity of the situation in the wake of high number of dengue cases pouring in the district at an average of over 20 per day, the district administration held a special programme along with the health department and district education office for some 400 principals and head-teachers of the government schools of the district.

Started with the initiative of Priyank Bharti, additional deputy commissioner, the meeting held was aimed at imparting awareness to the heads of the government schools so that water borne and vector-borne diseases could be checked. The participants at the meeting laid stress on awareness pertaining to dengue.

On the occasion, the District Education Officer Sudesh Bajaj directed all the school principals present on the occasion to make wearing full sleeves compulsory for both teachers and students. Dr Ajit Singh Chawla also spoke on the occasion and apprised the teachers and principals about the precautions and symptoms of the disease.

Heading: Vocational agri course begins at PAU - Indian Express
Content:
Additional session judge A K Mehta has sentenced a woman and her two sons to life imprisonment on the charges of committing the murder of their neighbour Kulwinder Singh, a constable in Punjab Police due to enmity.

The convicted persons are Harbans Kaur, her sons Baldev Singh alias Beda and Satnam Singh of Jhorran village in Raikot tehsil of Ludhiana district. The judge has also ordered them to pay Rs 5,000 each as fine.

"Keeping in view the nature and gravity of the offence committed by the convict, they were sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life," observed A.K. Mehta, Additional Session Judge (ASJ), while pronouncing the verdict.

A case in this regard was registered at Raikot police station, on March 29, 2003, under sections 304, 302, 307, 323, 324, 148 and 149 of the IPC on the basis of the statement of deceased's father Surjit Singh.

The police recorded the statement of Surjit Singh, who alleged that on March 28, 2003 at about 8 p.m., he along with his son, Kulwinder Singh was standing outside their house when Baldev Singh started challenging him.

After some time, he (Baldev) came along with other accused came armed with sharp weapons and sticks and attacked Kulwinder Singh. They were saying that Kulwinder Singh be taught a lesson for getting registered a criminal case against them. Surjit Singh alleged that he tried to save his son but accused also attacked him.

On the other hand, the accused pleaded innocence and claimed false implication, but no defence evidence could be produced by him before the court. Pronouncing the verdict, the court held that the prosecution had successfully proved the guilt of accused and sentenced accordingly.

Heading: Alter lifestyle to curb heart ailment - Indian Express
Content:
A vocational course on agriculture for promoting self-employment among youth began at Kairon Kisan Ghar on Monday. The course was inaugurated by the PAU Associate Director of Extension Education, Dr Kanwal Mahindra, who while speaking on the occasion said that youth should learn to be job creators rather than job seekers. He said that during this one-month course, the PAU experts will have discussions on dairy, poultry, vegetables, horticulture, farm management, floriculture etc. The course coordinator, Dr. T.S. Riar welcomed the experts and participants. Among those present in the inaugural session of the course were Dr V.K. Bhambota, Dr. Jaswinder Bhalla, Rupinder Kaur and Dr Pritpal Kaur Chahal.

Field day on pest management held

A field day on cotton pest management was organised in Fazilka by PAU Department of Entomology in association with Fazilka Farmers Organization of agricultural development. Dr. Manjit Singh Kang, Vice-Chancellor, PAU, was the chief guest on the occasion. Dr. Kang told the participants and mediapersons gathered on the occasion that holistic knowledge about the insect-pest management strategies developed by PAU scientists will help farmers to obtain a high-level of yield and profit. He also inaugurated a farmers service centre at the Grain Market in Fazilka.

Reddy is Rage's brand ambassador

Rage, a premium ladies' brand having their manufacturing unit in Ludhiana, has engaged Sameera Reddy as its brand ambassador for the coming winter season. Rage hopes to march ahead in the world of fashion with a new innovation in yarn and style, said a press release issued by the company.

Heading: Electroplaters hold annual meeting - Indian Express
Content:
Celebrating the World Heart Day, a free heart check-up camp is being organised from September 28 to October 4 at Ludhiana Mediciti Hospital. On the first day of camp, 218 patients were examined by a noted cardiologist, Dr Brajesh Badhan and Dr D.P. Marik, chief cardiac surgeon of Mediciti hospital. Basic diagnostic tests, blood sugar level, ECG and blood pressure were done free-of-cost at the camp.

Dr Brajesh stated that food habits, dependence on machines and stressful lifestyle had resulted in high incidence of heart diseases. Dr Marik also stressed that the adverse effects of changed lifestyle were causing heart problems in young people also. They stressed that early detection and treatment of hypertension, diabetes helped in preventing heart diseases.

Dietary advise along with same other information on heart problems were given to the patients. Dr B.S. Sekhon, MD of Ludhiana MediCiti, stated that it was necessary to create awareness about the causes and consequences of various diseases by organising seminars and workshops.

Heading: Mazdoor union decries globalisation - Indian Express
Content:
The 42nd annual general meeting of the city electroplaters was held under the chairmanship of Joginder Kumar, president of the Ludhiana Electroplaters Association.

Chander Parkash Sabharwal, general secretary, read out the minutes of the meeting while Sukhdev Raj Sethi, cashier of the association, placed before the members accounts during the period April 2007- March 2008 along with the balance-sheet, which was unanimously approved by the House.

Joginder Kumar apprised the members that a cluster had been approved by the Central government. He said that the state government had directed PSIEC to set up new focal points for electroplating industry at Ladhowal.

He also told that a deputation had a meeting with P.S Bhide, revenue secretary, last week in Delhi regarding the long-pending issue of levy of service tax on electroplating and zinc plating under business auxiliary service.

He also said that members of the association wold attend the 22nd National Steel Consumer Council to be held on in New Delhi on October 4.

Heading: Return receipt counters to remain open till 8 pm - Indian Express
Content:
More than 30,000 masons, carpenters, welders etc from all over the state participated in a rally organised by Punjab Nirman Mazdoor Union at the Grain Market on Monday.

Addressing the rally, Harinder Singh Randhawa, general secretary of the union, said that workers should get ready to wage battle against the policy of globalisation, which was the "root cause of unemployment in the country."

President of the union, Ganga Prasad criticized the state government for dilly-dallying the implementation of Central Act of 1996 despite clear orders of Punjab and Haryana High Court.

Mangat Ram Pasla, president of the Centre of Trade Unions, K.N. Ramachandran and many others addressed the rally.

Heading: Stone laid for Kup-Malaud road - Indian Express
Content:
Keeping in view of the income tax assesses, the Income Tax department has decided that the return receipt counters will remain open from 9.30 a.m to 8 p.m on Tuesday.

It needs to be mentioned that Tuesday is the last date of income tax returns for corporate assessee and all other assesses whose accounts are required to be audited under 44AB of the Income Tax Act 1961m according to a release issued by B.R Kaushal and Vijay Sharma, president and general secretary, respectively, of the Taxation Bar Association.

Heading: HC directs Centre to decide on PU retirement age - Indian Express
Content:
A new road from Kup to Malaud will be built at a cost of Rs 6 crores. The foundation stone for the road was laid on Tuesday by MP Sharanjit Singh Dhillon and zila parishad chairman Manpreet Singh Ayali.

Dhillon said that a total of Rs 120 crores would be spent to improve the condition of roads in Ludhiana district. However the road from Kup to Malaud is being constructed under the Prime Minister Gramin Yozna.

Mahesh Inder Grewal, former minister, was also present on the ocassion. Others who attended the function held on the occasion included Sukhwant Singh, member, Zila Parishad, sarpanch Gurmukh Singh.

Heading: Dr Kang yo-yos on V-C secy appointment? - Indian Express
Content:
PU staff may get five years more to serve the varsity

If allowed by the Ministry of Home Affairs, the entire Panjab University teaching staff will have a happier Diwali this year. For, if the Ministry allows the resolution passed by the Ministry of Human Resources and Development (HRD) as per which the retirement age of the teaching has been increased from 60 to 65 years, the same will hold true for the PU teaching staff as well.

In a significant direction, the Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed the Ministry of Home Affairs to decide the issue of enhancement of retirement age of teaching staff of Panjab University from 60 to 65 years by October 20. The directions were passed after Advocate Anupam Gupta, appearing on behalf of Panjab University, requested the court to pass the necessary directions as the issue concerning the enhancement of retirement age is hanging fire.

A bunch of petitions filed by several professors of Panjab University demanding directions to the university to increase the retirement age from 60 to 62 years is pending in the High Court. The Professors have taken the stand that since Panjab University is a Central University and that under a Central University, the retirement age of a teacher has been extended to 62 years, the same shall be applied in PU.

Contesting the plea taken by the professors, Anupam Gupta submitted that the direction cannot be applied to the university as it is not a Central University. Gupta said that PU is an Inter-State University and falls in the category of centrally-funded Institution.

Gupta also pointed out to the enhancement in retirement age introduced by Ministry of Human Resource and Development (MHRD). The Ministry has increased the retirement age from 60 to 65 years.

However, though PU is a centrally funded Institution, it does not fall in the category of MHRD, Gupta pointed out. He further apprised the Court that PU was under the purview of Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), which is yet to decide on the issue.

The Court asked the counsel to request the Ministry to decide on the issue. However, the counsel requested the court that in such cases which are of concern to several teachers, the intervention of the court was very essential. Gupta requested that the court should direct the MHA to decide the issue with immediate effect. Accepting the request, the division bench has directed the MHA to decide the issue by October 20 and file an affidavit to this effect.

Heading: Jaffar's ton steers Indian Oil into final - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Manjit Singh Kang, vice-chancellor, Punjab Agricultural University,as per the office-bearers of the PAU Non-teaching employees have assured them he would change his secretary very soon.

The development marks a departure from the stand taken by the V-C Dr Kang earlier. Throwing his lot behind the new SVC a few days ago, he had remarked that choosing a SVC was his prerogative and that he wanted to have such a person in the post who could share and work towards achieving his vision for PAU.

Notable here is that the recent decision of Dr Kang to appoint Dr P.P.S. Lubana as his SVC had the non-teaching employees up in arms for they claimed that this post belonged to the non-teaching cadre and that in case, Dr Kang did not revert his decision, the union wouls launch a protest rally. The union leaders held a meeting with Dr Kang today morning.

Giving details of the meeting, Lakhwinder Singh Sandhu, vice-president of the union, said, "Dr Kang's approach towards us was very positive. He has assured us that Dr Lubana's appointment is a stop-gap arrangement and that he would chose a suitable person from the non-teaching segment and renew this appointment."

Sandhu said, "Dr Kang told us that his SVC was transferred to GADVASU and that he did not want to keep the seat vacant for long as that would have had negative impact on the work. Thus he filled up this post by appointing Dr Lubana, but very soon a person from non-teaching staff will be chosen for this post."

Sandhu added, "The Dean, Post-graduate Studies, Dr S.K. Mann played a very positive role in the meeting and she pleaded the case on our behalf." "While Dr Kang has not given us any time frame, yet we expect the change to take place within the next 15 days," said Sandhu.

While Dr Kang was not available from comment, Dr P.P.S. Lubana, the man in the eye of the storm, refused to comment on the issue. Notable here is that last week, PAU Non teaching employees had held a protest rally when this issue dominated the rally. The union had announced that they would not rest till the time the post is given back to them. In reply Dr Kang had remarked that choosing a SVC was well within his prerogative.

Heading: Raikot police book four for murder - Indian Express
Content:
