According to medical education officials, the state government had introduced a system way back in 1972 under which students getting government or merit seats in state medical colleges have to sign a bond with the respective college to offer compulsory service at least for two years in rural areas of the state. The system was enforced to ensure that rural areas got sufficient medical services because most of the doctors refused to work in the backward and interior rural pockets.

A senior Health Department official said that since the state government was spending too much on medical education, the students must pay back by serving in the rural areas at least for two years. "The government expects a little from the students since it annually spends a hefty sum in educating and training them," said the official. Initially, the bond amount was meagre, but it was raised to Rs 75,000 a decade ago because most of the students managed to pay up and secure exemption. The students did so to migrate to Western countries seeking greener pastures, or work in urban centres where they earned more while enjoying a better quality of life.

The government further raised the bond amount to Rs 1.5 lakh but even this did not seem to work. Medical students again preferred to seek exemption from rural service by paying up the bond money.

The consequence of this has been an acute shortage of doctors in rural areas, with most of the Community Health Centres and Primary Health Centres in rural pockets being managed with skeletal staff though there is no shortage of money to pay for doctors or for medicines.

Though the government has appointed doctors from outside the state, particularly from UP and Bihar for PHCs and CHCs, the officials feel that the posting of local doctors was more necessary as they knew the local language and temperament of the people that helped a lot in treating the patients better.

According to figures available with state Health Commissionerate, only 403 doctors from all the 13 government medical colleges turned up to take rural jobs in the last three years though annually over 1,500 candidates obtained MBBS degrees from these institutions.

Between January 1 and August 31, 2008, the state government gave appointment letters to as many as 872 allopathic doctors for their posting in rural areas but only 69 of them turned up. The rest did not even show the courtesy of informing the department of their reasons for not joining duty. An interesting aspect of this was that even scheduled tribes and scheduled caste doctors refused to serve in their own areas where health services are badly neglected due to non-availability of medicos. The same is true even for ayurvedic and homoeopathic doctors who are equally unwilling to serve in rural areas. Only 98 out of 238 homoeopathic doctors appointed by the state government in the last eight months joined duty. The situation was a bit better in case of ayurvedic doctors as 457 of 607 appointed in the last eight months joined their duties in remote areas.

The Gujarat Public Service Commission, now at its wit's end to meet the shortage of doctors in rural areas, has been holding walk-in interviews every Tuesday to recruit doctors, but hardly few people turn up to take such offers.

Heading: SC stays trial of Sohrabuddin case - Indian Express
Content:
Corporate house employees come out of boardroom, join Navratri special dance classes

If you thought corporate culture is only about boardroom drama, think again! The corporates of Ahmedabad are flocking to training centres to learn garba and add zing to the vivacious festival of Navratri.

The companies too, are encouraging them to attend garba classes organised specially for them during late evening hours.

"We run a corporate batch in our academy where office-goers come to learn various styles of garba for Navratri. Candidates come in groups to learn dancing, which is organised by their companies. Also, there are office-goers who come individually to learn garba," says Abhishek Shukla of Desert Dance Academy.

With more than 50 garba teaching classes running across Ahmedabad, the training centres charge anything between Rs 300 and Rs 2,500, depending on the period of training.

This year, Hemant Kothekar of Zazzie Dancing Hall had candidates from Claries and Gujarat Gas. "We also gave lessons to a few employees of Vadilal at their homes," he says.

"We have a lot of working people coming to learn garba. The excitement is more in this age group than among youngsters. Many office-goers working in BPOs and even those having private businesses, keep their busy schedule aside and come to learn garba," claims Shukla.

While there are some companies that have organised garba competitions in their premises, others have arranged participation of their employees in dandiya groups in the city.

"I own a small company. My employees and I have been taking classes for quite sometime now. We thought of attending some classes, as we wanted to take part in dandiya where many other corporates will participate," said Pranav Bavishi, an entrepreneur in Ahmedabad.

Chetan Dave of Panghat Performing Arts said that employees of multinational companies have been flocking to training centres. His academy has 22 corporates taking training from him out of which 7-8 employees belong to multinational companies.

Heading: NAAC quality check for open universities - Indian Express
Content:
Further hearing will begin in the second week of November; MP Police to accord protection to victim's family

The Supreme Court on

Tuesday ordered an interim stay on trial proceedings in the alleged fake encounter killing of Sohrabuddin Sheikh by the Gujarat Police. It posted the matter for further directions to the second week of November.

While ordering the stay, a bench of Justices Tarun Chatterjee and Aftab Alam took note of how Rubabuddin Sheikh, Sohrabuddin's brother, and his family are under constant fear. The court, responding to a petition by Rubabuddin, directed the Madhya Pradesh Police to provide necessary protection to his family.

The bench, after a five-hour-long hearing, also ordered the secretary general of the apex court to seal all the records pertaining to the proceedings pending before the City Sessions Court, Ahmedabad.

The directions followed submissions by Additional Solicitor General Gopal Subramaniam, who is the amicus curiae in the case. He criticised the Gujarat government for its attempts to scuttle the probe. All the allegations primarily were targeted especially at Inspector General of Police Geeta Johri, whom the amicus blamed for misleading the investigations to protect accused police officers.

Senior police officers — D G Vanzara (DIG), Raj Kumar Pandiyan (SP) and Dinesh M N (Rajasthan Cadre IPS officer) — are among the main accused in the alleged fake encounter that took place on November 26, 2006.

Subramaniam submitted that it had even "forced" the trial court to frame charges in the encounter killing, forgetting that the apex court was monitoring the investigations.

"The investigation by Geeta Johri is shoddy, incompetent and designed to tamper with the truth," he argued while alleging that contrary to the initial reports that Johri was performing her duties in an impartial manner, she was actually acting in tandem with other top officials to tamper with the investigation and save the accused.

He submitted how two DSP-level officers, M L Parmar and M K Amin, who are also accused in the killing, were initially entrusted with the probe. He also said Solanki, a DSP rank officer, had conducted a detailed probe wherein he had mentioned the names of the accused officers and their role in the encounter. But Solanki's report was neither taken into consideration while "filing the chargesheet nor was it brought to the notice of the apex court by Johri".

In May 2007, the apex court had refused to transfer the investigation of the case to the CBI and had directed in July 2008 further investigations into the incident, after being satisfied with the probe.

Heading: Rizwanur death: Cops’ plan goes awry as court accepts surrender, not bail plea - Indian Express
Content:
Assessment system to be implemented from Jan next

An Assessment and Accreditation system will be in place for all open universities of India by January 2009. This new system will work on the lines of the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC), which assesses and accredits conventional colleges and universities.

The first draft manual regarding the system was prepared during the two-day conference, called "Open Universities in 21st Century: Assessment & Accreditation of Open Universities", organised by Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Open University on September 29 and 30 in Ahmedabad.

The Vice Chancellors (V-C) of all the 14 Open Universities of the country were present at the conference, which aimed at discussing various issues pertaining to Open University system in India and it's role in promoting education amongst the rural populace.

"The V-Cs of all the 14 Open Universities have been holding formal and informal meetings for the last 18 months in order to frame the guidelines for the Assessment and Accreditation system. We have consulted the NAAC in this regard," V N Rajashekharan Pillai, chairman, Distance Education Council (DEC), said.

He added: "As of now, the 14 Open Universities in India contribute around 20 per cent to higher education as against the 80 per cent contribution by the conventional universities in excess of 430."

A K Singh, V-C of Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Open University said: "We are also looking at factors like drop out ratios, skill oriented courses and roles and measures to tackle higher education. However, now we also want to ensure the quality of education. In order to impart quality education to the students, there is an urgent need of Assessment and Accreditation system."

He added: "We have drafted the

first manual of the Assessment and Accreditation system. We hope that the mechanism would be ready by December end. The system will be put in place by January 2009."

Heading: Sourav may play under Ranadeb in Challengers - Indian Express
Content:
Three police officers of Kolkata — one a former deputy commissioner — surrendered before a court in the city on Tuesday and were promptly sent to 14 days' in judicial custody on charges of criminal intimidation and abetting the suicide of computer graphic professional Rizwanur Rehman last September.

The officers had also moved an application for bail the moment they surrendered before a designated CBI court, hoping they would get it. But 14th Metropolitan Magistrate Madhumita Roy dashed their hopes.

These officers — former deputy commissioner and IPS Ajay Kumar, assistant commissioner Sukanti Chakroborty and sub-inspector Krishnendu Das — had been indicted by the Central Bureau of Investigation, along with four others, in Rizwanur's death. Rizwanur had married Priyanka Todi, daughter of prominent businessman Ashok Todi just days before his body was found on the railway tracks near the Dum Dum station on September 21, 2007.

The CBI took up the investigation and filed the chargesheet on September 22, 2008. The investigating agency found that these three cops were directly involved in coercing Rizwanur to break up his marriage with Priyanka. The other four includes Ashok Todi and Priyanka's uncle.

Home Secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarty said if officers spend more than 48 hours in jail, they would be suspended from service as existing service rules dictate.

However, the officers had also come with a plan. They also moved for bail, but the judge would not hear of it. Legal and police experts now feel the officers' sneaky move to surrender before the Bankshall Court was a blunder. Under normal circumstances, the case would have come up for hearing in the sessions court on October 27.

News spread immediately about the court's order, and the premises was soon swarming with officers. Damage control measures began and another appeal was moved before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate in the same court asking for a stay on this order.

Rejecting the appeal filed by accused police officers, Chief Metropolitan Magistrate S S Anand observed that his court was not empowered to stay the order passed by the 14th Metropolitan Magistrate.

"The court rejected their bail plea and sent them to judicial custody. They are to be produced after 14 days" said Partho Tapaswai, CBI counsel. The sudden move surprised the CBI which did not expect the cops to appeal to the Metropolitan Magistrate's Court since the next hearing was scheduled on October 27.

It is learnt accused officers are likely to move a fresh bail petition on Wednesday before the City Sessions' Court.

What they said
'It is a legal matter. It would not be appropriate for me to comment'Former Commissioner, Prasun Mukherjee
'What has happened is not right. He can never do such a thing'Abilasha Kumar, Ajay Kumar's wife
'We are happy. All those who are responsible for my son's death should be punished'Kiswar Jahan, Rizwanur's mother

Heading: Swimmer’s death: BASA set to introduce strict guidelines for long-distance swimming - Indian Express
Content:
Preparatory tournament shifted from Kalyani to Eden Gardens for convenience of players and officials

The upcoming Challenger Trophy, Bengal cricket's novel experiment this season, got a massive boost today with Sourav Ganguly making himself available to play in the preparatory event.

As things stand, Ganguly, who is in the news these days over whether he will be picked for the India-Australia Test series, could be playing for the side in the Challengers that will be led by ace speedster Ranadeb Bose.

"Sourav may be playing in the Challengers, it's good news for everybody. In all probability, he could playing for the team that will be captained by Ranadeb," said CAB joint-secretary Arun Mitra this evening.

Ranadeb, current Bengal skipper Laxmi Ratan Shukla and young gun Manoj Tiwary will lead the three teams in the 12-day preparatory tournament that will see Bengal cricket's top 36 players get some much-needed match practice to stake claim in the senior squad for the upcoming Ranji Trophy.

The Challengers, meanwhile, has been shifted from Kalyani to Eden Gardens. Initially, the CAB authorities had explained that the Kalyani ground has taken a battering from the rains, and hence, will not be able to host the crucial 12-day preparatory tournament.

However, CAB joint-secretary Mitra today came up with a different explanation. "The simple thing is, everybody wants to closely follow this tournament. The Kalyani ground is in very good condition, it would have made for a good venue. But, we want to host the Challengers here so that we all can closely follow it. And Eden is anyway in fine condition to host this event," Mitra said.

The CAB is also planning to reschedule the tournament and start it on October 12 instead of October 16, as announced earlier. The tournament has been planned as part of the senior Bengal probables' preparation for the Ranji Trophy Plate Group event that gets underway on November 3. Interestingly, some of the senior Bengal players have suggested a few names for the three teams that will lock horns in the Challenger Trophy. The CAB is mulling over the idea of naming the three teams Reds (Shukla's team), Blues (Ranadeb) and Whites (Tiwary).

Meanwhile, the CAB announced the Under-19 and Under-22 Bengal probables today. The U-19 probables' preseason camp will be held at Durgapur.

Heading: EB find red hot Mumbai FC too tough to handle - Indian Express
Content:
Panchu Gopal Maity is still trying to come to terms with Sampa Das' death. The secretary of Kumartuli Swimming Association (KSA) has seen Das from very close quarters. This untimely death has left him shattered.

"She came to me only the other day and asked for an entry form for our long-distance swimming championship. I can hardly believe that she is no more," Maity told The Indian Express.

Das died after a heart attack while competing in a swimming event at Chinsura. A very accomplished long-distance swimmer, who had participated in 24 national championships from the sub-junior level and won five golds, her death has left the entire swimming fraternity shell-shocked.

It is mandatory for the long-distance swimmers to fill up a medical form before every event. Das' medical form got the go-ahead from Dr Jadav Chatterjee. Also, Dr SP Chatterjee, who was appointed by the Bally Swimming Centre (BSC) said that the swimmer was medically fit. Her family members, however, reportedly said that the swimmer had a slight fever going into that competition. Das' dead body reached her Bally residence this evening. She is survived by her mother. The post mortem report is expected to reveal all.

Das' coach Surojit Ghosh, his brother Biswajit and the swimmers of that club believe it was an accident. The Bengal Amateur Swimming Association (BASA), however, feels that this should be an eye-opener.

Said BASA secretary Ramanuj Mukherjee: "We have three more long-distance swimming championships left this year. We want strict guidelines for those events. Appointment of qualified doctors and a foolproof medical check-up facility for the participants should be made mandatory."

Meanwhile, BASA president Ramala Chakrabarty said that they would announce a compensation package for Das' family.

Heading: No dredging in 20 years, Hooghly river draft now affects trade - Indian Express
Content:
The new kid on the block is on a roll. After deflating Mohun Bagan's ego the other night, Mumbai FC today accounted for another Kolkata giants, East Bengal in the I-League match at Yuba Bharati Krirangan. Felix Aboagye scored the all-important goal in the 23rd minute. Then the Mumbai FC defenders, led by an excellent Selwyn Fernandes took the centrestage. They rode their luck all right, but managed to keep a clean slate.

Mumbai FC coach David Booth said that their first four matches, especially the matches against Mohun Bagan and East Bengal would be very important. He wanted two points from these two matches. His got six instead. So, after two rounds, Mumbai FC are on top of the league standings with successive away wins.

East Bengal started as firm favourites, especially after their 3-1 win over Chirag United in the last match. But today, their midfield stood statuesque. Yusif Yakubu was not his usual self and operated at a walking pace. Only Rahim Nabi was purposeful and set up a fantastic opportunity for Sunil Chhetri in the 23rd minute. Chhetri's header was partially saved by Mumbai FC goalkeeper Kalyan Chaubey and the rebound fell nicely for Mehrajuddin Wadoo who shot over the crossbar from five yards.

The following counter attack saw the visitors go in front. Felix collected a Riston Rodrigues free-kick inside the box, dropped his marker Khelemba Singh with a lovely half-turn and placed it at the far post. After that they concentrated on tightening the defence as East Bengal pressed hard for the equaliser. Chances came thick and fast. Chhetri, who tried his heart out, came close to scoring twice. But Chaubey stood firm.

With no constructive midfield play, the hosts opted for high balls from the flanks. It, however, made the job easier for two Mumbai FC centrebacks, Fernandes and James Dissiramah.

East Bengal coach Stanley Rozario replaced Edmilson Marques with Asim Biswas after the break. It helped some good combination play upfront. But the visitors kept at least three players behind the ball every time and denied the red-and-gold strikers space to manoeuvre.

Booth was also spot on with his introduction of experienced Noel Wilson midway through the second half. More than anything else, it helped calm the nerves. He also tried to hit the opponent on the break. The ploy almost paid off when an unmarked Abel Hammond had a clear sight of the goal from inside the six-yard box. He headed wide.

East Bengal are considered to be Kolkata's best bet for this I-League. But they have some serious repair work to do as far their defence is concerned. It's their biggest concern.

Heading: Daylight robbery in Gariahat - Indian Express
Content:
Alarmed by the drafting problem faced by the Hooghly river, the Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT) officials held a seminar at the Hillary Institute on Monday to discuss the issue and its remedial measures. Lakshman Seth, CPM MP from Haldia, also attended the seminar.

The draft in the river is adversely affecting trade, and calls for prompt action. A K Bagchi, the director of marine department, KoPT, said dredging is the only solution to the problem.

"There are thick soil formations in the river. For this we have requested the Centre for five dredging machines. The flow of the river needs to be augmented for the purpose of better trade," Bagchi said.

The marine department of KoPT has written a letter to the Dredging Corporation of India stating that the navigable depth at Jellingham and Auckland has been reduced by 4 meters to 4.1 meters as against the targeted depth of 5.0 meters and 5.5 meters, respectively, as a result of inadequate dredging. Therefore, vessels need to be diverted to the neighbouring Paradip and Visakhapatnam ports.

The Haldia Dock Forum has been putting pressure on the Centre and state government for dredging to ensure better trade. It has also written a letter to the Union Shipping Minister T R Balu. But there has been no response from the minister's end.

There are, however, some basic differences among officials of KoPT and Haldia Dock Officers' Forum over the issue. Some of the officials alleged that continued negligence by the Centre and the indifferent attitude of the state government led to the drafting problem in the Haldia channel.

Owing to the draft, ships carrying heavy containers and oil tanks have to wait for the tide to reach their destination. Alarmingly, there has been no dredging in the Hooghly river for the last 20 years.

Haldia Dock Officers' Forum secretary, R K Burman, said the Haldia Dock Complex is facing a severe crisis now and it will be shut down by December 2008 if dredgers are not brought back to Haldia channel from the Sethusamudram project immediately. As the Supreme Court has stopped work at Sethusamudram project there is hardly any need for seven dredgers there. He threatened to resign if the dredgers are not brought back.

Addressing the issue, Seth, however, said: "There is no need to panic over the drafting issue. There are solutions for this problem. If port management is done by private players the performance will be even better."

The chairman of KoPT, Ashok Kumar Chanda, also observed that the problem is not always serious. He said: "Throughout the year draft does not remain the same".

Heading: Woman constable found dead in Barrackpore - Indian Express
Content:
In a daring daylight robbery, four youths decamped with cash, jewellery, antique watches and three mobile phones from a flat in Rashbehari Avenue on Tuesday.

The youths, posing as salesmen of a mobile company, forced their way into the third-floor flat of 82-year-old Sachindra Kumar Ray.

The robbers hit Ray on the head, before escaping from the spot.

After the robbery, Ray called his nephew Sabyasachi Banerjee and informed him about the incident.

Banerjee subsequently lodged a complaint with the Gariahat Police Station.

A police officer of the Gariahat Police Station said, "We are investigating the case."

Heading: No cause for worry over JE: experts - Indian Express
Content:
A woman constable, who had been recruited a month ago, died under mysterious circumstances at Police Training College (PTC) in Barrackpore on Monday night.

While police claimed that Junela Khatun (29) died of cardiac arrest, a section of the trainees alleged that overexertion caused her death. No police complaint, however, has been registered in the case.

Khatun, a resident of Nanoor in Birbhum, was undergoing training at the PTC. Police said she spoke to her husband, Mohammad Taslimuddin, over phone around 10:15 pm, and fell sick soon after.

"She went to the bathroom around 10:45 pm on Monday and complained of sickness. She fell unconscious after that," said Praveen Tripathi, Additional Superintendent of Police, Barrackpore.

Khatun was rushed to the PTC hospital, where doctors declared her dead on arrival. A postmortem was later conducted. Police, however, have not disclosed the details of the postmortem report.

Heading: Buddha slams Cong for singing Trinamool tune - Indian Express
Content:
Even though the poor surveillance work of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) has increased the chances of outbreak of vector-borne diseases, city entomologists have assured that there is the least possibility of an outbreak of Japanese Encephalitis (JE).

The cycle in which people get affected by JE is different from that of other vector-borne diseases. The JE virus is carried by birds like storks from which it gets transmitted to pigs by a vector, Culex Bishnoi.

Pigs and wild birds are the reservoirs of the virus. The virus gets transmitted to a human when the same vector that has already sucked blood from an affected pig stings a person.

Dr Amiyo Hati, former director, School of Tropical Medicine (STM), said: "The cycle of the JE is such that there are minimum chances for a city-dweller to get affected. Moreover, paddy fields are usual habitats for the vectors and hence these vectors are usually found in villages and not in a city."

Kolkata being a dengue and malaria-prone city, the residents have already developed a specific antibody that resists the JE virus. "A cross resistance mechanism will prevent the city-dwellers from being affected by the JE," said an entomologist of STM.

A research conducted by the STM says JE generally spreads over a large area but does not affect many people. "If the virus is transmitted to 500 people, then only one person might be affected. This unique feature of JE is termed as 'inapparent infection'. But if it becomes an epidemic then it can spread over a large area and may take several lives," said Dr Hati. He further added that in 1990, the disease took the form of an epidemic and nine districts of the state were badly affected.

Sarsuna resident Pralai Chowdhury, the only patient of JE in the city so far, has been admitted to the STM. Entomologists feel that although the disease was diagnosed in Kolkata, Chowdhury might have carried the virus from a rural area.

Heading: Green pandal stands out with climate change theme - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee criticised the Congress for demanding land from within the Tata Motors small car project at Singur. "The Congress is speaking in tune with the Trinamool Congress," he said. Bhattacharjee was speaking after an all-party meet to resolve the Singur crisis at the Writers' Buildings on Tuesday. The Trinamool Congress and Socialist Unity Centre of India boycotted the meeting.

Bhattacharjee said: "We placed a resolution at the meeting but while the BJP supported it, the Congress did not. They want land from within the project area and also want some ancillary units to be shifted. They have failed to understand the integrated nature of the project. We have consulted experts, who say the ancillary units cannot be transferred."

The resolution said while the interest of farmers has to be protected, industrialisation must also be kept in mind.

The Congress delegation comprised former mayor of Kolkata Subrata Mukherjee and Congress Legislature Party leader Manas Bhuniya. They placed a letter by Pradesh Congress president Priya Ranjan Dasmunshi in which he demanded that land from within the project area be given to the farmers who did not receive compensation package. "If the government can give 70 acres of land, then why not 170 or 200 acres?" said Mukherjee.

The chief minister, who has always said that nobody could stop the Tatas from resuming the work at Singur, was not confident enough on Tuesday. Asked whether he could give an assurance that the Nano will rollout from Singur, the chief minister said: "I cannot give this assurance. It depends on so many things and situations. But I can tell you that there is no slackness in our seriousness and efforts."

Bhattacharjee also clarified the agreement that was signed between the government and the Trinamool Congress and said the government could not give more than what has been offered. "The agreement mentioned that maximum land will be given from the project area. We first agreed to 40 acres and later we increased it to 70 acres. That is the maximum we could offer from within the project area. If we give more, the project will have to be scrapped," Bhattacharjee said.

He also took a dig at the Trinamool for its absence from the meeting. "They do not come to any meeting," said the chief minister.

Commerce and Industries Minister Nirupam Sen said the government was giving more than what was stipulated at the rehabilitation package Bill tabled in the Parliament. "The Bill said if the government gives an acquired land to a company it will have to give wages of 750 days to the affected farmer. But we are giving more than that," Sen said.

Meanwhile, Tata Sons' chairman Ratan Tata is coming to Kolkata on October 3 to meet the chief minister to find a way out of the Singur imbroglio. Sen will also attend the meeting.

Celebrities protest against new govt package for Singur farmers
Eminent personalities of the city organised a meeting at College Square on Tuesday to protest against the state government's latest decision on rehabilitation package for Singur farmers.

Under the banner of Shilpi Sanskriti Karmi Buddhijibi Mancha, Bibhash Chakrabarty, Shuvaprassanna, Samir Aich and Tarun Sanyal spoke on the need to honour the agreement between the Left Front government and the Opposition.

They said the government has gone back on its earlier decision of providing land to the farmers and was now offering them a new package.

"We were accused of being unreasonable. But all we want is that the issue should be resolved through discussions," said noted theatre personality Bibhash Chakrabarty.

"It is ironical that people who are protesting against Singur and Nandigram incidents are labelled as anti-development and anti-industrialisation. But that is not true. We want that everybody should be duly compensated," he added.

The protesters said the Tatas were projected wrongly in the state. Stating the example of tribal villages surrounding Jamshedpur, they said the company has done nothing for them and it was only the NGOs operating in those villages which provide them help, especially medical support.

They demanded that they would like to see the actual deal between the government and the company. "We want justice for the people. Until it is achieved, we shall carry on with our protests," Chakraborty said.

Heading: Traders demand extension of tax deadline - Indian Express
Content:
This year, the FD block Puja in Salt Lake has a greener side to it. On its 24th anniversary, the Puja committee has decided to adopt global warming as its theme to decorate its Puja pandal.

It is also among a handful of Puja committees in Kolkata which has received the recognition from the state Environment Ministry.

"This is undoubtedly the biggest Puja in Salt Lake ever. Every year we try to do something new," said Puja committee president Hironmoy Roy Chowdhury.

Last year, the FD Block Puja was in news after Harry Potter publishers Bloomsbury sued the decorators for copyright violations under the IPR regulations.

Not taking any chances this year, the organisers have selected a theme depicting effect of pollution and deforestation on the earth.

"While selecting the theme, we had ideas like the Beijing Olympics and Tata's Nano car. But there were several issues that restricted us from going ahead with these themes," said S Biswas, general secretary of the Puja committee.

More than 65 artists have constructed a towering pandal which is nearly 120 feet high.

"The pandal is in the shape of a globe. The southern hemisphere represents the earth, but in the northern hemisphere, we have constructed tall factories and buildings depicting a jungle of concrete. We will also construct mountains depicting melting of glaciers," designer Partha Ghosh said. Inside the pandal are depicted jungles and animals which are important for human existence.

"Close to the floor of the pandal, we will paint bright red flames depicting effect of global warming on the earth," said Ghosh.

The organisers have stuck to the theme while selecting construction material of the pandal as well as the idol of goddess Durga.

"The pratima (idol) will be painted with lead-free paint. In fact, the paint used for decorating the pandal is also lead-free," Biswas said.

In view of the recent terrorist attacks in major cities across the country, the organisers have adopted various safety measures to tackle any untoward incident. In consultation with the police, three close circuit cameras have been installed at the pandal.

Heading: Special security arrangement for Pujas - Indian Express
Content:
City traders want the government to extend the deadline for depositing service taxes considering a series of bank holidays across the state. Traders have to pay service taxes by the fifth of every month.

While individual customers can opt for ATMs to carry out day-to-day transaction, the city's trading community will face a lot of inconvenience. "It is not possible to carry out bulk cash transactions during bank holidays," said Mahesh Singhania, Chairman, Federation of West Bengal Traders' Association.

With Eid falling on October 1, and Gandhi Jayanti on October 2, customers are left with only two days to carry out transactions in banks on October 3 and 4. According to traders, even if Saturday is a half working day, cheques are not cleared on the same day. This means, if cheques are deposited on October 3, they will not be cleared before banks resume work on October 10 (banks are closed for Pujas from October 6 to October 9).

Heading: Officers indicted in Rizwanur get special beds, fans in jail - Indian Express
Content:
Considering a series of terror attacks over the last two weeks in different parts of the country, the state government will step up security during the Durga Puja festival.

Home Secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarti said: "Several incidents of terrorist attacks have been reported recently. To ensure proper security, we seek to bring managing committees of Puja, their volunteers and the police on a common platform in Kolkata and neighbouring districts of North and South 24 Parganas where the Puja pandals draw huge crowds."

He was speaking after a high-level security meeting held at Lalbazar on Tuesday. Kolkata Police Commissioner Gautam Mohan Chakrabarti said the police were looking at ways to plug possible loopholes that terror elements may take advantage of.

The home secretary added that while many close-circuit TV cameras and surveillance equipment are being installed at the pandals, there are plans to erect watchtowers near pandals.

"These watchtowers would be manned by the police and pandal volunteers. It may not be possible to screen every visitor to the city during the Pujas, but volunteers have been asked to stay alert. We have also planned to reserve beds in key hospitals in case a terror attack takes place," he added.

The meeting was attended by Director General of Police, Inspector General of Police (South Bengal), DMs and SPs of North and South 24 Parganas, top officials from the Kolkata Municipal Corporation and health and fire department.

Ever since the blasts in Delhi a fortnight ago, the city has seen a series of bomb scares that later proved to be hoaxes.

Heading: Crop damage: farmers up in arms against cement firm - Indian Express
Content:
As if to offer solace after the blow caused by the Central Bureau of Investigation chargesheet and the subsequent imprisonment, the three senior police officers accused in Rizwanur are being given a preferential treatment in the Presidency Jail.

They are allegedly lodged in the video conferencing room of the jail, instead of normal cells meant for undertrials. The trio is also provided with special beds and adequate number of fans in the room.

Even at the Bankshall Court lockup, the officers were kept out of the main lockup, given chairs to sit, allowed to use their cellphones and treated with crème crackers and tea.

"After reaching the jail, the accused asked the jail staff to keep them in a secluded place. They also demanded that they be lodged in the jail hospital but the doctor refused to issue the certificates required," sources in the police said.

"We converted the video conferencing room into a cell to accomodate the officers. Tomorrow we will shift them to some other location. We cannot afford to keep them with other prisoners, as many of them were arrested by the three officers," said a police officer of Presidency Jail.

He added: "They did not have food in the jail tonight. They carried their water bottles inside the jail."

"I cannot say anything now. Please talk to IG prisons," said S R Hussain, DIG prisons, when contacted by The Indian Express.

B D Sharma IG Prisons could not be contacted despite repeated calls.

"They are special people. They enjoy all the facilities, whereas we sleep in lockups. They get tea and biscuits and we are not allowed to see even visitors," said Choudhury Humayun Kabir, an undertrial.

Heading: Chamunda stampede: Himachal gets act together - Indian Express
Content:
Irked at the heavy damage to the standing crop following sliding down of thousands of tonnes of debris, hundreds of farmers and public representatives of Bagga Ser village and its adjoining areas are up in arms against the management of JP Cement company in Arki sub-division of Solan district.

The farmers who had suffered financial loss to the tune of lakhs of rupees following sliding down of thousands of tonnes of muck in their cultivable land have stopped the dumping of debris by the management of the company at Bagga Ser.

Upset over the alleged indifferent attitude of the management of company in not conceding to their demand, farmers and public representatives yesterday held a meeting at Mangal, urging the Chief Minister to intervene as dumping of debris has recently caused heavy damage to public paths, natural water sources, irrigation water channels and a temple in the area. The farmers alleged that the dumping of thousands of tonnes of muck at Bagga Ser has completely destroyed standing crop on several bighas of land at Bhalag, Samtyari, Bagga Ser, Traeda and Hawanipul villages. The maximum damage has been caused to crops like tomato and ginger.

"We have been repeatedly urging the management of the company to avoid dumping at the controversial site as it is destroying crops," said Mangal Vikas Parishad president N.L. Chauhan.He said that despite the repeated requests by the farmers, the authorities of the company are not showing an interest to address the problem. This has forced the farmers to stop the dumping operation of the company at the village. Chauhan said that after taking a unanimous decision, the Parishad had deployed some farmers at the controversial site to prevent the company's authorities from dumping the muck. The sliding down of muck had earlier caused heavy damage to some houses, standing crop, water mills, a school building, public paths and natural water sources in the last rainy season.

"The management of the company had assured the farmers to give adequate compensation for the crops damaged due to muck but despite the lapse of over a year, nothing has been done," said T.D. Bhardwaj, former chairman of Kunihar Block Development Committee.He said the debris had completely destroyed centuries-old natural sources of water, including some baolis in the villages. This poses a risk of water-borne diseases as farmers are forced to consume contaminated water.Bhardwaj said the discharging of polluted water by the company was leading to repeated sliding down of debris in the cultivable land.

Farmers demanded that the company should immediately remove the debris from the fields and restore the natural water sources. Besides, compensation should also be provided to the farmers whose crop had been destroyed.

Company president Rajeev Gaur was not available for comment. However, an official of the Revenue Department said that following complaint of farmers, the loss is being assessed.

Heading: Bitumen supply scam may run into crores - Indian Express
Content:
The stampede at Chamunda temple in Rajasthan, which has taken a heavy toll of life, brings back memories of a similar tragedy at the Naina Devi temple in Bilaspur district in August, which had left 141 persons dead and at least 80 others injured.

The state's Home and CID departments were quick to reiterate its instructions to all deputy commissioners and SPs to strictly follow the guidelines recently approved by the Cabinet for crowd management at temples, especially during Navratri and festivals.

Besides Navratri, which already has started attracting huge rush of pilgrims at the famous temples, like Jawalaji, Chintpurni, Chamuda, near Dharamshala, and Naina Devi, the government is attaching a lot of importance to the upcoming international Kullu Dussehra, beginning next week.

CM Prem Kumar Dhumal says the government has already asked the police and deputy commissioners to personally monitor the arragements and ensure safety of the pilgrims. "During the Dussehra festival, IGP (Law and Order) S.R. Mardi will be camping at Kullu to oversee the arrangements," he says.

Mandi Range DIG Anurag Garg is reported to have visited Kullu twice and taken stock of the arrangements. Says Mardi, "In the next two to three days,I will also reach Kullu."

Mardi was the first senior police official to have reached Naina Devi immediately after the tragedy and had camped at the site for almost a week. Since he has the first-hand experience at Naina Devi, the government has put him in a supervisory role at Kullu.

After the Naina Devi tragedy, where the local administration had come under sharp criticism, the government had set up an inquiry headed by Mandi Divisional Commissioner Ashwani Kapoor. The report of the inquiry, which severely indicted the Bilaspur administration, was accepted by the Cabinet last month and recommended action against the erring officials.

Heading: Mini-micro projects: HP proposes policy change - Indian Express
Content:
The total damages the state government is expected to suffer as a result of the bitumen supply scam of 2007-08 might run into crores of rupees.

The state PWD is under the scanner of the State Anti-Corruption and Vigilance Bureau in the scam in which supply of thousands of litres of bitumen from the Panipat refineries was delayed, later resulting in shortage of stock.

Besides the investigation into the extent of the involvement of officials and staff of the PWD in the scam and the role of Him Agro Industries Corporation that was the nodal agency for procuring supplies, the role of the transporter companies would also be assessed.

The four transporter companies involved were awarded tender for transportation of bitumen from refineries of Indian Oil Corporation Limited and Hindustan Petroleum Limited at Panipat to several destinations in the state. Preliminary inquiries reveal that though the condition on the tender called for transporting all supplies within five days after which a fine of Rs 10 per day was to be imposed on the transporters, the nodal agency appointed by the PWD did not take any action for the delay, even as in many cases the delay is of over six months.

The State Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau has called in records of 25 PWD divisions for detailed scrutiny on the basis of which a preliminary report would be prepared and sent to the state government to decide the further course of action. During the previous months, the Vigilance had conducted raids at 22 PWD divisions to check the stock registers in the stores, in which gross violations were found, signalling largescale bungling in the supply of bitumen.

Sources in the Vigilance say the later stages of the detailed investigation would involve questioning of many officials, right from junior engineers to the engineer-in-chief.

Heading: State SC welfare budget exceeds population share - Indian Express
Content:
Faced with over-delays and non-serious attitude of the hydro power companies, which were allotted mini-micro hydel projects during the earlier congress regime, the Prem Kumar Dhumal government has decided to act tough. Twenty-three companies have already been slapped with show cause notices. Only two companies have been granted exemptions and rest, will be made to part with the projects, said senior power department officials.

In past eight years, 259 projects were allotted to the private companies through MOU. Only 16 projects have been commissioned so far. Looking at the performance chart of the companies, few of them have not even obtained necessary clearances, the BJP government proposes cancellation of the allotments.

Nearly, a dozen allotments of the projects have already been cancelled after BJP's return to power. Ironically, some of the project, which have been delayed were allotted during earlier BJP regime.

"We held a day-long conference with the hydro power companies earlier this month and made it clear that the government will not allow delays unless there are genuine reasons," said Principal Secretary (power) Ajay Mittal.

Mittal said the issues raised by some of the Independent Power Producers (IPPs) are being examined and some changes in the power policy will be required. "We are working on these changes to simplify the procedure of getting clearances of different government departments," he said.

Currently the IPPS have to taken NOCs from at least nine government agencies, including local panchayat, IPH department and Fisheries. There is demand for granting one time NOC through a single window authority on the lines of the Industrial investments.

Mini-Micro projects, mostly located in the state's interiors, are considered to be low-cost green energy.The companies are entitled for 45 per cent subsidy up to Rs 2.25 crore for projects of one MW capacity.

Two years back, Himachal Pradesh had no written policy for allotment of the projects. There have been doubts regarding allotments made to big companies based in Andhra Pradesh ,Gujarat,UP, Delhi and Karnataka.

Mittal said the litigation, which the government has been facing, is a result of lack of transparency in the allotments and non-serious allottees. It has been a big blow to the state's drive for speedy power generation. "The government is spending more time in handling cases in the High Court than monitoring the progress of each projects," he said.

Inquiries reveal, approximately 108 projects allotted by previous BJP government between 1998-2003, are nowhere near completions and another 200 privatised during the Congress regime have been awaiting some of mandatory approvals. Around 80- 90 project allotments were cancelled during past five years but more than half of these were re-allotted to the investors. In all 38 other projects are still awaiting cancellations.

Heading: Incentives for being a good samaritan - Indian Express
Content:
The Scheduled Caste sub-component in the annual plan outlay of the state government has exceeded the total Scheduled Caste population of the state because of the welfare measures announced by the Bhupinder Singh Hooda government.

The government is however is not much bothered as it has much in its coffers to support its policies for the SCs.

The government has dedicated 21.35 per cent of the total plan outlay for the scheduled castes against their total population share of 19.35 per cent.

The financial arrangement in the annual plan for the Scheduled Castes has already increased more than three fold at Rs 6,650 crore against the earmarked amount of Rs 2,000 crore in 2003-04.

According to sources, it has been done with an eye on the ensuing Lok Sabha polls which would be followed by the assembly polls in the state.

The major financial burden has come because of the government's decision to provide 100 square yards to the families living below poverty line.

Though the land for these plots would be given by the village panchayats but the government has decided to provide a subsidy of Rs 50,000 to the scheduled castes for the purpose of construction on these plots. This assistance had been Rs 10,000 in the past. However, the scheme has also enlarged as it now includes all the BPL families irrespective of their caste.

The government has also decided to give financial incentive of Rs 1,500 for each scheduled caste woman for institutional delivery. This amount is over the Central government norms of Rs 700.

The government also increased the amount under Indira Gandhi Vivah Shagun Yojna to 15,000 from Rs 5100. It has also decided to include the BPL families under the scheme as well.

The state's decision to provide assistance to the villages with more than 50 per cent scheduled castes population has further increased the financial arrangement.

The government has recently decided to provide Rs 10 lakh to the villages with a population of 500, Rs 25 lakh for the villages with population between 501 and 1,000 and Rs 50 lakh for the villages where SC population is more than 1,000 persons.

And as per census-2001, there are 391 villages with more than 50 per cent SC population. Development works of these villages will be taken up in the next two years. During the year 2008-09 an amount of Rs 92.75 crore will be spent in the selected villages.

Heading: Plan for  increasing power demand - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana Police, in collaboration with New India Assurance and Oriental Insurance companies, has taken a new initiative by announcing an award of Rs 500 each to the first 200 people who extend their help to the victims of road accidents.

This decision was taken during a state-level seminar organised by Haryana Police for creating awareness about electronic gadgets and use of GPS (Global Positioning System) to prevent road accidents, under the guidance of Ranjeev Dalal, Director General of Police, Haryana and V.N. Rai, ADGP (Law and order) at Police Lines, Panchkula.

The seminar was presided over by B.S. Sandhu, IGP (Law and Order) along with R.C. Mishra, DIG and hosted by Rajpal Singh, AIG (Traffic) Haryana. Sandhu requested the insurance company representatives for financing the traffic rules and safety awareness campaigns through various media.

He said Haryana police has taken various initiatives including high speed interceptors and Traffic Police Stations, in each district, with facilities such as an ambulance with paramedic staff, crane, gypsy, motorcycle speed radar, camera and saw machines.

Rajpal Singh came with up with the idea of data sharing with insurance companies, so the regular offenders can be taken to task, either by increased premiums or by canceling their license.

He said people avoid getting involved because of procedural complications, with the new rules the victims aid need not go through the lengthy procedures. While participating in the seminar, Insurance representatives informed that Insurance companies paid about Rs 3,600 crore every year as claims to road accidents.

Heading: Maruti to set up new R&D centre - Indian Express
Content:
The Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN) and the Haryana Vidyut Prasaran Nigam (HVPN) have prepared an ambitious plan of Rs 3,581 crore to augment power transmission and distribution system in Faridabad. The plan will cater the load demand for the period up to 2021.

A senior official of the Haryana Power Utilities said DHBVN plans to create an infrastructural network of 33 KV sub-stations for electricity distribution in the district. Presently, there is a network of 66 KV sub-stations which are controlled by the HVPN. The DHBVN plans to set up 324 new 33 KV sub-stations in the district which would be connected to 220 KV sub-stations to get power.

The power utilities have long term as well as short term plans to strengthen power transmission and distribution system in Faridabad district. Under short term plan, it is programmed to renovate old transmission systems.

Heading: Police stop marriage of ‘minor’ girl - Indian Express
Content:
In order to strengthen its Research and Development base in India, Maruti Suzuki India has firmed up plans to establish a new R&D centre at Manesar. The company aims to develop new models for the Indian as well as the global market by developing an independent R&D centre which will be at par with the Suzuki Motor Corporation's (SMC) research centre in Japan. An official spokesperson of Maruti Suzuki India told The Indian Express that negotiations are on with the Haryana government for land and the project work will begin soon.

"The R&D centre is likely to be functional by the year 2010. We are also hiring engineers for our new R&D facility. At the beginning of the current fiscal we had about 270 engineers working with us and the number has grown to 570 now. We expect over a 1,000 engineers to be employed by 2010," said the spokesperson. Maruti undertakes Research and Development for its new models at SMC's research centre in Japan and its research facility is in Gurgaon. But with the new R&D centre coming up at Manesar, the company intends to shift the entire R&D base to India. The centre will also include a crash testing facility which will further reduce the manufacturing costs for Maruti.

Nearing its target of pumping in Rs 9,000 crore into the Indian market by 2010, Maruti has invested around Rs 5,000 crore in manufacturing operations in Manesar. The remaining Rs 4,000 crore will be invested in the development of the next generation KB engine plant in Gurgaon, an R&D facility at Manesar, a port at Mundra, rolling out new models like A-star and Splash as well as establishing regional stockyards and brand centres over the next two years.

"Our production capacity will be scaled up to one million units by mid of October to support the launch of A-star in November. We expect our current exports of 53,000 units per annum to increase to 2 lakh units per annum by 2010. To match the quality standards followed worldwide, we are upgrading our Tier-II suppliers by training them at our Centre of Excellence in Gurgaon," he added.

Maruti is conducting several pilot studies to bring services at the customers' doorsteps. The "express service" through which the customer can get his car serviced while catching a movie or the "night shift" model where the servicing can be done at night, is at the testing stage. "Experiments are going on at different locations, once successful the services will be launched in the entire country. Another focus of our company in the coming two years will be to roll out CNG models of our cars," said the official.

Heading: State’s first: Protesters booked for damaging hospital property - Indian Express
Content:
An unidentified phone call today morning led the police to Guru Nanak Palace, where a minor girl, Rekha, of Gopal Nagar, was to tie the knot with Ajay. The police stopped the marriage and called girl's parents to the police station.

SHO Rajinder Sharma said without verifying the facts, they would not allow the marriage to be solemnised. Later, the parents, who could not provide authentic birth proof, had to submit an affidavit, saying that their daughter was a major. Then, the police allowed the marriage to take place. Sources said mother of the girl, Asha Rani, said in her affidavit that Rekha was born on November 10, 1989, and had studied till class VII.

Police are still verifying the facts and a case would be registered if the information provided in the affidavit proves to be wrong, sources said.

Heading: Despite VB probe, work on Amritsar Mall goes on - Indian Express
Content:
State's first case under the Prevention of Violence and Damage to Property Act, 2008, was registered here against various persons for damaging property of Satyam Hospital on Kapurthala Road on Sunday night.

On the fateful night, when a person, who was shot dead by three persons for not delivering food order timely, was declared brought dead at Satyam Hospital, his relatives and friends ransacked the building.

DSP (City-I) Naresh Kumar said further investigation was on. Police sources said that the CCTV in the hospital had recorded important clues against the protesters.

Heading: UT Admn gives nod to e-sampark, sahaj safai kendras in all sectors - Indian Express
Content:
Regardless of the ongoing Vigilance Bureau (VB) probe into the irregularities in Omaxe Novelty Mall scam, the construction is going on unabated.

The Archaeological Survey of India had banned construction of the building, which is situated in the vicinity of the summer palace of Maharaja Ranjit Singh and has surpassed the prescribed height of 15 metres.

Sources said the project had long surpassed the two-year period since its plan was approved by the MC, though illegally, and the construction could not be carried on as further approval was not granted.

The nod of the government is also awaited. The Director, Local Bodies, in a recent communiqué, has directed the MC to seek approval of the government under Section 275 (3) of the Punjab Municipal Corporation Act (PMCA), 1976.

S S Sharma, a social worker who had highlighted the matter, has decided to approach the judiciary. Sources said as per a Section of the PMCA, the MC Commissioner has the discretion to prohibit illegal construction. "The construction is going on in connivance with ministers and higher officials. I wonder why the Local Bodies Department is not taking any action," he said.

Municipal Commissioner DPS Kharbanda, when contacted, said he was not aware of the matter. "I will get it duly checked," he said, adding that the VB probe was on in the case, and the MC House was yet to take a decision on the fate of the project.

"We have not yet received any direction from the government to stall the construction work," he said.

Notably, a month ago, the VB had summoned 10 officials of the MC to record their statements regarding irregularities in the case, which include anomalies in the change of land use and violations of the Punjab Municipal Corporation Act, 1976, besides forceful occupancy of a public street.

Heading: 14 months on, Mohali MC waits for vice-presidents’ poll - Indian Express
Content:
The UT Administration today gave its approval for the setting up of e-sampark centres and Sahaj Safai Kendras (SSK) in all sectors of the city, where the facilities do not exist. The proposal had been moved by the Municipal Corporation on Friday.

In a letter to Mayor Pardeep Chhabra, Finance Secretary Sanjay Kumar, stated that it has been decided to set up e-sampark and sahaj safai kendras in every sector, instructions for which, had been issued to the chief architect.

The e-sampark centres will provide a single window for a number of services, which include the payment of taxes, the issuance of bus passes, senior citizen card, disability identity card, disbursement of pension for old-aged persons, widows and the disabled, payment of electricity bills, issuance of birth and death certificates, the payment of water and sewage bills, open space bookings, community hall bookings, tenant registration, registration of domestic servants, passport application submission, sale of Chandigarh Housing Board forms and the payment of phone bills.

The Sahaj Safai Kendras plan was implemented in 2002 and there are more than 25 such centres at various sectors across the city.

There are, however, many sectors where the SSK has not been set up. Mayor Pardeep Chhabra said: "The work on starting the e-sampark centres and Sahaj Safai Kendras will be started soon."

E-sampark centre to open soon at Central Treasury

The UT Administration has decided to launch a new e-sampark centre in the hub of the city — Sector 17. The centre is likely to be launched in the next few coming days at the Central Treasury in Sector 17. The centre, construction for which is on the verge of completion, shall be catering to the communications and matters related to agencies like the Central Treasury, Municipal Corporation, District Courts, ISBT-17, Estate Office and General Post Office. The concept, which was prepared by officials of Central Treasury, was finally approved by the UT Finance Secretary Sanjay Kumar last week. "Central Treasury is located in the city's hub and operates as a nodal point for public visiting the place in connection with payments and receipts of their dues. With the opening of this Sampark centre, people will be immensely benefited. The helpline, once it starts functioning in Sector 17, shall definitely be a boon for the common man," said a senior Administration official. From the payment of electricity, water and telephone including mobile phone bills, to the sale of passport applications, stamp papers, bus passes, senior citizen cards, innumerable facilities shall be made available through the e-Sampark centre. A proposal is also in the pipeline for having a nationalised bank's branch in the Central Treasury. — ENS

Heading: Terror threats: State to spruce up intelligence network - Indian Express
Content:
Fourteen months after the expiry of the one-year term of its senior vice-president Rishav Jain and junior vice-president Harman Preet Singh Prince, the Mohali Municipal Council (MC) is still to hold an election to determine the new incumbents. But neither the district administration nor the Congress-supported ruling group of councillors seem bothered to hold the democratic process.

Terming it as the "murder of democracy", municipal councillor Kuljit

Singh Bedi, wrote to the Mohali Deputy Commissioner on Monday to immediately convene an MC meeting to discuss the election process.

In 2007 as well, former Deputy Commissioner H I S Grewal, had asked the local SDM Raghbeer Kaur Khaira, to convene a special MC meeting to hold the election.

In February, eight councillors, namely Rajinder Parsad Sharma, Manjit Kaur, Usha Rani, Parkash Wati, Amteshwar Kaur, Suresh Kumar, Gian Chand and Gurmeet Singh, had served a requisition under the provision of Section 25(2) of the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911, to MC president Rajinder Singh Rana, to convene a special meeting of the MC House for conducting the election of vice-presidents.

Equating the delay in conducting the elections to "violation of their rights", they had said the group in power was "avoiding" the issue as it sensed its "possible defeat".

"It was all politically motivated. The delay in polls and the stay on development works just shows the opposition's anti-MC and anti-public approach," said MC president Rajinder Singh Rana.

He, however, fell short of words when asked why he did not exercise his rights according to the provisions of the law to overcome the present stalemate.

Heading: Mohali cop held for ‘accepting’ bribe - Indian Express
Content:
Following recent intelligence inputs received by the Punjab government from their counterparts in Delhi regarding revival of terrorism, the state government is planning to strengthen the existing Intelligence Wing in the state by recruiting more personnel and imparting modern training.

According to high-level sources, the state government was recently apprised by the intelligence agencies in New Delhi of the possible terror threat to Punjab due to cross-border infiltration. "Concrete plans are in the pipeline for strengthening the intelligence network in the state," they said.

Media adviser to Punjab Chief Minister HS Bains said efficient men working in various wings of the Punjab Police would be shifted to the Intelligence Wing. "The CM has also given a nod to strength and modernise the intelligence network," he said.

Bains said the wing personnel would be given training at police academies in Punjab.

"Efforts are already on in this regard and a special budget is also under consideration," he said.

Heading: 3 held for murder of call centre employee - Indian Express
Content:
Policeman suspended, probe ordered

Assitant Sub-Inspector (ASI) of Mohali Police Ranjit Singh was arrested by the Punjab Vigilance Bureau (VB) on Tuesday for allegedly accepting Rs 2,500 as bribe.

Mohali SSP Jatinder Singh Aulakh has released his suspension order and initiated a departmental inquiry against the tainted cop, who was posted at a police station in Phase I, said the Vigilance Bureau DSP Sant Singh Dhaliwal.

He said one Pardeep Kumar, a resident of Phase II had lodged an assault complaint against his housemate Satish Chawla. Singh, who was assigned the investigation of the complaint, arranged a mutual compromise between both the parties, for which he allegedly demanded Rs 10,000 from Kumar. The deal was struck at Rs 5,000 and the first installment of Rs 2,500 was paid on the day of compromise and for receiving the remaining amount of Rs 2,500, the ASI called Kumar at Phase I police station this afternoon, said Dhaliwal.

He claimed that no sooner Kumar handed over the cash to the cop near a tea vend outside the police station at 1.30 pm, the VB sleuths caught him. A case under Sections 7, 13 (2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, has been lodged against the cop, who will be produced before a local court tomorrow, added Dhaliwal.

Speaking to Newsline, Mohali SSP Aulakh warned the district police against indulging in corrupt practices. He said corruption and dereliction of duty will not be tolerated and anybody found wanting will be dealt sternly.

Heading: 92-year-old widow of INA soldier awaits admn’s help - Indian Express
Content:
Three youth were today arrested in connection with the murder of a sales associate of Intelnet, a customer care centre of Vodafone on Saturday.

Devinder Kumar Sahota, a resident of Shivalik Avenue in Ropar was murdered by three motorcycle-borne youth while trying to resist an attempt to steal his mobile phone.

The accused have been identified as Devinder Singh alias Lala, a resident of Bassian village, Pawan Kumar alias Kala, a resident of Cholta Khurd village and Sandeep Singh of Malakpur village. Lala, allegedly stabbed Sahota five times.

The police have also recovered the dagger and a Yamaha motorcycle with a Mohali registration number, allegedly used by the youth, Mohali Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Jatinder Singh Aulakh told Newsline.

Varinderpal Singh, Superintendent of Police-City, who led the police team, told Newsline that two calls were made from Sahota's mobile by Lala, the main accused, which, led to their arrest. They also recovered Sahota's mobile, along with another dagger, which was not used in the crime.

Preliminary investigations have revealed that Lala is facing charges of cheating under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, while a case of causing hurt is pending against Kala. All the three are drug addicts, revealed Varinderpal Singh.

Sahota and Sandeep Dogra, were going back to their paying guest, after dinner at Gian Da Dhaba in the Industrial Focal Point, Phase VIII, at 9 pm. 

They were intercepted by three motorcycle-borne youth near the bus stop, who made enquiries about some address and Lala took Sahota's phone on the pretext of making a call.

He then sat on the motorcycle, with an aim of running away with sahota's mobile phone. Sahota, however, caught hold of Lala to get his mobile.

Provoked over this resistance, Lala, then took out a dagger and stabbed Sahota repeatedly on his head, chest, left forearm and wrist before fleeing away, Varinderpal Singh added.

"Lala had dialed his own mobile number and had also called an acquaintance. We were thus able to lay hands on him," the police officers said.

The police, meanwhile, are conducting inquiries in the case.

Heading: Starting tomorrow, holiday bonanza for Chandigarh babus - Indian Express
Content:
Her memory may be fading, but 92-year-old Gurbachan Kaur still recalls, albeit in snatches, the agony she suffered after her husband's demise.

Having suffered with her husband during the freedom struggle, this widow of Lieutenant Bhag Singh of the INA recently went through a surgery for broken hip, and is now looking for administration's attention.

Gurwinder Singh, grandson of Gurbachan Kaur, said his grandfather had been with the British Army before joining the INA and had founded the INA workshop here to provide artificial limbs after he lost a leg while on duty in Burma. He said his grandmother had always stood by his father during the freedom struggle and had shown exemplary courage in bringing up her six children, including five daughters, when his grandfather was jailed in Japan for seven years.

"My grandfather passed away in 1983. No government officials ever bothered to inquire about her health since she has been admitted to the hospital," said Gurwinder Singh. He said his grandmother had been conferred a Tamar Patra and pension by the government, but the authorities had been denying him the rights of a freedom fighter's kin.

Tarn Taran DC Khushi Ram, who has the additional charge of Amritsar DC, said he was not aware of the matter. "The district administration is doing its best to provide facilities to the freedom fighters and their kin," he said, adding that he would look into the matter.

Heading: Ravinder sent to judicial custody; says requires some time to record statement - Indian Express
Content:
October is the month of festivals but for government officials, the month is synonymous with holidays. Out of the 31 days in October, one can easily count 15 holidays, including the weekends. And if someone goes a step further by taking four casual leaves, then the total number of working days will be reduced to 10.

How: Let's enumerate the holidays first — Eight Saturdays and Sundays, October 2 (Gandhi Jayanti and Id), October 9 (Dussehra), October 14 (Maharishi Balmiki Jayanti), October 28 (Diwali) and October 29 (Vishkarma Day). Two restricted holidays are birth anniversary of Baba Banda Singh Bahadar on October 16 and Karvachauth on October 17.

Now: October 2 (Thursday) is a holiday. Take a leave on Friday and voila — an extended weekend awaits you. The same process can be repeated on Dussehra, which falls on October 9 (Thursday).

Then, if you combine October 14 (Tuesday), October 16 (Thursday) and October 17 (Friday) with two leaves, the holiday count will rise to nine days in a row.

In the last week, October 28 (Tuesday) is Diwali and the next day is Vishkarma Day.

"This month, attendance in government offices is expected to fall steeply as there are so many holidays and the festival season is beginning as well. It's rare for all Dussehra and Diwali to fall in the same month. Generally, most of the holidays are concentrated around April," said a government official.

September also ended with a bang — September 30 was a holiday on account of Aggarsen Jayanti. November and December have two holidays each. November 13 is the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak and November 24 (Monday) is Guru Teg Bahadur's Martyrdom Day. In December, Id-ul-Zoha is on December 9 and Christmas falls on December 25.

List of holidays

Eight Saturdays and Sundays, October 2 (Gandhi Jayanti and Eid), October 9 (Dussehra), October 14 (Maharishi Balmiki Jayanti), October 28 (Diwali) and October 29 (Vishkarma Day).

Two restricted holidays are birth anniversary of Baba Banda Singh Bahadar on October 16 and Karvachauth on October 17

Heading: Want to learn driving? Try - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi-based hotelier Ravinder Singh, the alleged kingpin in the cash-at-judge's-door case, was remanded in judicial custody on Tuesday after the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) refused to further his police remand.

The investigating agency, which had earlier moved an application in the Court requesting to declare Ravinder Singh a proclaimed offender, today refused to seek further police remand of Ravinder Singh. The CBI submitted that Singh, who remained in police remand for 10 days, is not required for further custodial interrogation. It might be recalled that CBI had failed to arrest Ravinder Singh, who surrendered in the Special Court of CBI, Jagdeep Jain on September 19.

Meanwhile, Ravinder moved a handwritten application requesting the court to record his statements under Section 164 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC). In his application, Ravinder stated that he wants to record his statement to unveil the truth and remove the burden on his conscience. The demand was not objected by the CBI.

"Are you not stable? Has CBI done anything wrong to you in police custody?," the Judge asked Ravinder Singh after which Judge Jagdeep Jain asked everyone to vacate the courtroom and spoke to Singh for 15 minutes.

On the other hand, CBI prosecutor requested the court that Ravinder Singh should not be kept in the jail along with other co-accused. On this, Ravinder Singh said that he has no objection even if he is kept with other accused.

The CBI demanded that Ravinder Singh's statement should not be recorded on the same day as of other accused in the court.

In the end, the Special CBI Judge made it clear that he had spoken to Ravinder Singh in person in order to know as to whether he is under some kind of pressure or not. "I have asked him if he wants to record his statement today itself but after pondering over, Ravinder said that he wants some time to record his statement."

The statements of Ravinder Singh will be recorded on October 3 at 11 am.

Later, Ravinder was allowed to speak to his wife and son inside the courtroom. Meanwhile, the CBI also submitted that it has no objection in releasing the amount of Rs 2 lakh seized from the residence of Prakash Ram, junior munshi of Sanjeev Bansal. Surprisingly, at 3.30 pm, another application, this time by the counsel of Ravinder Singh, was moved in the Court demanding permission to withdraw the application given by Ravinder Singh, wherein he had demanded permission to record his statements.

Refusing to allow the counsel to withdraw the hand ritten application by Ravinder Singh, the Court held that Ravinder Singh himself had moved the application and also assured the judge that there was no pressure on him to record his statements.

The judge held that Ravinder Singh should appear in the court on October 3 and tell the court if he wants to record his statement or not.

More witnesses examined by three-judge committee

The Examination of the accused and witnesses in the 'cash at judge's door' scandal by the three-judge committee continued at the UT guesthouse on Tuesday.

The committee comprises Allahabad High Court Chief Justice Hemant Laxman Gokhale, Jammu and Kashmir High Court Chief Justice K S Radhakrishnan and Delhi High Court Justice Madan B Lokur.

Rajiv Gupta, a property dealer from Panchkula and an accused in the case, was examined first. The committee also recorded statements of the original owner of a property located in Solan, of which Justice Nirmal Yadav is a co-owner now. The patwari and a few UT police officers were also examined.

Deviating from the announced schedule, the statement of Delhi-based hotelier Ravinder Singh was not recorded today. Moreover, the committee is yet to record the statement of Justice Nirmal Yadav. On Monday, the statements of Justice Nirmaljit Kaur, former Additional Advocate General (Haryana) Sanjeev Bansal and other accused were recorded by the committee.

Meanwhile, president and secretary of the High Court Bar Association met the committee members today. "We have requested the committee to ensure that the case is taken to its logical conclusion," said Rupinder S Khosla, president of the association.

Heading: Advanced buying leads to confusion - Indian Express
Content:
The Chandigarh Transport Authority has decided to come up with the first automated or virtual driving school and a testing centre on a Public Private Partnership (PPP) model for the city residents. Rejecting the earlier mooted plan of a normal driving school in the premises of the State Transport Authority (STA) building, this planned driving centre will be operated entirely on the basis of Information Technology.

According to officials, a special committee has already been formed to review the project. The possible site for the driving school is said to be the Traffic Park in Sector 23 or the Registration and Licensing Authority (RLA) building.

The project would be implemented on a PPP model for which bids would be soon invited from interested private companies.

Finance Secretary Sanjay Kumar said that keeping the space restriction and available technology in mind, the Administration had come up with the proposal of an automated driving school.

"Driving tests would be conducted with the help of automatic stimulators.The driving school too would work on the same principle. Though the expected time period for the implementation of the projects cannot be declared at the moment due to the involvement of a private company, it would take some time for the finalisation of the terms and conditions," said Sanjay Kumar.

The financial aspects such as the driving and testing fee are said to be decided after working out the costs with the private companies shortlisted for the project. It is said that the testing fee is likely to be somewhere between Rs 15 and 20.

Shelving of the earlier proposed plan of a government-run driving school within the STA building, Sanjay Kumar said that a virtual driving school would serve the purpose in a better way.

Heading: A salute to city’s creator - Indian Express
Content:
Prices crash, private traders postpone procurement

Even while both the Food Corporation of India (FCI) and the Punjab Food and Supply Department had not favoured advancing the paddy procurement date in the state in their reply to the Union Agriculture Ministry, the beginning of buying two days in advance has only resulted in confusion among agencies and farmers.

It was learnt that both the FCI and the Punjab Food and Supply Department, in their replies to the ministry regarding advancing procurement date in view of early procurement in Haryana from September 22, had stated that date need not be advanced as the paddy arriving early was not leviable and therefore would not come to the Central pool.

Terming the decision of advancing the date as political, officials of the procurement agencies said it has led to chaos and many of them had postponed auctions at mandis till October 1.

At Asia's largest grain market, Khanna, the advancing of procurement date saw crashing of prices and arrival of substandard paddy. Even private traders, who were so far buying from farmers, held a meeting today and decided to postpone purchases for at least a week. Harbans Singh Rosha, an arhtiya procuring paddy for private agencies, said the crop coming to the mandis was wet and they could not buy it.

"For now, we have decided to stop procurement for at least a week," he said. Yesterday, on Day One of procurement, the private agencies picked up 45,000 bags at a price ranging between Rs 915 to Rs 960 per quintal. However, today it was mainly the government agencies that procured nearly 15,000 tonnes.

However, the rates crashed to Rs 880 per quintal, the MSP, and were likely to hover around it, secretary of Khanna marketing committee Sukhwinder Singh Mangat said.
