The state, despite floods, is expecting nearly 140 lakh metric tonnes of paddy this year. Mandi Board chairman Ajmer Singh Lakhowal said he was travelling across the state mandis to ensure smooth procurement.

"We began with big mandis yesterday, where early-maturing variety has started to come," he said.

Heading: PU Syndicate fills vacant posts - Indian Express
Content:
A telegram announcing the appointment of Le Corbusier as the architect of Chandigarh will greet visitors at the Le Corbusier Centre, Sector 19, which will open to the public on October 6 (Corbusier's 121st birth anniversary).

In 1951, an official of the Punjab government sent a telegram to the authorities informing that a contract has been signed with Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret for designing the new city as envisioned by the then Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. Now, this document will be showcased at the centre.

The site of the centre was earlier functioned as the office of Corbusier and his associates. "The masterplan of Chandigarh was prepared in this very building," said V N Singh, who is overseeing the construction of the centre.

The nine-room centre will encompass work done by Corbusier during his stay in the city from 1952 to 1965. The first room will display information about the centre and the importance of the building.

The next will house archival records as well as showcase the city's history. Documents pertaining to the creation of Chandigarh, including plans and models made by Corbusier, will be showcased in the next room.

As Corbusier was an artist as well, his paintings will also be displayed at the centre. A digital library is also on the cards. A website, containing all relevant details about the centre, will also be launched on October 6.

The centre has received artifact specimens from the Foundation Le Corbusier in France, Canadian Centre of Architecture in Canada, Heidi Weber Museum in Switzerland, UT Department of Architecture, Government Museum and Art Gallery and Chandigarh College of Architecture. Besides, architects of the city, including M N Sharma and S D Sharma, have also contributed to the centre.

"This will be the third centre in the world dedicated to Corbusier — the other two are in Paris and Switzerland. We aim to preserve the city's heritage and highlight it as well. The whole city is an architectural marvel and a museum in itself. The centre will be a treasure house of information for the residents as well as tourists," said Singh.

Heading: Unruffled, Manpreet says he’s for ending subsidies - Indian Express
Content:
The much-awaited appointments to the vacant posts in Panjab University were finally approved on Tuesday. The Panjab University Syndicate cleared the appointments to the posts of Director Sports, Finance and Development Officer and Controller of Examinations.

Dr C S Grewal has been appointed as the regular university director of Physical Education. He was earlier working with the Punjab Engineering College.

The syndics also approved Professor Ashwani Bhandari, department of Mathematics and advisor (Examinations) to be given the complete charge of the post of Controller of Examinations.

Meanwhile, the appointments of Vikram Nayyar as the Finance and Development Officer (FDO) and Dr Amar Partap Singh, director-professor for Swami Sarvanand Giri PU regional centre, Bajwara, Hoshiarpur were also approved.

These posts have been lying vacant for long and the university had expressed its inability to fill up these posts due to the non-availability of 'suitable candidates'.

Apart from this, the Syndicate also approved the conferment of the Vigyan Rattan award upon G S Khush, Adjunct Professor, University of California, USA and the Udyog Rattan award to Sunil Mittal, Chairman and CEO, Bharti Group. Both are Panjab University alumni.

The syndics also approved the execution of an MoU with PGIMER for the enrollment and registration of candidates for pursuing their PhD research and the University of Western Australia for activities like exchange programme of staff, joint research activities, conferences, academic meetings and exchange of academic material.

The prevailing confusion regarding the nomenclature of University Business School (UBS) at Ludhiana too seems to have finally been resolved. The Syndicate clarified that the school has been named UBS, Panjab University Regional Centre, Ludhiana.

Admission cleared for suspended SOPU president

The Panjab University Syndicate cleared the admission of SOPU President Brinder Dhillon to the Department of Laws on Tuesday. Dhillon's admission was suspended after his name figured in a stabbing case in which Simrandeep Singh Sandhu, a law student, was seriously injured.

The issue was vigorously debated in the Syndicate meeting and most of the members had expressed their displeasure at the defiance of the chairman of the law department in denying admission to Dhillon despite the same being approved by the Syndicate.

Sources claimed that Syndicate members questioned as to why, despite Dhillon's admission being cleared by the Syndicate and the

Vice-Chancellor, the chairman had denied admission to him.

Taking serious note of the defiance by the chairman of the department, the Syndicate today passed orders to grant admission to Dhillon.

Sources add that Dhillon's suspension was unjustified as his name did not figure in the FIR registered after the stabbing incident. According to sources, "The authorities had decided that anyone whose name figures in the FIR should be placed under suspension but Dhillon's name never figured in the FIR, so how could he be denied admission."

Dhillon was arrested by the police along with Govind Khatra, another PU student, following investigations in the stabbing case and was later released on bail. Dhillon was thus denied admission to the third semester by the department. When contacted, Dhillon said, "It was merely due to an ego clash between various factions of PU authorities that my admission was kept pending. PU authorities had decided that any student whose name figures in the FIR would be denied admission, but my name is not there in the FIR. There was no justification for denying admission to me."

Heading: 25 kids among 35 held for trying to cross border - Indian Express
Content:
His call for reforms and ending sops has not been heeded, but Punjab Finance Minister Manpreet Badal says he has not given up hope and sooner or later others too would realise the need for fiscal reforms.

At his first meet-the-press today, Manpreet openly reiterated that as Finance Minister of a state reeling under an acute financial crisis, his job demands that he says the right things and presses for some hard decisions.

"If I love Punjab, I would have to chart the financial destiny of the state. I would rather change my profession than win as an MLA time and again without making any difference to the state or accomplish the task I am shouldering within the government," he added.

So while he feels these are exciting times to be a politician as the economy is booming and they can make changes, he said his position as Punjab FM was not an enviable one. "The challenges facing Punjab are enormous. The debt is around Rs 57,000 crore and growing. We have to stop borrowing for our day-to-day expenses and bring down our revenue and fiscal deficits. So when I speak, it is not to embarrass anyone, but I want to fight for Punjab," he said, while denying that he has ever been snubbed by the CM for his stand on reforms.

The Finance Minister said Punjab was critically short of at least Rs 3,000 crore, which could go into health and education sectors, which were being deprived of funds.

"These additional funds could come from additional taxes, better tax compliance or ending subsidies. But we need to significantly increase our plan size and there will be no stopping Punjab if we are able to tide over the financial crisis," he said.

His second major concern is the stagnant industrial sector, which has witnessed no buoyancy in the past 20 years. "It is only through industrialisation that we will take the next step to prosperity. We do not have the resources to hand out concessions or concede any sops to the industry. We need to spend around Rs 300 to 500 crore to develop a land bank in the state of about 10,000 to 20,000 acres by making a budgetary provision," he said.

The attitude of administrative machinery also came under a scathing attack of the FM. Asserting that they do not identify with the people they govern, he said, "We need to rectify administrative arrogance and apathy. They need to be sensitised towards the problems of the people of the state." When asked about controversy over delay in Finance Department's nod to the Speaker's tour, he said, "As a Finance Minister all I can do in this regard is reject files which do not adhere to the Punjab Financial Rules."

Heading: Another held, youths were inebriated, say police - Indian Express
Content:
BSF's 41 battalion today nabbed 35 members of five families, including 25 children and five women, for trying to cross the border in Tarn Taran. A case was registered against the accused, 30 of whom have been sent to jail after being produced in the court, while the remaining five have been sent in police remand.

Tarn Taran SSP H S Chahal said the accused were trying to cross over to Pakistan under the cover of darkness from Khalra sector. He added that during investigation, it had come to the fore that the accused had come from Myanmar through West Bengal and wanted to go to Pakistan. The SSP said Rs 1,527 in Indian currency were recovered from the accused.

Three held with heroin

The Tarn Taran police have arrested three persons, Sarvan Singh, Jugraj Singh and Saraj Singh, and recovered 3-kilogram heroin worth Rs 15 crore from them. Sources said the heroin packets had markings in Arabic and Saraj Singh possessed a Pakistani sim card, which he tried to destroy by chewing it. SSP H S Chahal said accused had links with smugglers based in Pak and the ones lodged in Amritsar Central Jail and Tihar Jail.

Heading: Moments  of truth - Indian Express
Content:
With the arrest of Harpreet Singh alias Dalli, a resident of Durali village , from Ambala today, two of the six youth, who allegedly kidnapped a German national from Hotel Taj GVK and molested her on Sunday, are in the police net. Another accused, 20-year-old Pankaj, was arrested on Monday. Harpreet has a previous police record with two cases of rioting and hurt registered against him.

According to the police, the youth did not plan to abduct the girl. "They were inebriated and just loitering around Hotel Taj when they saw the girl," said a police officer.

Both the vehicles — Mahindra Scorpio (HR-58-8123) and Maruti 800 (HR-01-S-8794) — used in the incident have also been impounded. The Scorpio belongs to one Kaka, a resident of Ambala and Zila Parishad president of village Kakroli. At the time of incident, it was being driven under a fake registration number (HR-58-2123), said the police.

Three of the absconding accused have been identified as Jolly (a resident of Samalkha), Sukhi and Sompal (residents of Bitta village). None of them have reportedly returned to their house since the police started conducting raids to trace them. All the accused are in their early 20s and small-time property dealers, said police.

During interrogation, Pankaj told the police that none of them own a car and had borrowed the Mahindra Scorpio for coming to Chandigarh. Later, he borrowed the Maruti car to drop the victim at Sector 20.

According to the police, the girl was taken to a farmhouse in Kardhana village on Jagadhari road. The victim has also identified the place. Experts from the Central Forensic Sciences Laboratory will inspect the spot on Wednesday.

Pankaj, meanwhile, was produced before the Chief Judicial Magistrate today and remanded in police custody for three days. While seeking custody of the accused, the prosecution pleaded that Pankaj had used a sickle to threaten the girl, which was later discarded by Jolly in a garbage dump near the farmhouse.

Talking to Newsline, Pankaj, said he was completely innocent. "In fact, I fought with my friends and saved the girl," he said. Pankaj added that after the girl drove the car out of the hotel, she was taken to a farmhouse in Samalkha. Later, they shifted to another farmhouse near Kardhana and then to another unidentified house. Pankaj evaded further questions on the sequence of events and his background.

Heading: Director’s cut - Indian Express
Content:
I write what I believe in, Sudha Murty portrays portraits from real life & experiences in her books

One thread is of truth and the other is that of imagination. Sudha Murty weaves them together flawlessly to create stories that are honest, simple and real. Novels, short stories for children, travelogues, technical books; the author and chairperson of the Infosys Foundation, who writes both in English and Kannada, doesn't restrict herself to any genre or image. "It's easy to write in Kannada, for in your mother tongue you can express many emotions in one word. But when I wish to be meticulous and precise, I write in English. While reading my books you don't need a dictionary, they sell without any promotions. I don't write for awards, money or publishers. I write what I believe in and honestly. Real-life experiences and how humans react to different situations engross me and form the foundation of my books,'' Murty was here to meet the team at Infosys Chandigarh and interact with members of the British Library on her books and writing style. Mahashweta, The Old Man and His God, How I Taught My Grandmother to Read and Other Stories...smiles the lovely Sudha are all about real people and experiences, every book beginning with a different inspiration. "I have to feel, see, realize the situation to write about it and in the long run, honesty always strikes a chord and appeals to readers. But yes, writing is a lonely process,'' when experiences become unbearable to hold in the head and heart, Sudha writes and what she gains in the process is sheer joy and pure happiness. Her canvas is large and as a writer when she meets people and deals with situations, she can easily translate them into stories and an eye for a story and ability to put it down with sincerity is what makes a writer. While writing, don't judge or decide for others, don't make any issue a moralistic one, Sudha who's been writing for more than 30 years gives valuable words of advice to young authors. As for what engrosses this voracious reader, Sudha says it's history which she now pores over, especially books written about India by foreigners, "it gives a further and absorbing view of India, for it's a country that never ceases to surprise.'' Write on.

Heading: Getting Personal - Indian Express
Content:
Stories form the epicenter of his mind space. Real-life incidents, people, bits and pieces of news, snatches of imagination...like little quakes they trigger off a stream of words that fill out blank papers on his desk. He carries them all over, these stories of his, till one fine day, one of them made a blast at the box office. Aamir was an unusual script and screenplay to be reckoned with. Who would have thought, that with a treatment so distant, yet palpable and a face not so familiar would make a dent? "But it did, didn't it," Rajkumar Gupta, debutante director of this common man's story was convinced his film will be a success. After lugging around the script, banging his head with producers and makers, knocking on moneyed doors, Gupta finally got UTV on his side. But why take Rajeev Khandelwal? "Because a star becomes larger than the character." But in Aamir, the Mumbai city was one of the characters - crowded, jammed, old,tired, blocks of buildings staring down..."and a camera movement following from a measured distance." Only a protege of Anurag Kashyap would traverse the cinematic territory like that! Assistant director to Kashyap on Black Friday and No Smoking, Gupta feels that a director needs to be sure and sincere. "He has to know everything, he has to believe in the integrity of the story," saying this Gupta cancels the thought of being genre specific. Although he stems from a league of bold and experimental filmmakers, he feels that typecasting in one role stunts the growth. "Being a master of all genres, now that's the true test of a filmmaker."

In Zirakpur with Mitul Dikshit at Dikshant International School, where he interacted with children, Rajkumar's journey from Hazaribagh in Jharkhand to the studios of Mumbai has been an interesting one. "The love for cinema was not a one-film affair. It was slow and steady, till I knew this was my calling." The writer in him comes first, he's writing constantly, penning yet another thriller-drama, getting inspired by real life, but not for long. "May be two more, and it will be pens down." The idea is to direct, to translate the script of another on to the screen. "Grand plans in making," he pans away.

Heading: And the winner is... - Indian Express
Content:
She's always been a head turner and while Meyhar Bhasin continues to walk the ramp (selectively though), not many are aware that the lissome lady also runs an academy of modelling and grooming. Now, the seven-year-old Meyhar Bhasin Academy in Delhi is spreading wings. "I've always wanted to come to Punjab and what better time than now," the model has tied up with Panchkula-based Vermanis to house her institute in Sector 2. "It's an attempt to provide a unique platform to people of all ages and walks of life to not only understand their potential but also learn social skills that will ensure success in both their professional as well as personal lives," spoke the immaculately dressed Meyhar at the formal announcement of her institute.

Having learnt herself through the "hard way", Meyhar says she decided to step on new turf as there weren't any professional personality grooming or modelling institutes this side of the country. "There is so much talent here but it's not in the loop like Delhi or Mumbai. Our aim is to offer that connection," Meyhar will dish out Personality Development Courses for people of all age groups here. "Courses for children as young as five years that's designed to teach them social etiquettes and formal dining apart from personal grooming," she adds. Also being dished out are grooming sessions for adults, modelling workshops and special sessions for would-be brides and corporate. Having previously trained Miss India pageant contestants to corporate managers, Meyhar is looking at just about anyone looking for a personality change. "Our modelling workshops are ideal for wannabe models looking to make a career." And the courses are priced at Rs 14,900.

As for her own career, Meyhar's just back from Paris and Dubai where she walked the ramp. "I have been emceeing for a while now apart from hosting shows on television." The latest being her live coverage of the India Couture Week. "I am now gearing up to host a beauty show on CNBC and another one on Star Sports." So does multi-tasking come easy? "Since it's all inter-linked I am making the most of it all," she signs off.

Heading: Foot loose - Indian Express
Content:
The girls outshone the boys, Sufi sounds scored over popular music and a television couple got their ticket to Bollywood....it's been a month of winning announcements on television

Day after day, week after week, month after month, each one of us has found favourites to tune into on television. We have dutifully watched the team of girls battle it out with the boys on the dance floor on Star One's Zara Nachke Dikha. We have also religiously tuned into NDTV Imagine to catch the various genres sing out loud on Lux Junoon- Kuchh Kar Dikhaane Ka and then we have also followed every move that the contestants made on their 13-week journey on Kaun Jeetega Bollywood Ka Ticket on 9X. Channel-surfing, late-night viewing, voraciously SMSing... at the end of it all, we were exhausted. The journey has been long, close to four months, and realising that the audience out there is looking for a breather, the results on all three popular reality shows are out! In case you missed out here's who won, what and where.

LADIES TAKE IT ALL: We always knew they were better. After four months and 23 episodes, 'The Girls vs Boys' war finally came to an end as the 'Meethi Churi' team walked away with the Zara Nachke Dikha Champions Trophy. With their grace, moves and style, the judges' verdict said that the girls were unarguably the best. Be it the perfection of Karishma Tanna, the sensuality of Mouni Roy and Narayani Shastri or the vibrant energy of Ashita Dhawan and Delnaaz Paul, the team showcased girl power all the way. In the final 'Face Off Round' Ashita amazed the judges with her incomparable steps and beat her toughest opponent, Bakhtyaar Irani. Along with Malaika Arora Khan and Chunky Pandey, the finale was judged by 'masterji' Saroj Khan, whose nazar did not miss a single mistake! Apart from top notch acts by the teams, the hosts and the judges; the finale included three hours of drama and a huge protest from the Tez Talwaars (Boy's team) who voiced their displeasure against the scores. However, the judges stood by their decision and unanimously said that they were very proud of the girls. Mouni Roy won the best dancer of the series and prize money of Rs 1 lakh. As the team prize, the girls will soon be off for a vacation to Egypt on a couple holiday!

SUFI SCORES AND SO DOES SHE: It's finally out in the open. Sufi scores over not just traditional fare but even over popular Bollywood music. The journey to decide India's favourite genre of music and its most talented singer came to a resounding finale with Harshdeep Kaur from 'Sufi Ke Sultan' being crowned the winner of Lux Junoon Kuchh Kar Dikhaane Ka. Wowing audiences with her melodious voice, Harshdeep left everyone spellbound with her matchless performance that garnered the maximum number of viewer votes to win the title. Over the past 17 weeks, Harshdeep fought off intense competition to emerge as the winner. "Manzilein unko milti hain jinke kadmon mein jaan hoti hai! Pankhon se kuch nahi hota, hoslon se udaan hoti hai!" remarked an overwhelmed Harshdeep at the end of the final episode which also saw wonderful performances by mentors Ustad Rahat Fateh Ali Khan, Ila Arun, Anand Raj Anand.

TICKET TO BOLLYWOOD: Popular television actor Naman Shaw and his partner Bindu have won the grand finale of the reality show Lux Kaun Jeetega Bollywood Ka Ticket on 9X that saw couples from various zones compete. The winning couple was formally given the title and of course a movie contract with Balaji Telefilms and Popcorn Entertainment by actor Suniel Shetty. This popular 'Jodi' had their mentor Shabana Azmi rooting for them right from the first episode and when their names were announced. "The journey of 13 weeks has been the most memorable. This ticket gives us the chance to try our luck in Bollywood which is the ultimate dream for every actor," chorused the couple.

Heading: Losses may cross Rs 1,000 crore mark - Indian Express
Content:
Homing in

If home décor is on your mind, then this is right time to do up your interiors in style. Home Spell, Sector 22, a fine furnishing store, promises to give top notch elegance to your interiors. Vipin Mahajan, MD, who has franchisee for Maishaa in Chandigarh, Panchkula and Mohali, tells us, "Used as bed-cum-quilt covers, the fine Japanese fabric is priced between Rs 1000 and 13000 per metre." They also have bed-sheets of Bombay Dying and Delmia. Home Spell also houses Magpie utensils that are made of pure steel from Germany and are priced between Rs 200 and Rs 60,000. Also worth a dekko here are imported statues, candles, and fragrances. What's more is that it has many products on about 50 per cent discount.

Watchful Care

Titan announced the launch of the Titan - WWF collection, a unique range of watches inspired by some of India's endangered species. The Titan -WWF collection is inspired from six endangered species - the Tiger, Indian Rhino, Gangetic River Dolphin, The Red Panda, Whale Shark and Oliver Ridley Turtle. Every watch in the collection captures the strength and beauty of each of these magnificent animals. The collection is a perfect accessory for the season. This unisex collection has been designed and crafted with great attention by Titan's in-house Design Studio in close consultation with WWF.

Jewel Delight

An enterprise headed by Rakesh Jain along with his sons Ankur and Sahil, Ethno celebrates its second anniversary. The group specialists in jadau jewellery, traditional and modern jewellery in plain and coloured stones and exclusive diamond polka jewellery from Jaipul. Clients can also get customized jewellery designed. All kind of solitaires from round to fancy shapes in all sizes are also available.

Heading: On way home, journalist shot - Indian Express
Content:
The eight-member Central team that is in Himachal Pradesh to assess the losses and damages caused due to heavy rains visited the Shimla district today. One team visited Narkanda, Kumarsain and Rampur while the other went to Theog Kotkhai, Gumma, Hatkoti and Rohru.

Briefing the media about the damages, Horticulture Minister Narender Bragta said, though the preliminary reports of the revenue and administration have accessed losses at Rs 510 core, the figure might cross Rs 1000 crore.

The state has submitted a loss report of Rs 2,076 crore to the Central team, said the officials of the revenue department.

"Forty-three lives, 481 cattle and 23,972 hectares of land under agriculture and horticulture was lost in Shimla district. Rs 15 crore were provided for immediate relief to families who lost their family members, cattle and crops and restoration of roads to ensure transportation of apple was done on priority basis," said Bragta.

Replying to a question, he claimed the administration the apple growers were not affected and National Highway and state highway were restored within 24 hours. "There are no apple boxes stranded in the orchards to my knowledge," said Bragta as he lashed out at former chief minister Virbhadra Singh for behaving in an irresponsible manner during the time of natural calamity.

"I have returned from a nine-day tour of the affected villages in the district, the former chief minister has no right to say that the administration did not restore the vital facilities in the area," said Bragta.

HPMC regional office to be shifted

It has been decided to shift the regional office of Himachal Pradesh Horticulture Processing and Marketing Corporation (HPMC) from Shimla to Gumma for better coordination. Bragta said in the meeting of the HPMC decision was taken to set up fruit processing plants in the apple belt of Rohru, Jarol, Kotkhai and Gumma by next year.

Heading: Delhi couple enters Guinness Book for max letters to editor - Indian Express
Content:
25-year-old journalist of news channel found dead in her car near Vasant Kunj

A 25-year-old journalist with the news channel Headlines Today died under mysterious circumstances while driving back home late Monday night. The police found Soumya Vishwanathan, 25, dead in her car on Nelson Mandela Marg, near Vasant Kunj, with a bullet lodged in her skull.

The police had initially received a call about an accident and found Vishwanathan's car smashed against the central verge of the road. But a postmortem at AIIMS found a bullet stuck in her right skull (see box). The police said she was shot from a close range; there are conflicting reports whether she was driving at the time.

Police said the incident occurred sometime between 3.10 am — when Vishwanathan last called up home after leaving office at 3.02 am — and 3.55 am, when a rickshaw-puller called the Police Control Room to inform about the incident.

"The murder motive is not clear yet. We are investigating it, and a murder case has been registered," DCP (Southwest) Shalini Singh said.

The police are still not clear whether it was a case of robbery, personal enmity or road rage.

Abhishek Bhalla, a colleague at Headlines Today, said Vishwanathan left the TV channel's office at Jhandewalan at 3.02 am after her shift got over. She lived in C-9, Vasant Kunj. "She was looking forward to meeting her sister and brother-in-law who had come down from Vietnam after a long time," Bhalla said. "She had even taken leave to spend time with them — she was to go on leave from Tuesday."

According to police, Vishwanathan called up home and spoke with her father at 3.10 am. She told him she would be home in the next 15 or 20 minutes, the police said.

The area's DCP and ACP were present at the AIIMS trauma centre on Tuesday afternoon and were informed by doctors that a bullet was found stuck in the skull. The windowpanes on the right-hand side were found broken. Officials said Vishwanathan's belongings were intact in the car.

The police are questioning the rickshaw-puller who called the PCR to get a lead in the case and are also checking the 25-year-old's call details.

"Soumya always was very enthusiastic about her work and was one of the best persons in the channel's production unit," Bhalla said. "She stayed back in office after the blasts in Gujarat and Maharashtra."

Ashwini George, a family friend and journalist at The Indian Express, said, "Her sister Shubha and Soumya's brother-in-law had arrived from Vietnam two days ago — she was very close to her sister."

She was cremated at Lodhi Road crematorium on Tuesday afternoon. A graduate from Kamla Nehru College, Vishwanathan passed out of the Indian Institute of Mass Communication in Dhenkanal in 2004. Her father M K Vishwanathan retired from Voltas company.

Bullet fired from country-made gun?
Police sources said postmortem has found the injury on her skull resulted from a 0.315-calibre bullet. They said a country-made pistol was used in all probability. Sources said they are also investigating the possibility of the journalist being shot inside the car — they feel it was not possible for the wound to have occurred from a bullet outside since the car was moving at a speed of 70 to 80 kilometres per hour when the incident took place.

The police have also found strands of hair in the car's backseat, as well as blood stains, which they are currently investigating.

Heading: Anti-smoking   campaign: AIIMS bans puffs at its campus - Indian Express
Content:
A Delhi-based couple have made it to the Guinness Book of World Records for writing the maximum number of 'Letters to Editors' in various Indian newspapers.

Subhash Chandra Agrawal, a businessman entered the record book for writing maximum letters in a life span, while his wife Madhu Agrawal for writing maximum letters in a year.

Agrawal has written 3,699 letters till January 31, 2006, and his wife penned 447 letters in 2004.

Agrawal wrote his first letter to editors in 1967 in Dainik Hindustan narrating an unpleasant experience with a bus conductor for not issuing a ticket.

Interestingly, the letter led to instant impact and authorities swung into action.

Sharing his passion for writing letters, Agrawal said, "After writing a letter to editor of newspaper, I realised the power of media".

Seeing the impact of his letter, Agrawal continued his passion to write despite his physical handicap, hardening of finger, which makes writing difficult for him.

Besides raising public issues through letters to editor, he gradually started using the Right to Information Act to bring undisclosed information into public domain. His RTI pleas range from travel expenses of judges to cremation facilities for public.

Heading: Friends recall Soumya: They always imagine her smiling - Indian Express
Content:
The country's premier medical institute, AIIMS, has taken a lead in implementing the nationwide ban on smoking in public places, by declaring itself a strictly smoking free zone from Wednesday.

"We have declared our premises strictly smoking free from today itself," Dr Bir Singh, Professor Community Medicine AIIMS said.

He added that the institute guards have been given the additional responsibility to ensure that no one smokes in the campus.

The move comes in the backdrop of the Union government's decision to ban smoking in public places from October 2, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.

"We decided to take the lead a day before the entire country does so to spread the message of anti-smoking," he said.

The ban on smoking in public places like offices, restaurants, hotels, court buildings, libraries and railway stations nationwide will come into effect from tomorrow.

A mini-exhibition on "Smoking and its ill-effects" has been organised for general public at the institute's Central Lawn and Raj Kumari Amrit Kaur OPD for a week.

According to estimates, 184 million people smoke every day which include 19 per cent Cigarette, 54 per cent bidi, 37 per cent Gutkha. An average of 2800 people die due to tobacco related diseases in the country.

Cancer of lungs, lips, tongue, oral cavity, throat and larynx, uterus and urinary bladder are some of the common tobacco related diseases.

"The country spends nearly 240 crores every year on tobacco related advertisements. Every year in India nearly one million people die due to tobacco consumption," Singh, also the Secretary-General for Indian Association of Preventive and Social Medicine (IAPSM), said.

Heading: Chandni Chowk to go 'green' with solar rickshaw - Indian Express
Content:
"Twenty-five is no age to die. I have a photograph of her smiling at her house, and half thought she would simply get up and start talking again," a friend, IIMC-Dhenkanal batchmate and journalist at one of the capital's dailies said recollecting Soumya Vishwanathan.

A favourite with every one of her batchmates and colleagues, she said Vishwanathan was "completely unassuming and quiet from afar, but if you got to know her, she was the most effervescent and fabulous person around." Another batchmate said, "At IIMC, miles away from home and feeling lonely, we used to end up criticising the food. After the second semester break, our entire class was on way back to Dhenkanal together and she had brought 150 idlis for us."

Another friend, also a journalist, said, "She was someone who must have scored the highest 'votes' on Facebook — always among top three 'most attractive, intelligent, smart, committed, organized' people. One of the youngest in the 2003-04 IIMC-Dhenkanal batch, yet with a very sound head on her shoulders, mature, sensible, and intelligent."

Batchmates, she said, remember her as someone with great potential, talent and focus. "TV production, filmmaking, documentary making was always her area of interest and that's exactly what she chose to do even after our diploma in English print journalism at IIMC. She had also done quite well at work and was one of those sought-after, dedicated and committed professionals."

"Soumya," her friend said, "got along well with everyone at our very diverse class at Dhenkanal and had practically no hang-ups. The moment I think of her I imagine her smiling — as graceful as ever and always a great peacemaker."

After joining work, "we only shared virtual networks like Orkut and Facebook and barely chatted. But I so wish we had — it still does not sink in that I can no longer post a 'Hey, how r u doing' on her Facebook wall or see her profile as a permanent fixture on the left side of my Facebook homepage.

"For Soumya, for all women journalists driving home after one of those busy nights at work, for a young life gone, I hope and pray that she may be at peace and get justice."

Heading: Private schools plea to govt: let us hike tuition fees to meet teachers’ pay raise - Indian Express
Content:
The historic Chandni Chowk areas of the national capital will soon witness solar-powered cycle rickshaws buzzing past its crowded arterial roads.

Developed by Durgapur-based Central Mechanical Engineering Research Institute (CMERI), the green rickshaw, named Soleckshaw, will be launched in Chandni Chowk on the occasion of birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.

The pedicab, built from the scratch within eight months, is easy to drive, both on plain as well as uphill roads, without any strain of imbalance, common in current cycle rickshaws.

It a re-designed version of the ubiquitous cycle rickshaw, is equipped with a robust low-power high-torque brush less DC motor developed by Crompton Greaves on specifications provided by CMERI.

Weighing about 200 kg, the pedicab, run by solar-powered battery, can ply at a maximum speed of 15 kmph.

"The Soleckshaw is robust and ergonomically designed to take the drudgery out of rickshaw pulling," Gopal Sinha, Director CMERI said.

A central solar panel has been set up in the Chandani Chowk Metro station area where the batteries for Soleckshaw can be re-charged.

These green environment friendly rickshaws are expected to ply within a three-kilometre radius from the metro station.

The solar-powered rickshaws will be initially introduced as a pilot project in Chandni Chowk and later extended to other areas in the city.

Delhi Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit will launch the Soleckshaw tomorrow in the presence of Science and Technology Minister and Chandani Chowk MP Kapil Sibal.

Heading: Sushruta Trauma Centre: Lone neurosurgeon gone, specialists available only in ‘office hours’ - Indian Express
Content:
The average hike is expected to be Rs 2,000 per quarter; likely by November

Private, unaided schools have sought the state government's permission to charge students more fees so that the implementation of the sixth pay commission recommendations — which means higher salaries for teachers and other staff — does not become a load on authorities.

Principal of Mahavir Model Senior School and Chairman of the National Progressive Schools Conference, S L Jain, said on Tuesday that the 100-member body had sent a request to the Directorate of Education for permission to increase fees by 50 to 60 per cent. Jain said: "The government has enforced the new pay scales and this has increased expenditure by almost 50 per cent on an average. We have approached the state under Section 17(3) of the Delhi Education Act to allow us to raise tuition fees."

The tuition fee covers the lion's share of a school's earnings. "We are totally dependent on it. Parents also know that a teacher cannot deliver if she is not paid what she deserves," Jain added. The Forum for Promotion of Quality Education, with 20 member schools, is also planning to put forward a similar proposal.

The increase in fees will be determined by each school. The average is expected to be Rs 2,000 per quarter — and the hike could be as soon as in November.

Education Minister Arvinder Singh Lovely had said last week that the audit reports of each school would be checked thoroughly before permission was granted to hike fees. The Director of Education, Government of Delhi, Chandra Bhushan Kumar, added, "We will meet principals soon to discuss the proposed increase. We realise a hike is required but the exact amount will be decided only once we asses a school's financial records."

Chairperson of Shriram School Manju Bharatram said various factors could determine the quantum of hike. She said: "Bigger schools — with almost 50 student per class — may not require the money as much as a smaller institution does."

Meanwhile, parents have no other option but to accept this imminent change, some cutting corners already while others blame the pay commission.

Tanu Mishra, whose daughter is in a West Delhi school, has said the school sounded out parents last month that fees would go up by almost 40 per cent. "My husband is a government employee, and also the sole earning member. This will eat into our resources," Mishra said.

Venu Mathur's daughter studies in a reputed school in south Delhi. She is already juggling her monthly expenses to accommodate this change. "We can't pull our children out of school. We have to pay," she said. Self-employed professional Shailendra Narain feels the same way.

"Employees will get annual hikes. But it is a little difficult for us," he said.

Heading: Mayor spends on study, projects stay on paper - Indian Express
Content:
At this hospital, trauma care is a nine to four job. And patients who come after work hours, pay dearly for the delay. Since midnight on Tuesday, the Sushruta Trauma Centre has been functioning without a neurosurgeon. This spells agony for road accident victims, especially the ones with head injuries.

The current neurosurgeon's contract was not extended and hiring a replacement was not on the priority list of the hospital administration.

With senior specialists available only from 9 am to 4 pm, patient care was already suffering. Now with the neurosurgeon gone, hospital employees are up in arms against the administration demanding better infrastructure.

Despite knowing that the hospital's only neurosurgeon was leaving in September, the hospital administration has not appointed another surgeon to take over his responsibilities. "In a trauma centre, most cases are of head injuries. In such a scenario having only one neurosurgeon is irresponsible. Things can only get worse when the only surgeon is also shown the door," said a senior doctor in the trauma centre.

So where does this leave the patient? Every time a head injury patient arrives at the trauma centre, getting a neurosurgeon to look at the patient will involve paperwork to request 'cover' from Lok Nayak Hospital, a task that could take hours which could prove fatal for critical patients. The hospital is already sharing its radiologist with Aruna Asaf Ali Hospital.

The Medical Superintendent Dr Yadu Lal dismissed these problems as petty office politics. "These are small issues common in every workplace. We have arranged for a cover from Lok Nayak Hospital till the government fills the post," said Dr Lal.

While trauma centres the world over are attached to big hospitals for back-up, Sushruta trauma centre was de-linked from Lok Nayak Hospital and set up as an independent unit in February 2007. Trauma centres are attached to big hospitals mainly to keep 30 per cent beds free in case of disasters and emergencies.

Patients, as per the rules, are to be shifted to the trauma centre's parent body after being given primary medical care within 96 hours. "The concept of keeping beds vacant for other trauma victims just does not exist here. Doctors come late to work, only one OT works and most patients keep waiting as surgeries are delayed with surgeons not available," said a senior doctor at Sushruta.

Heading: Electoral rolls of 24 constituencies out on October 6 - Indian Express
Content:
Rs 50 lakh gone 'learning' in 16 months, MCD yet to start most work

Mayor Arti Mehra has used up more than Rs 50 lakh of taxpayers' money on "study tours" in the last 16 months. This, even as some projects conceived by the municipality still remain on paper.

Among cities Mehra has toured in her mission to gain first-hand knowledge are New York, Paris, Liverpool, Brussels, Beijing Jerusalem, and that mother of expensive trips: the eight-day tour of to Germany and Italy last month that cost Rs 36 lakh. According to municipal figures, Rs 5.50 lakh was spent on Mehra alone during this trip.

Closer home, Mehra led an MCD delegation to Bangalore in October 2007 to study garbage management. On return, she assured that MCD would soon introduce the 'garbage-on-wheels' project that would go door-to-door to collect garbage. Eleven months on, leave alone initiating the project MCD is unable to even maintain existing dustbins or dhalaos.

Mehra, however, said technical bids for the project "are done — the financial bids, too, will be done soon."

But a cursory glance at MCD's pending list of projects tells the tale: most schemes promised last year are still at the stage of "proposed plans". Among these are the semi-automatic multi-level parking lots with smart cards, a municipal habitat centre at Raja Garden, making roads free of potholes, door-to-door garbage collection, and enhancing the Capital's green cover.

Interestingly, the MCD announced the need to construct semi-automatic multi-level parking lots with smart cards around this time last year. But it seemingly woke up last month and realised the need for more first-hand knowledge. Result: a delegation of seven senior officials, along with Mehta, flew off to Germany, and then to Italy.

Criticising the expensive tours, Leader of Opposition in MCD Jai Kishan Sharma said, "The concept of solid waste management is absurd for our country where most kitchen and household waste is fluid." Western countries, he said, usually generate a lot of solid waste that can be compressed and put to other use.

"The parking project has been floating for far too long now — the MCD should have made some headway by now," Sharma said.

He claimed Mehra is yet to submit reports of her study trips at the MCD. "What is the use of these trips if the civic agency doesn't benefit from knowledge gathered by our mayor?" he asked.

But Mehra said she has submitted all reports to concerned departments. "The tours are made to know how other civic agencies manage their civic issues," she said. "We have learnt quite a bit from these tours. This can't be called wastage of public money."

Heading: Court clears extradition of fraud accused to New Jersey - Indian Express
Content:
With the Assembly elections due in November, electoral rolls of all constituencies will be rolled out in two phases by October 15.

According to the Chief Electoral officer (CEO) Satinder Silas Bedi, electoral rolls of 24 constituencies out of 70 will be published on October 6. "We will first publish the electoral rolls for constituencies in West, North and South-west districts and then on October 15 photo electoral rolls of 46 assembly constituencies in remaining six districts," Bedi said.

"Once the rolls are published, we will start the process of distribution of voter identity cards," she said adding the department is yet to decide if the cards will be delivered at the voters' residence or a common point in the locality.

"Either way, there will be a receipt taken from the voter when the card is delivered," Bedi said.

As per the figures provided by the electoral office, the department has about 85 per cent photographs of electors in the city. The department could not provide the percentage of electoral rolls for the South West district of the Capital.

With discrepencies and errors within the draft rolls being picked by politicins in the monsoon session of the Assembly elections, Bedi blamed the casual approach of citizens for the same.

"While correcting the draft rolls, we realised that many mistakes have crept in because of the carelessness of citizens. This includes giving wrong names, pasting wrong pictures and also tick-marking the wrong box for the sex of the elector," she said adding that many citizens did not visit designated locations or website of the election office to check their particulars, details and pictures in the electoral rolls of their area.

"Even if we received only 1.3 lakh copies of form no 8, in which electors have sought corrections, in our own comparison, we have managed to pick out mistakes and corrected in about 8 lakh forms," she said.

To ensure clean electoral rolls during the polls, Bedi asked electors to assure that the Election Commission guidelines are followed and that their names are not found in more than one constituency.

Heading: No smoke without ire: In Gurgaon, corporates say stub it or face wrath - Indian Express
Content:
With the Delhi High Court dismissing the writ petition and lifting its protection from arrest, decks have been cleared for the extradition of fugitive Ram Kumar Mehbubani to the USA, where he is wanted in connection with dishonouring cheques worth US $ 40,000.

After Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (ACMM) A K Kuhar was apprised by a central government official that the petition filed by Mehbubani against his extradition inquiry had been dismissed, the judge directed for preparation of committal warrant against him.

As per the provisions of the Extradition Act, execution of the warrant led to the detention of Mehbubani, awaiting the final orders of the Government for exiling him to the foreign land to stand trial. Brought to the court in judicial custody during a recent hearing, Mehbubani also moved an application for granting him permission to carry case records, spectacles, religious books and a stick, as he has fractured his left foot.

Finding nothing objectionable, the court asked the Tihar Jail superintendent to consider his request as per the jail manuals.

Following an inquiry lasting more than a year, the ACMM had recently recommended the extradition of Mehbubani to the USA, noting there was a "prima facie" case against the fugitive.

The mandate was given after examining the extradition request of the US Police and the documents put forward by them in this regard.

He was, however, not taken into custody on the day the ACMM concluded the inquiry, as his writ petition was pending before the High Court and the same had stayed his arrest.

Another condition preventing immediate action in the matter had also come from the High Court, which has put an embargo on his extradition, saying that the final order passed by the ACMM shall be subject to the order passed in the writ petition.

Sixty-one-year-old Mehbubani had been on the run for almost 15 years before he was nabbed at the Chennai airport in May 2005.

It was alleged that between June 1992 and December 1993, Mehbubani had placed numerous orders of electronic equipment from one North Supply Company through wire transactions, but "stopped payment" of the post-dated cheques.

Heading: HUDA to launch new housing scheme for Gurgaon - Indian Express
Content:
After the Centre's announcement of a ban on smoking in all public places from October 2, corporate offices in the Millennium City seem to be taking no chances. Major firms like IBM, Ogilvy and Mather, Ernst and Young, Google and many others have issued advisories to all their employees, asking them to abstain from smoking within office premises.

As per the new order, in case anyone is caught smoking inside one's office premises, the employer could also be fined.

Incidentally, many real estate firms that have rented out office space to corporate houses have themselves sent out circulars to such companies, requesting them to direct all employees accordingly. Builders like Unitech and Vipul Facility, which maintain Unitech Corporate Park and Global Business Park respectively, have reportedly requested all corporate firms to inform their employees of the same. "We in any case do not allow smoking within office spaces maintained by the DLF. We have, however, once again requested all companies that function from our buildings to abstain from smoking within the premises, including terraces, stairs and passageways of such buildings," said Sanjay Rai of corporate communications, DLF.

"We have asked our employees to abstain from smoking within office space October 2 onwards; this will include car parking areas, balconies and even outdoor walkways. We have also issued an advisory to the effect," said an HR executive of IBM Daksh. "Anyone who does not comply with the rules could face a penalty or legal action," he added.

The Centre had announced earlier this month that smoking would be banned at all public places from October 2. The ban would include hotels, restaurants and offices. A fine of Rs 200 would be imposed on all those caught smoking in such places, Union Health Minister Anbumani Ramadoss had said.

Heading: Three days after Mehrauli blast, ‘unknown’ victim identified, critical - Indian Express
Content:
The dream of owning a house in Gurgaon without burning a hole in on'es pocket might soon be fulfilled with the Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA) set to launch a new Group Housing Scheme for the city.

According to sources, in order to meet the growing demand for houses, around 1000 multi-storeyed dwelling units are expected to come up in various sectors of Gurgaon, tenders for which will be floated in two months.

"We have sent details like availability of land, expected cost and number of plots, to the headquarters in Chandigarh. The formalities will take a month or two and after that we will start inviting applications from eligible registered cooperative group housing societies and welfare housing organisations for the allotment of land," said Madhu Pradeep, senior town planner, HUDA.

Under the scheme, out of over 500 plots of half-acre each, a certain percentage will be reserved for the economically-weaker sections, central government employees and defence personnel, said HUDA officials.

"We haven't yet decided how much area will be reserved for such categories. The general category will include societies or welfare housing organisations comprising members who either belong to Haryana or are residents of Haryana or were working in the state or Chandigarh for the last one year," officials said.

The scheme envisages there should be a minimum of 20 and a maximum of 90 members for the group housing society.

HUDA will allot housing sites to cooperative group housing societies registered with the Registrar, Co-operative Societies, Haryana and the Welfare Housing Organisations registered with the Registrar (Firms and Societies). "There are both incentives and penalty clauses in the construction of flats. If the construction is completed within three years of the date of offer of possession, a rebate of 10 per cent on the price of land (adjustable towards the future instalments) shall be given. However, if construction is not completed within five years, an extension fee will be charged for the extended period," Pradeep added.

"The plots will be allotted on a draw system," she said.

Heading: Life in jail for man guilty of raping daughter - Indian Express
Content:
One of the last 'unknown' victims critically injured in the Mehrauli blast on September 27, a 25-year-old as per the hospital records, was identified late on Tuesday evening when his brother showed up at the hospital three days after the incident.

Doctors and police have also confirmed his identity.

The boy, identified as Dipu, is a 23-year-old who came to Delhi from Lucknow 11 months back. He used to live in Gadaipur village near Mehrauli and worked as a security guard in a farmhouse there.

According to doctors, Dipu received serious head injuries and his face was badly damaged in the blast. "There is a 40 per cent chance of his survival and his condition is declining. If he survives, there is a very high risk of infection," said senior surgeon Manish Singhal of the AIIMS Trauma Centre.

Dipu's brother Shamsher got to know of his brother's condition and whereabouts only on Monday after he asked his other roommates to look for him, because he was 'missing' for the last three days.

"We last spoke to Dipu on Tuesday over the phone. He never visited his home after he left for Delhi 11 months back. His friends told me that Dipu had taken a day off work on Saturday and had gone to buy a small cylinder from the Mehrauli market," said Shamsher. He took the next train to Delhi when the news was confirmed to him, and reached here on Tuesday evening.

"Our parents have also started from Lucknow now and will reach Delhi tomorrow morning," he added.

Meanwhile, Dipu has been operated upon and is on life support and ventilator systems, but doctors say his recovery has not been as well as expected.

"The boy could not be identified earlier since his head was bandaged and his face swollen," said Dr MC Mishra, Chief Medical Officer of the Trauma Centre.

Heading: Artisans from Bengal work nights to give final shape to idols, meet deadline - Indian Express
Content:
Observing that a person who despite being a protector acts like a predator, deserves no mercy, a city court on Tuesday sentenced to life imprisonment a man found guilty of raping his teenaged daughter.

Additional Sessions Judge D K Sharma, refused to show leniency to convict Ram Dhavan, who had sought clemency in the punishment contending he was physically-handicapped. A father has the role of a caretaker with respect of his children but the present is an instance when somebody, who was duty bound to protect his children, had himself committed the crime against them, noted the court.

Pronouncing the sentence, the court referred to various judgements of the Supreme Court whereby it was held that convicts in such cases deserved stern punishment so as to act as a deterrent for society.

There is a possibility the teenaged girl might never come out of the stigma and the unfortunate incident would come in way of her leading a happy life, observed the court.

Adopting a human approach, ASJ Sharma said the court's duty would not be over with awarding the punishment and directed for sending a copy of the order to Delhi Government's chief secretary to find out ways to help the victim.

The incident dated back to September 1, 2005 when Dhavan sexually assaulted his 14-year-old daughter, who was staying with him after he separated from his wife.

The FIR in the case was lodged at Patel Nagar police station after the girl told her mother about the incident.

Heading: Sniffer dogs, RAF to guard Puja pandals - Indian Express
Content:
Gobinda Nath, an artisan from Kolkata, has worked tirelessly for the past four months shaping nearly 26 idols of Goddess Durga at the CR Park Kali Bari.

For Gobinda and 12 other artisans hailing from Krishna Nagar in West Bengal, these are months of painstaking labour all for the Bengali community in the Capital.

With barely a few days to go, Gobinda and his co-workers are working overtime to meet their deadline for giving in the idols. "We are now draping the idols in silk and lending finishing touches to them. The idols need to be ready by October 4. This year we have received orders from the NCR as well," says Gobinda Nath. "We barely get to catch sleep for a couple of hours these days, but the fact that so many people across the city will come to see our idols is inspiration enough for us to work hard," he added.

Bankim Chandra Pal and his brother Shontu Pal have been working at a feverish pace at the Minto Road puja pandal. While Shontu, perched on a platform, reaches for the idol with his last strokes of paint, his elder brother supervises closely.

"We take orders for idols from Nivedita Enclave, Kashmere Gate and Minto Road and spend over two months in the Capital," says Bankim, who spends these months before the Pujas away from his family in Krishna Nagar. "All the ordeals are worth it, not just because this is our livelihood, but also our way of praying. We might not even attend the Durga Puja here or see how people marvel at our works," said Pal.

Asked how long his family has been in the craft, Pal says, "Maybe a hundred years. My father and grandfather had been in this trade and I picked it up way back in my childhood."

Gobinda says the Capital's residents prefer traditional idols.

"People here are very particular about Durga idols. They always ask for authentic, traditional idols that are popular in West Bengal as well," he says.

Heading: Doubles trouble for India No 3 pair - Indian Express
Content:
Security concerns have been haunting the Delhi Police and puja organisers in the Capital this year. In the wake of the serial blasts, the police and organisers have drawn up a strong contingent of security guards and volunteers to keep vigil at the pandals and the Ramlila ground.

Puja revellers visiting the pandals might have to go through various rounds of security checks. "We are working closely with Delhi Police. Sniffer dogs, private security guards and a special contingent from the Rapid Action Force will be deployed near the pandals," said Pradeep Majumdar, secretary of Kali Mandir Society, CR Park.

The CR Park Mela Ground puja, one of the biggest in the area, will have around 25 CCTVs manned by the police.

"Apart from CCTVs, security guards and police force, we have also made arrangements for a crisis management team. This team will swing into action if anything untoward happens and this would include communicating with the police, ambulance, fire and medical aid," said Pranab Choudhury, secretary, stalls at Mela Ground, CR Park.

Organisers are upset with the Supreme Court directive to wrap up Durga Puja and Ramlila celebrations by 10 pm. "We have issued directives to organisers to meet the deadline or face the music," said Rajan Bhagat, PRO, Delhi Police.

Ram Kishan Gupta, chairman of Ram Lila Mahasangh Committee, said, "We are trying to discuss the issue with the Delhi Police and the Lieutenant Governor to convince them to extend the deadline to midnight."

Heading: Poor display raises questions, again - Indian Express
Content:
Air India's Francis Alwin and Shankar Gopal lose to Arup Baidya and Sachin Ratti, handing Railways Central Zone title

Francis Alwin and Shanker Gopal P of Air India, being the third-ranked national pair, had their 'India' emblazoned t-shirts on, going into their final Central Zone Badminton Championship match against unseeded Arup Baidya and Sachin Ratti of the Railways. The teams took to court right after Hemant Duggal pulled off a thrilling 10-21, 21-19, 21-14 victory over Utsav Mishra to bring Railways back in contention for the title they have lost twice in two years to the airmen, and they had nothing to lose but the championship.

Arup and Sachin took inspiration from the contingent of Railway players and officials who kept cheering for every point, and just when they looked like they were tiring, the pair had come away with the biggest upset of the day — thrashing Alwin and Gopal 21-13, 21-14.

The first game went according to plan, Sachin's short service and counter smashes from Arup ensuring smooth progress. In the second game, however, Gopal upped the tempo, mixing up drops with smashes from the net. But they went on to squander a 12-10 lead with a series of unforced errors and after drawing level on points, Sachin and Arup were back to their first-game strategy.

'Embarrassing' defeat
While Alwin looked tearful, Gopal, being the senior, kpet a poker face while describing the defeat as an embarrassment. "They were playing on their home turf, supported by a very noisy crowd. This added to the pressure of playing for the first time for Air India. But being number three in the country in doubles, losing to singles players can't be excused. This is an embarrassment for us. But we have to carry on," said Gopal.

On the other side of the net though, Arup and Sachin kept weighing their 12-year long experience of playing together. Coming from two distant Indian cities, Kolkata and Jalandhar, respectively, their first meeting was at a national camp in Ajmer in 1998. Sachin, currently ranked 18th in India and Arup, India no. 18 in singles, however, haven't played too many tournaments together.

"We might be knowing each other and have played together for long, but we haven't appeared in many tournaments as a pair. But the weight of our experience is good enough," said 28-year old Sachin. Having gained a bit of weight and playing against the third-ranked Indian pair, he had some specific strategies in place. "Being fitter than me, Arup was given the responsibility of covering the first court while I kept attacking from the third. It's good that all our plans worked and we clinched the title after being 2-1 down," added Sachin.

Heading: The Order of Phoenix - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi's women's team will return from the North Zone Inter State badminton championships after successfully defending their title, but coach Malvinder Singh appears to be more concerned with searching a way to arrest badminton's decline in the state.

The women were largely expected to defend their title in the face of inferior competition, particularly with Mohita Sahdev in the team, but it was the men's poor quarter-final finish that raises a lot of questions, feels Singh.

"I am very disappointed with the way our men's team played, particularly the youngsters. They aren't focused on the game, and their goals are different. Himanshu Kharbanda and Rohit Ranaut played like beginners; this was not expected from them," says the irate coach, speaking to Sportline from Jalandhar, the venue for the meet. The men's team lost to Chandigarh in their last-eight match.

"They didn't play to their potential, and the reason for that is poor preparation for matches. One needs to play in a lot of tournaments to get better, but they aren't doing that. They are young, but even against elderly opponents they're making avoidable errors. If they are leading 15-9, soon the score will be 15-all and they'll end up losing the game 21-15. Consistency is what is needed," he adds.

The North Zone Inter State meet, though, is not exactly a meeting point for the region's most talented players. "The competition is definitely not great. Delhi are the hot favourites among teams like Jammu and Kashmir, Rajasthan etc. Teams expected to pose a challenge to us are Punjab, Chandigarh and Haryana. They are about the same level as us. Mohita is a fine player, and she was expected to see us through to the title. I'm pleased with her performance," says Singh.

The junior boys team reached the semi-finals before losing to Haryana, while the junior girls were beaten in the title-match, also losing to Haryana.

Heading: ‘I wish I can party at 65 the way I can today’ - Indian Express
Content:
Zain Khan is mocked by schoolmates for his flop, but he is thinking of an action flick

Though director Lucky Kohli's Hari Puttar: A Comedy of Terrors didn't exactly rock the box office, the movie's young lead actor Zain Khan, 15, is raring to go. In fact, Khan considers himself fortunate to have been chosen for the film. "My friends at school mock me about it flopping, but I take it in my stride. After all, I've been lucky enough to act opposite experienced names like Saurabh Shukla and Sarika aunty. Failure is part of the process," says Zain, philosophically.

The film has been panned by critics as a bad version of the Hollywood classic Home Alone. Khan plays a 10-year-old, Hari Prasad Dhoonda, who defends his home, in the absence of his parents. "I am an ordinary teenager who likes playing pranks. In my previous film, Rahul Bose's Chain Kulli Ki Main Kulli, my character was naughty as well," says Khan.

A fan of fast bikes and racing cars, Khan is a National Motor Cross Champion and fancies seeing himself in an action flick sometime in the future. "There has never been an action flick made with the child actor in the lead role. I would love to a do film which has bikes, rock music and big stars. It would be fun to star opposite actors like Aamir Khan and Salman Khan. The bigger the star, the more you learn from the person," says the little Khan.

He seems unusually focused on his career for someone so young and acknowledges serious competition from other child stars. "These days I consider Darsheel Safari my closest competition, since he has set the bar so high for child actors," he says.

This Class X student has life figured out, or so he would want you to believe. With dreams of studying automotive design in future, he does not want to give up his Bollywood aspirations.

"Films will continue alongside my studies. I have managed to strike a balance. In fact I am shooting for Ken Ghosh's Happy Hamesha alongside Shahid Kapur and Jiah Khan where I play a dance student," says he. As for now this Puttar is on a roll.

Heading: Home Delivery - Indian Express
Content:
Tina Ambani bares her soul and shares her passion for the elders as her Harmony Silver Awards come up

In a nondescript shamble at Thakurdwar near Mumbai, amid a hundred or so senior citizens playing carrom, reading magazines or practising yoga, is where Tina Ambani, the wife of Anil Ambani, one of the richest men if not the most influential, seems to be at most ease. "Age ain't nothing but a number," she chortles to a 70-year-old man even as she strikes a cookie in.

"Our elders are not a liability; we can turn them into our strengths," says the fabulous-at-50 lady, talking about the Harmony Silver Awards that take place on October 7, at Rabindra Natya Mandir.

The awards (Rs 51,000 and a citation for each), instituted by her five-year-old Harmony Silver Foundation, are in their second edition. The jury comprises MP Priya Dutt, actors Om Puri and Victor Banerjee, Justice Leila Seth and The Indian Express Group Editor-in-Chief Shekhar Gupta, and awards are presented to "silvers" who've achieved something remarkable. Last year's winners included Chelekkodan Ayesha, an 80-year-old woman who gave her Class X exams along with her great-granddaughter, and is now the face of education in her home state Kerala.

"The number of our seniors is boggling; from the current 80 million, we will have 137 million seniors by 2012," says Ambani, "And I'm not scared of their growing numbers."

The Harmony Interactive Centre, where we are at, is a three-storey community centre where her initiative functions as a flagship. There are other spaces in Mumbai, Delhi and soon Bangalore, where elders collect to make friends, train in computers and yoga, learn about investments and the like. "They don't need care; they need interaction," she adds.

Ambani says that even though her parents are no more, she came from a "very secure and loved childhood, the youngest of nine siblings", who recently collected and toured the Ashtavinayak in Maharashtra.

Her mother-in-law, she says, is as close as one can get to being her mother. "I just love her; she's the most caring and giving person ever." It's probably for the same reason that she has dedicated her opening-soon hospital to her: it will be called Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital and Medical Research Centre, and will house a geriatric centre too. "There are only a couple of hospitals in the country offering geriatric care," reasons Ambani, who has also been elected to the board of trustees of the Peabody Essex Museum, US.

The lady, her chic rose-pink tunic and ice cube-size diamonds showing off her movie-star good looks, is also particular to bequeath the values she has learned to her sons, Anmol, 17, and Anshul, 13. Family time is where she finds her stress-buster. "My husband and I take the kids for African safaris twice a year," she says, citing a week as a long vacation. "It's fabulous; we're completely disconnected; there's no stress and no shopping to worry about," she laughs, adding that she's saturated with her purchases. "I can wear Abu-Sandeep with the same joy as my own designs made by my tailor."

While we find that hard to digest, Ambani hopes to have the same energy when she's "a silver" as she does today. "I hope to have achieved something and made a small difference by then. And I hope to party as hard," she laughs.

Heading: Police seek bomb disposal squad for the city - Indian Express
Content: Ornamentation is frowned upon at Address Home's second store at Ogaan, Hauz Khas —from chandeliers to candles, from furniture to vases, things spell a bold austerity trend. But don't discount the intrepidity of designs — there are acrylic chairs in pink, white, black and lime-green imported from France, hand-glazed, distended zig-zag vases and a delightful lamp from the Netherlands. At the 2,500 sq ft store spread over two levels, the lower level offers stuff like leaf-shaped candleholders, flute and martini glasses while the second level goes extravagant with opulent chandeliers, lamps and vases. "The collection changes every month," says Ranjit Singhi, creative director of Address Home. "There is an attention to colour, but it is balanced by a muted shade like charcoal. Also in textiles, we have used mixed media like silk with velvet." The prices here begin at Rs 450 and go up to Rs 1 lakh. An oval organza black lamp from Germany comes for Rs 39,000, and an acrylic chandelier in black and red comes for Rs 21,000. The hand-glazed matte vases begin at Rs 1,200 and go up to Rs 4,500, while an Inka jug from Poland costs Rs 3,900. Contact: 64670533

Heading: Taking viewers through a journey of colours - Indian Express
Content:
The city police is pressing for its own bomb disposal squad. The development comes following the fact that Ludhiana is on a high alert and in the last one week alone the city police and the railway police combined have received nearly seven calls on bombs. Though these calls turned out to be hoax at the end of the search, nevertheless for each of these calls the city police has had to call in a bomb disposal squad.

SSP R.K. Jaiswal informs, "Punjab has only one such squad which is based in PAP Jalandhar. Each time, we get a bomb call we have to call in this squad, which takes almost an hour or so to reach in the first place. Seeing this, we have written to the state government to let us develop a bomb squad from within our own force, so that we can work more efficiently and quickly."

The SSP adds, "For the festival season, we are on a alert and we should not forget that not only is this city bigger in size as compared to other cities but also has a large number of congestion and dense population points."

The memories of bomb blast that rocked the city in October last year on Id still haunt. This blast had left six dead and more than 30 people injured.

Apart from this, the Ludhiana police is also planning to procure the robot prepared by Dr Gopal G Mishra, an explosive expert. This is an indigenous kind of robot that helps disposal of the suspect material which could turn out to be bomb from a safe distance of say about 30 to forty feet. We are trying to get this robot for our city.

Meanwhile commenting on the hoax calls, Jaiswal said, "In some cases like that of yesterday where some objects were lying at Gill road, this could have been a bomb. However it turned out be an eating stuff. Yet, we get a number of hoax calls which is not a right thing to do for. After all bombs is not something to be taken lightly. We have decided that in case we trace a number of hoax caller he or she will definitely be punished."

Heading: List of candidates for Assembly  poll will be out soon: Tewari - Indian Express
Content:
His journey of images began with cartoons, then on to poetry, prose and now to photographs add paintings —somewhere in between. Jaswant Zafar, an engineer in the Punjab State Electricity Board, through his photographs, which are on display at the Atmosphere Art gallery, takes the viewers through a journey of colours, images and self.

The exhibition, which was inaugurated by Charanjit Singh Atwal, Deputy Speaker, Lok Sabha, Zafar's works have been described from excellent to telling pictures that force the viewers to stop and think.

Says Zafar, "These pictures are my journey which is spread over four years. In this journey, I have tried to break the boxes, the small compartments that we all have chosen for ourselves and prefer to live in them. My call is that let us all break out of these boxes and think with each other."

The engineer adds, "It would be too simple to say that all these are pictures of beautiful places for we all know how beautiful the Niagra Falls are or how magnificient our temples are. But then, my take is different. Let us try and see the unseen, hear the unheard, and feel what we all have not felt for so very long. Through my pictures I just want the people to stand and absorb the vibrations coming from them."

It is not for the first time that Zafar is so vocal about what he feels so closely. While he takes a dig at the system and politicians around us through the cartoons that he has been drawing for so many years for various newspapers and magazines, his book on poetry, `Assin Nanak de kee lagde haan,' which was released in the year 2001 not only brought a genre of poetry to the fore but also made people sit up and think. His latest work, "Sikh so khoj laye," which is a collection of essays on Sikh history and Sikh Gurus is again a well-received book, which is presently a talking point of Sikh and the intellegensia world over.

Heading: NSS volunteers donate money for Seechewal Trust - Indian Express
Content:
All India Congress Committee (AICC) spokesperson Manish Tewari today said that the party would finalise the lists of party candidates for the Vidhan Sabha (VS) elections in various states within next two weeks. Tewari has alleged that the state government was not properly utilising various funds given by the central government.

The AICC Spokesman said that the elections of state assemblies in Rajasthan, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh were due and the party would finalise it's candidates for these elections within next 15 days and after that these lists would be announced publically.

Talking to the media persons after a holding a meeting with the Congress candidates for Block Samiti and Zila Parishads, Tewari said that most of the funds were given by the central government for rural development in the state but the state governmnet was not giving the due credit to the centre. He said that the ruling alliance was claiming that all the money was being spent by the state. He said it was not true. He said that today's meeting was held and in which all the Block Samiti and Zila Parishad candidates were asked to collect information regarding the ongoing development projects in the respective areas.

The Congress leader also informed that they would seek information through the Right to Information (RTI) act. He said that by doing this, the concerned officials as well as the departments would be obligated to give correct information regarding the developmental projects.

Tewari further said that all the funds allocated by the Centre to the state were not implemented properly by the state government.

Heading: Politicos’ security set-up: Manpreet wields axe - Indian Express
Content:
The NSS volunteers of Khalsa College for Women, Sidhwan Khurd participating in 10 days NSS camp led by their principal Dr Paramjit Kaur, donated Rs 15,000 to the Ek Onkar Trust being run by Baba Balbir Singh Seechewal.

The Campers accompanied by the NSS programme officers Rajwinder Kaur, Varinder Kaur, Shalini Gupta, visited the Nirmal kuteya of Baba Seechewal at Sultanpur Lodhi to seek his blessings.

Seechewal in his address to the students, acquainted them with the historic importance of the place which was sanctified by the visit of Shri Guru Nanak Dev Ji in 15th Century. He exhorted the students to coordinate their efforts and energies for the upkeep of healthy and congenial environment in the society which will pave the way for the healthy citizens and healthy minds.

The students paid obeisance at the historic Ber Sahib Gurudwara and partook of the Langar in the community kitchen of the Sikh Temple.

Heading: Have faith in me, FM implores industralists - Indian Express
Content:
'Security staff attached to state politicians will be reduced to half'

Keeping police security is a status symbol for politicians. It only adds hassle for general public and an additional burden for the state's exechequer. This was stated by Manpreet Badal finance minister Punjab while interacting with industrialists at Ludhiana management association's meet held last night. He added,"at the moment a total of 8,000 police personnel have been deployed in service of various politicians.
