This number will be reduced to 4,000 soon and a meeting of ministers has been done on this issue.Not only this further the number will be reduced to 3,000 as well in the due course of time." Meanwhile it needs to be mentioned that salary burden of these employees is not less than rs 80 lakhs per month.

He added," not only this we have plans that anyone who wants police security will have to pay from his own pocket the salary of that employee which at the moment is being born by the Punjab government. However we have not yet decided on this issue as of now."

And today apart from the MLAs even the chairmen of various trade boards, organisations are also roaming along with gunmen for their personal security.

Manpreet, who has set an example by not taking any security and also driving his own car in a lighter mood said," nobody wants to kill a politician. The only way to kill a politician is by not voting for him or her and hence I don't foresee any major threat for security purposes. I have never felt the need to take security and rather I am more comfortable like this."

Heading: Metro in Ludhiana by 2014 - Indian Express
Content:
It's a very lonely journey and a thankless job. But I can't just run away; I have to brave the odds," Finance Minister Manpreet Badal poured his out to the industrialists at Ludhiana Management Association's meeting last night even as he beseeched the industrialists' to repose faith in him. "By doing it you will smoothen my journey as finance minister and help me ride out the heavy odds staring the state," said the emotional-looking FM.

The Minister voiced his concerns about pace of the state's progress. "I have a shortfall of Rs 3,000 crore funds and to take the state to new heights, we must give up all subsidies.This money rather should be pumped in health and education sectors where Punjab is lacking badly. I must say that Punjab "ne kadi vi taleem nu tasleem nahi keeta." Despite all odds, my revenue deficit which was Rs 1200 crores will come to zero by the end of this financial year because we are having a record VAT collection and even performance in other sectors is also improving."

Talking to the industrialists about their woes, the FM said, "Punjab lacks corporate culture and industrial base and the administrative's apathy is largely to be blamed for this. The administration is not able to identify the problems of the citizens. I personally feel that industrialists are neglected by government officials and most of the times rules leave them at disadvantage."

"The industrial growth is stagnant which is lower than agriculture and service sector at the moment. This needs to be given a serious thought," he said.

He informed the members of the association that the government was looking forward to develop a world-class social and physical infrastructure to speed up the state's growth to help the industrialists.

The FM however blamed the incentive packages given to the states like HP and J-K etc as a major disadvantage for Punjab. However he hastened to add: " However this tax holiday will end by year 2010. Hence we are left with just two years of misery now."

He also announced the plans including IIT at Ropar, IIM at Mohali, six-lane highway from Baddi to Ambala and Pathankot to Ajmer and much more. The FM said that it had been decided to increase the plan size by 25% every year and it will reach up to Rs 10,000 crore from Rs 4,000 crore for the state

Earlier Dr K.N.S. Kang, generals secretary of LMA, welcomed the FM while Anil Kumar, president, LMA, extended a vote of thanks.

Heading: Police begin reconstructing event, ‘victim’ leaves for Delhi with father - Indian Express
Content:
Light metro rail will be set up at a cost of Rs 10,516 crore

Corridors to come up at Ayali Chowk and Gill village

If one goes by the draft detailed project report (DPR) submitted to the Punjab Government by the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), the city will get its first light metro rail soon. It would be the first metro project in the state. To be set up at an estimated cost of Rs 10,516 crore with two corridors, it will chug by 2014. Meanwhile, Reliance Industries has given a proposal to the state government to start a similar metro at Amritsar too.

The draft DPR to Punjab Industrial Development Board states that the existing urban transport system of Ludhiana city, which is road-based, has already come under stress leading to longer travel time, increased air pollution and rise in the number of road accidents. With projected increase in the population of the city and augmenting of transport infrastructure assuming urgency, the provision of rail-based metro system in the city has been considered.

Studies have brought out that a light metro with a carrying capacity of about 25,000 Peak Hour Peak Direction Trips (PHPDTs) will be adequate to meet not only the traffic needs for the present but for the coming 20 to 25 years.

The two proposed corrdors are Ayali Chowk to BBMB Power House Corridor (15.79 Km) and Gill Village to Rahon Road Chungi Corridor (13.03 Km).

After examining the various options for the execution of the Ludhiana metro project, it has been recommended that the project will executed through a concessionaire on built-operate -transfer basis. The concessionaire's contribution will comprise his own investment of Rs 1,563 crore together with a loan of Rs 3,127 crore to be raised by him from the market. The concessionaire will get a 16 per cent return (post tax) on his investment, For this purpose the up-front grant will be Rs 5,826 crore. While the Punjab government contribution will be Rs 3,723 crore, of this it will pay Rs 530 crore to the BoT operator as upfront amount and provide land so the concessionaire can raise Rs 2,800 crore for the project. While the Centre's contribution will be Rs 2,103 crore which is 20 per cent of the project.

The DPR states that the state government should exempt Punjab from Value Added Tax (VAT) on the metro, also no tax should be charged on the electricity required for the operations and no municipal taxes.

Sources said that to avoid delays in processing the clearance of the project, the DPR states that the state government should approve it in principle and forward the report to Secretary, Union Ministry of Urban Development, for clearance advising the ministry to give in-principle approval.

Also a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) should be set up for the Ludhiana Metro to be registered under the companies Act. It should be a public sector undertaking (PSU) of the state government and be named "Ludhiana Metro Rail Corporation''.

An officer should be appointed on a special duty with adequate powers to process and peruse the sanction of the project. Also for first year an interim consultant should be engaged who should work for the SPV.

The report states that state government should freeze all future developments along the proposed route of the Ludhiana metro to avoid wasteful expenditure.

A senior official said, "The Ludhiana Metro will be based on the Hyderabad Metro Project with negative bidding a crucial part of the project. The state government will give prime land to the developer for real estate and thus the land value will be more and the developer will pay back to the government."

Heading: Three murder cases registered in the city - Indian Express
Content:
The German national, who was allegedly abducted and molested by six youth on Sunday, was to return to Germany on October 8.

She, and her friend Ina (also a German national), had come to India on September 23 for attending Ina's marriage with Hardeep Singh, a resident of Sector 20.

Hardeep, living in Germany for the last four years, had already married Ina there but the couple decided to solemnise their union in India as well. Hardeep's close associates told Newsline that he had returned to India about two months ago as his visa expired. "Ina and the victim were to leave for Germany with Hardeep's documents and initiate the process of acquiring permanent-resident status for Hardeep," the friend added.

"It was her (the victim's) first visit to India. Hardeep and his parents had even warned her of rowdy Indian youth but she had a friendly and warm nature. We advised her against going out at night as the city is not safe, particularly for foreigners, but she was quite daring and confident," one of Hardeep's friends told Newsline.

Late on Saturday night, Hardeep, Ina, Hardeep's friend Gaurav (also a Sector-20 resident) and the victim had gone to Hotel Taj GVK, Sector 17, for drinks and coffee when the incident occurred. Two Police Control Room personnel have been permanently stationed outside Hardeep's residence in Sector 20.

"Both the bride and her friend (the victim) had made several purchases from my shop. She (victim) was quite inquisitive about Indian tradition and culture and seemed taken with jewellery," said a shopkeeper in Shastri market, Sector 22.

According to the police, the victim is in Delhi now. Her father, a police officer in Germany, and three officials of the German Embassy escorted her there.

Before leaving Chandigarh, the police tried to reconstruct the sequence of events.

"We drove the girl from Hotel Taj asking her to guide the way. She remembered crossing a toll-barrier, which we presumed to be the Dera Bassi toll-barrier, and a couple of bridges, one of which we presumed to be the Ghaggar bridge. She did not mention a flyover, which proves that she must have been taken towards Nalagarh (Ambala) via Panchkula. Several pieces of the puzzle are still missing. The exact picture will emerge only when the rest of the accused are nabbed," said a police officer.

Heading: Heavy diet plus liquor equals to liver damage - Indian Express
Content:
Three separate murder cases were registered in the city on Tuesday. While two men were found dead, a man succumbed to his injuries in a local hospital. He was allegedly attacked two months ago and was recuperating in the hospital since then.

The watchman of the cremation ground at Lalton village was found dead this morning. Atma Singh (60) body had injury marks. A police party from the Sadar police station reached the spot to investigate the matter. Later, the police registered a murder case against unidentified persons and started investigations. However, no breakthrough has been made so far in this case.

In the second case, the decomposed body of 30-year-old Harinder Singh was found from his rented accommodation on the Daba road under the Shimlapuri police station. The youth, who was working in a private firm, is suspected to have been killed last week. After receiving information, the area DSP Harmohan Singh and SHO Pawanjit reached the spot to investigate the matter. A murder case has been registered at the Shimlapuri police station against unidentified persons. In this case also, the police have not been able to trace the accused so far.

Meanwhile, the Sahnewal police converted a two-month-old case of assault into a murder case today following the death of a man last night. The deceased, Nazar Singh, was beaten up by two persons two months ago at Sahnewal. He had been admitted in the CMC hospital since then. The Sahnewal SHO Jatinder Kumar told Newsline that this case had been registered against two persons Jatinder Pal Singh and Kulwinder Singh. The SHO said that further investigations were on in this case.

Heading: Dhussi Bandh at Maniawal washed away thrice in a week - Indian Express
Content:
"With up to 40 per cent of the population in the northern region believed to be highly prone to fatty liver problem, it is slowly emerging as most common adverse effect of consumption of liquor along with a heavy diet."

Dr HS Bindra, senior consultant of gastroenterology and hepatology at Mohan Dai Oswal Cancer Hospital, said this while saying that according to various studies conducted recently, it has been found that there has been a high increase in the number of persons suffering from liver problems.

According to an estimate, 50 per cent of the patients of liver problems are those who regularly drink alcohol. Dr Bindra was one of the participants at the recently concluded Asia Pacific Digestive Diseases Week (Gastroenterology conference) held in Delhi, who not only observed this but debated the pitfalls of the problem at length.

He said that heavy diet along with consumption of liquor gives rise to an enlarged liver, leading to serosis and liver failure. "It is proving to be a deadly combination especially for the people in the northern region, who are believed to be more prone to it," Dr Bindra said.

"People are taking to drinking with heavy intake of food and hence it results in fatty liver. The problem is becoming a major concern now. The only way to deal with it is to prevent it," he observed. According to Dr Bindra, the high incidence of alcohol consumption in the region is leading to severe liver problems, the magnitude of which was hitherto unknown.

"As compared to the previous years, the number of such patients has certainly increased as I have observed during my clinical practice over the years," he remarked, adding, "Moreover, a high incidence of Hepatitis C has also been seen lately and due to excessive dependence on alcohol, it is causing a lot of damage to the liver. About 10 per cent of cases of liver problems are therefore end up in liver and failure and an equal percentage falls prey to liver cancer."

Heading: Look, what am I carrying in my schoolbag today? - Indian Express
Content:
The villagers of Maniawal and surrounding areas did not catch a wink for the past four days. Reason: They are on job to repair the weak link of the Dhussi Bandh which has been washed away thrice in a week's time.

Though the teams from the Drainage department are also on the job to repair it using sand bags and trees, it has been of little help.

Jagraon SDM Gurloveleen Singh Sidhu said, "Around 200 metres of bandh has been washed away thrice in past few days. A fresh damage occurred this morning. I have been stressing the Drainage department to use stones instead of sand bags to avert any tragedy."

However, the Drainage department officials have a reason to explain their lax attitude. They rue that owing to lack of funds, they have not been able to repair the bandh. "The contractor is spending money from his own pocket for the repair work but he is not sure whether the money will be reimbursed by the city administration. Hence, the use of stones to fortify the bandh is not possible in the near future," said the officials.

Meanwhile, SDM categorically stated, "Though the situation is under control, we must take urgent measures. Villagers of nearly seven villages are leaving in fear."

The problem arose when water was released from the Ropar Headworks raised the level of the Sutlej to 80,000 cusecs. Instead of receding, the water level touched the 91,000-cusecs mark. But drainage officials said, "Damage occurs after the water recedes. Most of the time, the wave of the river water causes rapid erosion which causes damage."

Heading: Stray dog debate: NGO bats for sterilisation, says killing ‘barbaric’ - Indian Express
Content:
City schools are hassled as students carry cellphones, games and even porn movies to classes

After giving more than 50 confiscated CDs of games and pornographic movies to school principal, a teacher discusses the ways and means to tackle the problem.

Some primary level students bring fancy and luxurious items to flaunt them among their classmates. One day, one of these children managed to bring a Korean playstation and became the cynosure of all eyes. Helpless teacher says, "My cupborad is full of fancy confiscated items but this does not deter the children."

A prinicipal confiscated six cellphones in a span of one and half months from Class X and Class XI students. "The students also exchange objectionable CDs ", said a school principal. She f added that parents have been requested umpteen number of times to keep a vigil on their wards but they do not bother.

A senior school teacher said, "I seized three CDs from senior students. When the school principal summoned their parents, they refused to believe that their children got the CDs to the school."

Priyanka Mehta, Principal, Saraswati Modern School said," Children are pampered by their parents who instead of spending quality time with them give them money to splurge. It is not easy to check school bags every day. It is the responsibility of parents to check their wards' bag daily so that they do not carry any unwanted material."

Dr Sushma Jaswal, Professor, Human Development said, "Parents should not fulfill every demand of their children. Long exposure to television has raked their brains and they look out to try and find answers to questions. Internet makes all this easy. With parents not ready to share any responsibility, children have started behaving like adults. The sense of shame has disappeared among children means and they do not feel afraid of their parents and teachers."

Heading: Thane area burns in communal frenzy - Indian Express
Content:
Killing of stray dogs is barbaric and unconstitutional and does not help in controlling their population, but sterilisation can be a better tool. This is what an NGO, In Defence of Animals, has given in its written submission before the Bombay High Court where hearing on the matter is on.

According to the NGO, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) had adopted the strategy to destroy dogs in the past and failed. From 1939 to 1999, though the municipal body did away with 25 lakh dogs, it failed to control the stray dog population, the petitioner against killing of stray dogs states.

The NGO states that throughout the world, countries that opt for sterilisation have been successful in controlling dog population. "The same sentiment finds an echo in the submission made by the central government and affirmed by the WHO which contends that sterilisation is the only remedy to curb population of dogs," the NGO states.

Senior counsel Aspi Chinoy, who appeared for NGO Welfare of Stray Dogs (which is carrying out a sterilisation drive), submitted that although the population of the dogs really never went down, death due to rabies had been cut down by one-third. He argued that it was not right to say the city was at the mercy of rabid dogs.

The state government had earlier supported the BMC regarding the validity of the BMC Act which gives them powers to kill stray dogs. According to provision 191 B A (2) of the Municipal Corporation Act, the Municipal Commissioner at his discretion may sell, provide shelter or destroy stray dogs.

BMC had stated that it had the powers to kill the dogs. BMC had also stated before the full Bench of Justice Dr S Radhakrishnan, Justice D B Bhosale and Justice V K Tahilramani about the huge financial constraints in rehabilitation of stray dogs in dog shelters.

BMC contended there was no need for additional dog shelters as they had kennels. Besides dogs could also be given for adoption.

However, NGOs and animal activists say that the provision under the corporation act goes against article 51 A (g) of the Constitution of India which says it is the fundamental duty of every citizen to be compassionate to animals.

Earlier, an affidavit by the joint executive health officer G T Ambe stated that, "Maintenance of stray dogs at dog shelters involves huge expenditure running into crores of rupees which would be a huge financial strain on the MCGM. It is questionable whether MCGM should spend crores of rupees on feeding stray dogs when we do not do so for the poor in Mumbai, who are starving."

Ambe further stated that "Municipal corporation feeding dogs taken out of Mumbai certainly does not deserve priority over the poor people of Mumbai." The court was also informed that as per the dog census of October 2007, there are 70,182 stray dogs in Mumbai and 26,900 pet dogs.

The hearing will continue on October 10.

Heading: Cops should’ve been given a free hand - Indian Express
Content:
Clashes in Rabodi over Navratri pandal; 1 killed in police firing, several injured

A dispute over the location of a makeshift gate erected by a Navratri mandal led to clashes between two communities at Rabodi in Thane on Monday night, leaving one person dead, several injured and property worth lakhs damaged.

While one person was killed and several injured when police opened fire, it was the police, caught between the warring communities, who bore the maximum brunt. According to the police records, 39 police personnel, including eight high-ranking officers, were injured and one constable admitted to the Wockhardt Hospital in Mulund is reported to be critical.

Tension had been brewing in Rabodi for the last four days after an entrance made up of bamboo poles covered with saffron cloth and a saffron flag was erected by Navshakti Mahila Mandal at Rabodi Koliwada for Navratri celebrations.

"The people from the Muslim community objected to the saffron-clad kamaan (entrance) and there had been meetings between the two communities over the issue. They wanted us to either remove the saffron cloth or move the entrance back so that they would not have to walk under it," said Ratnaprabha Patil, president of the Navshakti Mahila Mandal. The clashes broke out on Monday evening when the police were trying to broker a compromise.

Patil said that all hell broke loose when an armed mob attacked the police station and then vandalized the entrance in the presence of policemen who were outnumbered by the mob brandishing knives, swords and lathis. What ensued was rioting and arson in which shops, residence and vehicles belonging to members of both communities were targeted. In all, 21 shops, four houses and 31 vehicles were set afire and a police chowkie, five shops, four houses and 38 vehicles were damaged.

The police resorted to firing in which a youth identified as Moshim Khan (22) was killed. Eighty-eight rounds were fired at four locations — Kranti Nagar, Bapuji Nagar, Laxman Patil Chowk and Paras Naka. Besides the 39 police and two Home Guard personnel, 21 civilians including three journalists were injured.

"Every year there would be a dispute over this entrance as they (mandal) would advance it further and there would be objections to it. This year things got out of hand," said Zubair Maniyar, a resident of Khaton Apartment which is a stone's throw away from the Navratri pandal.

Deputy Chief Minister R R Patil visited the area in the wee hours of Tuesday and took stock of the situation. Deputy Commissioner of Police Sudhir Dabhade said that the situation was under control as the streets were being patrolled by police, state reserve police force and the Border Security Force.

Heading: 12-yr-old boy booked for beating up classmate - Indian Express
Content:
A top Thane police official, who retired from service on Tuesday evening, claimed that the communal violence at Rabodi could have been dealt with in 15 minutes and with just half the number of policemen deployed if the police were given a free hand in the matter.

"Half the police strength and 15 minutes were all that was required to contain the situation, provided the police had been given a free hand without any political interference," said Joint Commissioner of Police (Thane) Madhu Shinde, who was injured in his leg while dealing with the clashes that broke out on Monday night.

"The morale of the police force has hit an all time low. Right now the police are working under immense stress and always hesitate to act boldly as they fear action against them," said Shinde. He claimed that human casualty and damage to property could have been reduced had there been no political interference.

The riots left one person dead, 62 people injured and property worth several lakhs damaged. Moshim Khan (21), a resident of Kranti Nagar at Rabodi who was killed in the police firing, hailed from Sultanpur district of Uttar Pradesh and was working as a cleaner in a truck.

Several people were deprived of their livelihood due to the violence. One of those affected, Bachhu Thakur, owned a stationary and mobile phone shop that was gutted along with a row of other shops in the Tapase Nagar area of Rabodi close to midnight on Monday.

"I never felt the need to insure my shop as I have been in this locality since 1984 and never perceived any threat to my shop. I know each and every member of the area," said Thakur.

Jainul Sheikh, who lived beside Rabodi police station, returned home on Tuesday after fleeing from a mob with his family, only to find it gutted. "All the cash kept in the house has been reduced to ashes and the jewellery worth Rs 50,000 was missing," said Sheikh. Several families had to flee from their homes in fear and are now living with their relatives.

Heading: Plea seeking to name Pradeep Sharma in extortion case rejected - Indian Express
Content:
A case of assault has been registered against a 12-year-old boy who allegedly beat up a girl of his class with a ruler on Monday for not "studying." The boy is a class 2 student of the Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Municipal School at Worli.

According to the NM Joshi Marg police, who have registered a case of assault against the boy, the students of the class were copying down their school work from the board in the absence of the teacher when the incident took place.

According to the complaint filed by the mother of Anamika Gupta (6), the victim, the boy, on seeing that the girl was not copying down what was written on the board, allegedly hit her with a ruler on her back and kicked her in the stomach. A case was registered when the family came to know about the incident from the school authorities.

However, according to the police, the accused boy has not been apprehended yet. "The accused is a child, therefore we haven't picked him up yet but can do so whenever we have to produce him in court," said Police Sub Inspector D Kasure of N M Joshi Marg police station. "I don't think it is of a serious nature since children fight all the time. The girl hasn't been injured seriously," Kasure said. However, when contacted, Ravindra Gupta, Anamika's father, said, "He hit my daughter quite mercilessly and without provocation. She was sitting quietly and studying at the time."

As to what action the school authorities were taking, Gupta said, "Anamika showed her bruises to my wife Ranju when she picked her up from school. When Ranju immediately showed this to the teacher, all he said was that it looks like some infection and told her to go to the doctor. Even the headmaster was not helpful. He and another teacher actually said that the accused boy was a good student who would never have done such a thing."

An irate Gupta said, "The police said they will get back, but they haven't yet." When asked if the boy had troubled his daughter before, he said: "I'm not sure, but she was saying that he had bullied her once or twice before."

When contacted, DCP (Zone 3) Ashok Deshbratar said: "The boy will be charged under the same sections of the IPC which are applied to adults in cases of assault. However, as he is a minor, he will be produced in Dongri Child Court and would go to Dongri remand home."

Heading: Govt comes to the rescue of city’s textile mill workers - Indian Express
Content:
A magistrate's court on Tuesday rejected the application filed by a scrap dealer seeking encounter specialist Pradeep Sharma to be named in the 1997 extortion case in which Daya Nayak is one of the accused.

Complainant Tariq Ahmed in his application claimed that along with Nayak even Sharma should be made an accused.

The Bandra metropolitan magistrate, however, rejected the application today and has adjourned the matter till November 5, thus granting time to the complainant to appeal in the sessions court.

Ahmed, who is a scrap dealer from suburban Kalina, has stated in his complaint that on March 19, 1997, Nayak and Sharma along with five others cornered him and threatened to kill him in an encounter if he failed to pay them Rs five lakh.

The complainant had also alleged that 15 days after the incident, Nayak had called him and demanded more money. Ahmed then filed a complaint with the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC).

The NHRC passed an order directing the then city police commissioner to enquire into his allegations. On July 24, 1998 the police commissioner wrote to State CID, who later booked a case of extortion and abduction.

Heading: Perfect Fit - Indian Express
Content:
It's mandatory for commercial ventures on mill lands to give priority to workers, dependants in jobs

In what may come as a welcome step for the workers of the now defunct textile mills of Mumbai, the state government has made it mandatory for the commercial ventures coming up on the mill lands opened up for redevelopment to give priority to the mill workers and their dependants in jobs.

A notification issued by the state urban development department on September 26 states that "recruitment to these diversified industries/ developments on mill lands shall be done only from the names recommended by the employment exchange" which is to be specially created for the eligible mill workers by the department of employment and self-employment.

The mill owners, developers and occupiers of the mill land are also required to submit the employee requirement in the development taken up to the exchange from time to time.

"If the mill owner/ developer/ occupier feels that before employing the selected eligible mill worker/ dependant, it is necessary to impart training in the relevant vocation, he shall arrange such training and shall finance such training. After successful completion of which the mill worker shall be absorbed in the employment for which he has been selected," it added. Any dispute in this regard is to be referred to the monitoring committee set up for the purpose, with its decision being binding.

The Bombay High Court on a PIL filed by the Girni Kamgar Karmachari and Kalyankari Sangh had directed the principal secretary, department of urban development, Maharashtra government, to draw up a definite scheme for the workers of the mills which had been closed either for relocation or redevelopment.

T C Benjamin, principal secretary, urban development department, said that the commercial ventures coming up on the mill lands would have to give priority to the workers of that mill itself or their dependants, and in case a suitable candidate was not arrived at, then candidates from other mills could be approached. In case a suitable candidate was still not shortlisted, then the monitoring committee set up for the purpose would have to be satisfied before recruiting other candidates. The workers on the rolls of these mills as on January 1, 2000 would be eligible for these jobs.

Datta Iswalkar of the Girni Kamgar Sangharsh Samiti welcomed the decision and but added that it was necessary to create a mechanism to monitor whether the rules for employment of the mill workers and their family members were followed.

Details of the educational qualifications of the workers, recovery of their financial dues, need for employment and training and the names of family members with their qualifications and experience have been sought from workers and unions through a public notice.

According to the proposed scheme to be implemented in a time-bound manner, the labour commissioner is to scrutinise by October 5 the information received from the workers and unions in response to the public notice and verify the eligibility of the mill workers and their dependants from the concerned mill owners by October 20.

The draft final list of eligible mill workers is to be prepared by November 5, and it is to be published by December 5 with a one month period for submitting objections. The final list will be prepared after the verification and will be submitted to the secretary of the department of employment and self-employment by February 5, 2009.

Heading: The fall of Enigma - Indian Express
Content:
Warm up to the age of aqua aerobics and pole dancing techniques, fitness trends that are here to stay

Whether you are looking for a fun new exercise to spice up your fitness regime, or ways to reduce stress, lose weight and enhance your performance there are more options than one springing up in the city. The fitness centres in the city are grappling with new techniques and ideas to keep the health-conscious Mumbaikar in check. The latest innovations in fitness keep us excited about getting in shape and a

welcome detour from impending boredom.

Many gyms in the city have introduced aerobics-based progammes which are inclusive of techniques like martial arts, yoga, dance and music. The Les Mills exercise programmes—a group exercise routine, started by an Olympic athlete Leslie Mills and his wife from New Zealand in 1968, has today found takers in the city. Fitness First at Oshiwara offers three of the eight varieties available—Body Pump, Body Combat and Body Jam. Bobby Suguitan, group fitness consultant here says, "Body Pump makes use of light weights, whereas Body Combat is a cardio workout, which uses elements of martial arts like tae kwan do, tai chi, muay thai, kung fu and karate." The centre will soon be introducing the Body Balance technique (which is yoga-based) as well. "In order to make them more popular, group exercises are choreographed to popular numbers. As soon as the students master a routine, which takes roughly around two months, they are introduced to a new technique."

It isn't just high-intensity fitness that we are looking at. Aqua specialist Deepali Jain's classes are an underwater adventure with people from all age groups performing simple, but challenging water exercises. "We use the water's buoyancy to best effect. Water offers 13 times more resistance than air, and you weigh only 10 per cent of your body weight in water, which eases the stress on the joints," says Jain, who has been conducting these classes since nine years.

She has recently introduced the Aqua Boot Camp which is inclusive of aqua tai chi, kickboxing and pilates. While an hour on the treadmill or stepper can leave you exhausted and 300 calories lighter, aqua boot camp burns up to 700 calories, says Jain, who offers this programme for both swimmers and non-swimmers. "It's best for people who are suffering from arthritis, multiple sclerosis and other joint problems."

Prameet Kotak, propreitor RAPTfx & raptfx.com has introduced a new fitness trend called functional training, which includes video analysis of posture and then recommending exercises. "I recommend exercises which can be done in your natural habitat and also squat training."

Gyms are also adopting dance techniques to attract people. Walk into Gold's Gym, Worli, and you will be surprised to see women in high heels and sassy clothes, twisting, twirling and dancing around a pole to burn calories. While pole dancing is still getting popular, it is Zumba— a mix of flamingo, tango and belly dance that has already created a fitness frenzy. Part dance, part aerobics, Zumba is another hour long routine that works almost every muscle in the body. Says Shalini Bhargava, director, JGs Fitness Centre, "Whenever you are doing Zumba, make sure you shed all your inhibitions and enjoy this form of dancexercise."

Heading: Out of the box - Indian Express
Content:
Enigma's latest album, Seven Lives Many Faces, falls short of expectations

When Enigma came out with 1990's Sadness (Part 1), it was a musical revolution of sorts. With its house-pop beats, the song became as instantly recognisable as any hit song by the Beatles or the Doors. Then came 1994's Return to Innocence, with its alternative rock vibes and Enigma became a name to reckon with. Now, 18 years since its first hit, Enigma has done what was once thought impossible: it has delivered a dud.

Michael Cretu, the man who is Enigma, has attempted to stick with the times with his seventh studio album Seven Lives Many Faces by weaving his signature style around the latest sounds on the block—he calls them "the dirtiest Bronx hip-hop beats." So while the mix of the pure sounds of the London Symphony Orchestra and Bronx-style beat boxing and turntable scratches are interesting, they're lamentable when compared to the exhilarating and deeply mysterious music of Enigma's early years. Cretu's attempt to fuse different sounds and languages in his music remains strong, but the new album makes it clear that some experiments are doomed to failure.

The lyrics are at best juvenile and at worst, laughable. Sample these lines from one track, Distorted Love: I need you, I love your body/you need love/touch me, I'll be your daddy/ smell me, I'll be your mommy. Then there is the track The Same Parents, with the mandatory and overplayed lament about how humankind is descended from the same set of parents, so why can't we all just get along. The absurdity is compounded by Cretu's singing voice which was never a strong point anyway. The music on the tracks sounds repetitive and after a point it is difficult to keep track of the songs.

The beauty of old Enigma lay in how its music seemed like it was whispering secrets and mysteries from another time. Those days are gone. The lush sounds of Enigma's trademark Gregorian chants and obscure woodwind instruments is history, if you go by the New Age synth sound that Cretu is now delivering. Priced at Rs 350, the album is only worth a buy if you're a diehard Enigma fan.

Of course, no album is without a saving grace and in the case of Seven Lives, it is the song Hell's Heaven, which has some of the rawness and edginess that made Enigma such a hit in its early days.

Seven Lives Many Faces, Rs 350

Heading: Two and only - Indian Express
Content:
Farah Siddiqui opens her new gallery with a packed calendar

The smell of fresh paint invades the senses as one steps into the 800-square-foot Farah Siddiqui Contemporary Art (FSCA). Named after its owner, the plucky Farah Siddiqui, it is the newest addition to the array of galleries in South Mumbai. It opens today with a group exhibition that showcases works of some of the most talented contemporary artists of the sub-continent.

Though the gallery, located near Radio Club, shares the neighborhood with Chatterjee & Lal by Mortimer Chatterjee and Tara Lal, Aditya Ruia's Bombay Art Gallery and Shalini Sawhney's Guild Art Gallery, Siddiqui isn't panicking. "It may seem intimidating to have a gallery near such established names, but I have found everyone very welcoming and ready to babysit me through any teething problems," says the art aficionado-turned-gallery owner.

Wanting to be taken seriously, the 27-year-old has carefully selected the artistes for her first group show that's on till November 15. It displays contemporary art from India and Pakistan who have worked in various mediums. In fact, it is hard to spot the predictable oil on canvas in this new space, which apparently costs as much as a 1,200-square-foot gallery in Germany.

"I want to extend art affairs beyond white-cube galleries. It's important to have a gallery space, but owners need to be adventurous about selecting artists. For this show, I have chosen Mehreen Murtaza and Sajjad Ahmed from Lahore, who have never showed in India, New York-based artist Chitra Ganesh, London-based Faiza Butt and Mumbai-based Riyas Komu and Prajakta Palav," says Siddiqui.

When asked if she has a penchant for artists from Pakistan, Siddiqui becomes defensive. "I want to show good art from all over the sub-continent and Asia. But art has outgrown provincial boundaries, though artists like Mehreen are affected by the political scenario in their immediate surroundings. Would you call Butt, who lives in London, a Pakistani?," she argues. The young gallery owner, however, adds that Pakistan has a lot of talented young artists and not much infrastructure. "That's why it's one of the more unexplored markets," says Siddiqui. She plans to have more shows featuring Indian artists living across the globe.

Keeping with the current trend of installation art, the FSCA's debut show will have Mehreen's sound installation, apart from her digital prints. "I already have two Indian collectors fighting over the sound piece," says Siddiqui.

Next on the FSCA's calendar are a talk by Lucian Harris, who will showcase rare films on the pioneers of Dadaism Marcel Duchamp and Man Ray. In January, there is a solo by Pakistani artist Ayaz Jokhio—his first in India. More shows are lined up to highlight the contemporary art, but Siddiqui prefers to keep them under wraps for now.

Heading: Unplugged and uncensored - Indian Express
Content:
The designer duo has made a fortune out of simple cuts and sharp detailing

If there are two people who will never doubt the importance of being in the right place at the right time, it is the Delhi designer duo Rohit Gandhi and Rahul Khanna. They were in Mumbai over the weekend to showcase at the Chivas Fashion Tour, at the ITC Grand Central, Parel. As the two were caught in Mumbai's infamous traffic, we wait. There is a general movement at the venue—of people, glasses, trays and photographers who are taking pictures of the setting in great detail.

Soon the two arrive, dressed in casual chic. They settle for the fountain (in the centre of the hotel courtyard) as the backdrop for our conversation. Gandhi is the more talkative one, while Khanna is the smiley one. "Rahul is the hardworking one. I party a lot," says Gandhi, pointing to his bulging tummy and the double chin. Khanna pats him on his shoulder, "We have had an awesome 11-year-long partnership. We are the biggest critics of each others work and we fight a lot. But our sensibilities match and we cannot think of working individually. At times I wonder how designers manage to pull off a collection single-handedly."

After graduating in New York and working with a fashion house there for five years, Gandhi launched H2O— a brand of mens' shirts and ties for the domestic market. It was only in 1998, he teamed up with Khanna to launch CUE. "We believe in wearability and not just designing for the ramp," says Gandhi, adding, "It is a compliment when the other designers too sport your clothes." Their collections are based on straight lines, with style statements as sporadic and intense as the interplay between matt and shine. They keep their silhouettes sharp and defined with an emphasis on fabric, cuts and a lot of detailing rather than on embellishment. And yes, their fashion shows are styled beautifully, like an avant-garde theatre spectacle. At the upcoming India Fashion Week too, they plan to stick to their signature colour—grey.

The two have made menswear their forte. They have dressed various leading personalities and their designs are available at four stand-alone stores in Delhi, Bangalore, Kolkata and also Mumbai. "But Delhi is the fashion capital," insists Gandhi. "Mumbai's fashion quotient is heavily influenced by Bollywood, whereas Delhi is where all the top designers emerged from." Khanna agrees. "Delhi and Mumbai are like New York and Los Angeles. NY always has an edge over LA, because they follow fashion conscientiously."

Much as they love the fact that their clothes are being worn by some of the most stylish people in the film business, they don't think they can design for movies. "I don't think we want to explore that space unless it is an intellectually stimulating movie like Black, for which Sabyasachi designed," says Gandhi nodding his head to take approval from his partner. "Also, we do not design for Bollywood specifically. Most stars wear our designs, because they like them."

Male Polish

Heading: Much ado about nothing - Indian Express
Content:
Them Clones talk about their new sound and album

When the Delhi-based rock band Them Clones first burst on the scene eight years ago, one of the questions doing the rounds was, "what does their name mean?" It's a relevant question and the answer is an interesting story. Drummer Surojit Dev explains, "We're hugely into Alice in Chains and our name is a play on one of their songs Them Bones." His brother and vocalist Prithwish Dev adds, "It's also a play on the fact that we're all working guys and when we perform on stage, we're more interesting and fun clones of ourselves." They chuckle as they explain this and you get the feeling that they may have fielded this question a number of times, but they don't tire of answering it. It's like a private joke they share.

Them Clones was born in the Devs' house eight years ago. Prithwish and guitarist Joseph L had been jamming since school and they'd always wanted to form a band. They asked Prithwish to join them as a drummer and they had auditions to recruit another guitarist and a bassist. The current lineup includes Gucci Singh as the other guitarist and Romit Gupta as the bassist.

The band is in the city to perform at the Blue Frog on September 30 and October 1. While the second day is for their original compositions, the performance on the first day was an unplugged tribute to some iconic alternative bands from the '90s, like Nirvana, Alice in Chains, Pearl Jam and Incubus. Which prompts the question: given that rock is always associated with noise, was moving to unplugged performances a deliberate attempt on their part to tone it down? Prithwish explains, "Playing unplugged involves a different level of intensity. It's like feeling something without actually touching it." Surojit says, in more prosaic terms, "We wanted to show that we can also play unplugged. All these alternative bands had great success playing that way. Look at Nirvana's Unplugged album. Also, we did want to mellow down our sound. When we first played this way two years ago, we were very well-received."

The band has won almost every competition they've participated in including Channel V's Launchpad, Jack Daniel's Rock Awards and have also played in London. Next on their agenda is cutting an album by the end of this year. "We'll start recording this month when our producer flies down from New Zealand. It'll be 53 days of non-stop recording," Prithwish says. What about a music video? Surojit says, "There will be no album without a music video. Even if we don't get so much airplay, if the music is played for maybe two hours everyday, we'll get enough exposure."

This is not their first gig in Mumbai. "Although Delhi has the home vibe, Mumbai has a lot of energy. After having heard us play so many times, people are beginning to remember our songs and are singing along," says Prithwish, with obvious pleasure. They've come a long way, indeed.

Heading: 25-yr-old arrested for stalking, threatening girl after break-up - Indian Express
Content:
Day Two and Day Three of Chivas Fashion Tour had us perplexed. Raghavendra Rathore, Vikram Phadnis, Malini Ramani and Rohit Gandhi-Rahul Khanna of CUE showed their clothes amidst rowdy crowds. The show was grossly mismanaged, with burly men mouthing profanities like it was about to go out of fashion. Anyway, guests Raveena Tandon with husband Anil Thadani, Rohit Roy, Shaina NC, Rohit Bal with Manish Malhotra, Niharika Khan and Alvira Agnihotri with Arpita Khan were seen cheering their favourite designers. Minissha Lamba, showstopper for Vikram Phadnis in a tiny gold number was the golden girl of the evening. On the final day, clothes definitely got better with collections from Rocky S, Ayesha

Depala, Wendell Rodricks and Shantanu Nikhil. Neha Dhupia and Dia Mirza walked the ramp for Shantanu-Nikhil. Rodricks used bows and frills on his clothes, much to our delight. Heading: Forgotten in Games hype: Jobs-for-farmland deal - Indian Express
Content:
The railway police have arested a man who cut his left wrist at the Churchgate station last Wednesday apparently after a failed relationship. Twenty five-year-old Prateek Bariya took the drastic step after his female friend refused to speak to him and allegedly ended the relationship.

Soon after the incident, the girl along with her father approached the MRA police. They had earlier lodged a complaint against Bariya on May 3 this year. The MRA police, however, refused to file an FIR against Bariya. The father and daughter then approached the railway police who lodged an FIR and arrested him on September 24. According to sources, the girl and Bariya were in a relationship, but due to some reasons, it did not last. After this, Bariya began harassing and threatening the girl through SMSes. She then lodged a complaint against him at the MRA police station.

A day before the incident on September 23, Bariya, resident of Sat-Rasta, Mahalaxmi went to the building where the girl resides in Bohra Bazar fort and threatened her. Next day, when the girl was going to her college, Bariya was still at her building. He forcibly sat inside the taxi that the girl hired to go to Churchgate station. She then called her father to the Churchgate station. Bariya was reprimanded by the girl's father after which he cut his wrist.

The GRP, who finally registered the case, produced Bariya before Railway court at Mumbai Central on September 25 where he was released on bail.

A police official on condition of anonymity said, "Police cannot refuse to lodge FIR, even if the place of accident does not come under its jurisdiction. In this case, a complaint was already lodged. How can the police wait for a major accident? What if the lover had thrown acid on the girl's face?" MD Rasdkar, senior police inspector, Churchgate station, said. "Case is registered under Sections 506(2) and 504 of IPC. Bariya has been released on bail."

Heading: Corporators keen to turn legislators - Indian Express
Content:
MADE TO BE BROKEN: Decade after court ordered first preference to villagers in construction work at complex, sports authorities still hire from outside

In 1992, the gram panchayats of Balewadi and Mhalunge villages gave up their stake on about 165 acres of grazing land to allow the construction of a sports complex for the Commonwealth Youth Games.

In 1998, the Bombay High Court ruled that whenever work came up, the state sports department would give first preference o 100-odd affected people of these two villages.

For the last couple of years, work has gone on at a furious pace on the Shri Shiv Chhatrapati Sports City, or Balewadi sports complex, which is all but ready for the Games from October 12. Not one of the affected villagers, however, is involved in the hectic activity.

On Thursday, the villagers plan to demonstrate in front of the complex to highlight the raw deal they got from he authorities.

"After surrendering our claim on the land, after more than a decade of struggle, and despite the interim High Court order, we remain deprived of the guaranteed employment," Ajay Kamble, who has a family to run but can earn only when odd jobs in construction come up in and around Balewadi village.

Struggling to find work was all the more difficult to take, he said, because of the amount of construction taking place in the sports complex for many months now. All local villagers have been kept out of it.

These villagers, most of them illiterate, used to graze their cattle on the land. After they surrendered it, milk is no longer their source of livelihood.

The sports directorate had promised hem jobs in the mid-1990s. "They did not keep their word. We first approached the industrial court to seek permanency in employment. However, that was denied; the sports department said that they had no work to offer. We then approached the High Court, and the interim order was passed in our favour. Now, even that order has not been executed," Kamble said.

The order, issued on July 12, 1998, states: "In the event the respondents (sports department) creates any job either permanent or temporary to which the members have to fulfill the criteria for employment and whose names are in that event (list), the members of the petitioner union (villagers) who were employed (temporarily) for doing work at the sports stadium will be given first preference over others considering their suitability."

In the mid-1990s, some villagers did get some temporary work. But that lasted only a couple of months.

Kamble said that the sports authorities have made fresh recruitments and are in the process of recruiting another 200 for the Youth Games. Villagers, who wrote repeated letters to the sports authorities, are peeved at not being considered. They said they too were adept at such work such as masonry, gardening as well as anybody else.

"Ever since construction for CYG started, we have sent over 20 letters to various authorities in the sports department but there has been no response," Kamble said.

Balu Mohol of Mhalunge village said that it is getting increasingly difficult to make ends meet. "We have had no permanent employment ever since our sole means of livelihood - cattle rearing - was taken away. Such a big event is happening and they are ignoring the villagers," he said.

Senior sports department officers said they did not want to comment.

The villagers have filed another civil application in the High Court, which is expected to take it up for hearing this week. Advocate Vaishali Sarin, who is representing the villagers, said they have also sent letters to Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh and Suresh Kalmadi. "If justice is not meted out to these villagers, we will go on an unending strike," she said.

Heading: As police debated, this man bled to death on the road - Indian Express
Content:
Civic leaders in the race for two extra Assembly seats created by delimitation

The number of Assembly in Pune city has gone up and so have the hopes of at least a dozen corporators wanting to graduate to the Assembly. They are in the run for the seats created after the delimitation exercise. The seats have gone up from six to eight.

The aspirants have already begun their preparations, wanting to make sure they do not lose out if their party high commands set preparedness as one of the criteria for the party ticket.

With sitting legislators not expected to let go of their seats, the dozen elected members of the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) eager to move a notch higher in the political ladder, are after the two extra seats.

Among the frontrunners is the leader of the house in the PMC, Anil Bhosale of the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP). Other NCP corporators in the race are Bapu Pathare, Chetan Tupe, Bapu Karne, Dilip Barate, Subhash Jagtap, Akrur Kudale and Vikas Dangat. Kamal Dhole-Patil is the lone NCP MLA from the city.

Congress with three sitting legislators — Chandrakant Chhajed, Balasaheb Shivarkar and Ramesh Bagawe—¿ also has a number of fresh contenders for the Vidhan Sabha ticket. "The addition of two constituencies has raised our hopes," an aspiring Congress corporator said.

The Congress contenders include city unit chief Abhay Chhajed, party leader in the PMC Ulhas Bagul, Deepak Mankar, Kamal Vyavhare and Narayan Rane-supporter Vinayak Nimhan.

Leader of opposition in the PMC, Vikas Mathkari, leads the BJP brigade nursing ambitions to enter the Assembly, while Ujjwal Keskar and Ashok Yenpure are also in the race. Former corporators Vijay Kale and Yogesh Gogawale too are on the list of contenders. BJP Pune chief Girish Bapat is the sitting legislator from the city.

A BJP leader said, "Many corporators are interested in making it to the Assembly, but it all depends on the seat-sharing with alliance partner Shiv Sena." Awaiting the party nod from Shiv Sena are deputy mayor Chandrakant Mokate, Standing Committee Chairman Shyam Deshpande and Sachin Bhagat.

Mahrashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) corporators eyeing the Assembly include Ravindra Dhangekar, Kishore Shinde, Vasant More and Raju Gorade. "The party high command will take the decision, but we are getting ready to contest the Assembly polls. We have started reaching out to the people and apprising them of the failure of the sitting legislators," Ravindra Dhangekar, an MNS leader in the PMC, said.

But there is at least one corporator who is seeing beyond the Assembly seats. He is BJP corporator Anil Shirole. The corporator is gearing to take a quantum leap, from PMC to the Lok Sabha. He has been tipped to be the candidate for the Lok Sabha polls. "Senior party leaders have given favourable signals about my candidature for the Lok Sabha," Shirole said. He too has started his work for the elections. The focus of the party is presently on the Lok Sabha polls and decisions for the Assembly polls would be taken later, said Shirole.

Heading: Heart of Sassoon’s cardio department stops beating - Indian Express
Content:
Injured in an accident on Monday night, a man bled to death on the busy Magalwar Peth junction Tuesday, having lain unattended, alive and dead, for 17 hours before the police finally removed the body around 6 pm. Locals residents say he died for want of medical help.

The police had been informed but did not intervene. The spot is barely 500 metres from the Bund Garden police station and Narpatgiri police chowky, and there is a debate over jurisdiction.

A constable of the Bund Garden Police Station "We sent a police van to the spot around 4 pm ." He said he did not know anything about any calls while the man was alive.

Ainul Shaikh Abdul Aziz, who runs a travel agency, said, "We were was in our office near Bund Garden police station around 11 pm on Monday when I heard the screech of brakes. When we came out we saw that a man had been hit by a dumper. He was bleeding from his mouth and nose; we carried him to the edge of the road and gave him a bottle of water."

Aziz's friend friend Ezaz Shaikh dialled 100 and informed the police. "They promised to send someone to take the man to a hospital. We also informed two policewomen and two policemen from Narpatgiri police chowky, but they said this place is not under their jurisdiction," Aziz said.

When Aziz left office around midnight, the man was still there. He was alive and sitting up.

"Today evening around 4, when I came to office again, I was shocked as I saw the man was still there, unattended and now dead. That means for 17 hours nobody from the police came to his help and the man died of what may have been internal injuries," said Aziz.

This is not the first such incident. On June 26, Express photographer Arul Horizon found an injured man lying unattended near the Bund Garden police station. He informed the police but found the man still at the same spot two days later. He then made sure the man was taken to Sassoon General Hospital.

Heading: Go veg, says PETA - Indian Express
Content:
Lone heart-lung machine shut down for repair

The cardio-thoracic surgery department at the state-run Sassoon General Hospital has been closed for the last ten days, as its sole heart-lung machine needs to be 'revived'.

The machine needed urgent servicing, said the head of the department, Dr Arvind Inamdar. "With only one heart-lung machine at the department, the monitor has been continuously on. We had to shut it down for maintenance," Inamdar said.

The syringe pumps needs oiling and the whole place has to be fumigated. With 25 heart surgeries and other procedures done every month at the five-bed ICU of the department, doctors fear one heart-lung machine cannot take the load.

The heart-lung machine, often referred to as the pump, does the work of the heart and lungs during heart surgeries. The device is used in open heart surgery when the heart is stopped for the operation. The machine has a chamber to receive blood from the body which is normally the responsibility of the heart's right atrium.

The blood is then pumped by the machine through an oxygenator, normally the responsibility of the right ventricle. The oxygenator removes the carbon dioxide and adds oxygen, normally the work of the lungs. The machine then pumps oxygenated blood back into the body, which is what the left side of the heart does.

The heart-lung machine is connected to the patient through a series of tubes. Once the operation is over, the surgeon gradually allows the patient's heart to resume its normal functioning and the machine is disconnected. The heart-lung machine will again begin functioning on October 3.

Because of the maintenance work, angiographies and heart surgeries have been rescheduled, Inamdar said adding that there were plans to procure another heart-lung machine so that there would be no need for shutting down the department for maintenance.

Heading: Traffic signals in sync: trials to take off tomorrow - Indian Express
Content:
Go vegetarian! This is the message the youth arm of PETA wants to send out this Gandhi Jayanti. To mark Gandhiji's birthday and celebrate World Vegetarian Day, petaDishoom, the youth arm of People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals or PETA took out a march starting from the hostel ground of the College of Engineering in Pune, going till Sambhaji Park Road with hundreds of concerned citizens also joining it. Simran, a member of PETA said, "The march has been organised in honour of Mahatma Gandhi, who was a vegetarian and encouraged others to eat vegetarian and healthy food."

During the march the demonstrators congregated in a field and positioned their bodies to form the phrase -Go Veg. They were wearing animal masks and holding signs and banners with pro-vegetarian messages. The demonstrators also tried to bring out the benefits of consuming soya milk instead of cow's milk. "Soya milk is a healthy and a humane alternative to cows' milk, which is often adulterated and cruelly obtained," said a participant. The march was in collaboration with World Alliance for Youth Empowerment (WAYE), the youth arm of Sri Sri Ravi Shankar's Art of Living and ProSoya Foods. "Our mission is to empower young people: physically, spiritually, economically and socially to enable them to shoulder the active responsibilities towards contemporary issues and challenges facing their communities and societies at large," said Khurshed Batliwala, director of WAYE. When asked about vegetarianism, he added, "I don't eat my pets - why do you?"

N Jagirdar, ProSoya Foods' vice president of marketing, said, "There is also the larger issue of animal welfare. That is why ProSoya and PETA are working together to raise awareness among people for harmonious co-existence with animals. PetaDishoom has also tied up with Pune's College Of Engineering for their Technical Fest called Mindspark 2008 in organizing a march for animals.

Heading: Youth Games bring schools closer to nature - Indian Express
Content:
As a part of the attempt to synchronise traffic signals of the city, the traffic police will conduct a dry run on the VIP corridor from Pune Airport to Balewadi from October 2.

Speaking about the project, Srinivas Bonala, additional engineer (special projects) of Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) said, "The entire stretch of about 18 kilometers has been divided into six clusters for the purpose of synchronisation. The work has been completed and all signals on this route including those at Gunjan Talkies, Parnakuti, Wadia College, Regional Transport Office, Engineering College, Sancheti Hospital and the India Meteorological Department have been synchronised."

"The first dry run will be on October 3 and 4, the second one on October 6 and 7 and the third one on October 8 and 9," said Mahesh Patil, Deputy Commisioner of Police (Traffic). Elaborating on the necessity for three dry runs, he said that it would help in finalising the time interval for each signal.

"The signal synchronisation work is taking place on major roads in the city, which attract a lot of traffic from the feeder roads (small lanes) that merge with the main road. If a feeder road requires a green signal for 30 seconds, but only 20 seconds are allotted to it by way of synchronisation, it will result in a traffic jam on this feeder road. The dry runs are to ensure that this does not happen," Patil said.

Bonala said that other than signal synchronisation, poll painting work and installation of surveillance cameras at certain places have also been carried out.

"Two types of cameras will be put up at 68 spots in the city for tracking speed violation and detecting cases of red light jumping by vehicles," said Patil. Although the project was taken up before Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG), the system will continue even after the games, Bonala said. The PMC is also prepared to take up synchronisation work on the Fergusson College Road and Senapati Bapat Road. Work has already been completed on Laxmi Road, J M Road, Bajirao Road, Tilak Road, Shivaji Road and Karve Road.

Heading: Marathi literary convention to be webcast live - Indian Express
Content:
It never occurred to Rashida Khan, mother of Amanullah Khan, that the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) would spark an interest in gardening and waste management in him.

"Ever since Aman started participating in an environment awareness programme in school, he has become more environment-conscious. He even bought a couple of potted plants for our garden," she said.

Aman, a student of class VIII of Epiphany High School in Guruwar Peth, was part of the waste management and water audit project in his school. "We calculated the total strength of the school, the water usage and even suggested a rain harvesting project for our school. In the waste management project, we made vermicompost baskets, a smaller version vermicompost pit," he said. The school's wet garbage is now disposed of in these baskets prepared by each class.

Fatima Kalaiwala of Mount Carmel High School in Lullanagar, again a class VIII student, as part of the air audit (for the games) found that most of the 500 vehicles that entered the school every day, including buses, vans and vehicles of parents who drop their children, had their Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates. "Owners of vehicles that did not have one were asked to get one and requested to update them regularly," she said, adding that since then, she has stopped using her vehicle for covering short distances. She rather walks or rides a bicycle.

Kiran Raut, Class XI student of Mount Carmel, found during land audit that there are 127 kinds of trees and plants in her school. "We found the names of insects and birds that visit our school premises. Although, I know that this was part of CYG's Environment awareness project, I would like to continue participating in similar projects," she said.

The EAP was implemented in 60 city schools including Abhinav English Medium School, Gurukul, More Vidyalaya, Moledina High School, Dastur School, City International School to name a few. Students of the Department of community medicine, Bharati Vidyapeeth (University) Medical College doubled up as volunteers to implement this programme. Project coordinator of EAP Varsha Vaidya said, "We conducted about a dozen activities as part of this programme. These included lectures on various environmental topics like rainwater harvesting, waste management, vector-borne diseases, film and puppet shows, riverbank cleaning, poster competition, environment quiz competition." Every school has prepared reports of the land, water, air and energy audits. "We plan to compile these reports and release a summary soon," Vaidya said.

Somya Mishra, student of Bharati Vidyapeeth Medical College and school coordinator says, "A significant aspect of this project is that the lectures were prepared by medical students for school students. It was a learning experience for them as well, for the content has to be informative yet simple." The EAP will conclude by awarding the 'CYG Pune 2008 Green School Award' and 14 prizes per school during the games.

Heading: Campaign to replace bulbs with compact fluorescent lamps - Indian Express
Content:
The first Vishwa Marathi Sahitya Sammelan (World Marathi Literary Meet) to be held in February 2009 would be webcast live on www.mmbayarea.com. This is the first time that any Marathi Literary Meet will be seen live, online across the world.

Akhil Bharatiya Marathi Sahitya Mahamandal (ABMSM) and Bay Area Maharashtra Mandal (BAMM), San Francisco, are organising the sammelan at San Hose from February 14 to 16. Sagar Yeolekar, member of the executive body of BAMM, while addressing a press conference arranged to inform about the travel plans for representatives interested in participating in the sammelan, said that the organisers plan to webcast the whole Sammelan live. "We have already started the online registrations on our website. Marathi people from Canada and Singapore have shown interest in coming for the meet," said Yeolekar. "But there are limitations on people coming to the US, considering the costs and distance. So, we are using the technology to reach out to Marathi people across the world," he added. Yeolekar said that the BAMM is also considering a tie-up with a news channel. Bhushan Kelkar, member of BAMM said that as this is the fist World Marathi Literary Meet, something different should be done to make it big. "We will be arranging traditional events like Grantha Dindi, seminars and Kavi Sammelan, We want to introduce some new concepts like seminar on Marathi in today's global context and so on," he said.

Heading: A lesson in discipline as youth from remote village becomes Army officer - Indian Express
Content:
In order to promote Compact Fluorescent Lamp (CFL) and phase out ordinary bulbs to reduce carbon emission, two city-based NGOs—BAIF research and development and Rotary Club of Poona West—have launched an awareness campaign. Posters will be displayed at electrical shops as part of the campaign, where consumers will be educated about the adverse effects of ordinary bulbs on the environment.

"Global warming is a severe problem directly linked to the carbon di-oxide production, which in turn is directly linked to the energy consumption of people. Consumers must know that CFLs are five times more efficient and each of them reduces carbon production by 125 kg per year in comparison to ordinary bulbs," said BAIF president and managing trustee Narayan Hegde.

The posters will start appearing in electrical shops near the cash counter in another two weeks. The NGO's will also talk to shop owners to promote CFL. According to Hegde, consumers also stand to gain Rs 400 per year if they replace ordinary bulbs with CFL ones. "It may look expensive in the beginning, but once people understand the economic and environment benefits, they will find it a win-win situation," he said.

An ordinary bulb costs about Rs 30 while a CFL costs around Rs 110. However, CFL consume five times less energy and have a lifespan of four years, each bulb saving half a tonne of carbon di-oxide. According to BAIF, there has already been a 20 per cent substitution of CFL because of price reduction in the last two years and Hegde said that this would improve in the coming months.

Depending upon the success of the campaign, BAIF is also planning on approaching the producers with a petition to stop the production of high carbon yielding bulbs. "If the people respond well, there is no reason why we cannot ask the producers to stop production. But it will be a slow process. A lot of poor people may not be able to afford CFL even if it is more efficient in the long run," Hegde said. With the help of Rotary, BAIF is also targeting school children in the city to raise environment awareness.

Heading: PCB to organise ‘Grand Carnival’ during CYG - Indian Express
Content:
For 22-year-old Nilkanth Balasaheb Jathar, the journey from his native village to becoming a sentinel guarding the borders had begun with a simple dream. Hailing from Mungusgaon in Ahmednagar district, Jathar is about to be commissioned as a lieutenant, the first member of his family as well as the first person in his village to don the uniform of an officer in the armed forces. His 49-week training schedule will start from October 11 at the Officer's Training Academy (OTA), Chennai.

"This is a dream come true. I come from a military background, with my previous three generations having served the Indian armed forces. I have grown up listening to their heroic tales," said Jathar. Unlike Jathar, his forefathers were jawans in the forces.

Commenting on his success, Jathar's mentor, lieutenant colonel Pradeep Brahmankar, director, Apex Careers said, "He comes from a village with a population around 900. The village is not only remote but does not have access to basic sources of information like newspapers. Nilkanth's achievement thus becomes very creditable". Jathar comes from a family of four. His father is a retired radar operator, his mother a housewife and his brother a farmer. The entire village as well as his family is proud about his achievement. "Now that I have got an opportunity to represent rural India, I want to reach out to villages and inspire the youth to join the armed forces. Villages have a lot of talent. In fact, the adventurous lifestyle of rural India is the best foundation for joining the Army. My selection proves that it doesn't matter which place you belong to make the mark. What is important is following your passion and the rest will fall into place," he added.Jathar secured a rank of 264 in the national OTA merit list. Jathar had completed his schooling from a local school, following which he went to Mumbai and joined Somayya College of Science. After graduating as an external candidate, he realised that his communication skills were not good.

A stint at a call centre improved his ability to communicate. Equipped with the required skills and willpower, I was ready for the examination." Participation in village level activities gram swachchata abhiyan and water conservation scheme also helped inculcate social values in him, added Jathar.

Addressing a press conference here on Tuesday, Amreysh Dubey, director, BRAND Knew, said, "The company is investing around Rs 65 lakh into the Grand Carnival. Out of this, the PCB will contribute Rs 35 lakh while the remaining amount will be raised through sponsors. A major chunk of the total investment will be spent on hoardings and giving the M G Road area a facelift." Sponsors should pay using A/C payee cheques. Elaborating on the Grand Carnival, Dubey said, "The three-day celebration will get going on October 14 with a carnival, where children from PCB-run schools will welcome visitors. Apart from music and dance performances, laser shows and bicycle stunts have been planned, Dubey said.

When contacted, PCB chief executive officer S K Sardana said, "Plans are in place to ensure that the M G Road region will sport a festive look during the CYG and the Grand Carnival."

There is a need to bring private industry and the armed forces community on a common platform and facilitate more cooperation between the two sectors, S Radhakrishnan, deputy director, (Sc 'G'), National Chemical Laboratories, said here on Tuesday.

"Modern warfare involves a lot of state-of-the-art technology, which requires various high-tech materials that contains polymers. Such materials are produced and used by defence forces in many advanced countries and we cannot afford to be unaware of what gadgets are being used to counter enemy forces," Radhakrishnan told a press conference. "Also, polymer-related products can play an important role in reducing the weight, that is, cargo of a soldier, such as ammunition, bulletproof vest and other gear," he said.

The defence sub-committee and polymer sub-committee, in collaboration with the Mahratta Chamber of Commerce, Industries and Agriculture (MCCIA), have organised a seminar on 'Application of Polymers in Defence,' on October 7 to generate awareness about the advantages of polymer and polymer-related products in defence equipment, Radhakrishnan said. Southern Command GOC-In-C Lt Gen Noble Thamburaj would be the chief guest at the seminar, which would be attended by several senior officers of the Southern Command, apart from officials of the Defence Materials and Stores Research and Development Establishment and Armament Research and Development Establishment. "The seminar will focus on bringing the polymer industry and the defence forces community together to discuss new polymeric materials, applications and future requirements," Radhakrishnan said.

Heading: Heart-stopping - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has opposed the fare hike by the Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML) and asked the authorities to first strive to improve its services. The BJP has also threatened to hold agitations if the PMPML does not withdraw the hike.

Similarly, they also urged him to add more number of buses to the fleet and also asked the official why some of the bus-routes have been cancelled.

Later, talking to media persons, Shirole said, "The PMPML authorities have no concrete plans to upgrade its services. Despite not making any improvement in the services, the administration has hiked the charges, which is not fair."

Heading: The Cultural thread - Indian Express
Content:
Aortic Aneurysm can be fatal. Unfortunately it is usually detected only accidentally during a medical test or procedure

Imagine the horror of Mahendra Rapole, when he walked into Ruby Hall Clinic, Pune for a minor ailment, but was informed that he needs to be urgently operated for an aortic aneurysm, or he will not survive long. He was lucky, you may not be. The name may be a tongue twister, and may not be mentioned as often as Cancer or AIDS, but it's as lethal. And if that hasn't piqued your curiosity, then read on.

What are aortic aneurysms?
The Aorta is the major blood vessel that feeds blood to the body. An Aortic Aneurysm is a weakened and bulging area in the aorta. The aorta, about the thickness of a garden hose, runs through the center of your body. Because the aorta is the body's predominant supplier of blood, a ruptured aortic aneurysm can cause life-threatening bleeding.

World Heart Day was observed on September 28 and on the occasion Dr Shirish Hiremath, director of Cardiology, Ruby Hall Clinic explained that Aneurysms usually do not cause any symptoms until they become very large or rupture. Often, the most common symptom is death itself. Aneurysms in the abdominal aorta often are found coincidentally when the individual undergoes a medical test or procedure for some other reason."

How do they happen?
An aneurysm occurs when the wall of the aorta becomes weak or damaged. The aorta, the main artery supplying blood to the body, exits at the top of the heart and curves downward, passing through the chest and abdomen. Over time, the constant pressure of blood flowing through a weakened area can cause a section of the aorta to slowly enlarge. Bulging can occur in any artery in the body. It is most common in the abdominal aorta.

Screening for aortic aneurysms: Immediate treatment can be life saving for aneurysm. Screening is recommended for certain high-risk groups such as:
* Men 65 or older who have been or still are smokers
* Men over 50 and women over 60 whose parent or sibling had an aortic aneurysm.

Treating Aortic Aneurisms:
Once detected, close monitoring of the aneurysm size is the proper treatment for most people. Ultrasound/CT scan in every six to 12 months is the usual monitoring strategy. Any abdominal aortic aneurysm larger than about two inches (5.5 cm) in size requires surgery to repair it. This may vary by individual patient.

Preventing aortic aneurisms
* "No medicine can prevent an aortic aneurysm", says Dr Hiremath. However, measures can be taken that will help keep your blood vessels healthy and strong.
* Eat a low-fat, low-cholesterol diet.
