Heading: High oil bill pushes up trade deficit - Indian Express
Content:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and ICICI Bank on Tuesday reassured the bank's investors and customers about the financial health of the country's second-largest bank, saying ICICI Bank was well-capitalised and has enough cash to meet depositor demand. ICICI Bank shares which tumbled 12 per cent on Monday, bounced back by 8.42 per cent on the Bombay Stock Exchange on Tuesday and the Bankex Index rose 4.9 per cent after the RBI issued a statement to clarify the bank's financial position.

KV Kamath, managing director and CEO, refuted the rumours about the financial ill-health of India's largest private lender, saying, "The absorption of the impact of the current market conditions on investment portfolio valuations will not pose any challenge to the bank's capital position."

"ICICI Bank Ltd is aware that rumours are being repeatedly circulated in certain centres regarding the financial strength of the ICICI bank. The bank states that these rumours are baseless and malicious," Kamath said. The bank's capital adequacy ratio (CAR) was 13.4 per cent as of June 30, more than the minimum 9 per cent required by regulators, Kamath said.

According to the RBI statement, there are reports in a section of the media that based on rumours regarding the financial strength of ICICI Bank, depositors are withdrawing cash at its ATMs and branches in some locations. "It is clarified that ICICI Bank has sufficient liquidity, including in its current account with the Reserve Bank of India, to meet the requirements of its depositors. The Reserve Bank of India is monitoring the developments and has arranged to provide adequate cash to ICICI Bank to meet the demands of its customers at its branches and ATMs. ICICI Bank and its subsidiary banks abroad are well capitalised," the RBI said.

Earlier, the bank's joint managing director, Chanda Kochhar, had said ICICI Bank might have to set aside an additional $28 million for potential losses on the 57 million euros ($82 million) in Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc debt held by its UK unit. The bank recorded $100 million in marked-to-market losses for the fourth quarter ended March 31 on overseas investments. For the fiscal year, the writedowns totaled $170 million.

However, mainly due to the ripple effect of the US financial crises across Asian markets, the BSE Bankex and Sensex depreciated by 12 per cent and 13 per cent, respectively, in the past four weeks whereas the ICICI Bank share price went down by around 20 per cent during the same period. The bank on September 17 denied rumours senior managers were selling shares.

Kamath said ICICI Bank has a very strong capital position, having proactively raised Rs 20,000 crore (about $ 5 billion) in June 2007, almost doubling its capital base. It has a networth of over Rs 47,000 crore (ie over $10 billion). "The bank"s CAR is among the highest levels of capital adequacy in large Indian banks. This reflects the healthy capital position and comfortable level of leverage,"ICICI Bank said.

Kamath on rumours

"There is a pattern to the whole thing... They (rumours) happen at a particular time and in a certain manner... in global context this type of rumours are the work of people who manipulate markets. The rumours impact stock price and can be used as an effective tool to achieve certain ends."

Reserve bank on ICICI Bank

Heading: Rel Money gets nod to acquire 10-pc stake in NMCE - Indian Express

Deficit up after the Indian crude basket hit $118.8 A barrel from $66.4 in the corresponding period last year, says an RBI report

Big portfolio outflows

Portfolio investment, RBI said in its report on Balance of Payments, witnessed large net outflows ($4.2 billion) in Q1 of 2008-09 due to large sales of equities by FIIs in the Indian stock market reflecting bearish condition in stock market and slowdown in global economy. Private transfers, which include remittances from Indian workers abroad, local withdrawal from NRIs etc, increased to $12 billion in the first quarter in 2008-09 from $ 7.8 billion a year ago. NRI deposits, both inflows and outflows, remained steady. Invisible payments increased by 14.8 per cent in Q1 of 2008-09 compared to 22.6 per cent during the same period last year.

Heading: Reliance Infratel IPO to be on hold, says Anil - Indian Express
Content:
Financial services firm Reliance Money has obtained approval from the Ministry of Consumer Affairs to acquire a 10 per cent stake in the National Multi-Commodity Exchange of India (NMCE) Board.

"We are pleased with this development, as it marks our foray into the national commodity exchange space that is expected to cross an annual turnover of Rs 74-lakh-crore (volume) by next year," Reliance Money director and CEO Sudip Bandyopadhyay said. Reliance Money had proposed to acquire a total of up to 26 per cent stake in NMCE in two phases. NMCE had accordingly applied for approvals from the regulator Forward Markets Commission (FMC), which in turn, recommended the acquisition to the Ministry of Consumer Affairs.

The Anil Ambani-led Reliance ADAG is the first large business group to get into the commodity exchange space in India.

Heading: Insurance cover for MF products to stay - Indian Express
Content:
Reliance Infratel, an Anil Dhirubhai Ambani Group (ADAG) company, will not enter the capital markets anytime soon. The initial public offering (IPO) of the company will be deferred till the markets gain stability. "Markets are choppy at this point of time and all of you are aware of that, in the present conditions we do not expect an IPO for Reliance Infratel," said the company's chairman Anil Ambani at the annual general meeting (AGM) of Reliance Communications (RCom).

The group had announced the IPO for its telecom tower firm Reliance Infratel, which was estimated to raise close to Rs 6,000 crore, in February. The public offer, which was planned, had got a regulatory go-ahead with Sebi's issuance of observations on the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) on May 12. As per the norms, it was required to close the IPO within 90 days of issuance of SEBI's observation — the period that ended on August 11. It was anticipated that the group might revive the process for IPO by filing a fresh draft prospectus. Reliance Infratel is 95 per cent owned by the ADAG and 5 per cent by foreign investors.

Addressing the AGM, Ambani said that the company is targetting 10 crore subscribers over a couple of years.

He also said that RCom would now curtail its capital expansion plan as the expenditure of the firm has reached its peak. "We are at the peak of our capex cycle. Starting next year, our capex intensity is likely to decline significantly. This is a transformational phase for our company with many of our large-scale initiatives currently at a project implementation stage," Ambani said.

Heading: Tata, SAIL ore reserves to be reassessed - Indian Express
Content:
In a significant move, insurance regulator IRDA has asked life insurance companies to put on hold the decision to discontinue offer of group covers on mutual fund products. Life Insurance Council, the association of insurance companies, had earlier decided to discontinue the offer of group life insurance cover on mutual fund products with effect from October 1, 2008.

"IRDA has advised the Life Insurance Council to review and put on hold the decision to discontinue offer of group cover," a SEBI release said. The council had earlier decided that the insurer would not sell group covers to mutual funds that bundle life insurance with units and thereby create competition for ULIPs. The IRDA fiat will come as a major relief to some fund houses involved in selling schemes bundled with insurance cover, said an analyst.

The decision taken by the Life Insurance Council, a self-regulatory body, was significant since some of its members have a common parentage with asset management companies (AMCs). AMCs have been complaining about life insurers invading their turf with unit-linked insurance plans with a predominant equity bias.

Association of Mutual Funds in India (Amfi) had recently approached market regulator SEBI to permit them to sell insurance products to their investors and collect premium from them.

However, according to insurers, present insurance regulations require them to maintain a solvency margin of 150 per cent, which is much higher than the capital requirement norms for fund houses.

Significant Reversal

•Life Insurance Council had decided to discontinue the offer of group life insurance cover on MF products from October 1, 2008

• Insurance regulator IRDA has asked life insurance companies to put the decision on hold

•The IRDA fiat will come as a major relief to some fund houses involved in selling schemes bundled with insurance cover

Heading: Combating terror - Indian Express
Content:
The mines ministry does not seem to be enthused by the domestic steel industry's bid to ensure raw material security through captive iron ore mines. It has decided to reassess the exact quantum of iron ore in the existing mines of steel giants such as Tata Steel and state-run Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) to check if they actually need more for capacity expansion.

"As new steel plants demand captive (iron ore) mines, it is important to know the size of the existing resource. We have decided to start a re-assessment exercise, but it will take some time. They (SAIL and Tata) were the pioneers and got the best mines," mines secretary Shantanu Consul said.

The ministry's move assumes significance, especially at a time when SAIL, Tata and many others are mid-way through their big-ticket capacity expansion projects. Tata Steel plans to increase its capacity five-fold over the next 10 years to 25 million tonne entailing an investment of about Rs 1 lakh crore. Besides a 12 MT greenfield plant in Jharkhand, a 6 MT project in Orissa and a 5 MT plant in Chhattisgarh, it plans to double its capacity in its Jamshedpur facility to 10 million tonnes. For these, Tata Steel requires about 1.8 billion tonne of additional ore.

Similarly, SAIL which plans to hike steel output to 26 MT at an estimated expenditure of about Rs 54,000 crore, needs an estimated 5.74 billion tonne ore over the next 50 years, of which 2.71 billion tonnes is required for its existing and new plants in Jharkhand. The decision to reassess needs will certainly not go down well with the companies which argue that for lowering production costs, access to raw materials is crucial.

What is surprising is that the Indian Bureau of Mines, a PSU under the Mines Ministry has undertaken such an exercise earlier. The mining industry reckons that the quantum of reserves in the existing mines of SAIL and Tata Steel amount to about 35 per cent of total reserves in India. To get a factual position, it has even called for an independent survey by Mineral Exploration Corporation Limited.

Putting a lid over the debate between captive mining and merchant mining, Consul said these would have to co-exist. "Mining as an independent activity and must go on. Captive mining, on the other hand, is there to stay," he said.

Who's got what?

•Industry reckons SAIL, Tata Steel have 35 per cent of country's reserves

• Ministry decides to reassess the exact quantum of iron ore they have

• SAIL, Tata mid-way through big-ticket capacity expansion projects

• The companies say to lower costs, access to raw materials is crucial

Heading: Explained - Indian Express
Content:
• This refers to 'NSA meets top US anti-terror outfits'. Of late, there have been reports in the media that India should learn from the US how to prevent terror. A step has been taken in the right direction but one wonders why so much time was wasted? Finally the NSA has set the ball rolling but we still have a long wait to see any visible effect. One is curious, meanwhile, as to where the government will begin.

— Deepak Chikramane

Mumbai

• The national security advisor, M.K. Narayanan, did get to meet the US director of national intelligence, Mike McConnell, to learn how the US successfully prevented terrorists from repeating 9/11. That is as far as it goes. How effectively a policy works depends on the political will of the party in power. Unfortunately the Indian government fails on this count. Let's take an example: acting on a tip off from one of the arrested terrorists, the Delhi police arrest two students of the Jamia Millia Islamia University. While the matter is still under investigation, the Jamia VC sanctions legal aid for them. A senior Congress leader, and Union minister, endorses the VC's action. By its vote bank politics, the ruling UPA turns a success into defeat. What will even the best of advice do if this is how the government acts?

— R.J. Khurana

Bhopal

• If India's capital, bearing the brunt of successive blasts, is not safe, how can we ensure the security of the country as a whole? Politically, we have no means of combating terrorism as the government is busy dealing with the United States. Let the Union government display its political will to deal with terror and then seek advice from India's friends.

— Anuvrat Arya

New Delhi

Tread with caution

• This refers to the editorial 'Friend in deed'. While the editorial justly praises Manmohan Singh and George W. Bush on the civilian nuclear deal, some of its observations seem far-fetched. The suggestion that India and the US now consider an unprecedented political co-operation to stabilise Pakistan and Afghanistan is one example. Such an effort will have military implications and might even involve India indirectly in the US war on terror in Pakistan.

— Ramesh R. Jadhav

Pune

Not quite enough

• L.K. Advani he needs to be told that, in the Indian context, secularism means an abiding respect for all faiths, as well as allowing them to be practised without fear or favour. The continuing attacks on Christians in Orissa and Karnataka, where the NDA calls the shots, has significantly damaged India's secular image. As the prime minister designate of the BJP, Advani would need to do more than merely highlight his Christian schooling.

— J.M. Manchanda

New Delhi

Heading: Nuclear ambiguity - Indian Express
Content:
Indian Parliament •Money bills must be introduced by the government of the day

US Congress• Any member can introduce a money bill

Indian Parliament•Money bills must be introduced in the Lok Sabha

US Congress•Money bills must be introduced in the lower house, the House of Representatives

Indian Parliament•Bills are sent to "select committees", which can discuss them; or they are opened for more general discussion outside — the Bill is "circulated"

US Congress•Bills are sent to committees, which are subject-specific; committees can recommend changes, or can simply ignore the bill, and are thus more powerful

Indian Parliament•The bill is then returned to the house, where a vote is taken on it

US Congress• If the committee permits, the bill is then subject to a vote in the house

Indian Parliament•A vote must be taken, unless a "dilatory motion" is passed, for example to re-refer the bill to a committee

US Congress•Members can block a vote in any of several ways, including — in the Senate — by "filibuster", by going on speaking for hours till the time for debate has ended

Indian Parliament•If the bill is passed by one house, it is referred to the other, which may amend or reject it — unless it's a money bill in the Rajya Sabha

US Congress•If the bill is passed by one house, it is referred to the other which may amend or reject it — even if it's a money bill

Indian Parliament•The amended or rejected bill is returned to the originating house, which summons a "joint committee" from both houses to hammer out the inconsistencies

US Congress• The amended or rejected bill is returned to the originating house, which summons a "conference committee" from both houses to hammer out the inconsistencies

Indian Parliament•If the joint committee doesn't manage to agree, both houses meet together and vote on the bill

US Congress•Once a bill has been passed by a conference committee, it goes directly to the floor of both houses for a vote, and is not open to further amendment. If the conference committee cannot pass the bill, it doesn't go further

Indian Parliament•A bill passed by parliament is expected to receive presidential assent

US Congress•A bill passed by Congress can be vetoed by the president; it then needs a two-thirds majority in each house to "override" the veto

Heading: Playing with fire - Indian Express
Content:
Despite the high level Indian political engagement with the Chinese leadership in recent weeks — the foreign ministers met earlier this month in New Delhi, the National Security Adviser traveled to China a few days later and the two prime ministers talked in New York last week — Beijing's ambiguity on the Indo-US nuclear deal persists.

A commentary in the latest issue of 'Beijing Review' remained sceptical in its assessment of the 45-nation Nuclear Suppliers Group's decision on September 6 to support the Indo-US nuclear deal. On the one hand, the analysis by Pang Sen, the Director General of UN Associations in China, offers some sense of realism that has entirely escaped our own communists. "The NSG's decision is a diplomatic victory for India as it is a tacit acceptance of India's absence from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) and a declaration of forgiveness for the nuclear weapon tests conducted in 1998, which at the time were mostly condemned by the international community".

In a punchline, Pang Sen adds, "When a gigantic and growing economy defies the world and demonstrates its nuclear abilities, economic might wins out in the end".

India's rise and its nuclear differentiation from Pakistan, however, is a major concern for China. "Pakistan, India's neighbour and rival, clearly has reason to worry", the 'Review' says."Regional stability and the global non-proliferation regime would have been better served", Pang Sen argues by quoting Islamabad's reaction, "if the US had considered a package approach for both India and Pakistan, which conducted its first nuclear weapon tests two weeks after India"."China hopes the NSG will equally address the aspirations of all parties (read Pakistan) for the peaceful use of nuclear power", he said. "Only time will tell", the analysis concludes on an ambiguous note, "Whether the NSG decision would turn out to be a blessing or a blow to the international non-proliferation regime".

Engaging Kayani

It stands to reason that the implications of the Indo-US nuclear deal must have figured prominently in Pakistan Army Chief, Gen. Ashfaq Pervez Kayani's trip to China last week.

Gen. Kayani was ostensibly there to observe the People's Liberation Army's exercises called "Warrior 2008". The visit, however, was important enough for Gen. Kayani to head to Beijing within hours after the Marriott hotel bombing in Islamabad.

During his five day visit to China, Gen. Kayani met with the top Chinese leadership. The Chinese defence minister, Liang Guanglie was quoted as telling Gen. Kayani that "China will further strengthen Sino-Pakistani ties and relations between the two armed forces" in the changed circumstances. New Delhi, naturally, would look beyond these boilerplate statements to assess how exactly China might compensate Pakistan after India's successful civil nuclear initiative. Despite Islamabad's hopes that China might sell new nuclear reactors to Pakistan, there is no evident way in which Beijing can get a deal similar to that the NSG has approved for India.

Gen. Kayani is more likely to have discussed the longer term strategic and military consequences of the Indo-US nuclear deal for China and Pakistan. Amidst mounting tension with the United States and growing gap with India, the Pak Army is looking for strong security assurances from its 'all weather friend', China.

For Beijing, the challenge in turn, lies in maintaining what it might see as a necessary balance, nuclear and military, between India and Pakistan. India, on its part, would closely monitor the planned visits of President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Yousuf Raza Gilani to China in the coming weeks.

Burma grip

In a study released Monday, EarthRights International, a Western NGO, has drawn attention to a dramatic surge in the presence of Chinese multinational corporations in Burma over the last one year.

In what has been billed as the most comprehensive survey of Chinese investment in Burma, the ERI points to 69 Chinese MNC'S involved in 90 completed, current and planned projects in the hydropower, mining and resource extraction sectors in Burma. Earlier ERI research done during 2007 had identified only 26 Chinese companies pursuing 62 projects.

The ERI report comes only a few days after the Burmese government confirmed that Chinese state-controlled China Non-Ferrous Metal Group will proceed to mine nickel in the Mandalay region. Analysts say this US $ 600 million dollar venture could be one of the largest contracts in Burma that could export up 40 million tons of nickel ore.

The writer is a Professor at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore iscrmohan@ntu.edu.sg

Heading: Bailing out an ocean - Indian Express
Content:
In an article in the latest issue of CPM organ People's Democracy, general secretary Prakash Karat questions the wisdom of the government and finance minister P.Chidambaram in persisting with economic reforms that have burnt the US in the form of the present crisis. He argues that the US crisis must open the eyes of all the political parties who have uncritically supported financial sector liberalisation like allowing FDI in the insurance sector, favouring the privatizing of pension funds and supporting the takeover of Indian private banks by foreign banks by allowing up to 74 per cent stake. "After the bursting of the real estate bubble and the financial crisis in the United States, one would have expected this ardent advocate of financial sector reforms to rethink. But that has not happened," he says.

Karat says that investment banks and hedge funds in the US played a key role in restructuring the financial system which consisted of the use of derivative instruments like options and futures. It is this unbridled financial speculation through use of dubious instruments driven by greed for quick profits which has led to the current financial meltdown. In the Indian context, he says the New Pension Scheme, if implemented, would lead to thousands of crores of rupees of the employees going into the stock markets, and no regulatory authority can stop the wild fluctuations in the stock markets. The New Pension Scheme does not assure a minimum return to employees, he adds. "The finance minister and the ruling establishment are not concerned about what would happen to the savings of ordinary people, or, the pensions of the working people, or, how public investment would be affected if India gets subjected to the rapacious deregulated financial system prevalent in the US. But all other non-Left political parties should ponder over the course which has been adopted in the name of pushing through reforms," he concludes.

PM in the people's dock

The editorial accuses Prime Minister Manmohan Singh of violating many of the assurances given by him in Parliament on the nuclear deal and says such a betrayal of trust by the PM has serious consequences, both for India's future as an independent nation in the world and for the future of India's parliamentary democracy itself. "In the final analysis, the executive (government), whose head is the prime minister, is answerable and accountable to the legislature. The negation of this accountability is the negation of the Indian constitutional scheme of things," it says.

Claiming that many of the nine assurances that the PM had given in Parliament were systematically violated in the run up to finalising the deal, it says in the bargain, India ends up being tied to US imperialism's global strategy impinging severely on our independent foreign policy and sovereignty. "The issue, thus, is not one of accepting the CPI(M)'s or the Left's critique of this deal as being against the fundamental interests of India and reducing India into a subordinate ally of US imperialism. The issue is whether the prime minister of India will remain loyal to his own assurances to his own people made in the Indian parliament?...... "What we are asking is simply this: the prime minister must stand by his own assurances to the parliament. Otherwise, as he is fond of repeatedly stating in the parliament, history shall judge him. Prior to that, however, the Indian people shall surely do so," it says.

Worst is yet to come

In an article titled the end of an illusion, noted economist Prabhat Patnaik talks about the financial crisis that has gripped the US. He says even if the bailout of distressed financial giants manages to prevent a severe economic crisis, it will certainly not be able to prevent a recession which appears to have already set in.

The state of credit will continue to be difficult for sometime to come, which will only worsen the recession. Even the financial crisis will not be over with the current "bail-out" package, he says.

After the Bear Stearns episode earlier this year every one thought that the worst was over, but it wasn't. The same perhaps is true of the present. The system of course will recover, but the form in which it will do so is unlikely to be the same as before. And this will open up new possibilities of praxis, he claims.

Heading: The past is a foreign country - Indian Express
Content:
It is no surprise that the recent meeting of the New Global Champions comprising mid-size successful corporates, organised by the World Economic Forum in Tianjin, China, was dominated by the current financial turmoil. China has high stakes , not only because of its large dollar-denominated assets but also because of the broader consequences of this crisis. To the extent that its exports get impaired it will seek to reflate domestic consumption even while addressing new concerns on pollution, improving food safety and calming the unease from growing income and regional divides. Its sovereign wealth funds also have an exposure in some of these troubled banks and financial institutions.

However current efforts in the US to deal with the crisis are essentially quick fixes. They do not address some long term endemic issues —

First, there were serious macroeconomic concerns which had remained under-addressed for some time. Structural imbalances arising out of low savings and high consumption in the US and relying on savings of others, particularly China and Japan, could not continue for ever. Even for a dominant economy like the US, a combination of high current account deficit with high fiscal deficit was overdue for a correction. The debate on the current crisis overlooks the need to redress these embedded structural imbalances. These will inter alia imply tha consumption levels in the US need to be better aligned with their propensity to save.

Second, the current bailout package can only worsen the US fiscal deficit. The prices at which these toxic assets are eventually sold may be lower than the cost of acquisition. A significant scaling back on defence expenditure would reqire a broader consensus after the election. Rising fiscal deficits also circumscribe commitments on tax breaks and new expenditure programmes. Thus the rhetoric generated in the electoral debate might not translate into practice.

Third, it is ironic that the IMF has suddenly woken up with a start. In a recent interview, its managing director Dominique Strauss-Kahn stressed the need for wider international consensus to address the current turmoil. This is characteristic of Bretton Woods institutions which react well after the event but still seek to play a constructive role. They promise to become more vigilant in future, commit to greater reform and pledge to reinvent themselves, but once the crisis blows over it goes back to business as usual. Under the IMF charter, it is expected not only to review government policies but also the regulatory environment in so far as they affect overall stability and growth, as well as suggest appropriate diagnostic measures. Clearly this crisis did not happen overnight and the Fund's surveillance mechanism failed to detect it, much less raise any alarm. There is no doubt that this turmoil will have serious contagion effects elsewhere. Strauss-Kahn is right that the Fund should play a bigger role but who is listening to it? Has the institution been refashioned to detect, prevent, mitigate and enforce a new set of rules that would undoubtedly be necessary?

Fourth, the moral hazard questions go beyond regulatory failures. It is even broader than assignment of responsibilities, the poor judgment of rating agencies whose objectivity was compromised while seeking collateral business, and ethical issues in determining the compensation of CEOs and senior management. They raise issues of a more conscionable burden-sharing between taxpayers, ordinary shareholders and those responsible for running these companies. Any response which solely vindicates the critique that while profits are private, their debts are public, will lack credibility. To what extent should the taxpayers pay for the failed judgments of rating agencies, regulators and the senior management of these institutions?

Finally has market economics been buried for a while? While the pundits of high finance obviously have a lot to explain and correct, it would be unwise to draw exaggerated conclusions. The broader principle that while markets cannot play God, they remain the most efficient arbiter of resources, foster innovation, and enable competition to improve productivity, cannot be abandoned in haste. No doubt minimising market imperfections, improving regulatory oversight, objective assignment of risks and emoluments which better balance rewarding entrepreneurship with a sense of fairplay and equity remain policy challenges. These serious moral concerns need to be addressed in an appropriate manner. However in emerging markets like India it would hurt growth if the broader approach to improve the cost and quality of financial intermediation through competitive market economics is totally reversed. No doubt, policies and their pace must be nuanced to suit specific country needs. In the short run, easing liquidity constraints, encouraging inward capital flows and shoring up confidence will remain critical. However sound judgments cannot be replaced by transient panic. Maturity lies in drawing the right conclusions.

The writer is a member of Rajya Sabha

Heading: 800 projects, Rs 150 crore; talking statistics for MC’s vision for city growth - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Former Improvement Trust chairman goes underground - Indian Express
Content:
The Municipal Corporation has spent nearly Rs 150 crore on various development projects across the city. There are close to 800 projects being undertaken in various departments of which over 300 have been completed.

Estimates up to September reveal that the maximum amount is being spent on civil works with nearly Rs 109.41 crore having been allocated for the same.

Meanwhile, Rs 6.56 crore has been spent on works undertaken by the Electrical division while Rs 5.68 has been spent on projects undertaken by the Horticulture Wing.

Besides, projects have also been undertaken by the Public Health Wing that includes upgrading the storm water drainage as well as sewerage system and laying pipes for various purposes among others.

The maximum number of projects has been undertaken in the ward of the Mayor Pardeep Chhabra. There are as many as 62 different projects worth Rs 16.10 crore that have been started in Sectors 16, 17 and 22.

A large part of this is being used for the renovation of the MC building in Sector 17. Five new parking lots are also coming up and an amount of Rs 1.22 crore is being spent on this. Around Rs 4 crore is being spent in Sectors 16 and 22.

Chhabra says, "There are a number of projects that have been undertaken in the colonies, villages as well as the sectors. We are aiming at the balanced growth of the city."

With Rs 10.64 crore being spent in her ward, councillor Raj Kumari Mishra is not far behind Mayor Pardeep Chhabra. Her ward includes the Industrial Area, Sanjay Colony as well as Colony Number 4.

As many as 51 projects amounting to Rs 6.96 crore have been sanctioned for the ward of councillor Davinder Singh Babla that includes Sectors 27, 28 and 30. Councillor Chandermukhi Sharma's ward — Sectors 1 to 11 — currently has 53 projects on course at an estimated cost of Rs 8.74 crore.

The wards of councillors Ram Sumer Morya and Manjit Singh Chohan have, meanwhile, been allocated the least amounts of Rs 39 lakh and 96 lakh respectively.

Heading: Only 29 assembly sittings held in 18 months: MLA - Indian Express
Content:
Controversial former Congress MLA and ex-chairman of Amritsar Improvement Trust (AIT) Jugal Kishore Sharma, who is wanted in the 32-acre land scam by the Vigilance Bureau, has gone underground.

The Vigilance sleuths have conducted several raids in vain to trace him and his former boss and local bodies minister Chaudhary Jagjit Singh, also an accused in the case.

The local residence of Sharma wore a deserted look today, and his personal staff said they were not aware of his whereabouts. They added that he had left home a few days back.

"We are looking for Sharma, the prime accused in the land scam, and others," said Vigilance SP Chaman Lal Sharma. "We will nab them soon," said a Vigilance officer, adding that raids were being carried out all over the state and in Chandigarh. Apart from Sharma and Chaudhary Jagjit, Brig GS Khehra (retd) and Subash Sharma, a partner in Veer Enclave, are also wanted by the Vigilance for questioning.

Both the leaders were once close confidants of former CM Captain Amarinder Singh, who has been expelled from the Vidhan Sabha in this case, which pertains to the exemption of 32 acres from the chunk of total land acquired by AIT for a Trust's scheme near New Amritsar areas during the previous Congress regime.

Former Congress Speaker of the Vidhan Sabha and Capt Amarinder's bete noire Bir Devinder Singh had raised the matter, and alleged tampering with the assembly's records related to an inquiry into the scam.

"I am not aware about Sharmaji. I am not in contact with him," said Ravi Sharma, personal secretary of Jugal Kishore Sharma. Mobile phone of Sharma has been switched off and the family members refuse to talk.

This is not for the first time that Sharma has courted controversies. He was often accused by the Trust members of keeping them in the dark and pushing various items through the general body meetings without circulating agenda copies to them.

The Veer Enclave's 32 acres' exemption was also cleared during one such meeting, after which some Trust members had raised hue and cry, but Sharma went ahead.

Rampant corruption in the functioning of the Improvement Trust under his chairmanship was also talk of the town. Besides, he had used his influence to get a huge commercial building come up near the Municipal Corporation in utter violation of the norms.

Chaudhary is also an accused in the Ludhiana's City Centre scam.

Heading: Bomb hoax creates panic in Mansa - Indian Express
Content:
In the last 18 months of the SAD-BJP rule, the total time that was utilised in the Punjab Vidhan Sabha during all the sessions was a little over 110 hours.

This was stated by Sukhpal Singh Khaira, Congress MLA from Bholath, today. He said the information on the "inadequate" number of sittings and the time consumed was based on the bulletins issued by the Punjab Vidhan Sabha. Khaira said ever since this government came to power, only 29 sittings were held.

Addressing newspersons, the Congress MLA said he has written to the President to intervene since the purpose of the House was getting eroded.

He said, "The opposition MLAs are being ignored by the ruling members. The only place left for opposition to air their thoughts is the Vidhan Sabha. Going by the data, the assembly has met and consumed merely 0.8 per cent of the total time since the formation of the government." Giving an example, Khaira said the last session, from September 4 to September 10, had one sitting for obituaries, followed by one for discussion the next day and then four off days, and finally one sitting on the last day. "In this entire monsoon session, the time utilised was 7.16 hours," he said.

In the letter to the President, Khaira expressed the need to redefine the functioning of the legislators. "The legislators should meet on the pattern of the Lok Sabha MPs so that the House can contribute productively," he said. He alleged that the government was bypassing the opposition MLAs. "Grants of Rs 2 crore in constituencies are being doled out. Defeated MLAs are disbursing funds, inaugurating events and laying foundation stones," he said.

Heading: Kohar, aide acquitted - Indian Express
Content:
A Call from a mobile phone at the landline number of Station Superintendent of Mansa Railway Station at 11:30 am kept the staff of railways, GRP, district administration and local police on tenterhooks for more than six hours today.

The caller said a bomb has been planted in the last bogey of a passenger train that runs between Hisar and Bathinda. The train, which was coming from Bathinda, had just left Sada Singh Wala village for Mansa when the call was received.

The Railway authorities informed the district administration, which got the train vacated at Mansa Railway Station.

Even as authorities claimed that nothing suspicious was recovered from the train, search operation was on in the 14-bogey train by several teams, among them anti-sabotage squads, till the filing of this report.

Out of the total 14 bogies, 11 were meant for passengers and rest for goods and luggage.

"Speaking in Hindi and claiming to be hailing from Rohtak, the caller said the bomb would explode in 35 minutes," Mansa Station Superintendent Inderjit Singh told The Indian Express. "When I asked his name, he disconnected the line," Inderjit said, adding, "An alert was sounded immediately."

In the afternoon, passengers were made to board the Ferozepur-Delhi train.

Meanwhile, as the landline number of the station superintendent had caller identification facility, the number of the caller was found to be from the Punjab circle.

However, the calls made by the police to that number yielded no results. "The calls did get through on a number of occasions, but no one answered," said Mansa SSP Manminder Singh.

Sources said that the police were using the Global Positioning System (GPS) to know the whereabouts of the caller.

Heading: Report lifts state’s spirits amid FICCI’s dampener - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Revenue Minister Ajit Singh Kohar and his personal assistant Jarnail Singh were acquitted by a local court in the case of corruption and disproportionate assets. After the court appearance, Kohar told mediapersons that he was falsely booked in the case by the previous government. Interestingly, after the change of guard, the Vigilance Bureau, which had filed the case earlier, had submitted the cancellation report.

Notably, out of the total 18 accused, 16, including son of Kohar, Naib Singh, and his wife, were earlier discharged.

The VB had accused Kohar of possessing benami properties worth over Rs 20 crore, which was disproportionate to his known sources of income, and booked him on August 9, 2002, under various sections of the IPC and the Prevention of Corruption Act. The case was registered by the then VB SSP Lok Nath Angra.

The VB had earlier alleged that Kohar had purchased properties in the name over dozen persons, who had agreed to become witnesses in the case. However, they turned hostile in the court and claimed that they were the real owners of the properties. Last year, the VB filed an application in the court for the cancellation of the case on the ground that it could not garner sufficient evidences. But Kohar and his PA were tried because the charges against them had been framed before the filing of the cancellation application.

Heading: Punjab signs MoU for luxury train - Indian Express
Content:
For Punjab, this could salvage some lost pride. With FICCI downgrading the prospects of investment in the state as "pessimistic", the state government is seeking solace in a report by the Center for Monitoring of Indian Economy (CMIE).

The CMIE, in its report for 2007-08, said Punjab was emerging as a favorite destination for entrepreneurs and industrial houses and got an investment of $13.72 billion of which 50 per cent was under implementation. The report by FICCI, presented on Friday, came as an embarrassment for Punjab Industries Minister Manoranjan Kalia, who was the chief guest on the occasion.

The CMIE said besides real estate projects, a lot of investment had come in manufacturing sector followed by services, electronics and construction. The report has credited the state for the FDI flow, citing the Luxmi Mittal Bathinda Refinery Project.

Talking to The Indian Express, Kalia said the government was committed to improve the shortfalls mentioned in the FICCI report. The minister said the investment in the information technology sector has started to flow. "We had recently held a meeting with many IT companies. The government is planning to offer them special zones for setting up units. Dedicated power supply too is being contemplated," he said.

The CMIE report said the manufacturing sector, textiles, chemicals and paper industry had received maximum share. The report by FICCI was jointly drafted by Konard Adeneur Foundation (KAF). FICCI's findings had said 62 per cent of respondents took a pessimistic view of Punjab as an investment destination, while only 9 per cent were optimistic. Another 52 per cent felt that industries in the state were facing difficulties and not growing.

Another industry body, Assocham, has also released its report on Punjab. It has suggested that Punjab was losing crores of rupees annually on account of free power to farm sector.

Punjab's new industrial policy is on the anvil. It is based on inputs submitted by the UNIDO, which was engaged by the state government for suggesting a roadmap for Punjab's industrial growth.

Heading: Green Zone - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab today signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Ministry of Railways to start a luxury tourist train, which will be manufactured at Railway Coach Factory, Kapurthala.

The MoU was signed by Principal Secretary, Tourism, and Chief Executive Officer of the Punjab Heritage and Tourism Promotion Board Geetika Kalha and Executive Director (Tourism and Catering) of Railway Board, Ministry of Railways, Ashok Kumar at Rail Bhawan in New Delhi.

Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, Union Minister of Railways Lalu Prasad Yadav, Union Minister of Tourism and Culture Ambika Soni and Minister for Tourism and Culture, Punjab, Hira Singh Gabria were also present on the occasion. Kalha said the proposed train would cover popular destinations in north India, including Amritsar, Anandpur Sahib, Chandigarh, Dharamsala, Patiala and Kurukshetra, besides Agra, Delhi and Jaipur in its seven-day itinerary.

The train equipped with five-star facilities will have salons, multi-cuisine restaurant cars, lounge bars, observation cars with a viewing gallery, gym, spa, library, games room and a computer centre. The project was expected to be ready within two years.

Badal said with this train, the unexploited tourism potential of the state would get a further boost. He urged Lalu to defer the Punjab's share of Rs 20 lakh per trip of the luxury train for at least three years till the project becomes economically viable. Lalu agreed to the demand.

Heading: Electricity cuts are back - Indian Express
Content:
With the changing scenario on both the residential and official front, parking problem is causing lot of inconvenience. Those who are making new complexes are using the underground area for the purpose. But those with the green fingers here also find one or the other way to make the area green. In the jungle of concrete even a single plant is eye soothing. In the accompanying picture, provision has been provided to grow small ground cover plants. Those with weak stem or the trailing type are most suitable. Asparagus, wudeleia (the one in the picture with serrated margined leaves and yellow flowers) is another good choice.

* I want to plant kinnow now in my home garden. Am I late or in time? Where can I get good quality plants?
Ranjit Sidhu, Mohali
Ranjit, you are very much in time. For getting good quality plants approach Punjab Agriculture University and ask for virus free kinnow.

* Should I start putting seeds of winter annual for preparing seedlings. When should these be transplanted?
Rani Aggarwal, Chandigarh
What are you waiting for? Go ahead and do it fast. These should be transplanted by the mid November.

* Suggest some colour scheme for winter annuals and what plants will suit for this purpose?
Manorma, Chandigarh
For winter flowers the colour scheme suits in case of those flowers that bear profusely, like phlox, stock, verbena, candytuft etc. nowadays, one can get name-it-you-get-it colours in most of the flowers. Do some exercise seeing the availability.

* Can I sow English type of radish and also the red round radish?
Manpreet Singh, Panchkula
Wait for some time more, say a month, for the English radish but go ahead with red round type.

For gardening queries, ask Dr Green at satishnarula@yahoo.co.in

Heading: God of big things - Indian Express
Content:
The residents, who were hoping that October will bring relief from power cuts as the paddy season is over, got a rude shock today, when the Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB) re-imposed four to six-hour power cuts in the state.

The reason being given for load-shedding is that the power purchase agreements expired on September 30, and the board had no choice but to impose cuts to fill the gap between demand and supply.

PSEB Member (Distribution) HS Brar, while talking to The Indian Express, said, "We had not expected a sudden change in the weather. Once again the AC load has increased, leading to an additional 250-MW burden. We had to re-impose power cuts, which had ended in September-mid."

While Ludhiana is facing cuts for about six hours, Amritsar, Jalandhar and Patiala remain in dark for about four hours.

Rural areas too are suffering cuts in the range of six and seven hours from today onwards. Due to snow in the hills, hydel supply has also been reduced from existing 350 lakh units to 285 lakh units. However, the industry is not facing weekly off.

PSEB authorities said they were purchasing about 500 LUs of power from outside from today as against 800 LUs till yesterday. The authorities have not hinted at relief till the time the temperature dips.

Heading: Ravana’s new look - Indian Express
Content:
Rama and his lila never fail to draw audiences

It's a story that you can never get enough of. Year after year, we flock to see the win of good over evil, as Rama's charisma draws audiences across generations and sensibilities. Night after night, the dramatic folk re-enactment of the ten-day battle between Lord Rama and Ravana as described in Ramayana gets more absorbing and engrossing and Ramlila is a hit all the way. The act may have altered over time, but the essence and the spirit is intact, precisely why for years Ramlila Committees are always set to make the show a memorable one. The thunderous applause as Rama sets his foot on stage, the audience whistling and adding its bit as the story proceeds adds to the festive feel.

"My children and I don't miss a single day of action. It's a great way to get them in touch with tradition and reaffirms our faith in the good,'' smiles Piyush Khanna. Following a family tradition of more than 35 years now, Swami Ram Prasad's Party is here all the way from Vrindavan for the 10-day Ramlila programme at Indradhanush Auditorium. Directing the show is Swami Prasad's son Prathmesh, who has been involved with the act since he was six, starting with playing various roles, including Rama. "Now I prefer to be backstage,'' Prathmesh travels across the country every year to stage Ram Lila and their party is a four-time winner at the National Ram Lila Mela. The story, traditional music, costumes and live interaction with the audience agrees the director makes Ram Lila so popular, in spite of the new versions of it on television and in films. What sets their show apart, he says, is the fact that they continue to use traditional music and dance and don't follow the Bollywood beats. "It's all folk-based and all the 30 actors are from Braj, so it's a very authentic feel to the show,'' Prathmesh says they've upgraded the costumes and added more colour to the stage and the effect is stunning.

For the last three years, the Market Welfare Association of Sector 31 has been showing Ramanand Sagar's Ramayana to large crowds, and it's children, quips BN Kaushak, that they want to reach out to. He agrees the magic on screen may not be the same as that of a live performance, but feels it's a good start to get the younger generation acquainted with our culture.

There are no jitters among the actors of the Shree Ram Lila Committee, as they get ready for the first day, first show of Ram Lila at the Parade Grounds. Since '53, their tryst with tradition continues uninterrupted. "Last year, we improved on the technical aspects and the response of the audience was superb,'' Suresh Bakshi talks of the 90-foot stage, great sound quality of the pre-recorded dialogues, tight script, continuous scenes sans any curtains and of course, experienced actors. What makes the show an-all time hit, adds Bakshi is because people relate to it at every level, "the classical pattern of verse is unique and people appreciate things which are deep, meaningful and honest. '' The show must go on!

Heading: Brush with freedom - Indian Express
Content:
Project Dashagriva is complete and the result is fascinating

Remember we brought you a story a few days back that mentioned fashion design students of the Inter National Institute of Fashion Design (INIFD) working on a project to give Ravana a new improvised look for this Ramleela? Well, Project Dashagriva is complete and the result is fascinating. Students have designed the costume which signifies four Vedas, six shastras and ten heads earned by Ravana. The front of the dress signifies the Tandava Nritya of Natraj which principally depicts Shakti of Shiva. The outfit's waistline has a painted Lord Kuber which depicts that Ravana is the God of Richness. 'Kaal' has been tied at the right leg of Ravana which symbolizes that he is the slave of Ravana. The centre motif of Ravana shows the Jagrit Kendilini Shakti and Nine Chakras. Not many are aware that Ravana was an exemplary scholar and an expert in 64 art forms which is been depicted in his new makeover. The team of 15 students which undertook extensive research for the project include: Arka Mriyank, Rashmi, Aashish, Robin, Sumit Rana, Punkaj Prabhakar, Anupam, Madhuri, Sapna, Pradeep, Shalini, Akansha, Shaina, Aakriti and Priyanka. Stepping in the costume and taking it on stage will be city's Sunil Sharma who plays Ravana at the Parade ground Ramleela.

Heading: For better & verse - Indian Express
Content:
Here's art for a cause. City based artist Prem Singh is one of the 74, and India's only artist, to be featured in a book titled Freedom and Art through an event called "Set a Book Free" on October 2 when all artists featured within the pages of the book will place a copy in a public location to raise interest. A collaborative effort by the Mirca Art Group, the book is an international coalition of professional artists and is set for release tomorrow. Artists from worldover have come together to raise voice in support of Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, who has been under house arrest in Myanmar for the past 18 years over her bid for political freedom. "To keep the flow life freedom is a must. Suu Kyi's struggle is very humanistic with an obvious concern to fulfill man's aspirations. The struggle may go on for years and years but nobody can deny the eternal truth that life thrives on freedom. If it is Suu Kyi's it should be the concern of the global society."

Each work of art is accompanied by a statement about the synergy of freedom and art in the world. Singh shares, "Freedom is imbibed in art. I never felt any kind of restraint from anywhere while expressing my inner voice into visual voice. As long as the child is alive in me, the freedom of expression happens." Singh believes that an artist plays an important role in the society, "An artist is a thinking man. He lives in the society and through his artistic expressions highlights his visionary concerns by making visible from the invisible with obvious urge to share with the art lovers," meaning that the society and the artist are knit in a permanent bond. But the relationship isn't always warm. "Works of art have often come under the 'moral' scanner. When they are given a form hitherto unknown to the eyes of the society, sometimes illiterate, ignorant and inflammatory charges are inflicted upon an isolated artist with the deliberate intent of paralysing him," he signs off.

Heading: The Lens Travelogue - Indian Express
Content:
A travelling festival to bring poetry films to Chandigarh

Think films, and it's either fiction or non fiction. But this is not the case with Sadho. Their mission is to take great 'poetry to people' through the innovative use of arts, media and social action, in the form of a rare third genre of cinema, poetry films. And their next stop is none other than Chandigarh. As a part of its travelling festival, Sadho will bring about 25 to 30 of its selected 85 films to the city. These will be presented at two screenings on October 4 and 5. Interesting, The curator of film fest, Jitendra Ramprakash, hails from Chandigarh. The screenings will also include a film by Amtojh Sandhu, a filmmaker-photographer-painter, from the city. Now based in London, her film "Ya Devi - The Goddess" will be showcased. The venues are: October 4 - State Museum, Sector 10 and October 5 - Rock Garden. For more details, visit - www.sadho.com.

Heading: Sporting Fashion - Indian Express
Content:
Navneet Saxena shares his journeys across the countries through Travel Melange

The camera is often your best companion during your travels. For Navneet Saxena it is always so. And now through Travel Melange, a photography exhibition, he presents some unique insights into the cities he has visited around the globe. Sixty photographs take you through the candid, interesting and beautiful places and moments. All the photographs are printed on metallic sheets that adds to the clarity of the pictures.

In the images of Canadian landscape the snow-laden mountains become a giant protagonist. 'Lake Peyto' captures the placidity of the water, the perfection of the natural cuts, lines and curves. Two photographs capture rare and beautiful sights of Niagara Falls, one with both falls of USA and Canada in the same frame, the second displays the rainbow lights on the falls at night. The Toronto skyline becomes the main player in some clicks but it's the captures of the colourful gay parade that steal the show. "Nobody in the country has so far exhibited the gay movement, I believe we should speak out in their favour so that they are brought from the fringes to the mainstream," maintains Saxena. The pictures of the curved escalator and the Nokia convention centre are a fine study in architecture and photography. The colourful Las Vegas, the 'awake-even-at-3am' life of San Francisco, and a candid Cheetah Girls hoarding form quite a contrast against the quiet Pebble Beach, "that's where Brad Pitt and George Clooney live!" chips in Saxena. Saxena's lens also beautifully captures the chiselled perfection of the Grand Canyon and the unique texture of the of the ocean.

Mauritius landscape is all about colours -- be it the clear waters of the turquoise sea or the 200 square metre piece of land that has seven shades! The subtle orange sky reflects its colours in the sea and the bright sunset into the heart of the sea is a delight for the sea lovers. A lone white lotus rests in the middle of a water body amidst dark pinks and light green. 'The Sentinel' is wonderful in its composition. The Dubai skyline takes centre stage with the world's only seven star hotel, the tallest building in the world and more. And as if by cue, the last exhibit drops a tear from snow!

On till October 4 at Punjab Kala Bhawan

Heading: Voltage fluctuations, powercuts are a routine affair in Kharar - Indian Express
Content:
After several senior leaders of the ruling Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) came out in support of SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, as the next chief minister, the main oppostition Congress too, pitched his name for the post.

In a statement issued today, Kharar Congress MLA Balbir Sidhu, asked Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, to step down as CM, to pave way for Sukhbir to take over the reigns of Punjab.

"In view of his growing old age, Badal senior should now take voluntary retirement from politics, because he doesn't even remember his announcements and statements made on the floor of the House," said Sidhu, while referring to the CM's recent statement, expressing ignorance over the revival of the long pending Dashmesh Canal project.

Sidhu said that in reply to his question over the Dashmesh Canal in the Punjab Assembly, the CM had submitted that Rs 500 crore was earmarked for completion of the Dashmesh Canal, which would cater to Mohali, Kharar, Zirakpur, Dera Bassi and Banur, which were facing an acute water shortage and would fulfill their irrigation and potable water needs.

"Even the SAD had made a promise to this effect in its manifesto of February 2007 Punjab Assembly elections," said the Congress MLA. He said that while issuing such 'irresponsible' statements, the CM was either playing 'dual' tactics or showing his 'inability' to continue on the post.

Sidhu also countered the tall claims of the SAD-BJP combine to develop Mohali as the 'future city' with world class infrastructure.

"Actually, the government has not yet released a single penny for Mohali. The present situation is that it is a picture of total neglect with potholed roads, power and water crisis, unsanitary conditions and bad condition of parks," he said, while demanding that the state government should provide adequate civic amenities to the residents of Mohali.

Heading: Hooda promises incentives on International Senior Citizen’s Day - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the summer season draws to a close, there is no respite for the residents of Kharar and its adjoining rural areas as they continue to reel under acute power crisis.

Unscheduled powercuts ranging between 4 and 8 hours everyday, voltage fluctuation and tripping have become a routine.

Besides frequent tripping and voltage fluctuation, the powersupply to the area remained suspended from 9.30 am to 1.30 pm on Wednesday. This was barely a day after the voltage plunged to such low levels that even tubelights and fans could not function.

"Due to voltage fluctuation, our electric appliances are being damaged, but the PSEB officials appear least bothered," said Anju, a housewife, while threatening to approach the Consumer Forum for seeking compensation for the loss.

Apart from the long unscheduled powercuts, the local PSEB office imposes scheduled cuts ranging between 6 and 8 hours in certain areas, on the pretext of

maintenance, at least once a week.

"We don't know what type of maintenance they do? Neither have we got respite from the voltage fluctuation nor from unscheduled cuts and tripping," said a shopkeeper Surinder Kumar, who is among the large number of local traders facing losses of their products stored in refrigerators and deep fridges during long powercuts.

PSEB officials, as usual, attribute the unscheduled powercuts to orders from the Power Controller in Patiala apart from blaming the increasing load on transformers for voltage fluctuations.

They, however, justify the scheduled powercuts for undertaking routine replacement of old wires and other machinery.

The Kharar residents, meanwhile, have urged the PSEB higher authorities to immediately improve the deteriorating power situation in the area failing which they warn to take to streets to express their anguish.

Heading: College students take part in NSS camp - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda, today, announced various incentives for senior citizens on the occasion of International Day of Senior Citizens in Sector 25. These included institution of state-level awards, identity card for every senior citizen, 50 per cent concession to women above 60 years on state roadways buses, setting up of senior citizens' clubs, distribution of spectacles and implementation of Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizen Act, to ensure their security.

Hooda said Haryana would enforce the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizen Act, passed by the UPA government last year, with an aim to protect the interests of the elderly.

The CM, who earlier laid the foundation stone of a building for Senior Citizens Club, said such clubs would be set up at five other places, including Jhajjar, Rohtak, Bhiwani, Sonepat and Hisar.

He also gave two state awards, each of Rs one lakh and a certificate, to two senior citizens, 112-year-old Chhano Devi of Mitathl village and Bhagwan Das Grover, a resident of Karnal.

Social Justice and Empowerment Minister Kartar Devi, Chief Secretary Dharam Vir, Principal Secretary M L Tayal, Secretary Town and Country Planning D S Dhesi, Deputy Commissioner Rajendra Kataria and Navraj Sandhu were also present on the occasion.

'Old age brings loss of income, friends and companions'

"Old age usually brings with it, a reduction in income, changes in family composition and equations, and loss of friends and companions.
The distress this brings is further aggravated by various age-related disabilities. Much of this can be avoided if one is forewarned and forearmed against this eventuality," said PH Vaishnav, President, Chandigarh Senior Citizens' Association, while addressing a function at the Bhargava Auditorium, on the occasion of International Senior Citizens' Day today.
Dr AR Kidwai, Haryana Governor, was the chief guest of the occasion. He released the souvenir of the Association and honoured 19 persons, who had worked for the ideals, for which, the Association stands. The function was followed by a programme by Dolly Guleria.
