Heading: Post-encounter, ‘everything has changed’ for residents of Batla House - Indian Express
Content:
The Two Most Historic Train Journeys of MAHATMA GANDHI
The evolution of Mahatma Gandhi, from his birth on October 2, 1869, till his martyrdom on January 30, 1948, and the growth of the Indian Railways from its birth on April 16, 1953, till India's Independence on August 15, 1947, run as fairly parallel histories. Mahatma Gandhi had travelled extensively in trains both during his long formative years while fighting racial discrimination faced by Indians in South Africa, and then across the length and breadth of India while leading India's freedom struggle against colonial rule for over three decades. Here's recapturing what I consider to be the two of the most historically train journeys associated with the Mahatma: from mohandas to mahatma

Soon after his arrival at Durban (South Africa) from Mumbai in 1893, barrister Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, then 23, had to go to Pretoria where a legal case for which he was engaged was being contested. In those days, trains ran from Durban to Charlestown, the onward journey being performed in stage coaches up to Johannesburg and from there to Pretoria by train. Young Mohandas suffered a series of racial indignities from Durban to Pretoria but, historically speaking, the most memorable incident was that of his being asked to step off the train at Maritzburg station (capital of Natal, 117 km from Durban). This was his maiden railway journey in South Africa on a dark winter night, and he was thrown out because a white passenger would not travel with a "coloured" person in the same first-class compartment. Mohandas protested that he had a first class ticket, but was still asked to move to the van compartment. On his refusal to do so, he and his baggage were thrown out and the train left. Gandhi remained at the station in extremely bitter cold the whole night. In his own words, "I began to think of my duty. Should I fight for my rights or go back to India, or should I go on to Pretoria without minding the insults, and return to after finishing the case? It would be cowardice to run back to India without fulfilling my obligation. The hardship to which I was objected was superficial — only a symptom of the deeper disease of colour prejudice. I should, if possible, try to root out the disease and suffer hardships in the process. Redress for wrongs I should seek only to the extent that would be necessary for the removal of the colour prejudice. So I decided to take the next available train to Pretoria." (Excerpted from An Autobiography: Part II Ch. IX). Thirteen years later, this philosophy of the young barrister gave birth to his unique philosophy of satyagraha in 1906 at Johannesburg. And, thus, began his long journey from 'Mohandas' to 'Mahatma'!

THE LAST JOURNEY
Mahatma Gandhi was martyred on January 30, 1948, and was cremated the next day at Rajghat. The whole world mourned. His ashes were carried in a special train from New Delhi to Allahabad on February 11, 1948 for immersion at the Sangam — the confluence of Ganga, Yamuna and Saraswati. Thus ended the long and deep association of Mahatma Gandhi with the railways, which had started sixty years earlier in January 1888, when Mohandas had first travelled by a train for a part of the journey from Rajkot to Bhavnagar (the rest was covered on a camel cart).

In the middle of a coach on a raised platform stood the urn containing the 'ashes'. Hymns and prayers were chanted throughout the journey. Dense and mournful crowds had collected from distant areas at stations all along the route to pay tearful homage to the Father of the Nation. At Rasulabad, a small station 60 miles from Allahabad, the train was halted for the night, and next morning it arrived at Allahabad as scheduled at nine. The crowd there was unmanageable. The urn was transferred from the train to a specially prepared truck, which moved to the Sangam, followed by a mammoth crowd.

Nearly three million people, including Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Patel, Maulana Azad and other leaders, and Gandhiji's sons Ramdas and Devdas, witnessed the immersion of the ashes .
- DR Y P ANAND, Former director, National Gandhi Museum; Former chairman, Railway Board.

DID YOU KNOW
Mahatma Gandhi travelled for the first time in a train in January 1888 when he travelled from Rajkot to Bhavnagar — to join Samaldas College. At Maritzburg railway station in South Africa, on the night of July 31, 1893, Mahatma Gandhi was thrown out of the first class compartment since he was a 'coloured' man. This incident strengthened Gandhiji's life-long commitment for struggle against racial discrimination. Years later, travelling with him in 1927, at the Lucknow station some Europeans objected to his son Devdas travelling with them in the "European & Anglo Indian" compartment dressed in a dhoti. All this while Gandhiji himself was travelling in the third class compartment. A heated argument ensued but finally Devdas had his way. The train left Lucknow station with Devdas and the ladies travelling together.

Earlier, travelling in 3 UP Mail from Burdwan to Kalyan, enroute Poona in 1915, Gandhiji could not enter the third class compartment because of the rush. As a result he had to get inside the inter-class compartment for which he was promptly fined. Writing in Young India in 1929 and concerned over the poor condition of toilets in Jodhpur State Railway, Gandhij asked the state railways to provide better sanitary conditions for passengers travelling in third class compartments. His relentless pursuit finally led to provision for better toilet facilities for these passengers. Mahatma Gandhi's last train journey was from Calcutta to Delhi on September 7, 1947.
- VIKAS SINGH, rail enthusiast

Heading: Lawyers, activist barred from meeting Delhi blast accused - Indian Express
Content:
Almost two weeks after the September 19 encounter, life for residents in the cramped Batla House lane in Khalilullah area refuses to slide back to normalcy.

Badar and Afzal Tasleem make special arrangements to pick up their children after school. The brothers live together in house number L 17. On the building's right-hand side is L 18, an address they no longer want to be associated with.

"Only families live on both sides of this lane. Most of the people here have school-going children. We all live here and want to have normal, stable lives. But after the encounter, everything has changed,"' Afzal Tasleem says.

Badar has four school-going children, while Afzal has one.

"Before this, our kids used to come home from school on their own. Now we go pick them up as we are scared for them. Even they are scared for their own lives; they are also scared of the cops. The firing happened on a Friday, and the entire episode has disturbed our Ramzan," he says.

Badar recalls the tenants living on the fourth floor of L 18 before Atif and his friends came to live there. "Most of the houses in this area are let out, but in our lane, families live together on rented accommodation. Before the students moved in on the fourth floor, an elderly lady lived there with a girl. All families living in the area are well settled. The fourth floor of L 18, however, did not have a metered electricity connection. A common meter was installed only recently for the entire building. Atif and his friends probably arranged for a steady electricity connection," he says.

They are saddened that the 'young boys' had to die without a trial but are also angry at the way their lives had to change suddenly.

"I don't understand why the police had to keep up barriers even a week after the encounter occurred. What are they trying to tell us? It's just a method of intimidation," Afzal says.

The police had put up barriers on both sides of the lane after the encounter. They were removed a week later when Congress leader Kapil Sibal visited the encounter spot. Even after that, police presence in the lane has been heavy.

Batla House residents to donate blood for blast victims
Following the Mehrauli blast, residents of Batla House have decided to hold a blood donation camp for the Delhi blast victims. "We will have a blood donation camp in front of the Khalilullah Masjid on October 3, a day after Eid. We want to express our solidarity with the people who have been affected by the bomb blasts in Delhi,"' said Asif Mohammed Khan, former MCD councillor.
—ENS

Heading: Police quick reaction teams formed to beef up security in Noida - Indian Express
Content:
Former Union law minister and advocate Shanti Bhushan and lawyers of Delhi blasts accused Zia-ur-Rehman were not allowed to meet the boy in the police's Special Cell on Wednesday. The lawyers will now approach the High Court for permission to meet him.

Accompanying the lawyers was activist Arundhati Roy, who claimed the policemen "scoffed and laughed at them". Rehman's sister Saira Bano was also part of the delegation. The lawyers said they were asked to get a court order. The Supreme Court has framed a guideline on the rights of the accused. The Delhi Police has been briefed on it, Shanti Bhushan said, adding that the police had violated the instructions of the apex court.

The Supreme Court has said a memo of arrest needs to be issued to immediate family for counter-signature, particulars of officers who arrest and interrogate should be recorded and when in custody the accused is entitled to have a friend or a relative with him. The apex court also said the accused should be medically examined every 48 hours when in custody and that his lawyers can be present when he is being interrogated.

"There was just an inspector present in the police station who did not identify himself and refused to allow us in," Bhushan said. The lawyers approached Home Minister Shivraj Patil on Wednesday evening and then gave the police a written application. "A duty officer, who did not identify himself, kept the application and refused to give an acknowledgement receipt for it," Bhushan said.

Heading: Power shortfall of 300 MW, Delhi overdraws despite ‘warning’ - Indian Express
Content:
After the meeting between senior UP government officials and industry representatives last week, the Gautam Buddha Nagar police have formed two quick reaction teams (QRTs) in the district. The teams will take care of security-related issues of industrial enterprises.

The teams are being constituted by the district police to tackle any untoward situation. The Superintendent of Police R K Chaturvedi said that besides QRTs, an industrial relations unit has also been constituted and has started functioning to redress security concerns of industrial units. "The teams will begin preparing a data bank of email ids, telephone and mobile numbers of managers and senior officials of national and multinational firms. This will ease the task of contacting managers," Chaturvedi said.

In Ghaziabad, similar measures have already been adopted to handle the security situation. "We already have three QRTs and are equipped to take care of industrial security issues here," said L Ravi Kumar, SSP, Ghaziabad.

Meanwhile, Graziano Transmissioni India Pvt Ltd has changed the private firm that was earlier providing security to its plant. "We have employed Group 4 Security Services to handle our plant's security at Greater Noida," said the company's personnel manager, L K Gupta. He also informed that in the absence of a CEO, the company is at present working just one shift of eight hours. Earlier, it used to operate 24 hours, Gupta said.

Heading: For Delhi women, city roads at night spell terror - Indian Express
Content:
A day after Delhi was issued a warning by the Northern Regional Load Dispatch Centre (NRLDC) to "maintain grid discipline", the Capital was overdrawing from the Northern Grid yet again. With power demand peaking at over 3300 MW, Delhi was struggling with a shortfall of almost 300 MW and had to resort to overdrawing at various points in the day.

In a stern message, NRLDC officials had warned Delhi of a strict penalty if the city kept flouting grid discipline. The officials asked Delhi to resort to load-shedding, if need be, instead of constantly overdrawing.

"There was a constant shortfall of almost 150 to 200 MW today as well and load-shedding had to be resorted to in a few areas," said S R Sethi, Delhi Transco's Director (Operations). A bulk of the shedding was carried out in areas like C R Park, Greater Kailash Part II, Vasant Kunj and a few areas in Central Delhi.

"Discoms have to be prepared in advance to meet the demand everyday. Last month, Power Minister Walia had told discoms to have their Power Purchase Agreements in place in order to ensure minimum load-shedding during the festive season, but clearly that is not happening," a senior Power department official said. Discoms, however, argue they have to resort to load-shedding not due to shortage, but more often due to "frequency issues". With Delhi's power generation usually falling between a dismal 950 to 1050 MW, the Capital is left with no option but overdraw from the Northern Grid.

Heading: Police relent, Ramlila deadline now midnight - Indian Express
Content:
The murder of Soumya Vishwanathan in the early hours of Tuesday morning has once again raised security concerns, not only for other women journalists who travel back home at late hours, but also other women professionals who need to work round the clock.

Newsline spoke to a few professionals after Tuesday's incident and found that many women think they have no option but to feel a constant sense of insecurity in living in a city like Delhi, which is unsafe at all hours. And the city only gets worse, with empty and desolate stretches on roads that they invariably need to take to reach home.

Nupur (name changed), a singer with a famous five-star hotel in Delhi, usually drives back home after midnight. "I've been driving in Delhi for the past 22 years. What happened to Soumya is unfortunate and could have happened to any of us, but the incident won't deter me from driving back home at late nights. My working hours are such that I have no option," she says.

Driving her Maruti Alto every night, the 40-year-old travels from Connaught Place to Gurgaon, taking the route from Dhaula Kuan to NH-8 and then home. "Delhi is scary, but I try to drive at normal speed, don't wear revealing clothes, and make sure that the windows are rolled up at all times," she says. Nupur says there have been incidents in the past when she was chased by groups of inebriated boys, "but in such situations I only ignore them, drive faster and slow down in a populated area".

Naina Agarwal, a 26-year-old creative writer with an advertising agency in Jungpura, has always been scared of driving in Delhi at late hours. "Whether day or night, I make sure all doors are locked properly and the windows rolled up. I even try to avoid red lights at night, as they are places where people notice that a girl is driving alone. When I have to stop, I just try to remain unnoticed," says Agarwal, who drives her Honda City car to Dwarka from work.

While she prefers to avoid driving after 11 pm and takes the office cab instead, if work goes on beyond 11 pm, Agarwal usually takes the Ring Road till Dhaula Kuan to reach NH-8, then takes the Rao Tula Ram flyover and the Dwarka Underpass to reach home.

For Vandana Mehra, an employee with PepsiCo, worrying starts right after 10.30 pm. "From Kalkaji I go to Gurgaon every day, and usually get late at night. Apart from the fact that I keep my Maruti Wagon R car's doors and windows properly shut, I make sure to call my husband every 30 minutes to tell him about my whereabouts," says Mehra. She also has all her close relatives' numbers on her cell phone's speed dial list. "I cannot trust the cops," she says.

"With incidents like this one, which make us more insecure, it is important to promote the culture of 'working from home' for women who need to work late," the 30-year-old suggests.

Heading: Court slams MCD for issuing notice to remove kiosk of disabled man - Indian Express
Content:
After initially setting difficult deadlines for Ramlila and Durga Puja committees in the wake of the recent blasts in the Capital, the Delhi Police has given in to the demand of the Ramlila committee for extending the closing time.

Ramlila celebrations might now be extended till midnight, instead of the earlier deadline of 10 pm set by the police.

The Mahasangh Ramlila Committee has received permission from the Delhi Police for the extended the Ramlila timing.

The police have directed all Ramlila committees to follow a set of safety guidelines for addressing potential security threats. The committee was, however, adamant on it demand. Ramlila Mahasangh Committee Chairman Ram Kishen Gupta said, "We have followed all the guidelines set by Delhi Police, which is why we requested for an extension of the time limit."

Rajan Bhagat, spokesperson of the Delhi Police, said, "Delhi Police have issued 98 rules and directives to the organisers with specific instructions that they are to be strictly followed." Ramlila committee members say they have arranged for security on their own as well. "During Ramlila this time, we will be using door frame metal detectors and hand-held metal detectors at all entry points. Thirty CCTVs that are also to be installed at the entry and exit points," Gupta added.

Delhi Police has also directed all Ramlila committees to extend the height of the boundary wall to seven feet and carry out the verification of all volunteers involved in the security arrangements with the Delhi Police.

Heading: Tuning In - Indian Express
Content:
For fifty-one-year-old Balbir Singh, rendered disabled in an accident and earning his living through a PCO booth in PVR Naraina premises since 2004, the kiosk allotted to him by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) under the quota for the handicapped was his only means for making ends meet, being the sole earning member of his family.

All of it changed when a showcause notice arrived from the civic body directing him to shift his kiosk to another spot near a drain, with electric poles and trees surrounding the site. Since Singh had never flouted any norms or shifted from the original site allotted to him, the reason as cited by MCD—that Singh had shifted his kiosk from the originally allotted site to another place, thus violating norms — was beyond his comprehension.

The MCD further averred that it had received complaints from a number of people, including the area councillor, which said that Singh's kiosk was obstructing the flow of traffic.

Hassled, Singh moved the court door seeking reprieve against the sudden change of stance by the civic body. He placed all records, including a No Objection certificate from the traffic department, before the court and said that his kiosk had never posed a traffic problem.

The MCD, however, stood firm on its contention that Singh had changed the location of his kiosk and that there were numerous complaints from the market association and the councillor.

When asked for written records of the complaint, the civic body cut a sorry figure, saying they had only received "oral" complaints.

Similarly, when the court inquired about the original site plan, which was allegedly flouted by Singh, they failed to produce any record of it either, while the DCP (Traffic) confirmed through his report that the kiosk was still at the allotted site.

Infuriated, Additional District Judge (ADJ) Kamini Lau slammed the MCD for asking Singh to move from the site without any reasonable ground whatsoever. "Under no circumstances will this court allow any instrumentality of the state or any institution to misuse or abuse its authority to the prejudice of a common man, particularly a severely disabled person who is unable to stand up against this kind of institutional pressure initiated under the influence of a powerful lobby of shopkeepers and the area councillor," said ADJ Lau. Noting that the act was "highly improper", the court also criticised the Deputy Commissioner of Karol Bagh zone for proceeding with the notice and asking Singh to shift under apparent pressure from area councillor Malti Verma while the matter was still pending before it.

ADJ Lau termed the action as a violation of the principles of natural justice and said such victims have to be protected from this kind of harassment by the courts.

Staying the operation of the notice, the judge has now restrained the MCD from dispossessing Singh of his kiosk or passing any order against him, till the matter is decided by the court.

Heading: Real Realm - Indian Express
Content:
After almost three decades, singer Asha Bhosle and filmmaker Dev Anand will be working together again

It was the year 1980 when Asha Bhosle sang Jab chhaye mera jadoo in Dev Anand's Lootmaar. Now, after a gap of 28 years, the singing diva is getting set to collaborate once again with the evergreen hero himself, Dev Anand, for his forthcoming film, Charge Sheet. "It's a nice feeling to work with Dev saab once again," says Bhosle. A murder mystery, the film will have Anand play a retired CBI officer along with Jackie Shroff as a corrupt policeman. Like all of Anand's recent films, the rest of the cast is replete with newcomers. "Dev saab is an extremely interesting personality because when he talks you feel he's no more than a 20-something," says Bhosle, of the 85-year-old Anand.

Bhosle recently celebrated her 75th birthday with the launch of an album Precious Platinum. The nine-track album has been composed by Nitin Shankar who leads Bhosle's current band. "The album is a compilation that is not entirely different from what I have been singing but I think it should appeal to my fans," says Bhosle.

But ask her if she feels any different about life's platinum milestone and she promptly clarifies that age for her holds absolutely no meaning. "I feel no different. It's not about age, it is about being young at heart and I like to look at life that way," she says.

Bhosle, who turned composer just once in the past with the record Aap ki Asha, says it's unlikely that she'll ever be composing music on a regular basis. "I have five restaurants functioning across countries including Dubai and Kuwait serving Indian cuisine apart from the usual shows and travel that take up most of my time," she says. On current composers, her favourites include Shankar Mahadevan and Pritam. "They're good, though I feel the essence of older music directors occasionally creeps into their melodies," says Bhosle, a tad mischievously. Well, didn't somebody say there's no original idea left in this world?

Heading: Haute and Cool - Indian Express
Content:
From bomb blasts to urban development and child soldiers, 14 artists reflect on varied issues through their work

Are there issues which are popular but unreal, or popularity which is materialistic?" When curator Ranjita Chaney approached artists with this loaded question over a year ago, she hoped to get them thinking about their surroundings and wider concerns that otherwise don't find representation on canvas. "I wanted them to reflect on popular reality. The term is a cliché but I knew the interpretation would vary," notes Chaney. The conviction stood true and the discussions have found varied hues in the artwork that is on display currently at The Stainless Gallery in an exhibition titled "Popular Reality".

Comprising work by 14 artists — Apurba Nandi, Dileep Sharma, Gaurvi Sharma, Josh PS, Murali Cheeroth, Manil Gupta, Nandan Ghiya, Pradeep L Mishra, Sharmi Chowdhury, Tushar Joag, Vibha Galhotra, Vivek Vilasini, Viveek Sharma and Gigi Scaria — this dwells on issues ranging from urban development to the recent spate of bomb blasts across the country.

If Gigi Scaria depicts the cost of urban development in his work titled The Billboard, Tushar Joag reflects on the modernization of Mumbai through the pen and ink work on paper titled Crawford Market. Nandan Ghiya, on the other hand, compels onlookers to consider the consequences of turning children into soldiers on the war field through the acrylic on canvas titled Mission Abortion that has an armed foetus juxtaposed with a pregnant woman. "The practise is prevalent in different parts of world from Afghanistan to South America and Africa. The unborn children are urging their mothers to opt for abortion rather than subject them to such a cruel fate," says Ghiya.

Delhi-based Manil Gupta takes a more philosophical route as he paints illusions in shades of black and white on his canvases titled Do you see the Grand Illusion and Inevitably Real. "The first portrays how everything is an illusion and nothing is real. Most of the beliefs are part of what has been passed on. In the second canvas, I have tried to showcase how in life moments of chaos and happiness coexist," says Gupta.

As Delhiites give their verdict on reality, as perceived by the artists, the exhibition will soon invite reactions from across the globe when it travels to Dubai and Mumbai later this year.

The exhibition is on at The Stainless Gallery till Oct 7. Contact: 9971164477

Heading: Chopin Board - Indian Express
Content:
If you are gearing up for a new winter wardrobe, don't forget to invest in experimental wool sweaters, the kinds showcased at the Australian Wool Innovation's fall winter collection 2009 held at InterContinental The Grand earlier this week.

In a small fashion show, models Indrani Dasgupta, Sonalika Sahay and Amanpreet Wahi walked the ramp in formal and casual wear that ranged from oversized coats in hairy yarn and bright fluorescent colours to tartan pencil skirts.

The men's collection was just as hip — front-tapered jeans and slim silhouettes, designed to show off

a toned body to flattering effect.

Gothic boots, bright tights and faux fur leg wear completed the boho chic look.

The unconventional colour palette moved between camel and cognac, rich Barolo reds and midnight blues to brilliant plum.

"The look was created with the Indian winters in mind," said Pascal Senkoff, regional manager of the Australian Wool Association, Asia. Now, only if the mercury would dip.

—Suanshu Khurana

Heading: Marathi Sahitya Sammelan likely to be held in city - Indian Express
Content:
Seenu Singh is one of the few Indian names among the up-and-coming classical pianists. Now Belgium-based Singh is ready to hold his first major concert in Delhi this week — and, as in most of his performances, this one will feature his favourite classical composer, Frédéric Chopin.

"I was two when my father brought home a tape of the polonaises of Chopin. Without even knowing what it was, I found myself fascinated," says the 23-year-old, who left India as a child. As a six-year-old, he began to tinkle out nursery rhymes on the piano, and, after a while, smaller compositions of Chopin. Soon, the government of Flanders began to promote his Chopin Recital in institutions across the country.

"Chopin's music is a union of elegant, expressive melodies and experimental, rich harmonies, all combined with brilliant piano technique," says Singh. A frequent visitor to India, he performed the Chopin Recital in Mumbai earlier this year and then followed it up with another in Pune.

His recital in Delhi will be at India International Centre on Oct 3. Contact: 24619431

Heading: Butt ban choked in confusion - Indian Express
Content:
The 82 nd Akhil Bharatiya Marathi Sahitya Sammelan – All India Marathi Literary Meet - is likely to take place in Pune. Maharashtra Sahitya Parishad, representative body of Pune is ready with the proposal and expected to pass it over to Akhil Bharatiya Marathi Sahitya Mahamandal (ABMSM), the apex body, soon.

"We are ready with the proposal and will pass it over to ABMSM very soon," said a member of Maharashtra Sahitya Parishad on condition of anonymity. "It is expected that the budget of the Sammelan will go up to around Rs 2.5 crore. We have also shown readiness to raise the money," said the member.

If Pune gets to host the Sammelan, it will be the fourth one in Pune district. Previously, two Sammelans under the chairmanship of P B Bhave and Rajendra Banhatti were held in the city and one was held at Alandi under the chairmanship of Shanta Shelke.

After the row over organising the Marathi Literary Meet in the US (San Jose), the ABMSM took a backward step and declared that the Meet in the US will be termed as the World Marathi Literary Meet and not the official Sammelan of the ABMSM.

The ABMSM, which is the appointed body for holding official Marathi Sahitya Sammelan every year, had shown readiness to hold the official Sammelan at Ratnagiri. But Nagar Vachanalay of Ratnagiri declined the invitation and declared that the Sammelan in Ratnagiri – Sharada Sahitya Sammelan - will not in anyway be connected to the ABMSM.

The ABMSM then had options of Thane and Parbhani. But both the cities have shown disinterest in organising the Sammelan. "Thane and Parbhani have conveyed their decision that they would not be able to organise the Sammelan owing to unavoidable circumstances," said Kawtikrao Thale- Patil, president, ABMSM.

Thale- Patil declined to make any comment on the proposal of Pune. "I have received two phone calls from two cities interested in organising the Sammelan. I am sure they will be sending their proposals in writing. But I cannot reveal the names," he said. However, he did admit that there is a talk over Pune sending a proposal. "The final decision will be taken in a meeting of the ABMSM to be held in November.

Meanwhile, even though the name of the other city interested in organising the Sammelan is not yet disclosed, a member of Maharashtra Sahitya Parishad said the other city is near to Pune. "But Pune is front runner in the race," he added.

Heading: Can’t spare hands, too many other things to do, says police chief - Indian Express
Content:
It's come into effect. Everyone wants it, welcomes it. Implement it? Each agency points at the other

Starting Thursday, smokers will have to go out on the streets for a forbidden puff. Or so the law says. Introducing a ban is one thing; implementing it is another. The stumbling block is the confusion over who will enforce the ban.

The Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) is quick to point out that the "basic, nodal enforcing agency" is the Food and Drug Administration. The FDA, in turn, cites lack of clarity in the rules and says the police have a key role to play.

The police, for their part, say they have too much on their hands to spare time or men for ban enforcement. (See adjoining story)

The ruling does list some of the agencies it wants to ensure that smoking is banned. Among these are the police and NGOs.

Municipal authorities appear satisfied if no one smokes at civic hospitals. "Our hospitals already have no-smoking zones... The FDA is the basic nodal agency to implement the ban," PMC chief medical officer Dr P S Dhaigude says.

FDA joint commissioner Prahlad Apshingekar says, "The government is not very clear on the number of monitoring authorities. Police too have an important role. We will start imposing fines once we get a copy of the notification."

Campaigners for the ban welcomed it, though not all were sure that it would work. The city unit of the Indian Medical Association (IMA) said not enough places have been made smoking-free. "The notification should have included more places. I don't feel it will have much of an impact," says Dr Avinash Bhondwe, president of the unit.

Dr Kalyan Gangwal, crusading for a tobacco ban, cites history: "The government banned gutkha, too, but it is still available. The smoking ban is welcome but it should be followed up with strict implementation."

The notification bans smoking in any building, private or public. There can no longer be designated smoking rooms at companies, including those in the IT sector. The ban will be in force also in small cafes, restaurants, pubs and discotheques. At hotels with accommodation for 30 or more, there must be a separate enclosure for smokers and special ventilation arrangements.

PASSING THE BUCK
Pune Municipal
Corporation: Passes on the buck to Food and Drug Administration, says it is the nodal agency for enforcing the ban

Food and Drug
Administration: Says government not clear on number of monitoring authorities, says police have key role

Pune Police: Say they can issue notifications but they have neither the manpower nor the time to take up the job full-time, with Games round the corner

Heading: Line-up of commandos selected for Games - Indian Express
Content:
The police left no doubt that they are not taking implementation of the smoking ban too seriously.

Police Commissioner Dr Satyapal Singh said he cannot delegate any men exclusively for cracking down on people smoking at public spaces. He said the police had too much on their hands already: checking crime, tackling a terror threat and handling Commonwealth Youth Games security.

"I can only appeal to people, but cannot devote my staff for this. With the Commonwealth Youth Games in a week, my staff are busy," Singh said on Wednesday.

A senior official from the ministry of health services said the police cannot shirk their responsibility. "It is a notification that has to be enforced and it is the police who have to take the action. The notification gives them the power to fine any public smoker," he said.

Heading: Demand up, supply thin: brace for loadshedding - Indian Express
Content:
BIG EVENT, SPECIAL UNIT: Young and active, they will tackle terror and crime

The Pune police have formed a special commando squad, comprising 50 "young and active cops" for keeping a vigil on crime-prone areas of the city during the upcoming Commonwealth Youth Games. The squad was flagged off by Police Commissioner Satyapal Singh on Wednesday.

"They will be deployed in sensitive areas under the jurisdiction of police chowki and will respond to any sudden attack. They will be extensively used for ensuring security in the city during the Youth Games," Singh said.

The commandos have been equipped with motorcycles, carbines, sticks and walkie-talkies. Additional Commissioner of Police (crime) Rajender Singh said that the commandos are with crime control, but would be working in teams for all four police zones in the city. Around 50 motorcycles and other equipment for the commando squad were purchased from funds allotted for Youth Games preparations, he said.

"The number of commandos differ from zone to zone, depending on the number of police chowki in its jurisdiction. We have identified roads where chain-snatching, robbery and other crimes are frequent. The commandos would be patrolling these roads. We expect that the presence of the commandos will reduce the response time if any crime takes place," Deputy Commissioner (crime) Anil Kumbhare told reporters.

"All the commandos are young and have a strong physique. They will keep a close watch around the Commonwealth Youth Games venues. In case of a terror threat or attack, the commandoes will be specially used for tackling riots and controlling mob in sensitive areas," Kumbhare said.

Eid today, security up
Pune police have increased security in the city for Eid on Thursday. "About 25,000 people would be visiting the Eidgah at Golibar maidan on Thursday. We appeal to people to avoid bringing mobile phones, carry bags or water bottles while coming to pray," said Joint Commissioner of Police Rajendra Sonawane. The Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad has conducted checks at various spots. Several CCTV cameras were installed around Golibar maidan. Two inspectors, 11 sub-inspectors and110 constables have been deployed.

Heading: Expose your sweet tooth to puneshop.com - Indian Express
Content:
More loadshedding may be in store for the people of Pune, with the revised zero loadshedding model yet to take off. With the demand for power in the city at around 308 MW, franchisee Tata Power Company has not managed to meet the entire requirement and the supply is varying day by day.

S P Nagtilak, chief engineer (Pune division) of the Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL), told The Indian Express that zero loadshedding could not be implemented from October 1 as planned owing to limited power supply from the state grid and other sources. According to Pradeep Bhargava, state chairman of the Confederation of Indian Industry, MSEDCL had made it clear that additional power would not be required from July to September.

The miscalculation meant that for the power purchase agreement supposed to be effective from October 1, 150 MW of power supply was felt to be enough for zero loadshedding. Meanwhile, the demand has gone up to 308 MW in Pune. While the franchisee TPC has been able to procure power on a daily basis, the supply is inconsistent, sometimes as low as 88 MW.

Power is also drawn from the state grid but is still short of demand, resulting in power cuts ranging from one to three hours. Shantanu Dixit, coordinator of Prayas Energy Group, explained that as per the new load-shedding protocol, the MSEDCL has implemented loadshedding of five hours and 45 minutes, up from the previous three hours. The Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC) has asked the power utility to supply data on the present loadshedding protocol within ten days.

Heading: Civic activists question rationale behind PMPML fare hike - Indian Express
Content:
Shop online from Chitale Bandhu Mithale, whose wares have delighted for decades

For decades, its sweets, namkeens and dairy products have dominated the plates of Maharashtra's households; now you can buy those online.

Chitale Bandhu Mithaiwale already has two major shops in the city, with a network of agents and distributors across the state, and a monopoly on items such as bakarwadi.

Starting this Diwali, puneshop.com will make its reach even wider. If you live in Pune or Pimpri-Chinchwad, just log on to the website and the entire range of Diwali sweets will be at your disposal. Payment will be accepted online and the order will be delivered at your doorstep in two to four days.

The number of items for sale online will go up to 50 by November 15. As of now, the Diwali range includes 12 items.

"The demand is high... we decided to initiate this facility with the festival season in mind," says Srikrishna Chitale, one of the owners.

Amarake Services has created the online service. Its owner, Rajashree Saraswate, explained why: "They are one of the topmost brands and their outlets see unending queues."

A special feature on sale will be a corporate gift box that will have the four main traditional faral items: chakli, chivda, ladoo and shankarpali. "The box will also have discount coupons for travel and various brands, as well as our vouchers that can be redeemed during the next online order," says Chitale.

"Our other special Diwali items include rawa laddoo, motichur laddoo, besan laddoo, shev, chakli, kadboli, karanji, anarase and bakarwadi."

The gift box is priced at Rs 111; buyers need to order it in multiples of 10. It will be delivered between October 18 and 27. Two percent of the sales proceeds of the gift box will go to Lokmanya Public Charitable Trust, Dapoli, for a solar lighting project.

Heading: In Khadki, over 1,200 BSNL phones go dead - Indian Express
Content:
In the wake of the hike in bus fare charges by Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML), the PMP Pravasi Manch has sought to know the rationale behind the fare hike and has filed a complaint with the State Information Commissioner Vijay Kuvalekar (Pune division) against the Regional Transport Authority (RTA).

The PMP Pravasi Manch, along with a host of other organisations, has urged the PMPML administration that instead of increasing the fare and make things difficult for commuters, the PMPML administration should focus on enhancing the overall management.

Activist Vivek Velankar and Jugal Rathi pointed out that by raising autorickshaw charges, inaddition to the existing bus fleet and better management of bus routes, the PMPML administration has registered about 20 per cent profit in the last few months. "This proves that despite any fare hike, it was able to garner some profit. Hence there was hardly any need to further increase the fare charges, " Velankar said.

"We have sought to know the rationale behind this fare-hike. We have demanded this from Dr Nitin Kareer, the chairman of the Regional Transport Authority (RTA). However, the RTA is evading divulging any information regarding this. Therefore we approached the information commissioner and filed a complaint in this regard," Rathi said.

Meanwhile, Pune Bus Pravasi Sangh,Janwani, Parisar, Pune Zilla Molkarin Sanghatana, Sarthi, Sajag Nagrik Manch, Surajya Sangharsha Samiti, have threatened to carry out a protest rally against the fare hike on Saturday at 3 pm at the Deccan Gymkhana Bus Stop.

Heading: After war of words, Pawar, Kalmadi to share dais - Indian Express
Content:
Over 1,200 Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) connections in Khadki exchange area have been disrupted in the last two days following cable thefts.

This time, a BSNL security guard was also thrashed by gang of 10 to 12 men on late Monday night on the Bombay-Pune highway near Wakdewadi as they damaged and went with one of the four cable wires that the company has lost in the past two days.

To guard BSNL cables from being stolen, the company has posted a crew of ex-army officers at various places in the city. But they have not been able to deter thefts. "The last such incident happened a few months ago, when a BSNL security guard was manhandled in Yerwada as some miscreants stole cable wires. This happened many times in the past as well. We have filed police complaint each time, but no action has been taken yet. In the coming week, we will meet the police commissioner to brief him about the situation again," said V K Mahendra, principal general manager, BSNL.

There are about 30 ex-army officers who BSNL has recruited as security guards at various parts of the city, but they do not carry heavy arms. "In some secluded parts of the city, when it comes to muscle power, our guards have been overpowered by these gangs," he said.

In this case, the four 400-pair cable wires and one 200-pair cable wire were damaged and stolen in the last two days. Three days ago, a 1,200 cable pair was stolen on Fergusson College Road as well.

"In the past week, the severity of cable thefts has increased. For the people stealing these cables, its a windfall as they can sell copper at Rs 350 per kg. Even if they sell at the black market, they will get Rs 150-200 per kg," said Hemant Borale, deputy general manager, West.

The connections which have been disrupted are on Bombay-Pune Road, Fergusson College Road, Ganeshkhind road, Bhandarkar Road, Kohinoor estate, part of Elphinston road, Bopodi, Sawantnagari, near Harris Bridge at Dapodi.

Heading: Senior Citizens are treasures of society: Anna Hazare - Indian Express
Content:
All eyes would be on Thursday's function organised to felicitate Congress leader Ulhas Pawar where NCP chief Sharad Pawar and city MP Suresh Kalmadi will be sharing the dais for the first time after the city units of Congress and NCP engaged in a war of words over the opposition by the ruling alliance in the standing committee to allot funds for promotion of the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG). Incidentally, the state NCP is holding talks with the Congress for an alliance at elections for a few local civic bodies.

Both the leaders will come together at a function organised by Pune Navratra Mahotsav to felicitate Congress leader Ulhas Pawar at Ganesh Kala Krida Manch. Congress corporator Ulhas Bagul has been organising the Mahotsav every year.

The ruling NCP, along with Shiv Sena and BJP, had last week rejected the civic administration proposal to sanction Rs five crore for promotion of the CYG with the Congress, alleging that the move was politically motivated since Kalmadi is the chairman of the organisng committee of the Games. The NCP chief too had supported the stand of local unit of NCP saying that public money should not be used for publicity of the games.

On the previous occasion when both the leaders shared the dais for a function of Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC), Kalmadi had appealed to the NCP supremo to bring the two parties together in the city as they are at the state and national levels. However, Pawar had ruled out the idea saying he won't get into local affairs of the party.

The local units of NCP and Congress have been at loggerheads in the city with the NCP ruling in the PMC with support from Shiv Sena and BJP while the Congress is in opposition.

Heading: Commonwealth Youth Games: UoP exams rescheduled - Indian Express
Content:
"Senior citizens are treasures of Society and they should be respected as Matru Devo Bhava; Pitru Devo Bhava, Acharya Devo Bhava. This is the soul of Indian culture and should be practised by the younger generation," said social crusader Anna Hazare on Wednesday.

"Any elderly abuse should be brought to the notice of concerned authorities," he said, speaking on the occasion of International Senior Citizen's Day.

Hazare emphasised the need for Right to Information Act being utilised for the benefit and Welfare of Senior Citizens.

Those present on the occasion included senior stage and film artiste Ashalata and Dr Ramachandra Dekhane, a well-known scholar of a folk and saint literature.

The special programme for senior citizens was organised by Athahsri Foundation which was attended by senior citizens of the city and surrounding areas to packed capacity at the Yahswantrao Chavan Auditorium. The programme was inaugurated by Shashank Paranjape, managing director, Paranjape Schemes.

On the occasion, Dekhane performed his special show 'Bahurupi Bharud' which received tremendous applause from the audience. Actress Ashalata was interviewed by Dr Sangeeta Bapat. Ashalata recalled her theatrical and film career. Senior citizens attending the function were delighted by the performance.

At the concluding ceremony, 20 volunteers and a few senior citizens were felicitated by Hazare and the renowned Gandhian was given a standing ovation by the senior citizens for his excellent service to the society.

The directors of Athashri Foundation Dr Sharachhandra Gokhale, S R Rairikar and Dr Vishvas Mehendele were present on the occasion. Neela Deshpande compered the programme.

Heading: GANDHI:the reel life - Indian Express
Content:
Naturally the first thought that comes to one's mind when hearing the word Japonism is that it has something to do with Japan. One would not be entirely wrong in that assumption, except that the word originated in France. It was first used in 1872 by author Jules Claretie, to describe the influence that Japan had on the Impressionist and Post Impressionist painters like Edward Manet, James Tissot, Toulouse-Lautrec and Vincent Van Gogh.

Some may argue that it was larger reflections of the increased trade of Japanese goods like vases, screens and kimonos, among the European gentry. The masters of the Edo period often known as Ukiyo-e artists began to be known in Paris as collectors, writers and critics sailed off to Japan in the 1870s. They brought back with them, prints and curios that created a taste and influence.

However it was more than a mere reflection as some artists, like Van Gogh went on to embrace some of the stylistic features of Japanese art its calligraphy and colours. It was however a short-lived experiment for the painter and it never really pervaded or became a permanent fixture in his art.

Later however artists like Gustav Klimt incorporated Japonism as a painterly vocabulary in his art while Georges Bigot, even moved to Japan to study and imbibe the culture there. The fascination for Japanese culture can also be seen reflected in theatre in productions like Madame Butterfly.

It showed up in textiles jewellery and graphic design. Much later filmmaker Francois Truffaut made humorous comments on the fascination with Japan in Paris in his film Bed and Board where its protagonist Antoine (Jean-Pierre Léaud) has an affair with a 'Japanese beauty'.

Demystify art, e-mail georgina.maddox@expressindia.com

Heading: No Eid celebration this year for Malegaon blast victims’ family - Indian Express
Content:
Over five decades, Mahatma Gandhi's life is a story all filmmakers have wanted to tell

Few men's life stories have been experimented with as much as Gandhi's. The attempt to discover and highlight a whole new aspect of the life of the man who changed the destiny of a nation has been an irresistible lure for filmmakers down the years. With more than a dozen interpretations on the leader's life and times that included his ideologies, struggles, strengths and even weaknesses, having been put before the public to date, we ask a cross section of cinemagoers as to which film they feel did justice to the man and made the most impact on their hearts and minds.

Siddharth Kavadia, student
According to me the best-portrayed image of Gandhi was by the British actor Ben Kingsley, in Richard Attenborough's 1982 film Gandhi, which also won the Academy Award for Best Actor and the Golden Globe Award for New Star of the Year. The film not only spoke about Gandhiji's personal or political life during the independence movement but also depicted the growth of Gandhi as a political leader and national hero who became an inspiration for all the generations.

Ketan Bafna, businessman
Lately, I have seen Anil Kapoor's Gandhi, My Father; I really liked the film as it shows a side of Gandhi that me may not have known to many of us. Gandhi is known as father of the nation, but the film shows another aspect portraying the troubled relationship between Harilal Gandhi, enacted by Akshaye Khanna, and his father, Mahatma Gandhi, reprised by Darshan Jariwala. But I also liked Richard Attenborough's Gandhi and Kamal Hassan's Hey Ram where Naseeruddin Shah played Gandhi.

Adinath Khedkar, student
I am a big follower of Gandhiji, and in literature he has been my best subject for study. Although many films based on Gandhi and his values are very good, I feel the theme of Lage Raho Munnabhai was a different experiment to reach out to maximum audience specially the youngsters. It popularised gandhism values and showed the audiences how Gandhigiri works amid corrupt system. It also showed the relevance of Satyagraha and with a comic theme it also became commercially successful. Many times movies made on such topics become a documentary type and failed to attract common man's interest. After the film there were many real life incidences, heard of, where Gandhigiri was used as a tool to fight corrupt practices.

Snigdha N, executive
I think Richard Attenborough's Gandhi was the best depiction of Bapuji. Although, in today's era of commercial cinema, many films play around the theme of periodic films, and perhaps, some movies to an extent, reflect the interpretation of the subject; this was not made keeping in mind the box-office collections.

Sangharsh Kesar, manager
My choice is Swades; the film depicts Gandhi's values in true sense relating it to the current day situation. The film portrays a person, who despite all the big opportunities he has got, thinks about community development and giving back to the society. In the last two decades the trend has been that people study in India and then go to western countries to earn more and everyone is bothered about personal development in terms of money, fame and other luxuries of life.

Prakash Petve, chartered accountant
I really liked the Marathi play Mee Nathuram Godse Boltoy . It features the circumstances of Gandhi's assassination very well . Gandhi himself was a great author; his writings have always inspired and interested me. Talking about films, I think Shyam Benegal's Making of the Mahatma was an excellent piece of work. Besides, I also like Lage Raho Munna Bhai; it is a lesson for all of us.

Malvika Thete, student
Although Swades was not a film that featured Gandhiji's personality, I feel it was a true depiction of his teachings that are needed in today's era.

Scripting Mahatma
2007: In Anil Kapoor's Gandhi, My Father, Darshan Jariwala portrayed Gandhiji in an estranged relationship with his son Harilal.

2006: Dilip Prabhavalkar, in Lage Raho Munna Bhai played Gandhi. The new term Gandhigiri emerged.

2005: Mohan Jhangiani depicted Gandhi, in a cameo, in the film Water

2005: The film Mangal Pandey —The Rising, ends with footage on Gandhi.

2005: Maine Gandhi Ko Nahin Mara is a story of an Alzheimer's patient who begins to believe that he was accused of being the man who assassinated Mahatma Gandhi.

2004: Swades the film featuring Shahrukh Khan, "epitomizes Gandhi's values" according to Mahatma Gandhi's great-grandson, Tushar Gandhi.

2001: Surendra Rajan plays Gandhi in the film Veer Savarkar.

2000: Mohan Gokhale, in the film Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar portrays Gandhi

2000: Hey Ram, a film made by Kamal Hassan portrays a would-be assassin of Gandhi and the dilemma faced by the would-be assassins in the turmoil of post-partition India. Naseeruddin Shah portrays Gandhi in the film.

1998: In a biopic of the founder of Pakistan Mohammed Ali Jinnah, Sam Dastor portrays Gandhi in Jinnah

1996: Rajit Kapur portrays Gandhi in The Making of the Mahatma, a Shyam Benegal film about Gandhi's life in South Africa.

1993 Annu Kapoor portrays Gandhi in the Ketan Mehta's Sardar.

1982 Ben Kingsley depicts Gandhi in the award-winning film, Gandhi, directed by Richard Attenborough. The film won eight Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Actor.

1963 Gandhi is portrayed by JS Casshyap in Nine Hours to Rama based upon the 1962 book by Stanley Wolpert.

1980: The opera Satyagraha, composed by Philip Glass, with a libretto by himself and Constance De Jong is based on Gandhi's experiences in South Africa.

Mee Nathuram Godse Boltoy is a Marathi play that explores the rationale and circumstances in which Gandhi's murder was plotted and carried out.

Heading: Powerpuff girls - Indian Express
Content:
When 61-year-old Mohammad Hanif Sheikh Chand went to his uncle's pan shop at Bhiku shop in Malegaon , after a sumptuous Ramzan dinner on Monday, little did he know that he would land up in the hospital just minutes later.

Hanif and his nephewShiekh Tarikh Sheikh Azis (22) were severely injured in the blast that occurred on Monday night barely few metres away from the pan shop.

Soon after the blast, Hanif was rushed to Noor hospital in Malegaon, where doctors advised Hanif's relatives to rush him to Mumbai for advanced care as they sensed serious complications. "We rushed him in a private car to the hospital at eight in the morning, his condition is very serious," said Jabir Sheikh (29), Hanif's son. Hanif was rushed to King Edward Memorial hospital in Mumbai. Hanif sustained severe brain injuries and burns on his feet.

"Barely a kilometre away there is a big ladies' garment market at Anjuman Chowk. Since there were barricades near the cloth market, the attackers probably parked the bike a little away. It was the time when people returned home after namaz and the chowk usually is crowded with people," said Jabir.

The sudden transition of visuals from a fully lit chowk with people all around and a festive atmosphere to a grave surrounding with blood bottles has left Hanif tensed and baffled. "He has not seen anyone parking the bike, all he recollects is the sound after the blast," said Jabir.

"The patient was brought to KEM hospital in the morning on Tuesday, he requires surgery as he has a depressed fracture of left frontoparietal bone. Also his feet are burnt," said the on-duty administrative medical officer at KEM hospital.

Living a retired life after working, as a driver, Hanif was not unnerved even after the 2006 Malegaon blasts.

With just a day left for Eid, Sheikh's family members are left with no choice but to juggle duties to look after Hanif and his cousin nephew at hospitals in Mumbai and Malegaon instead of preparing for the festival.

Heading: A common thread - Indian Express
Content:
A rare public marriage of two art forms

For centuries music and painting have inspired each other. Hector Berlioz's dramatic symphony Romeo et Juliette inspired Marc Chagall's famous painting on the ceiling of the Opera Garnier in Paris and Don Maclean's hit song Vincent, with its famous opening lines, "starry starry nights", was inspired by the life of tortured artist Vincent van Gogh and his most famous work Starry Night. Still, it is rare to see the two art forms inspire each other in a live performance. But yesterday that was exactly what audiences witnessed at the Nehru Centre, Worli, as musicians Niladri Kumar, V. Selvaganesh and Jayateerth Mevundi performed even as painters Prithvi Soni and Ravi Mandlik created art simultaneously.

The concert, called Reflections, was organised to celebrate International Music Day on October 1 and was an effort on two levels. Organiser Shashi Vyas informs, "The word 'reflection' can mean two things—one is mirror image and the other is introspection. We're trying to create an environment where music and painting will reflect each other in a more physical sense. We're encouraging the audience to ponder deeply on this relationship."

Mandlik believes that painting has a deep connect with music and this concert will turn it into a performance art. "I usually listen to music while I'm painting. But then, I'm always alone in my studio," he says. "This was a different experience as I painted in public. The audience could see how the two art forms inspire each other, as the music and the paintings were spontaneous," the painter adds. Sitarist Kumar too stresses that spontaneity is key to the concert. "In fact, 95 per cent of all music performances are spontaneous. You can have a basic structure that you follow, but you can't fix every aspect of your performance. That will definitely come across in the concert."

The event was also meant to give the audience greater insight into the world of art. Vyas says, "All artists are inspired by their predecessors. For instance, Niladri's work is inspired by Pandit Ravi Shankar. So while the older audience might have got a nostalgic enjoyment out of listening to some familiar strains, the younger generation was exposed to something new."

Heading: Auxiliary claims Melbourne Trophy in a record time - Indian Express
Content:
On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, we take you khadi shopping around the city

Khadi Gramodyog Bhavan, Fort
One of the most prominent addresses on Dr D N Road in Fort, the Khadi Gramodyog Bhavan, is a perennial favourite for all. There are 14 Khadi Bhandars in Mumbai but this one is the best. Inaugurated by Morarji Desai in 1954, this place is where you can find endless yards of khadi; in various colours and varieties. Choose from saris, kurtas, dhotis, bed linen and much more. The first floor is also a good place to buy souvenirs. A fabulous common ground for the partriotic and the fashionable, Khadi Bhandar truly rocks.

Bombay Electric, Colaba
After the wave of Gandhigiri swept the nation, it is no surprise that multi-designer store Bombay Electric too is turning towards handspun, hand woven khadi. By Hand, a special week-long khadi exhibition that opens today will present a host of NGOs and artisans who have specialised in the art of weaving and natural dying. Hand-dyed shibori scarves, handwoven stoles in natural dyes, kishmish collection of handwoven khadi, natural indigo dyed daywear, block prints and Naga handwoven material are what you can choose from here.

SATTVA, Khar (W)
This store, run by Saakshi Bhandari, meets the demands of fashionistas and suits the budget (clothes are priced Rs 2,000 onwards). A lot of young designers retail here. This season watch out for a whole lot of designs in handspun khadi. Beautiful new colours—pinks, beiges, ochres, greens—ones that one generally doesn't associate with khadi are stocked. The well-styled clothes are ideal for evenings as well as daywear. The silhouettes are primarily western and include bunched up tunics, puffed sleeves, pin-tucks, flowy dresses and much more.

Kora Kendra, Borivali
Khadi has come a long way from being termed as the dress of a politician or a journalist. Walk into Khadi Centre and you will witness a host of college kids, office-goers and even boutique owners hoarding this ancient fabric. Over the years, the khadi centre has undergone multiple changes to match with the changing times. It offers a variety of khadi cloth pieces, saris and kurtas in different colours and textures. The store also stacks different perfumes including sandalwood, rose, neem and lavender, packed in lovely wrappers.

Shudh Khadi Bhandar, Dadar
Located right opposite the Dadar railway station, this store is one of the oldest symbols of our freedom movement. One glimpse and you will feel like it's a mini version of Fort's Khadi Bhandar. It is more a retail joint and it's USP is the organic khadi and silk-khadi materials. Here, you can choose from a variety of textures which are picked up by the young and hip to create designs to go with the times. Next time you are in Dadar, make sure you head to this place.
