Heading: Narrow escape for Pandit XI - Indian Express
Content:
ONGC lived up to their favourites tag as they trounced Mumbai Customs 4-1 in a Group B encounter in the MFL Elite Division League at the RCF ground in Chembur on Wednesday. Meanwhile, another seeded team Central Railway struggled to hold Mumbai United to 1-1 draw earlier in the day.

Mumbai Customs, who had thrashed Union Bank of India last weekend, did not combine well today and allowed the ONGC forwards to dictate terms right from kickoff. Malsawmdawngliana aka Dawng, Tarif Ahmed, Lalmuan Puia and Dhanesh MC complemented each other well in front, creating a lot of problems for the Customs defence. Dawng struck in the 14th minute, while Puia drove a ball from the top of the box into the left bracket in the 30th minute.

Immediately after the lemon-break, Tarif Ahmed deftly relayed a ball from the left flank over the head of an advancing Customs goalkeeper, Bunty Dhiman for Dwang to run in and nod into goal. The Customs team regrouped after that and with the advent of Stalin on the right flank created a few chances. It was from one such move that Nitin Shetty scored, pushing the ball past a diving Bilifinag Nazary. Keniston, who went in as a substitute for ONGC in the dying minutes of the game, with the light fading fast, ran in from the left flank and got his name on the score-card in the 87th minute.

The Central Railway -Mumbai United match was made interesting by the sending-off of the railway goalkeeper Kunal Sawant in the 60th minute of the game. He ran out to fist a ball, overstepped the 18-yard-box and to everyone's horror brought down a Mumbai United striker who was goal bound. Mumbai United had struck first through Anthony Agbaraji in the 52nd minute and Sumesh T then drew parity for Central Railway two minutes later.

Though the railmen were reduced to ten men -goalkeeper Raghu Khanolkar being pressed into service -they withstood the pressure exerted by the United forward line manfully and would have been happy to grab a point from the encounter.

The Budweiser 'man-of-the-match'award winners for the two matches were Raghu Khanolkar from Central Railway and Malsawmdawngliana for ONGC.

Heading: Indian ruggers hope to outdo the Lankans - Indian Express
Content:
Chandrakant Pandit XI stuttered their way to a two-wicket victory in their second round encounter over Hemant Waingankar XI in the Shalini Bhalekar Memorial Cricket (MCA under-22 trials) Tournament at the Ramesh Dadkar Maidan on Wednesday. Pandit XI were poised 21 runs away from victory with three wickets in hand at stumps yesterday, and they managed to reach their target of 99, with the additional loss of a wicket today.

Ravishankar Singh was adjudged the man-of-the-match for his second consecutive nine-wicket haul. He has easily proved to be the bowler of the tournament so far, and will be pleased about finishing up on the winning side this time around, after winning the award in Pandit XI's loss to Lalchand Rajput XI in the first round. Bhavesh Patel remained unbeaten on 15 in the end, as Dhawal Parab's 4 for 37 went in vain for Waingankar XI, who will be extremely disappointed with their batting collapses in both innings.

Rajput XI and Pandit XI are now joint leaders with six points each, while Dilip Vengsarkar XI and Waingankar XI trail them with five points to their tally.

Brief Scores

Waingankar XI 84 & 119 lost to Pandit XI 105 & 99 for 8 (Raheman Sufiyan 28, Bhavesh Patel not out 15; Dhaval Parab 4-37, Sachin Wagh 2-21).

Heading: Transcending barriers: Alarmel Valli on the language of dance - Indian Express
Content:
Not quite a Mendis-mesh of this-spin or that-spin proportions, but Sri Lanka's rugby team has been a spider's web, undeciphered by the Indian ruggers for as long as they can remember. Undeterred by their persistent negative margins of scores against their island-neighbours, the Indian 7s squad, led by Nasser Hussain sets off to Hong Kong for the Rugby World Cup 7's Asian qualifiers to be held this week where they are grouped alongside the hosts and Sri Lanka, with King Bruce's determination.

"There've been many close games with Sri Lanka, but they are way faster than us. Physically we're almost the same, the playing mentality too, but somehow we've not managed to beat them," Hussain says, of a sub-plot within the tournament - a challenge that would be best overcome. Ranked 11 in Asia in the Sevens - the shorter, pacier format of rugby - India might not make the final grade for the final event in Dubai next year with just two qualifying, but a few upset wins at the 12-nation event would be a good start to India's 2010 Commonwealth Games preparations, which will begin in right competitive earnest now.

For a national team - still rugby newbies - and starved of international fixtures, the Hong Kong event is an opportunity to flex their recently-toned muscles. The team - a skeletal framework of what will be flehsed out for 2010 - is distinctly new-look with Delhi debutant winger Vishal Vashisht lending his express-pace to the team, while Mumbai boy - forward Rohaan Sethna who has taken big strides when transforming from junior-to-senior, also getting a look-in for this shorter version.

Comprising 3 from Mumbai, as many from Delhi and 6 from Army - the national champions, the squad, coach Usaia Biumaiwai believes has it in them to put it across the Lankans - a modest, realistic target for the mild punchers from Asia. Playing on artificial turf will be a novel experience for most of them, which will need getting used to. "The idea will be to keep possession against the Lankans," Hussain says, adding the team would need to stay composed if they have to put it across the Lankans on Day 1.

Through performance in this meet, the Indians are also hoping to gain a few invitations to 7s tournaments - Nairobi and Dubai, in order to accumulate playing hours internationally, ahead of the 2010 spectacle. "We don't get to prove ourselves otherwise, very few opportunities," Hussain says, with the Bombay Gymkhana calendar this year not featuring an international. But micro-managing their challenge, the Indians - who ran Thailand close earlier this year - will hope they get past the Lankan barrier.

Heading: Police beef up security ahead of Eid - Indian Express
Content:
For me, to dance is a means of communication between soul and soul, to express what is too deep, too fine for words," says dancer Alarmel Valli, quoting another legendary dancer Ruth St. Denis. One of the most well-known exponents of Bharatanatyam in the country, Valli will be performing at the NCPA, Mumbai on Thursday to mark the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti. Her piece, titled The Forgotten Seed is an attempt to remember a fractured unity ¿ between the sensual and the sacred, the natural and the divine, the prosaic and the poetic. "It is a tribute to Mahatma Gandhi's commitment to a heritage of harmony," she explains.

Valli worked on the concept and script of The Forgotten Seed with poet Arundhati Subramaniam. "I have always had the greatest admiration for Arundhathi Subramaniam, as a poet and writer," says Valli, adding, " But I also respect her as a rasika of rare sensitivity and clarity of vision, whose intuitive knowledge and understanding of the finer nuances and aesthetics of classical dance make her an ideal person for me to work with."

The Forgotten Seed draws from an eclectic range of sources, including the Rig Veda, the Kamba Ramayana as well as the akam and puram tradition of Sangam poetry. Valli believes that this ability to fuse with other art forms ¿ modern or classical, Indian or foreign ¿ is intrinsic to Indian classical dance. She says, "To be a true liberal is to be able to appreciate, or at least accept the entire gamut of artistic expression, whether modern or traditional. In this context, any work of fusion that brings together classical dance with other art forms, like modern music, installation art, foreign dance forms, or film, has validity — provided it also brings true talent, creativity integrity and passion to the production."

Valli believes that classical dances are languages where every step is an alphabet and every movement a word. She explains, "In all the years that I have performed, in diverse forums in India and abroad, whether in colleges or museums, villages or temples, to audiences spanning a vast spectrum of cultures, tastes and experiences, I have never ceased to marvel at the unfailing power of our classical dance to transcend cultural and linguistic barriers and to touch people at the most intense level."

Valli who is the founder of Dipashikha, a centre for fine arts is also a guru to several students on Bharatnatyam. So does she find teaching a natural part of dancing? says, "When dancers teach, there is always the danger that the student, often unconsciously, along with the vocabulary and grammar of dance, also absorbs the teacher's mannerisms and personal style, becoming in the process, a clone or shadow of the guru." However she does enjoy her role as a guru. "I would consider myself fortunate if I could help my students understand some of the complex layers and myriad dimensions of Bharatanatyam and to help them to see it as a rich, dynamic and continuously evolving dance form."

Heading: Cine workers on strike, TV shooting schedules worst hit - Indian Express
Content:
Following the recent blasts in Malegaon and riots in Rabodi at Thane, the Mumbai Police have tightened security to ensure smooth Eid celebrations of in the city on Thursday.

According to the police, more areas have been covered under patrolling and volunteers from various communities have been roped in to maintain peace and security at areas where Eid celebrations will be held. Sensitive areas like Bhendi Bazaar, Nagpada, Crawford Market, Pydhonie, Bandra, Jogeshwari and Mahim will be given special attention as large groups of people are expected to gather there to celebrate Eid.

Moreover, various entry and exit points of the city will be closely monitored by the police. In order to keep a close vigil, the police will also be keeping an eye on various lodges and hotels in the city.

"Bomb disposal squads and teams of sniffer dogs will also be deployed at various parts of the city to avert any untoward incident. Also, we had meetings with heads of Mohalla committees in order to sensitize them about the issue and to encourage them to be alert and to cooperate with the police in times of crisis," said a senior police official.

When contacted, Joint Commissioner of Police (Law and Order), KL Prasad said, "There will be an increase in the number of volunteers this year. A force of 40,000 police personnel will be deployed at various spots throughout the city to ensure smooth Eid celebrations. Apart from the police, around 20 companies of various para-military forces like BSF, SRPF will also be called in to maintain law and order situation."

Heading: State asked to reconsider furlough plea of murder convict - Indian Express
Content:
Shooting schedules of television shows and films were affected when nearly two lakh cine workers went on an indefinite strike called by the Federation of Western India Cinema Employee (FWICE). The workers are protesting against inadequate and delayed payment of wages and lack of regulated working hours.

Dharmesh Tiwari, general secretary of Cine and TV Artistes Association and president of FWICE, said, "We don't call this a strike... It is a non-cooperation movement. The workers are present on the sets but are not working. This will continue until our demands are met."

The FWICE comprises nearly two lakh members of the 22 unions, including actors, writers, music composers, directors, spot boys, lightmen and cameramen. Tiwari said producers often do not honour the MoU signed between them and FWICE on wage contract of the workers.

"In the MoU it's clearly specified that there will be a yearly increment but it doesn't happen. Also, we have been requesting the producer bodies to pay the workers directly and not entertain any middlemen but that also doesn't happen," added Tiwari.

It's difficult to gauge the impact of the strike on the film industry since no major shoots except Shah Rukh Khan starrers Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi and Billoo Barber are planned in Mumbai for the next few days. The strike is not effective for crews working abroad.

For the television industry, the Bollywood workers' strike has indeed thrown the shooting schedules off track. Notorious for its hectic schedules that are often equated with slavery, the production houses are twiddling their thumbs as they await the association's next move.

Rajan Shahi of Director's Kut Productions said, "There was a rumour doing rounds two days ago but we received no prior intimidation. The shooting is stalled indefinitely and we have already suffered losses up to Rs 7 lakh."

In a press statement, Sangram Shirke, president, Western India Film Producers' Association (WIFPA), claims that the notice for the strike was not served as per the Trade Union Act.

The biggest grouse of the television producers in the whole affair is that they fail to understand the reasons for the blanket ban.

Abhimanyu Singh, MD, Contiloe, says that not every production house can be accused of delayed payments, hence the strike is uncalled for. "These are specific issues and can be taken up with individual production houses. Moreover, during an economic slowdown, there is only as much one can pay for a job. To excel in it and to move up the organisational ladder is up to an individual," said the producer.

Shahi, on the other hand, claims that no demands were brought to his table, therefore, the strike, to him, seems unfair.

The TV production houses are waiting for a resolution though most feel that such extreme actions only breed animosity between the parties without yielding much result. The industry, however, seems to be open to negotiations.

Balaji Telefilms, the largest content provider for television today with over eight shows on air currently, is touted to have been affected the most. Its GM (Operations) Ketan Gupta, when contacted, was unavailable for comment as he was at the association office for negotiations.

The preliminary talks with all four producer bodies — The Indian Motion Picture Producers' Association, Producers Guild of India, Association of Motion Pictures Producers and WIFPA — have failed. In fact, WIFPA has even termed the cine workers agitation as "fake."

The TV production houses are waiting for a resolution though most of them feel that such extreme actions only breed animosity between the two parties without yielding much result. The industry however, seems to be open to negotiations.

Heading: Now, dine at a railway station on Central Railway - Indian Express
Content:
High Court said that the competent authority has not applied its mind while considering plea

Directing the state government to reconsider the furlough application moved by a murder convict, the Bombay High Court observed that the life threats given to the family of the victim by the convict at the time of the offence do not form a basis to deny him the right to be released on furlough.

A division bench of Justices A P Bhangale and K J Rohee directed the state government to reconsider the furlough application of Shammu Damu Yuwane, who is presently lodged at the Amravati Central prison, observing that the competent authority has not applied its mind while considering the plea.

Yuwane, a resident of Nagpur, was convicted by a sessions court on January 29, 2006. He had applied for furlough leave on December 19, 2007 which was rejected by the competent authority in its order dated May 2, 2008. The plea was rejected citing a few reasons including the possibility of public peace and tranquility being endangered if petitioner is released. Also, the order stated that the surety given by the petitioner was not competent.

Yuwane challenged the decision in the High Court stating that the grounds on which his plea was rejected were not proper. Accordingly, the court ruled that the police report states the convict had threatened family members of the victim at the time of the offence. "We fail to understand as to how from the alleged threat one can jump to the conclusion that the public peace and tranquility would be endangered in the convict is released on furlough," the bench observed.

The court further observed that no reasoning was given by the police in regards to the surety it mentioned was not competent. Accordingly, the High Court quashed the order rejecting the furlough leave application of Yuwane on September 24, and directed the officials to reconsider it.

Heading: MTHL  receives good response, 20 companies show interest - Indian Express
Content:
More food plazas planned, railways to monitor hygiene

The Indian Railway Catering and Tourist Corporation (IRCTC) added another feather to its cap with the launch of 'Re-Fresh', its first food outlet on the Central railway (CR) line. A leading restaurateur has been given the licence to operate the outlet.

The outlet will function like a restaurant and will offer various types of cuisines, including Jain food items. It would render services round the clock. The services will include 'take-away' facility. One of these food outlets would be opened at Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus station.

The move is expected to go down well with the travellers, especially those who often need to catch trains at odd hours.

Sowmya Raghavan, General Manager of the CR who inaugurated the food outlet said, "This was eagerly awaited as 3 lakh passengers use the CST station everyday. The hygiene would be monitored by the railway." This is the third outlet by the IRCTC on suburban rail platforms, the other two being at the Mumbai Central and Churchgate station. Rajeev Sharma, Group General Manager, IRCTC said, "The fourth is in pipeline and is to come up at the CST station but it would cater to the suburban railway commuters." He added, "We have requested for space to CR and Western Railway (WR) at the suburban stations on both these lines."

 JN Lal, Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) of the CR said, "There would be more such outlets on the suburban railway."

The IRCTC wants space at the Bandra, Andheri and Borivali railway stations on the WR and at Thane and Kalyan railway stations on the CR line to start similar food outlets.

Heading: On Gandhi Jayanti, students will pledge to work for peace - Indian Express
Content:
The state government's ambitious Mumbai Trans Harbour Link (MTHL) project, which was embroiled in several issues, has received encouraging response with over 20 Indian and international construction companies expressing interest to design and construct the sea link. In the past the project faced problems including 'unrealistic' bids that resulted in the cancellation of the last tender and the state government opting to wholly fund the project's construction.

The Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC), which will implement the sea link project, had invited Expression of Interest (EoI) on September 9 from contractors to design and construct the sea link on a turnkey basis. "We've received great response from companies across the world expressing interest in designing and constructing the sea link, including international firms," said Samir Biswas, Joint Managing Director of MSRDC.

According to SB Nage, Chief Engineer, MSRDC, 22 companies responded to the EoI. "The who's who of Indian construction firms have responded, while around 10 international companies have their expressed their interest," Nage said. He said that companies like Lloyd's construction, Gammon India Ltd, Larsen & Toubro Ltd, among others have shown interest to construct the 22.5 km sea link. The project involves construction of an approach road on Sewri side, bridge across inter-tidal zone on both sides, deep sea zone, via duct and embankments.

The tendering process, for this much delayed project has begun with the MSRDC giving out the tender notice on Wednesday. It is expected that the bids would be in by the third week of November, while the letter of acceptance after due evaluation of the bids is tentatively scheduled to be handed over by fourth week of January.

The eight-lane sea link, which is estimated to cost around Rs 6,000 crore, is proposed to commence from Messant Road on eastern side of Sewri railway station on Harbour Line and traversing through the creek waters will meet the main land near Shivaji Nagar and terminate on National Highway 4B at Chirle in Navi Mumbai.

The proposed sea link offers to cut the distance between the two locations by 15 km and reduce travel time from more than two hours to about 30 minutes. According to sources in the MSRDC, like the Bandra-Worli Sea Link that is being constructed on contract basis, the proposed MTHL could also be a cable-stayed bridge.

Heading: Senior RBI official jumps to death from office building - Indian Express
Content:
This year on International Non-Violence Day (October 2) one thousand students in the city will take a pledge to work towards peace and non-violence. The Bombay Sarvodaya Mandal, along with Mumbai University's Mahatma Gandhi Peace Centre and the Sadbhavna Sangha will be organising the ceremony.

The students participating in the march will be from the National Service Scheme (NSS) and will come from around 70 colleges across the city. The oath will be administered by the Vice Chancellor of Mumbai University, A D Sawant. Students will march from Churchgate and Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus to the Convocation Hall at the University campus in Fort. The students will carry placards and banners, with slogans like 'No More Violence, Peace is our Mission' and 'Be the Change you want to see in the World.'

"We want to promote the values of non-violence, tolerance, and respect for all human rights. We hope to inculcate a sense of non-violence in the students through lectures, and peace songs," says TRK Somaiya, a programme co-ordinator from the Gandhi Sarvodaya Mandal, adding that 3000 other NSS students appeared for the Gandhi peace exam, which was conducted across different districts in the state.

"It would be nice to reach out to people and train people in non-violence and also to teach them how to deal with differences, first in their homes, then in their workplaces and in their communities," says Manisha Sen, co-ordinator at the Mahatma Gandhi Peace Centre, which functions out of the University of Mumbai campus, and is in the process of charting out courses for the same.

The Gandhi Sarvodaya Mandal has also sold more than 50,000 books for their community service project this year. In the period between the second and 10th October, there will be seven lakh students in India participating in various initiatives held by the Gandhi Sarvodaya Mandal in association with other organisations.

Heading: Sangh says Rabodi riots ‘pre-planned’ - Indian Express
Content:
A Deputy General Manager with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) committed suicide by jumping from the eighth floor of the RBI building at Bandra-Kurla Complex on Wednesday afternoon. According to the police, 51-year-old Sushant Kumar Patnaik left behind a suicide note stating that nobody was responsible for his death.

Patnaik jumped from the fire exit on the eighth floor of his office building at around 1.30 pm. He was immediately rushed to the Sion Hospital where he was declared dead on arrival.

"We found a letter in his pocket with the words 'No one is responsible'. It had his signature and the date," said Police Sub-Inspector Shabbir Qazi of the Bandra-Kurla Complex police station. "Many people were present in the office, but since he was a senior officer, Patnaik had a cabin to himself and no one suspected that he was about to take his life," he added.

According to the police, the fire exit is usually deserted and hence the possibility of someone seeing Patnaik and stopping him was low.

The police questioned his colleagues, but they were unable to pinpoint any reason that could have led Patnaik to end his life. Even his 22-year-old son, whose statement was recorded at the hospital, could not throw any light on the provocation for the suicide.

Patnaik had been transferred from the RBI headquarters in Fort to the Bandra-Kurla Complex office in August. However. after having reported to work for a day, he had gone on leave and resumed duty three days back.

"While it is too premature to ask the bereaved family whether he was undergoing any stress which may have prompted the extreme step, we have learnt that he had undergone a leg operation. He had been involved in some accident in September and had to be operated upon. But we are yet to ascertain whether that has any link to the suicide," said Senior Police Inspector Rolphi Pereira of the Bandra-Kurla Complex police station.

Patnaik was residing at the RBI quarters at A K Vaidya Road in Goregaon (East) and is survived by wife and two children.

Heading: In Thane’s most sensitive areas, there are too few policemen - Indian Express
Content:
In the face of allegations that the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) and Bajrang Dal had instigated the riots in Thane, the Sangh Parivar outfits went on the defensive on Wednesday and alleged that "fundamentalist Muslims" and outfits like the banned Student Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) were responsible for the "pre-planned" flare-up.

VHP leader Venkatesh Abdeo also blamed extremists for a similar communal clash at Murud in Raigad and sought to corner the state government over the high number of casualties among police personnel in the Thane violence. "It is condemnable but also laughable. The state government's security mechanism has collapsed. How can a government which is unable to protect its policemen protect the people?" said Abdeo. He added that the attacks on the police showed the strength of the attackers and claimed that the riots were "pre-planned."

Abdeo also blamed politicians like Mumbai Congress president Kripashanker Singh and NCP Thane unit chief Jitendra Awhad for trying to pander to minority votes.

"Someone else has instigated the riot, but the Bajrang Dal is blamed for it. This is an attempt to defame it. People know who has indulged in rioting," said Abdeo, pointing to newspaper reports blaming the Sangh Parivar outfits for the communal disturbance. Abdeo and VHP Thane chief Dr Sunil Ranade said that the Bajrang Dal cadre had in fact helped the police quell the disturbance.

Ranade alleged that the riot had not been sparked off over the issue of an arch of a Navratri pandal being set up close to a masjid, as was being alleged, and claimed that the riots were pre-planned. He also alleged that "SIMI and fundamentalist Muslims" had used the issue of the arch as a "pretext" to spark off the disturbance, and pointed to statements made by outgoing Thane joint commissioner of police Madhu Shinde about sleeper cells being active in the area.

Heading: Four arrested on murder charges - Indian Express
Content:
While officials admit Rabodi needs many more policemen than it now has, Mumbra and Bhiwandi stations don't even have their sanctioned strength

As the mood outside turned increasingly hostile on Monday night, the phone inside Rabodi police station in Thane remained silent. The police station has only one phone, and it was out of order. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone I) Sahebrao Patil confirmed it had been out of order, but said the service had been restored on Wednesday. When this reporter tried calling, the number was still out of service.

Even all 54 lower-ranking policemen ranging from police constable to assistant sub inspector and five officers attached to the Rabodi police station were clearly an insufficient force. "The area is hyper-sensitive," said Madhu Shinde, who retired as joint commissioner of police on Tuesday. "We need many more men in Rabodi police station than the current strength."

The chowky had, in fact, been converted into a full-fledged police station in March 2008 owing to the population around it — over 80,000 — and also to deal with the communally sensitive nature of the area, cosmopolitan upper middle class housing complexes alongside a mostly slum settlement dominated by Muslims. Curiously, the sanctioned strength for Rabodi police station is only 19. "The figure is of the time when the Rabodi was just a police chowky," said Additional Commissioner of Police (West Region) Vivek Phansalkar.

The story is repeated across Thane district's sensitive areas where police stations face an acute shortage of manpower.

In Mumbra, one of the largest ghettos formed after a large-scale exodus from Mumbai following the 1992-1993 riots, The police station has 52 men less than the sanctioned strength of 170 (see box), despite the continuing problem of illegal constructions and attacks on government officials.

After the Mumbai Crime Branch recovered RDX from Mumbra following the 1993 serial blasts, combing operations have been frequent, the last being only a week ago following the arrested of one alleged member of the Indian Mujahideen from here.

The powerloom town of Bhiwandi, on the radar of Intelligence agencies and with a history of communal violence, has a sanctioned strength of 721 men. Its current strength is 625. Only in July 2006, two people died while protesting the construction of a police station next to a mosque, followed by the lynching of two policemen. And last week, the Mumbai Crime Branch arrested one alleged IM member from here too.

There is worse: Two police stations within the zone, Nizampura and Bhiwandi, are annually flooded in the monsoon.

The tale differs slightly at Mira Road, where the existing strength exceeds the sanctioned strength. However, local police officials have long pointed to the need for a second police station in the area. "The proposal of setting up Navghar police station is pending with the Home Department for two years. The new police station will take care of the Naya Nagar area," said Additional Superintendent of Police (Thane rural) Deepak Sakore.

Heading: For city kids, Bapu is nature’s father too - Indian Express
Content:
The police have arrested four persons for allegedly killing a man on February 5, this year.

SP (D) Gurpreet Singh Toor said on February 5, the police had found the body of one Rishipal from canal side in Dugri.

On investigation, it came to light that Mukesh Kumar, deceased's brother-in-law and three more persons were involved in the murder.

The police have arrested Devinder, Neeraj, Sunny and Mukesh on murder charges. The fifth accused Deepak Batra is lodged in the jail. "Deepak was on parole at that time and is undergoing sentence of five years in connection with some other case," said Toor.

Throwing light on the reason for muder, the SP said, "Two relatives of Rishipal did not like the way he had illicit relations with a few women. Unhappy over this, they involved three of their friends and murdered him," he added.

Heading: ‘It’s just another day in the twilight of our lives’ - Indian Express
Content:
As the nation observes a national holiday on account of the birth anniversary of the 'Father of the Nation' Mahatma Gandhi, the Newsline team does a recce of the city schools to find out if young minds know about the real Mahatma Gandhi or country's second prime minister Lal Bahadur Shastri — who also shares his birth anniversary with Gandhi.

Manan Arora, a Class III student, said, "Mahatma Gandhi was an old man. He used to wear spectacles and was the 'father of nature'. Lal Bahadur Shastri was the first president of India."

Unable to recollect Gandhi's ideals, Puneet Verma, a Class II student said, "He was a great man and is known as father of world." When asked as what he did for India, the little boy said, "Tomorrow, the nation will celebrate his birthday and our school has declared a holiday." He had no clue who Lal Bahadur Shastri was. Innocently, he said, "I don't know, madam did not tell me about him."

Sniggy, another primary school student, after recalling some of the stories he has heard about Gandhi, said, "He was a freedom fighter. He used to tell people not to fight. After he uttered the word 'Hey Ram', he died. Lal Bahadur Shastri was a very good human being. He used to deliver long speeches in the public."

Saksham Kohli, a Class V student, said, "Gandhiji's full name is Mohandass Karamchand Gandhi. He was a freedom fighter and was a great leader." But he too was unaware of Lal Bahadur Shastri.

Aviral Kumar, a Class VIII student, could only tell, "Gandhiji taught us non-violence. Lal Bahadur Shastri was the prime minister of India who died at Tashkent due to cardiac arrest."

Heading: Parents plotting against our marriage, alleges NRI girl - Indian Express
Content:
Ask me about anything else but my children. They are dead for me as I am dead for them. If they cannot look after me when I need them the most, how can I call them my children"? This is how 78-year-old Kaushlaya reacts when asked about how she landed up as an inmate in Swami Vivekanand Vridh Ashram at Model Town, some 12 years ago.

For hundreds of such elderly persons like her, the International Day for the Elderly on Wednesday, was just like any other day today. While some of them have now lost any hope of being together with the family which have disowned them for various reasons, others keep waiting for the seldom telephone calls from a couple of relatives.

As for the 65 inmates of the old-age home, they also went about their daily routine in the same old manner - bed tea at 5.30 am, breakfast at 8 am, lunch at 1 pm, afternoon tea at 4 pm, satsang at 5 pm, dinner at 8 pm and milk at 8.30 pm.

"This is how I have been spending my days for the last 12 years. At the most, I sit at this verandah along with my new found 'father' I found here," Kaushalya pats on the back of 91-year-old Harbans Lal, who shifted to the ashram some 10 years ago.

Harbans had one of his two sons looking after him, but after his death at the age of 45, he had no other choice but to come to live as an inmate here since his second son declined to look after him. "However, my daughters are sweet, they still want me to come to them, but I asked them to leave me here," he tells.

As for Kaushlaya, she has three sons and two daughters. Two of her sons are living in the city only but she says that she has never been visited by any of them all this while. "Only one daughter visits me, but that too seldom," utters Kaushalya and starts sobbing.

The day was designated by the United Nations General Assembly in 1990 to pay respect, show care and honour towards the elderly in the society. And as per an estimate, the number of elderly has been increasing considerably over the years. According to UN, one in every 10 persons is today above the age of 60 which will go up to five in ten persons by 2050.

"This country only salutes the rising sun, nobody likes to worship the setting sun here," yesteryears' actor Gurudarshan Singh Josan, who was once known as Darshan, sums up his life in the old age home with a metaphoric explanation. He has been living at the Red Cross Senior Citizens' Home at Sarabha Nagar for over seven years now. "There is no respect for the elderly in this country," he fumes.

"We are paying to live here and the cost is Rs 1,800 per month. Though we do not mind that, still somebody should ask, is this how you should treat the elderly?" asks another inmate at the Senior Citizens' Home. "We are a culture which is known to give respect to elders. But alas, all that is history now. They should remember they will also get old one day," he says.

Heading: Scholars wait in desperation as Sutton House grabs the booty - Indian Express
Content:
New York-based Kuldeep Singh married Lovejeet Singh Virk on September 29

A New York-based girl who defied her parents and married a man of her choice is now struggling to save her marriage from the wrath of her parents and other relatives.

At a press conference held today, Kuldeep Kaur, a resident of New York, USA, claimed that she married Lovejeet Singh Virk on September 29 and even registered her marriage. Kuldeep added, "My parents do not approve of this marriage and are trying to implicate my husband and other family members in false cases. I even fear for my life as some people in the police are very close to my parents."

On her step to come out in open over the issue, Kuldeep says, "By doing this, I just want to tell my parents that I am happy and no body from Lovejeet's family has forced me to marry him." Kaur added, "My parents must understand that as I'm above 18 years of age I can choose a husband for myself," she said, adding that she wants her parents to stop harassing her and his new family.

Talking about her coming to India, Kuldip said that, "I boarded a flight and landed here on September 18. We got married on September 29."

In a complaint filed to the NRI Cell, she alleges that her parents and relatives are trying to implicate her husband in false cases. "Even a few unidentified persons threatened my in-laws at their home in Tajpur area. A few of our relatives serving at high posts in police are helping them in doing so," she claimed adding that she apprehends loss of life and liberty at the behest of her parents.

In the complaint posted to NRI Cell through a registered post, the couple has sought protection. "We could submit the complaint personally as we apprehended that her parents would try to kidnap her. If this happens Kuldeep would perhaps be killed as they are taking it as a prestige issue," commented Kuldeep Singh Virk.

Kuldeep in her complaint has named her farther, mother, relatives residing in Bariana village in Jalandhar district and a police officer posted at Banga, district Hoshiarpur.

The incharge of NRI cell, Ludhiana Police, Navreet Singh said they had yet not received the copy of the complaint. "We'll look into it once we get the copy," he added.

Heading: Id musings in faraway Lucknow - Indian Express
Content:
At the Punjab Agricultural University the message is clear — research can wait, it is the VIPs who matter more.

This university which was waiting for a power hotline for the past couple of months to carry out their research work on time, finally got a hotline but for Sutton House. Sutton House is the VIP rest house of the university.

In March, the university had deposited Rs 1.25 crore with the Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB) for allocating a dedicated power hotline to the university. Owing to incessant powercuts, the research work on the campus was being affected. All along this summer, powercuts began at 10 am and stretch through the evening. Some scientists had even claimed that they had lost valuable data and research samples due to powercuts.

Dr V K Sharma, estate officer-cum -chief engineer, PAU, explains, "We needed a hotline as VIPs come and stay here. The CM himself frequents this place. The guest house is centrally air-conditioned. Though Sutton House has a provision for gensets, they are not powerful enough to run ACs." The estate officer added, "This is something we did on priority but very soon the rest of the university will also be on a power hotline. We are pursuing the case quite diligently."

It has also been learnt that for the rest of the university, the procedure is slightly long. The electricity board has proposed to set up a 60 KW sub-station on the campus to carry power to the required places.

A senior faculty member of the university, on the condition of anonymity, said, "There are departments such as soils, plant breeding, biotechnology and others where power is more important than the guesthouse. No doubt, VIPs come here but some other arrangements could have been made for them."

Heading: Mark of mahatma - Indian Express
Content:
Being an Afghan, I feel, means not losing courage in the face of the biggest crisis. I remember the time when I used to live like a refugee in Iran. Those were the worst years of my life. Hard work was not a problem because I am an Afghan. Being deprived of an education was not a problem because I could understand that I was a refugee. It was being abused with foul language that I couldn't take every day. But now, all is well since I got the scholarship from the Government of India. I realise how changes in Afghanistan turned my life around totally. Now, small problems don't matter to me and I realise that my homeland means everything to me.
—Sayed Ahmad Shaheer (BA Final)

It is the second consecutive year students from Afghanistan studying in the Lucknow University are celebrating Id-ul-Fitr away from home and memories of 'watan' (homeland) are a mixbag.

Their experience in India is most cherished and they soak in every event or festivity.

"Oh, I thought it was 'dus chehra' named after the ten-headed Ravan," exclaims Qahid Hamid when you spell out the name of the 'Dussehra' to him.

A Hindi film and music buff he only rues "why do Hindi films show Afghans in such bad light, like for example the protagonist in Subhash Ghai's 'Black & White who wants to blow up the Red Fort on August 15. India is so friendly and helpful to Afghanistan; why would any Afghan want to cause death and destruction in India?"

His friends chorus his sentiment and abhor Pakistan for the bad name it brings to the Afghans with ISI and Taliban.

"Most of us have grown up in the shadow of the gun," says Khalid Ahmadi (B Com final) wryly as he recalls how as a kid on the street he would have to duck and lie prostrate on the ground on hearing the swish of a rocket missile fired some corner of his city Kabul. But having come to terms, it is wont of him and his friends back home to celebrate Id going out on a trek, a long drive or a trip to another city and of setting up barbecue to whip up meaty delicacies.

"We never got to see the good times our grandparents tell us about," says Emal Momand (BA final), who hails from the Mazar Sharif province. "Throughout our childhood we were witness to the bloody coup that overthrew the Russian powers.

There is no count of how many innocent Afghans lost their lives," he says.

Hashmat Hanifi missed all the action since he was brought up in North West Frontier Pakistan.

"No matter which part of the world you are in, Id is the glorious thread that bonds Muslims hailing from or living in any part of the world," says Hashmat, in finalyear B Com.

"Our country is so beautiful, replete with rich resources of copper, uranium and petroleum...such serene mountainous and riverside landscapes...my heart bleeds to see the present situation, moreso on occasions such as Id and particularly when we are away from home," drawls Ali Habibi, pursuing Bachelors in Business Management from the New Campus of Lucknow University. He a The young men have scant aspirations as of settling abroad, even though their parents goad them to look for avenues in Australia, Europe and America. "Who would be happy to settle away from home? And in the US of all the places, a country which has turned Afghanistan into its ground for the battle against Russia? Our friend Saffi, was appointed by the US Army to serve as an interpretor and has been promised the Green Card. But, is he happy? Don't even ask us," says Khalid.

But, for all the strife that tears their motherland apart, all the Afghans staying in Lucknow for studies, are optimistic that some day Allah would be kind, their education would hold them in good stead and if not them, the generation after them will wake up to happier Id mornings.

Amen to that.

Heading: Mob attack minister for removing road barricade - Indian Express
Content:
State Lalit Kala Akadami, Lucknow has put up for sale imprints of rare paintings of Mahatma Gandhi by various artists. The paintings depict the life and times of the Father of the Nation

Lucknow in his speeches

Uttar Pradesh—erstwhile United Provinces—is known for its contribution to the freedom struggle, but did you know that on his first visit to its capital for his non-cooperation movement, Mahatma Gandhi had rebuked the people of Lucknow, for being indisciplined and indulging in lavishness. But in one year, Lucknow proved its love for the motherland till in 1921, Gandhi agreed that it had done its bit in the movement.

The UP State Archives has a collection of 30 speeches of Mahatma Gandhi, delivered here between 1920 and 1921, when he visited Lucknow, Aligarh, Kanpur, Bareilly, Shahjehanpur, Varanasi, Mathura, Agra and several other cities to spread the movement. The archives has also published a book Gandhi speaks on noncooperation in UP with translation of all his speeches and recorded by the British officials, along with notings of the officer recording the speech.

On February 26, 1921, Gandhi was addressing a meeting of farmers and local residents on the banks of Gomti near the Ironbridge.

He found a large number of people smoking bidi and ganja, not paying attention and even creating disturbance. Also, he felt women were finding it difficult to be in the crowd. He said: "I again ask you to do your bit for the noncooperation. Let us obey the commandments of God, not to drink, not to smoke, not to indulge in evil ways and regard strange women as our sisters and mothers.... "

The speeches reflect Gandhi's change in opinion about Lucknow, but also how he looked up to UP to become an integral part of the freedom movement, if Hindus and Muslims joined hands.

"Hindus and Muhammadans should remember that today, they are both in danger. If this cruel government (the British) can render our 7 crore mussalman brethren helpless, it can render 30 crores Hindus helpless too," Gandhi had remarked at the Rifah-e-Aam Club in 1920. He continued with the same remarks in Jhansi a few months later , saying

"Hindus and Mussalmans should realise that if we don't purge our hearts of feelings against each other India will always remain a slave..." Talking about the book, the regional archives officer Prabhakar Johri said it was a collector's item not just for those who are inspired by Mahatma Gandhi, but also those who want to know more about the State's contribution to the Non-Cooperation Movement.

The book can be obtained from the State Archives in Lucknow.

SAMPLE THESE:
DATE: October 15, 1920
PLACE: Rifah-e-Aam club,Lucknow

"I am happy to be in Lucknow but at the same time I want to tell you that if you want to learn to be successful in the campaign of non-cooperation we must learn discipline.....

I would respectfully tell you I do not want to see pleasure in Lucknow. I want to see fakiri (poverty) in it. I found there was poverty in Farangi Mahal and dry bread was being eaten there, hence, I stayed. If both Hindus and Mussalmans want to do your duty to the country, you must become true slaves and leave all lavishness...."

DATE: August 7, 1921
PLACE: Aminabad Park, Lucknow

"... I have not come to Lucknow for the first time and I am happy to say that Lucknow, more or less, has paid its share to the non-cooperation movement...."

Heading: Maya repackages Maya repackages Noida for investors - Indian Express
Content:
Minister for Culture in the state Cabinet Subhash Pandey narrow escaped from a mob fury after his associates and escorting policemen indulged in altercation with a group of protesting people who had blocked Chandauli- Varanasi road on Wednesday morning. Angry mob smashed windowpanes of minister's car.

The police had a tough time escorting Pandey to safety.

The police also registered a case against residents of Chaurahat village at Mughalsarai police station in Chandauli district.

Additional Superintendent of Police (ASP), Chandauli, Piyush Srivastava said that while 21 villagers have been named, 250 others have been held for attacking minister's car and staging the road blockade.

The villagers had put barricades on the road and were demanding restoration of electricity supply that was snapped eight days ago, Srivastava said.

The minister's men provoked the agitators by throwing away barricades aside and misbehaved with the locals, the ASP said.

Heading: Two-member committee to probe flyover mishap - Indian Express
Content:
With recurrent incidents of violence sullying the image of Greater Noida — the industrial showcase of Uttar Pradesh — the Mayawati government is making all out efforts to re introduce the area to the investors in a fresh way.

The government is advertising Greater Noida as "a city planned from scratch to remain ahead of times — offering world class environment for growth."

To attract investors, it is using phrases as "own, develop and operate India's largest Sports City in Noida."

The state government has also earmarked 750 acres of land in Noida, exclusively for this purpose.

Also to regain the trust of industries, the government has given the additional charge of Labour Commissioners to the CEOs of the twin towns.

Besides, it has constituted an Industrial Relations Unit comprising two deputy superintendents of police to sort out the industry related issues.

On August 14 during a protest by farmers on the issue of the land acquisition issue the police had to open fire in which five persons were killed and many others were injured. This was followed by the lynching of Graziano Transmissioni's CEO by factory workers on September 23.

Five days later, another CEO of a software company, Expedien E Solutions, was attacked.

The government officials admit that the incidents have temporarily caused an anti-industry climate.

"The investment is still not a problem in Noida and Greater Noida because of its strategic location. The demand for land is phenomenal.

Yet there is a need to improve the environment for which steps are being taken," one of the officials said. Units of more than 35 companies, including some big international names like Videocon, Daewoo Electronics, Moser Bear, Honda Siel, Escorts Yamaha, Asian Paints, LG Eelectronics, HPCL, already exist in Greater Noida. Others like Wipro, Pepsi, Vectra have acquired spaces. Besides, Greater Noida has seven notified SEZs and eight formally approved ones

Heading: Lok Ayukta indicts education minister for irregularities in teachers’ posting - Indian Express
Content:
Following the flyover collapse at the Lucknow-Faizabad road, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) decided to set up a two-member committee on Wednesday to probe possible shortcoming in the construction of the flyover.

The committee comprises Professor A K Nagpal, Head of Department of Civil Engineering, IIT-Delhi and Mahesh Tandon, Managing Director of Tandon Consultant Private Limited, New Delhi.

Officials of the NHAI said the committee will check the design of the flyover for any inadequacy which might have led to the accident. Experts will also test the quality of the materials used in the construction.  

NHAI General Manager R B Sinha has asked the committee to suggest remedial measures and additional safety measures in order to prevent the recurrence of such incidents in future.

The committee has been asked to submit its report within 21 days. The NHAI Project Director, M K Jain, said the committee will visit Lucknow this week to initiate the inquiry. Jain said: "Prima facie, it appears that the bearings of the girder had slipped, leading to the crash. But the exact cause would be known after the report of the probe agency."

The flyover was being constructed by the Hindustan Construction Company (HCC). Jain said action may be taken against HCC if any irregularity was reported from their side in the investigation.   

The company, meanwhile, has announced a compensation for the victims. "Rs 1 lakh will be paid to the next of the kin of each deceased and Rs 25,000 to each injured person," said U Bhattacharya, Project Manager, HCC. The project director clarified that the flyover was part of the East-West Corridor and not the Golden Quadrilateral.

The East-West Corridor project was started in October 2005, with the aim of developing a 3,640-km highway, connecting Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Bengal and Assam.

In UP, the corridor starts from Shivpuri at UP-Madhya Pradesh border and ends at Kushinagar district at UP-Bihar border. Initially, the project was to be completed by October. "Some complications in land acquisition process and other hurdles delayed it by over one year. But it will be completed positively by December 2009," Jain said.

Heading: Public service panel moves High Court against ‘malafide inquiry’ by govt - Indian Express
Content:
The Uttar Pradesh Lok Ayukta has indicted Minister of Basic Education Dharm Singh Saini and former Secretary of Basic Education R P Singh for irregularities in the posting of Basic Shiksha Adhikaris (BSA).

"The practice (appointment of BSA) was illegal. It violated High Court orders and was inspired by self-interest," stated a report of Lok Ayukta N K Mehrotra, which he recently submitted to Chief Minister Mayawati. A copy of the report was also sent to the chief secretary. Mehrotra said: " We have conducted a probe and sent the report to the chief minister and the chief secretary. We are investigating two more charges against Saini and its report would be sent to the government soon."

The inquiry was conducted following a complaint by Shahbuddin, a Varanasi resident, who is a member of the National Minority Education Commission.

The Lok Ayukta report stated: "The illegal appointment of the District Institutes of Education and Training (DIET) officers as BSAs is spreading corruption and maladministration in the basic education department. In 60 of the 70 districts in the state, lecturers of the DIET were appointed as BSAs." The Centre had launched the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyaan (SSA) for qualitative improvement of primary education and DIET was supposed to undertake training programmes for teachers in districts. "The posting of DIET lecturers as BSAs was hampering training programmes and SSA funds were being misused," said the report.

The BSA posts have always been considered lucrative. The BSA appoints primary teachers in state-run schools and looks after their transfer and promotions. Teachers often pay bribes to get a posting close to urban centres. The BSA also controls the services of the Shiksha Mitras and the mid-day meal scheme.

The annual budget of SSA for 70 districts of UP is Rs 2,800 crore. According to the report, "Self-interest of the accused is evident in posting the officers of DIET as BSA. Without such interest no person would do an unethical and illegal act." The report cites an example of M P Singh, a DIET officer, who was posted as BSA. "Singh, during his posting as BSA at Gonda, was suspended after serious corruption charges were levelled against him by the then District Magistrate O N Mishra in January 2007."

The report said as soon as Saini became a minister in May 2007, Singh was reinstated and given a posting in Varanasi and the chargesheet on him was not filed.

"In Varanasi too, Singh had of corruption charges against him and the DM had recommended action in May, but no action was taken," said the report.

The Lok Ayukta has recommended that for curbing the corruption and misappropriation of the SSA funds, the BSAs and other officers involved in the SSA, who are facing corruption charges, be removed from their present assignments.

Heading: No Eid celebrations for Sanjarpur - Indian Express
Content:
The chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC), Ram Sewak Yadav, and three other members have moved Allahabad High Court against a vigilance inquiry ordered against them.

Their writ petition alleges that the "inquiry is illegal" and motivated by the "malafide intention" of the state government.

In the petition, the chairman also mentioned: "On August 28, Cabinet Secretary Shashank Shekhar Singh warned me of punitive actions if I and the other members do not resign. I informed the Governor about the incident the next day."

On August 27, the government had ordered the vigilance inquiry against the UPPSC chairman and members Somesh Yadav, C N Singh, Zahid Khan, Dr Pankaj and A K Chaturvedi for alleged irregularity in the selection of Provincial Civil Services (Judiciary) 2003 and Women Medical Officers (Allopathy), 2005. The inquiry also sought to know the assets of a few of them.

Ram Sewak told The Indian Express: "The Bahujan Samaj Party government has initiated an inquiry against me and other members, who were appointed during the Samajwadi Party regime."

While the inquiry is directed against six persons, the government has spared three members, two of whom were appointed during the BSP government and one in the SP regime.

The UPPSC has eight members and a chairman.

The charges of the irregularity had surfaced in 2003 from some of the candidates in the exam.

They took the matter to the High Court and subsequently to the Supreme Court, but both courts gave clean chit to the UPPSC.

In case of the 2005 selections, 27 complaints were filed and the UPPSC had instituted an internal inquiry. Even so, the matter went to the High Court, but the candidates lost the case.

"One can well guess the intention of the state government in that it has ordered a vigilance inquiry even after the decision of the apex court," the chairman said. "The state government wanted to appoint its own men and has resorted to illegal means to remove us. Since it cannot oust us before our six-year term expires, it is trying to harass us," he said.

The petition challenged the inquiry on the ground that the UPPSC was governed by the Uttar Pradesh State Public (Regulation of Procedure) Act 1985 and the state government or any other state agency does not have any power to remove its members or initiate any inquiry against them.

The petitioners' counsel R N Singh requested the court to stay the operation of the inquiry.

The Division Bench of Justice Janardan Sahai and Justice Poonam Srivastava asked the government to file a counter-affidavit within three weeks.

The next hearing is on October 20.

Heading: No intelligence cadre to probe serial blasts yet - Indian Express
Content:
Donning new attire, wearing fine perfumes and feast are a traditional part of celebrating Id. But the residents of Sanjarpur town in Azamgarh have decided to give the usual fervor a miss after the town hit the headlines following the encounter in Delhi in which two of its youths were killed.

Rather than sporting colourful decorations, the town was plastered with banners at market and other places demanding justice and impartial inquiry into the arrests made by various state police.

Shadab alias Mister, local Samajwadi Party leader and father of alleged Indian Mujahideen operative Saif, said: "How could the residents engage in merrymaking and enjoy the festival when two youngsters have been killed and several others arrested?"

"We, in Sanjarpur, believe that the police has framed the youths, without concrete evidences," he said.

Another resident Iliyas Ahmed, who runs a general merchant shop, said: "We will offer the Id prayers and go back to our home. There will be no celebrations, no exchange of greetings."

Station Officer of Sarai Mir police station Kamleshwar Singh said the decision of not celebrating the festival has been taken only at Sanjarpur. The people at other nearby areas like Sarai Mir have not taken any such call, said Singh.

Heading: In UP’s sugar heartland, mill employees live in constant fear - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when investigators have traced the roots of the Indian Mujahideen — the outfit allegedly responsible for the recent terror attacks across the country — to UP's Azamagarh district, the state government seems to have put the idea of creating a separate intelligence cadre on the backburner.

The government's intention to create an intelligence cadre was announced four days after blasts rocked the courts in Lucknow, Faizabad and Varanasi on November 23 last year.

But the process of creating an intelligence cadre is yet to begin, said Additional Director General of Police (Intelligence) Malkiat Singh. "The government has not sent any proposal in this connection," he added.

According to Secretary (Home) Renuka Kumar, the concerned file was sent to the finance department when there was talk of constituting such a cadre. "Right now, I am not in position to tell you the current status of the project," she said.

The original idea was to recruit dedicated staff from the local intelligence units and provide them specialised training. The first step in this regard was to lay down the parameters for the selection of candidates. This was never done, a source in the Home department said.

The blasts in Delhi, Jaipur, Ahmedabad, Bangalore and Mumbai have all been linked to the UP network of terrorists. Until the Delhi Police first came out with its disclosures, the UP Police had no clue about Indian Mujahideen's presence in Azamgarh and other places.

The name of Abu Bashar, who was arrested by the Gujarat Police in connection with the Ahmedabad blasts, had also figured in the interrogation report of one of the accused in the UP court blasts case, but the intelligence unit had failed to work on the information, said an officer.

Heading: As ‘killer’ weed blooms, a fresh look at its poison - Indian Express
Content:
The recent lynching of the CEO of the Noida-based Italian firm Graziano by angry factory workers hit the headlines, but it is nothing new in the state's sugarcane heartland where managers live in a constant fear of being gunned down.

In the past, three top executives of different sugar mills in crime-infested west UP have been murdered. The state government has not provided special security cover to the sugar sector, which is the backbone of state's economy, say sugar mill executives, who are so fearful that they refuse to come on record.

Rather frequently, one comes across suave, soft spoken, safari clad executives with guns tucked in their waistband. "I got it when I was posted in west UP," one chief executive of a sugar mill reveals hesitantly.

While some executives have got arms licences, others move around with armed private guards. "We are even ready to pay for police gunners," a mill owner said. This April, a senior DGM of Shishir Bajaj-managed sugar major, Bajaj Hindustan Group, was shot dead in Kinauni near Meerut.

Siddharth Upadhyay was shot outside his own office by gunmen who came in a car. The police arrested several persons, two of them women. It was alleged that gangsters running benami contracts in sugar mills killed Upadhyay, as they wanted some lucrative contracts. In Muzaffarnagar district, Subhash Chand Jaggi, vice-president of the Triveni Group sugar mill was gunned down on December 29, 1999. The police arrested the alleged killers. "They were acquitted by the court after the witnesses turned hostile," said mill officials. "Jaggi was killed because he was not succumbing to pressure from some local mafias," one of the officials said.

In UK Modi Group's SBEC sugar mill in Baghpat district, , J K Chopra, DGM (Engineering) was shot dead around four years ago, while he was out for his morning walk. He was killed because he allegedly refused to give a job to a youth, Braham Pal of Barwala.

The assailant was later shot dead by the police in an encounter. The lucrative contracts have spawned well-organised mafias. Apart from contracts for seasonal labour and transport, there are contracts for boiler ash, press mud, bagasse, scrap and handling of sugar bags. The bagasse contract of a fair sized unit could run upto Rs 3 crore.

Sugar mills, the only big industry in most parts of the industrially backward state, have become a favourite milch cow. The mill owners sometimes hire their own securitymen but even so, the system is not foolproof. Sugar mill employees have been robbed on roads.

The government should make a special policy for security of the sugar sector. The top brass of the mills should be given police gunners, say sugar mill executives.

According to IG Police (Meerut Zone) Gurdarshan Singh, a Deputy Superintendent of Police has been made the Industry Relations Officer in Noida and Greater Noida after the Graziano episode. A police helpline and Quick Response Teams have been formed that are equipped with video cameras and riot-control equipment. "There is no blanket security cover plan for sugar sector. The SSPs of respective districts individually assess the ground situation and take action," Singh said.

Police officers are not in favour of providing individual police escorts to mill owners and executives. "The mill management can hire security for their officials. The police can give security clearance and training to those guards," said a police officer.

But mill employees said that there have been several instances where private guards were attacked when they tried to act. The state government has, meanwhile, decided to form two Quick Reaction Teams (QRT) to contain such incidents.

Heading: LU initiates proceedings to suspend two students - Indian Express
Content:
It has been almost two years since the publication of a preliminary study on the possibility of a wild weed causing "encephalitis deaths" in Saharanpur and adjoining areas. Now, its principal investigator Dr Vipin M Vashishtha, a pediatrician in Bijnore, is all set to take his study to the next step.

He now plans to find out the cause of toxicity of the weed in collaboration with the scientists of the Indian Institute of Toxicology Research (IITR), Lucknow.

Dr Mukul Das, Head of Food Toxicology Laboratory at IITR, said they were planning to visit the affected areas and assess the situation "before finalising" their report.

Even the Central government has called a meeting of experts on October 8 in New Delhi to discuss the issue. As many as 16 experts of various institutes like National Institute of Communicable Diseases, Indian Academy of

Pediatrics and the National Institute of Nutrition, Hyderabad will be there. Vashishta has also been invited.

The weed, Cassia Occidentalis, is locally called Pamad or Kasondi. Consumption of its seeds leads to encephalitis-like symptoms. Often unsuspecting children eat the seeds and die.

Vashishta said his study was based on clinical findings, "wherein I had questioned children and their parents in Saharanpur and connected their illness with eating of this weed named." As for the toxicity of the weed, he had some references of some earlier studies that were done on animals. His next study is going to focus on the toxicity caused by the seeds in humans. "I am collaborating with IITR because they are the experts and rightly equipped to take up the toxicity study," he said.

Vashishta said more places, like Moradabad in UP and Roorkee in Uttarakhand, have reported cases of illness caused by the weed.

The period from September to December is when the weeds bear fruit.

"We already had one case in Bijnore where the child had symptoms of fever, vomiting and then he became mentally unstable and finally succumbed to the disease within two days after eating the weed," said Vashishtha.

Heading: Chief Secy Office not above RTI, says Information Commission - Indian Express
Content:
The Lucknow University (LU) has initiated the process for the suspension of students Shailendra Verma and Vineet Verma for their alleged involvement in the abduction of a fellow student.

On Wednesday, LU Chief Proctor A N Singh said: "Santosh Yadav was reportedly kidnapped and robbed by a group of students near IT crossing last week. Shailendra and Vineet, students of BSc and MA respectively, were allegedly involved in the incident. They were named in the FIR lodged with the Hasanganj police."

According to the police, Vineet, a student leader, was the nephew of a minister in the BSP government.

Besides a fine of Rs 200, smoking or pan masala consumption on LU campus is going to cost the students more from October 2.

While prohibiting smoking and chewing of tobacco on campus, LU authorities said on Tuesday that if any student was caught flouting the rule, a negative entry will be made in the character certificates, a spokesman said.

Heading: Gagan stays on top in Indian Amateur Tour - Indian Express
Content:
Refusing to allow the state Chief Secretary to keep his office above the Right To Information Act, the State Information Commission has asked Atul Kumar Gupta to appoint a Public Relations Officer (PRO) in the next 15 days and make the related information public.

While issuing the order, Acting Chief Information Commissioner Gyanendra Sharma quoted judgments of other states in similar cases. The Chief Secretary's Office, he said, comes under the category of "Public Authority" under Section 2(H) of the RTI Act.

Hearing the appeal of petitioner Paras Nath Verma, on June 26, the Commission had asked the Chief Secretary if any public information officer had been appointed in his office. Sharma had also asked the Chief Secretary to explain why his office does not figure on the government website along with other departments.

In reply, the Chief Secretary had stated that his office does not fall under the purview of "public authority" and could not be listed for seeking information through RTI.

Disposing of the case, Sharma asked the Chief Secretary to appoint a Public Information Officer and make his phone number and office address public.

Heading: Many in the BCCI point out that this winter could be Ganguly’s swansong; but the left-hander begs to differ - Indian Express
Content:
Gagan Verma continued his run on top of the LG Indian Amateur Tour Order of Merit after a good showing at the Golden Greens Amateur where he finished tied for third place. Making his move up the table with two back to back wins was Rashid Khan who climbed another seven rungs to find himself at eighth position and a few good shows away from the top billing.

Saurabh Bahuguna and Abhishek Jha maintained their standing at second and third place respectively while Vikram Rana followed them at fourth. Manav Das who had missed out on the Northern India Amateur came back at the Golden Greens Amateur with a top 10 finish and was placed at fifth position.

Going into the next leg of the season all eyes will be on Rashid Khan who is still not as high up on the merit table as he should be because he does not have the nine events everyone else has notched up.

If he continues like this, there is absolutely no doubt that by the time the 2008-09 season of the Indian Amateur Tour comes to a close he will be right on top of the pile.

The next big assignment for these stars on the Indian Amateur Tour is the Eisenhower Trophy where they will be representing India in what is undoubtedly the most prestigious tournament at the Amateur level after which Rashid Khan will be off to Brazil to compete in the Faldo Series Grand Final.
