Heading: Golden Handshake, Or Is It ? - Indian Express
Content:
Such things happen only with Sourav Ganguly. For almost a month, the buzz in the Maidan has been that it's finally curtains for Kolkata's most famous sporting icon on the international front after an eventful 12-year ride. But in a huge surprise for the cricket-crazy city this afternoon, Ganguly was included in the Indian team for the upcoming high-profile Test series against the visiting Australians.

Ganguly's induction into the team for the Australia series comes as a breather three weeks after the former Indian skipper was ignored for the Irani Trophy's Rest of India team earlier last month. Ganguly's harsh exclusion from the Rest of India squad on September 8 was then seen as a message to the 34-year-old batsman from the national selectors to call it a day, as the just-concluded Irani Trophy four-day match was being deemed as the platform for selection for the Australia series.

However, in a marathon meeting in Mumbai, the Kris Srikkanth-led selection panel picked Ganguly for the first two matches of India's four-Test series against Ricky Ponting & Co. Ganguly will be part of the Tests in Bangalore and Mohali. The series gets underway on October 9.

The man in the centre of the storm himself played his usual hide-and-seek game earlier in the day, sending shutterbugs into a tizzy, before showing up at Eden later.

What makes Ganguly's so-called return to the team for the Australia series more interesting are disturbing suggestions from certain sections of the cricket administration fraternity — that his inclusion could be a sort of golden handshake. As reliable sources in the BCCI told The Indian Express, the Board has lately been toying with the idea of offering the senior, ageing players in the team an honourable exit, working out some sort of a 'VRS' for the seniors.

Ganguly himself vehemently rubbished such speculation over 'golden handshake', terming it as nothing but baseless rumour. "There's no such compromise," the elegant left-hand batsman literally thundered when asked by reporters about suggestions of a possibility of a 'deal' with the Board.

Says Maidan veteran Gopal Bose, who has played a pivotal role in Ganguly's career: "Well, I get the impression that this could be a case of golden handshake, as many are suggesting. Maybe the Board is giving subtle signals to the seniors (read: Ganguly, Dravid, Laxman, Kumble) to make up their minds to call it quits, and in return, they would be awarded with spots in the upcoming home series against Australia and then England."

Another Maidan veteran, Sambaran Banerjee, who was the national selector when Ganguly made his international debut in 1996, reckons that today's development is hardly a surprise. "Sourav, after all, has all the world's experience. And for a home series as big as this one, the national selectors had no option but to rely on the seniors in the team like Sourav and the rest." The former selector however shot down suggestions of a possible 'golden handshake'.

Heading: Panel for autonomous body on education - Indian Express
Content:
Once at loggerheads, Dalmiya now all praise for Ganguly
CAB boss offers Sourav senior Bengal captaincy, says state team needs him in this hour of crisis

That Jagmohan Dalmiya and Sourav Ganguly don't share the best of relationships is the worst-kept secret in Indian cricket. However, on a special day like this, the veteran cricket administrator didn't mind showering praises on Ganguly, who has in the past openly gone against him over issues off the field.

In an unusual change of guard, CAB president Dalmiya heartily welcomed the national selectors' decision to persist with the former Indian captain for the upcoming Tests against Australia. Speaking to reporters after a 10-minute closed-door chat with Ganguly at his Eden Gardens office, Dalmiya said: "We are all happy for him (Ganguly). I wish him all the best for the two Tests against Australia." Not very elaborate, but strong enough comment, considering the kind of uneasy stand-off they have had ever since the Greg Chappell-email leak episode in September 2006.

Dalmiya also said that an experienced warhorse like Ganguly doesn't need anybody's backing to earn his place back in the national team.

Interestingly, Dalmiya also pointed out that he has requested Ganguly to lead the senior Bengal team in the upcoming Ranji Trophy. "I've talked to him to play for Bengal in the domestic season. I have also requested him to take up the senior Bengal captaincy at this critical juncture when we are relegated to the Plate Group. He is the best person to lead the side and take Bengal into the Elite Group again. Ganguly's presence will inspire and motivate the youngsters in the team to perform."

Heading: HC terms primary teachers’ training institutes illegal - Indian Express
Content:
To do away with a number of regulatory bodies in higher education, the Yashpal Committee, appointed by the National Knowledge Commission, has suggested that an autonomous body dealing with higher education be set up.

In a meeting with the Vice-Chancellors of colleges and universities of the state at Jadavpur University on Wednesday, the commission sought their views on the matter. The Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta, Suranjan Das, said: "Although the committee has suggested a regulatory body, it may lead to over-centralisation ."

"Some of the recommendations of the Yashpal Committee like interdisciplinary research and undergraduate education at all the universities are very important for the higher education," said Siddhartha Datta, Pro Vice-Chancellor of the Jadavpur University.

The other recommendations of the committee include making IITs full-fledged universities, so that teaching of all the disciplines of science and engineering could be carried on along with other streams of social sciences.

The committee also held the Jadavpur University as a model of a technology-based university with high quality of education in humanities.

The committee is also of the opinion that inspection and monitoring of educational institutions should be reduced drastically and the accredited institutions should be given more leverage.

Heading: For CPM units, Town Hall available at Rs 10 - Indian Express
Content:
The Calcutta High Court on Wednesday declared 122 Primary Teachers' Training Institutes (PTTIs) in the state illegal since these were not recognised by the National Council for Teachers Education (NCTE).

A Division Bench of Chief Justice S S Nijjar and Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose said these institutes should have sought recognition from the NCTE in accordance with the law.

The Bench also directed the institutes to return the money taken from the applicants for admission to the 2005-06 session. The NCTE had issued a circular in 2006 terming the institutes invalid, as they had not sought recognition from it. Subsequently, a Division Bench of the High Court passed an order restraining the admissions and the PTTIs could not admit students after 2006.

The Wednesday's ruling came during the hearing of a PIL filed in 2007 by Tulshi Bakshi, a resident of Kolkata.

Bakshi had alleged that the PTTIs were not recognised by the NCTE and the West Bengal Board for Primary Education had allowed them to run till 2006.

Responding to the judgment, School Education Minister Partha De said: "I have learnt that after a definite period the certificate of all the students who have passed from PTTI has been termed illegal." De added that the state government may challenge the matter in the Supreme Court or could opt for an out of court solution with the NCTE by paying a fine to the regulatory body. The government is waiting for the final copy of the judgment and will take the decision after considering its legal implications, he added.

A senior CPM leader and member of CPM committee on education told The Indian Express that the state government is coming up with the Primary Service Commission for recruitment of teachers in the state.

There has been no recruitment of primary teachers in the state for the last two years after the PTTIs ran into a legal hurdle and about 16,000 students could not appear in the examination. Thousands of students could not be appointed as their degrees have been termed illegal. Students caught in the stalemate are turning to politicians so that they can mount pressure on the state government for an out of court settlement of the issue.

A section of the students, along with the Trinamool Congress, will organise protests in the city this month on this issue.

Heading: Security stepped up ahead of Puja - Indian Express
Content:
Town Hall — the most prestigious auditorium of Kolkata — has been much used and abused by the authorities. Recently, the building was rented out at a measly Rs 10 to the Student Federation of India (SFI), the student body of the CPM , for holding a conference for the All India SFI Seminar.

The normal charges for renting the Town Hall, however, are a whopping Rs 10,000 for four hours. According to the rules of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC), the Town Hallcannot be rented out at a token money to any of the political parties.

Faiyaz Ahmed Khan, MMiC (advertisement and amusement), however, had different take. "We have ensured that all political parties can be given the halls and auditoriums including the Town Hall and the Netaji Indoor Stadium for a token price. In this case we do not discriminate between our party and the opposition parties," he said.

There are, however, provisions to slash down the charges in case of seminars and conferences, which are organised to serve a social purpose.

A trustee board was constituted in 2000 to maintain the Town Hall. Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya, Municipal commissioner Alapan Bandyopadhyay and Khan are among the members of the trustee board.

A civic official claimed that renting the Town Hall for political programmes by charging a token amount is not only illegal, but also results in huge losses for the civic body, which spends approximately Rs 60-80 Lakh annually to maintain the heritage hall.

The Town Hall is frequently rented out to several private news channels. Sources said the private parties are charged Rs 10,000 for four hours and the amount of money increases if the programme exceeds the duration.

Although the KMC has fixed the renting charges for every auditorium and hall under its jurisdiction , the rule often gets relaxed for organising political programmes. Only nomial amount is charged in such cases.

The opposition parties, however, alleged that the Town Hall has never been rented to them at a token charge.

"I cannot remember when our party has been given the Town Hall at a token price. The bodies associated with CPM keep on using the heritage hall by paying either a nominal charge or no charge at all," said Javed Ahmed Khan, leader of the Opposition. "Despite the fact that the CPM is the richest party in the state, it keeps on taking advantages using its political power," he added.

The members of SFI appeared to be quite ignorant about the issue and did not reveal the actual amount of money paid to the Town Hall authorities.

"We were given the Town Hall at a token price but I do not know the amount of money paid for the programme," said Kaustav Chatterjee, state secretary of the SFI.

The civic officials in the charge of the Town Hall, meanwhile, denied all the allegations.

"Although, we were asked to give the heritage hall at a token price but later we collected Rs 10,000 from the SFI for holding the conference there," said a senior civic official.

Heading: Aftab Ansari, aides grilled over recent terror attacks - Indian Express
Content:
In wake of the recent bomb blasts across the country and the stampede in Jodhpur, the state government has taken up a series of measures to ensure safety and security during Durga Puja.

A meeting was held at Lalbazar police headquarters on Tuesday which was attended by top brass of the state police and the Kolkata police, besides representatives of 25 puja committees of Kolkata and the suburbs.

While 50 beds will be earmarked for emergency in all the five medical college hospitals, the government has also given Rs 10 lakh to each of the hospitals for buying medicines.

"The Kolkata police officials are talking to private nursing homes to check if they can earmark some beds. All blood banks have been told to stock up blood and organisations that run ambulance services have been told to be alert," Home Secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarti, who presided over Tueday's meeting, said on Wednesday.

The government has also issued a set of guidelines to the puja committees.

These include identifying exit points at puja pandals, announcement through microphones, setting up of watch towers, control rooms manned by representatives from the police, health department, fire service and Calcutta Electric Supply Corporation, and arrangement of adequate water and sand.

"The volunteers of the puja committees will be trained for a day by the police. We have also told the committees to prepare a rescue plan in case of an emergency," the home secretary further said.

He added the Kolkata police are raising a 680-strong security force to provide security for the Metro Railway. "We requested the Centre to send CISF for the security of the Metro Railway. But they said they will require at least two years for doing that. So we are raising this force," Chakrabarti said.

Heading: Singur may not hit US investment in Bengal - Indian Express
Content:
The mastermind of the Khadim abduction and the American Centre shootout, Aftab Ansari was interrogated by the Kolkata Police on Wednesday over the recent terror attacks in the country.

The detectives of the state's Special Task Force also grilled Jamaluddin Nasir, Happy Singh and Aquib Ali.

From 2 pm to 6 pm, the team had interrogated the four separately at the jail superintendent's office.

According to sources, they were also questioned about their links with Students' Islamic Movement of India (SIMI).

Rajiv Kumar, Special Additional Commissioner and Joint Commissioner, in-charge of the STF, however, said the questioning was routine.

"From time to time, we interrogate such criminals," said Kumar.

In their requisition slip, the team had stated that the interrogation was to get information regarding case number 50, dated January 31, 2006, in which Lashkar-e-Taiba operative Aquib Ali was arrested from Bowbazar under charges of anti-national activities and under Explosive Acts.

But sources in the STF said that Ansari and his henchmen were associates of Amir Reza Khan — a fact which came up during the investigation of Khadim chief Partho Roy Burman's abduction.

Amir's name had surfaced after the arrest of five youths in Mumbai in connection with the recent terror attacks. His name is now on the top of the investigation list.

The Mumbai police have already taken details of the Khadim abduction from the Criminal Investigation Department and the old files have come out of the closet of the state police.

According to the latest information received by the state intelligence agencies, Amir has settled in Pakistan.

"But the Mumbai Police believe that the other accused in the related cases have joined hands with Amir after he fled the country. They now want to keep tabs on every accused not behind the bars," said a STF source.

Amir is the brother of Asif Reza Khan, and they were the residents of Central Kolkata. Asif was accused in several cases of extortion and kidnapping and was picked up by the Uttar Pradesh STF.

He was transferred to the Gujarat Police custody in connection with the kidnapping of a businessman there. He was killed in an encounter in 2001 while trying a jailbreak.

Police said Asif was into terrorist activities as well. After his death, Amir took over his mantle.

Heading: Buddha smokes away ban, police confused about implementation - Indian Express
Content:
The Singur imbroglio is not likely to deter the prospective US investors to invest in West Bengal, said John Davison, Minister-Counselor for Economic Affairs at the US Embassy in New Delhi.

"There is not any apprehension among US industrialists about investing in Bengal," he said at an interactive session of the Indian Chamber of Commerce on Wednesday.

The US Consul General in Kolkata, Beth A Payne, said:

"Investors look for transparency and stability before making investment. If these factors are absent, there could be some hesitation."

Regarding Singur project, Davison said: "Tata Motor's Nano car is being widely reported in US media. It is not just a car, it symbolises the maturity of growing Indian middle-class and their aspirations for an inexpensive car."

He assured that the crisis in the US economy will not have an adverse impact on the Indian economy. The US administration is drawing up a rescue package to restore the institutions, he said.Davison visited the Frito-Lay factory at Sankrail in Howrah on Wednesday.

"It is astounding that the factory came up in only eight months. More impressive was that many of the employees were youths,"he added.

Heading: Rizwanur named uncle, cops guilty in ‘suicide note’ - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the ban on smoking in public places comes into force from October 2, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee said he had no plans to quit smoking.

"There are more important things and problems in the country to pay attention to," said Bhattacharjee, when asked whether he intends to quit smoking. His chamber, where he has been taking puffs, would be termed a public place from Thursday. Incidentally, smoking at the Writers' Buildings has been banned six months ago. But most employees do not care about the law. From Thursday, however, even the private cabins of IAS officers and ministers would be termed a public place and invite a ban on smoking. One would have to shell out Rs 200 if caught smoking in public places. Streets, bus stops, restaurants and even offices, both private and public, come within the definition of a public place.

The Kolkata police, however, is clueless about the implementation of the rule. "No order about this has come to me," said Javed Shamim, Deputy Commissioner (DD) of Kolkata police. The definition of a public place has also confused the police. "It is not clear what is a public place. How can my office become a public place? What harm would it do if I smoke inside closed doors without affecting others," said a police officer. Some officers say that this ban would take some time to be enforced. "The basic question about who will enforce the ban has not been defined. This will need some time," said a senior police officer.

Heading: Few sigh in relief, others wary of following orders - Indian Express
Content:
Sessions court grants interim bail to three policemen

Rizwanur Rehman held his uncle and four others "morally responsible" for his death in his "suicide note". On Wednesday, as the CBI placed the note before a court as part of its chargesheet, interim bail was granted to Ajay Kumar, former deputy commissioner of Kolkata police and two other police officers who were the main accused in the case.

In the note, Rizwanur wrote, "The people actually and morally responsible for my death are my uncle Saidur Rehman, uncle-in-law Anil Saraogi, Sukanti Chakraborty, Gyanwant Singh, Ajay Kumar and MLA Javed Khan."

The CBI retrieved the note from Rehman's computer, which was recovered from the home of his maternal aunt after his death on September 21, 2007. The document had been deleted from the computer and the agency retrieved it from its hard drive. The CBI is treating it as a suicide note.

Despite their names in the note, however, former Deputy Commissioner ( Headquarters) Singh, Trinamool MLA Khan and Saidur were not chargesheeted because the CBI could not gather evidence against them. "Only evidence matters in court," said an official of the agency.

According to sources, the persons named had acted with malice and were instrumental in breaking Rehman's marriage with Priyanka Todi.

In the note, Rehman wrote: "...I am leaving this world forever. We live in a so called secular country. But in the last 20 days, I have seen the true face of the administration, which runs on money. There is no law to protect common man. I know I should have contested (my case) in a court of law...but what after that... my in-laws would have made sure that our lives were ruined for ever."

The Sessions Court, meanwhile, granted interim bail to the three policemen on a bial bond of Rs 10,000.

The court also imposed a condition that the officers will not leave the Calcutta Metropolitan area without the permission of the CBI court till October 27. While granting bail, Ghosh observed that it was not possible for the accused officers to influence the 184 witnesses named in the chargesheet.

The CBI had filed the chargesheet against Kumar, Sukanti Chakraborty and Krishnendu Das on September 20 in the CBI court, which had directed them to appear on October 27. The police officers, however, had surrendered on Tuesday.

The officers filed a bail petition on Wednesday. The counsel of Ajay Kumar, Milan Mukherjee pleaded that his client is a government servant and has cooperated with the CBI. It was argued that the CBI had not issued any warrant and had requested the magistrate to issue summons.

Mukherjee also argued that the CBI brought the charge under Section 506 of CrPC, which is not a cognizable offence. The counsels of the other two police officers also pleaded the same.

CBI counsel Partha Tapaswai contended that the trio would try to influence the witnesses as they enjoyed tremendous clout. The court granted bail but reiterated the earlier order of the CBI court, directing the officers to appear in the court on October 27.

Home Secretary Asok Mohan Chakrabarti made it clear that the state government had washed its hands of the accused police officers.

"While doing my duty, if I do something that is not approved by the government, then it will not be responsible for my act," he said. He was waiting for a report on the officers supposed to be sent by Kolkata police commissioner Gautam Mohan Chakraborty.

Heading: Walled City traders ask for tight police security - Indian Express
Content:
RIZWANUR DEATH CASE: BAIL APPLICATION OF COPS

While IPS officers at the Lalbazar headquarters rejoiced at the granting of interim bail to the three police officers — Ajay Kumar, Gyanwant Singh and Krishnendu Das — implicated in the Rizwanur Rehman death case, lower-ranked policemen said they will now think twice before carrying out any verbal order of their seniors.

The policemen, who had gathered at the session's court to know the outcome of the bail plea, raised slogans in favour of the order as soon as the bail was granted to the officers. The mood spilled onto to the Lalbazar once the news reached there.

A deputy commissioner of the Kolkata police said, "It was a terrible day yesterday. We all were extremely upset after the court did not grant them bail." An IPS officer said: "Yesterday was the birthday of Ajay Kumar's son. I really feel bad for his family." He and many other officers claimed that they could not concentrate on their work on Tuesday.Many officers, however, could not comprehend why the accused policemen decided to surrender before court when they were slated to appear on October 27.

R K Johuri, a retired IPS officer and former president of the West Bengal IPS Officers' Association, said, "The incident is shocking." Present secretary of the association, Harman Preet Singh refused to comment on the issue saying that the matter was sub-judice.

Lower-ranking officers at Lalbazar were, however, apprehensive that after this incident, many would not feel confident to carry out verbal orders of the seniors. "The two junior officers, especially Krishnendu Das, just followed orders of their senior officers. Now they have been implicated. This will definitely make us doubtful whenever we receive any order from a senior," said a sub-inspector of the dacoity section of detective department.

A policement said from now onwards written orders would be preferred.

"This lack of confidence among junior policemen may severely affect the functioning of the police," said an inspector of the detective department.

"Das' career has been badly affected. He was not given promotion and has been treated like a pariah for the last one year. How much more does the society want him to suffer," said a former colleague of Krishnendu Das.

Heading: No, minister! MLAs shoot down Bill proposing salary hikes of ministers - Indian Express
Content:
The walled city's prime shopping hotspots — Mangal Bazar and Nawapura — get at least 300 enthusiastic customers in an hour during the Navratri season. However, shopkeepers are wary of the steps taken by the police and hope for a strong security cover.

Manu Soni, a garment shopkeeper said CCTV cameras should be installed in the area. "For a cricket match, they can install 30 cameras outside the Reliance Stadium. Why can't they put cameras here? There are more people in these narrow streets than one can see," he said.

But Inspector B N Chawda of the City police said that shopkeepers need not worry about security, as regular staff is sufficient to monitor the area. "Bomb Detection Squad has been deployed in the area in case of any untoward incident. We are operating with the regular police force that frequently patrols in the area," he said.

All the push carts and laaris have been removed to avoid commotion. "We know that a lot of people come for shopping, so we have removed the laaris and push carts to avoid commotion in case of a bomb threat," Chawda said.

Prakash Zala, a laari owner in Navabazaar, said that the police decision is a big loss for him. All these years, people would complete their shopping and flock to his laari to eat. "I know it is because of the bomb blasts. But now I do not have an alternative as my laari is not permanent," he said.

Garment-seller Deepak Jain said that though the turnout is high, most are just passers-by. "They hardly come inside the shops. But still, intensified security is required considering the present state of affairs and the recent blasts," said Jain.

Heading: Retired MSU profs under SOG scanner - Indian Express
Content:
Cutting across party lines, MLAs belonging to the ruling BJP as well as the Congress have objected to the government's move to raise the monthly salaries of ministers and ministers of state. This was one of the main reasons why the government was forced to withdraw, at the eleventh hour, an official Bill to amend laws relating to the salaries and allowances of ministers, members, Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Gujarat Legislative Assembly during the three-day monsoon session that concluded on Monday.

The MLAs are reportedly angry with the government for not conceding their two main demands — increasing their monthly basic salary from lower to higher scale payable to Class I government officers, and also allowing them to travel by train in the Class I A/C coach along with co-travellers.

"After a series of discussions between the MLAs and the whips of the BJP and Congress, a consensus was reached that the salaries and allowances of the members will be hiked. But we saw later that the Bill contained a provision seeking to increase the ministers' salaries and allowances by 25 per cent of the amount being paid to the MLAs," said Shaktisinh Gohil, Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly.

Gohil told Newsline on Wednesday that as per the original law, ministers are entitled to a raise of only 10 per cent in their salaries and allowances of the total amount being paid to the MLAs. Not only this, the government has not accepted the MLAs' demand to allow train travel by Class I AC coach, instead of the existing facility of travelling by Class II AC coach and Class I non-AC coach.

The MLAs also wanted the government to raise their salaries and allowances payable to Class I government officers at higher category, rather than at lower category as is the existing practice. But this demand was also ignored by the government.

When contacted, the Minister of State for Parliamentary Affairs, Amit Shah, said that the MLAs' demands are "unjustified" and cannot be conceded. "The government will have to entail an additional burden of over rupees three crore annually if the demand is met," he said. About the 25 per cent hike as sought in the "withdrawn Bill" for the ministers, he said "there is nothing new in it".

BJP Chief Whip R C Faldu said it was unfortunate that it was because of the "non-cooperative stance" adopted by the Opposition Congress that the government was forced to withdraw the amendment Bill on the members' salaries and allowances.

Faldu said he would have to check if there was a provision in the Bill to hike the ministers' salaries/allowances by 25 per cent of the amount payable to MLAs.

"If a consensus is reached among all the 182 MLAs, the government may bring the same Bill again in the House during the next Budget Session," he said, adding that MLAs should appreciate that the government had agreed to increase the telephone allowance for the MLAs from Rs 4,000 to Rs 5,000 per month.

Yet another provision in the amendment Bill entitles all elected members to seek free medical treatment in some of the leading private corporate hospitals in the state. At present, MLAs get such a facility only in government and municipal-run hospitals in the state.

The withdrawn Bill also sought to allow the elected members to travel by air in lieu of train travel subject to the conditions that the difference between the air fare and railway fare shall be borne by the members. At present, each of the legislators get over Rs 22,860 per month in salaries/allowances, while the monthly pay packet of ministers, Leader of the Opposition, and Speaker is put at over Rs 30,000. Apart from the salary, every MLA is paid for telephone usage, services of personal assistant and postal and stationery charges.

Heading: Court remands ten accused in police custody till October 8 - Indian Express
Content:
M S university (MSU) dons who retired over the last decade have come under the scanner of the district Special Operations Group (SOG), which is probing the origins of the terror calls and letters threatening bomb blasts in Vadodara and other districts.

Twelve threat letters were mailed in the names of three professors of the MSU Business and Economics department. The SOG has officially asked the Heads of Department (HoD) of the varsity to furnish details of all professors who had retired over the last 10 years.

All the three dons named in the terror mail — Seema Bakshi, J R Mohite and DV Baloni — are from the Business and Economics department. The letters were sent to various temples, educational institutes and other public places in Jamnagar, Porbandar, Amreli, and Ankleshwar. In addition, Ambaji temple, Ahmedabad-based Bhadra Mandir and Dwarka Temple also received the threat letters, said Inspector K M Polra of SOG, Vadodara.

"Seven letters were sent in the name of Bakshi, two in the name of Baloni and three in the name of Mohite," Polra said. Bakshi retired 12 years ago and is now based in Shimla, while the other two professors are still active in their fields. "SOG suspects that the culprit(s) may be well acquainted with the professors and could still be working in MSU, since he or she has mentioned the names of the retired professors," Polra said.

SOG does not rule out the possibility that the main culprit is someone who was or is still with the Business and Economics Department of MSU, said Inspector S M Alsika, SOG Vadodara. Meanwhile, D V Baloni, one of the three professors confirmed that SOG has queried him in this connection.

Parimal Vyas, who was the officiating dean of MSU Commerce faculty confirmed that the SOG had sent an official communiqué seeking the details of retired professors. Polra said, "The communiqué, along with the terror letters, was sent to all HoDs so that they could analyse the handwriting in the letters. Their inputs will be valuable since they are in constant touch with students, clerks as well as teachers."

The postal seal on the terror letters showed that most of these were mailed from Raopura area of the city, he said. The letters have been written mostly in Hindi in a scribbled running handwriting and are not more than a paragraph. Polra said: "There is no good usage of vocabulary and the letters are largely a jumble. Atankwad, SIMI, Jihad, Turkistan, Abu Bashar and Bomb Rakha Hai are some of the words which are common to the letters. In addition, the letters also mention that SIMI has received Rs 1.5 lakh from Abu Bashar."

Heading: Police bust gang involved in robbing homosexuals - Indian Express
Content:
The designated Metropolitan Court hearing the Ahmedabad blasts case on Wednesday remanded the ten people accused in the Ahmedabad serial blasts case, including mastermind Mufti Abdul Bashir and Sajid Mansuri, in police custody till October 8.

Zahid Sheikh, Imran Sheikh, Iqbal Sheikh, Samsuddin Sheikh, Yunus Mansuri, Gyasuddin Ansari, Arif Kagzi and Usman Agarbattiwala, along with Bashir and Sajid Mansuri, were arrested on August 17 by the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB).

Their present remand comes under a case registered with Naroda police station. They had been previously sent to police custody in the Civil Hospital blast case and the Khadia blasts case.

The remand application submitted by the DCB states that custody of the accused is sought to probe their links with international terrorist organisations and to find out their source of funding. In addition, their role in the conspiracy of Naroda blasts needs to be probed further.

According to the DCB, the accused were in constant touch with Afzal Usmani, a SIMI member who was in Ahmedabad on July 26, the day of the blasts.

The DCB is also looking towards understanding how the accused could be brainwashed into the planning and execution of the serial bomb blasts.

Heading: CAG report blames mandarins for short recovery of stamp duty, registration fee - Indian Express
Content:
Varachha police on Tuesday night arrested a gang of five teenage robbers who specialised in robbing homosexuals. The police seized cash, jewellery, 22 mobile phones and diamonds from their possession.

The accused have been identified as Hiresh Vaghela, Jashu Maisurya, Ankit Chotalia, Yogesh Haryani and Sanjay Haryani, all residents of Varachha. The accused, who were arrested from Sardar Nagar area in Varachha, have confessed to have robbed more than 35 people.

According to police, the accused failed to give satisfactory answers when questioned and thus were detained and interrogated. The teenagers broke down during questioning.

The police said that they were shocked when the accused disclosed their modus operandi. One of the gang members, according to the police, used to stand near public toilets, gardens and other public places and tried to catch the attention of homosexuals passing by, while other gang members kept waiting in a nearby area to keep a watch on their gang member. Later, when the first gang member got his catch, he took the person to a fixed location and robbed him along with other gang members.

Varachha police Inspector V B Patel said: "This gang had spread huge panic in Varachha area. While committing the robbery, they threatened the victims with making their personal details public. As a result, not a single complaint was lodged as people felt ashamed to contact the police. Not even a single person had come to the police station for their valuables, cash, jewellery mobiles and diamonds."

Heading: Sahara faces penalty of over Rs 48 crore for alleged stamp duty evasion - Indian Express
Content:
The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India's latest report has pointed at a short realisation of stamp duty and registration fee amounting to Rs 55.45 crore in as many as 327 cases in the state during 2006-07.

The report gives wrong classification of documents, irregular acceptance of time barred cases, incorrect grant of exemption, under-assessment of stamp duty and under-valuation of property among the few reasons for short recovery of the stamp duty and registration fee.

Giving a few examples as to how the acts of state government officials resulted in short recovery, the report says that deputy collectors of 11 districts, including Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Vadodara, Rajkot and Bharuch districts accepted appeals of more than 200 aggrieved parties after the expiry of the deadline.

Quoting provisions of the Bombay Stamp Act, 1958, applicable in the state, the report says that Chief Controlling Revenue Authority (CCRA) was not authorised to accept appeals filed after the deadline decided by the competent authority. However, in all these matters, time-barred applications were accepted by the deputy collectors contrary to the provisions of the Act, resulting in short recovery of stamp duty to the tune of several crores of rupees.

In their replies to CAG queries, the deputy collectors said CCRA had powers to condone delay but the report affirms that the BS Act does not authorise the CCRA to condone delay for any reason whatsoever.

The report also points out the evasion of payment during land transfer in over 78 cases during 2004-05 and 2005-06 in Bhuj, Jamnagar, Rajkot and Surat districts. According to the report, neither did the allottees make any payment on account of stamp duty nor did the collectors ask for the same.

The report also mentions loss of stamp duty and registration fee owing to authorities charging stamp duty for only one matter or transaction when the documents comprised of several distinct matters of immovable properties. The report quotes several cases of such lapses in Ahmedabad, Rajkot, Surat and Vadodara districts.

According to the report, the state government lost stamp duty amounting to Rs. 40 .11 crores due to wrong classification of deeds in the five districts of Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Bhavnagar, Anand and Rajkot between 2004 and 2005. The report says that instead of charging 8.4 per cent of duty, it was charged at a rate of one per cent only due to wrong classification, thus causing huge losses to the state exchequer.

Heading: City slums show the dark side of urban development - Indian Express
Content:
The Jamnagar district administration has issued a notice to Sahara Prime City Limited (SPCL), a subsidiary of the Sahara Group, to pay a penalty of Rs 48.69 crore for allegedly evading stamp duty.

Jamnagar Deputy Stamp Duty Collector Chandrakant Pandya confirmed that the notice relates to SPCL's ambitious housing project at Dhuva village, some 8 km from Jamnagar city. SPCL has denied the allegation.

The Jamnagar project was one the high-end self-sufficient townships that the Sahara group headed by Subroto Roy had announced in 217 cities across India. While SPCL was issued the penalty notice early last month, its brokers were asked to pay up two days ago. The registration of land documents was done at the office of the Jamnagar sub-registrar on June 5, 2008.

According to officials, the total stamp duty evasion discovered amounted to Rs 4.86 crore. Under the Mumbai Stamp Act Section 39 (1), duty evasion attracts a penalty 10 times the evaded amount, which in SPCL's case means Rs 48.69 crore. "SPCL has been asked to respond by October 14," said Pandya. SPCL's AGM, Suryavir Singh said, "In the first place, we have evaded no stamp duty. And imposing a penalty of over Rs 48 crore on an alleged evasion amount of over Rs 4 crore has no basis."

Heading: Police name three for allegedly issuing duplicate voting cards in BU election - Indian Express
Content:
Sprawling industries and emerging urban lifestyles in Ahmedabad enfolds in itself a dark and morbid life of scarcity, filth and deprivation. Nearly 41 per cent of people in the city live in slums.

There are 792 slums spread all across the city. Migrants from Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh who come in search of a livelihood also live here. But the majority comprises scheduled castes and scheduled tribes. A good percentage of migrants from Bengal and Bangladesh is also seen.

For their betterment, the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) runs the Slum-Networking Project (SNP), which has received help from Gujarat Mahila Housing SEWA Trust, SAATH (NGO), and the private sectors.

Under the SNP, slums are entitled to get electricity, water supply, sanitation, streetlights, paved roads, sewage and solid waste management, and storm water drainage facilities.

Electricity being a major issue in slums, AMC started the Slum Electrification Project to give streetlights. Under the project, Torrent Power takes electricity to the households. About 1.47 lakh homes have got electricity under Tatkalik Ane Saral Vij Jodan Yojana. Ramapirno Tekro, Poorpidit Nagar, J P Ni Chali, Soni Ni Chali, Kagdiwad, Millat Nagar, Shah Alam and Dudheshwar are a few slums that have got the benefit of electricity.

Not all the slums are included in the SNP, said AMC's additional city engineer, Anand Patel. Tenements that are less than 40 square feet need a No-Objection Certificate. There are at least 7,000 households that do not come under the project. "AMC is proposing some plans to JNNURM for these pockets," he said.

"We have to pay Rs 750 for the connection and an additional Rs 250 to fix the metre box. Every month we get a bill of Rs 150-200. We cannot afford to pay more than Rs 1,000 for a connection," said Gita Rabari, a slum-dweller of Baba Ramdev Nagar of Chandloda slums in Isanpur.

A Torrent Power officer said: "Before the project was initiated, a survey was carried out. According to the details available with the AMC and the Ahmedabad Urban Development Authority (AUDA), there were 2.49 lakh slums in Torrent Power Limited's distribution area. Out of this, only 0.96 lakh were electrified. With the new settlements of about 8,800 new hutments, 14,000 households are yet to be electrified."

With nearly 25 per cent of the slums not having electricity, slum-dwellers have resorted to stealing it from those who have installed metres. There are also 'dealers' who illegally supply electricity to houses.

"My paan shop hardly provides me with any money. Therefore, I supply electricity to houses. I get the wire connections from an electricity metre in the neighborhood. Five to six houses can get electricity from one wire in just Rs 150," claimed Raju (name changed).

While government officials are trying to convince the illegal electricity suppliers to get metres provided by the municipal corporation, the slow process of getting electricity after filling up the application form puts off many.

"I had applied for electricity months back. I own a shop. They are asking us to pay Rs 3,600 to get a connection for commercial usage," said Bharat Thakore, a paan shop owner in Chandlodia slum.

"We are planning to appoint an individual from the slum itself who can take our applications in bulk and give them to the municipal corporation. This will fasten the long awaited process of getting electricity. When we are ready for legal connections, we are being asked for more money," said Thakore.

Heading: Weights and Measures Department cracks down on stall owners at garba venues - Indian Express
Content:
The Bhavnagar police have identified two senate members of Bhavnagar University and a school principal as accused for allegedly issuing duplicate voting cards for the election held on Sunday for six senate posts in the university.

Out of the three, Rajesh Joshi (appointed by the Chancellor) and Upendrasinh Rana (Elected Graduates Science Faculty) are current senate members of the varsity, while H V Gardi is the principal of a local school in Vavdi village.

"We have not arrested them yet as the V-C is not in town and his statement is very important on this issue," said Inspector M S Adyaru, A-Division, Bhavnagar city.

On Monday morning, H C Trivedi, Vice Chancellor (V-C) of Bhavnagar University received an anonymous letter with proof papers attached of duplicate and dummy voters involved in the Sunday election. Immediately, a 10-member committee was formed to look into the matter.

"We opened all the ballot boxes in front of the election committee and found duplicate cards in those of the commerce and law faculty. We also found that these duplicate cards were not printed at the press where the university regularly prints its stuff," said Trivedi.

He added, "After the incident, we didn't start the process of vote counting on Monday."

When asked whether there will be a re-election and when the process of vote counting will start, the V-C told Newsline: "I cannot comment on that. As of now, we just want to identify if more people are involved in this cheating case. There is no doubt that this incident is a slap on the face of university management."

He added, "I have no information about these three people whom the police have identified as the accused. But we will take strict action as per university norms against the people involved in this matter."

Heading: Strict police vigil in garba venues - Indian Express
Content:
City-based NGO, Lok Jagrut Mandal (LJM), along with the state Weights and Measures Department has embarked on an initiative to keep tabs on stalls selling food and refreshments at the most happening garba venues on all nine days of the Navratri festival.

While LJM and the Weights and Measures Department covered nearly 22 stalls of the famous United Way of Baroda (UWB) Garba, the team will now keep an eye on the stalls at the United Arkee Garba Ground and other venues in the city throughout the festival.

Jitendra Srivastav, LJM president, said, "LJM submitted an application to Vadodara District Collector Vijay Nehra on September 9 about stall vendors cheating customers during Navratri by charging them extra for food, refreshments and even water."

He added: "We also noticed that stall owners never put a price list approved by the district authorities on display. All these issues were mentioned in the application. Mr Nehra forwarded our application to the state Weights and Measures Department."

Now, two inspectors of the department have been assigned the duty of keeping tabs on the stalls, which are cheating the customers by charging them extra.

Srivastav said: "LJM members will also accompany the inspectors of the Weights and Measures Department to inspect the stalls. The department will continue the drive throughout the nine days of Navratri. If the vendors do not comply with the set norms, a case will be filed against them."

Heading: Non-Gujaratis gearing up to add zing to Navratri - Indian Express
Content:
Serial bomb blasts and terror attacks having riddled the country, Navratri this year is being celebrated amidst tight security with special policemen in plain clothes deployed in the garba venues in Ahmedabad.

"This year, we are extra vigilant. Police personnel in plain clothes are keeping a close eye on the activities in garba venues. These are specially trained personnel from the city police and the special branch," Ahmedabad Police Commissioner (city), O P Mathur said.

City cops, already on high alert after the July 26 blasts, have been alerted again after the blast in Modasa and the recovery of 17 crude bombs in Kalupur.

According to police, the security arrangements have been made stringent at all the big garba venues on the S G Highway. Most of the venues, said cops, witness over 10,000 visitors daily and police are taking no chances with the security measures.

The police have ensured a detailed security programme, including CCTV cameras at popular venues.

The traffic police are also taking no chances and have asked all the garba organisers to ensure that parking of vehicles is at a distance from the venue.

"In addition, there will be strict vigil over vehicles parked at the parking lots. A separate entry and exit points for two-wheelers and four-wheelers is being discussed. The traffic police are going to launch special drives against drunken and rash driving in the area during the festive season," a police officer supervising security arrangements said.

Heading: From utensils to American diamonds: ‘Lahni’ gets bigger with time - Indian Express
Content:
As the Navratri fever catches on, the non-Gujaratis living in the state are also gearing up to dance in tune with the garba crazy crowd of Gujarat.

Gujarat has a sizeable percentage of non-Gujaratis, who are flocking to the garba training centers across the state to learn the traditional dance steps. Even the ones who are barely acquainted with the culture of Gujarat are more than excited to play garba in the nine-day festival. "Around 95 per cent of non-Gujarati candidates come to us every year to learn the traditional garba styles. This year my batch consisted only of non-gujarati population. Most of them do not even know the local language, but are equally enthusiastic to play garba this year," said Dharmesh Soni, who runs Rhythm Dancing Hall in Ahmedabad. In order to learn a folk dance, one needs to have the knowledge and understanding of the traditions and culture of that particular land. And despite being migrants to the state, the non-Gujaratis have coped up with the Gujarati culture.

"Garba is a very unique dance form. I wanted to learn garba as I was very impressed with the energy of this festival. Being a non-Gujarati I cannot dance as flawlessly as Gujaratis. But that has not stopped me from enjoying the festival. The verve of Navaratri encourages me to pick up my dandiya sticks and dance all night," said Meenu Shekhani, a trainee at Rhythm Dancing Hall.

Surya Singh, a homemaker, said: "I came to Ahmedabad to work. I do not know their local language. But the Gujarati culture gets on to you and encourages you to adapt it. Every non-Gujarati should learn garba to know this rich culture better." The training institutes in Ahmedabad have welcomed the non-Gujarati population with open arms. "There is a high percentage of non-Gujaratis coming to our institute. They are not familiar with the culture and language of the state, but their enthusiasm to learn garba is commendable. It is little difficult to train them as they are not aware of the traditional Gujarati dances. However, they grasp the dancing styles very fast," said Soni.

Navratri has now become a platform for cultural synthesis, wherein locals and migrants exchange and adapt each other's culture. This fusion has led to the inclusion of Bhangra, Rajasthani and Kutchi styles in Gujarati dance forms. Garba organisers also encourage Punjabi and Hindi music so that people of various backgrounds can enjoy the festival to the maximum.

Heading: Gujarat Vidyapith discontinues master’s programme in Gandhian Thought - Indian Express
Content:
Customarily it has been limited to stainless steel vessels or household items. But, the 'lahni' (gift) is getting bigger with time, thanks to the availability of sponsors and generous donors. Lahni is a gift given on the last day of Navratri to young girls who worship the goddess through Garba during the nine day festival.

"It is taking a sophisticated form. Earlier the Garbi mandals used to distribute items like a stainless steel thali (plate) and Katori (mug). But now, girls are gifted with items like golden chain, diamond ornaments or even electrical appliances," said Suresh Mistry of Jai Khodiyar Garbi Mandal in Rajkot.

Rudra Charitable Trust that organises Garba near Paldi is planning to gift American diamond jewellery sets to girls this time. "Garbi mandals can afford much better gifts for the girls now," said Aanand Parikh of Rudra Charitable Trust in Ahmedabad.

"Girls always compare their lahni with each other. So organisers too have to get the best gifts for their participants'", said Kishor Patel of Shiv-Shakti Garbi Mandal in Rajkot

Besides, organisers always make sure that the lahni item can be used by the girls in future. As per the customs, lahni is never used by the parents. Girls include the lahni in their aanu (wedding gifts given to the bride by her parents). Keeping this in mind, the organisers select items that can make a perfect aanu starting from dinner sets, home appliances, jewellery and even furniture.

Generally, the lahni is far more expensive than the registration fee collected from girls. Various Garbi mandals have fee ranging from Rs 100-500. "'We collect the falau (amount) from the residents of societies and add this amount to the registration fee paid by the girls. This makes it easier for us to give away expensive items as lahni. As these young girls are considered an avatar of the goddess, residents willingly give huge amounts," said Janak Kotak of Junction Garbi Mandal in Rajkot.

In addition, commercialisation has helped small organisers collect huge amounts for lahni.

The competitions and expensive gifts have been made possible due to the availability of sponsors, said the organisers.

Heading: Police foil man’s self-immolation bid - Indian Express
Content:
Authorities say the course does not hold any relevance in providing employment to students

The Gujarat Vidyapith has decided to discontinue its regular master degree course in Gandhian Thought and Social Science from this year onwards. According to the authorities at the Vidyapith, the course was suspended as it does not hold any relevance in providing employment to the students in present scenario.

The Gujarat Vidyapith has been running a number of courses in Gandhian Thought, Peace, Non-violence and Disarmament under the Department of Gandhian Studies and Peace Research Centre. The Centre, which has been operating since the year 1971, offers degrees such as M.Phil, Ph.D and M.A. While some of the courses are regular, others are done through correspondence.

Rajendra Khimani, Registrar of the Gujarat Vidyapith, said: "The concerned course was a regular course. Students are not going to get jobs in the present scenario after doing a course which is based on a philosophical subject."

He added: "So, we decided to discontinue the course from this year. However, our other courses on Gandhi's message of peace and non-violence are on and we are planning to make them more intense."

Sources say that the Department of Gandhian Studies and Peace Research Centre has not been getting enough students for its courses and this could be the reason behind the discontinuation of the master's degree course. However, Khimani dismissed this claim.

According to the figures provided by the center, only 88 students have studied the regular masters degree course since 2005.

Heading: City to breathe easy this Gandhi Jayanti - Indian Express
Content:
A self-immolation bid by a 37-year-old man was foiled by the city police outside the BJP office in Khanpur area on Wednesday. According to the police, Harjendrasinh Mato, resident of Nava Vadaj area, attempted to set himself on fire to protest against the alleged harassment he faced at the hands of a city corporator's relative. Mato has been arrested on charges of 'attempt to suicide', the police said.

Mato, who owns a shop in Satyam Shopping Center in Nava Vadaj staged a demonstration outside the BJP office in Khanpur, reportedly to protest against a relative of Nava Vadaj corporator, R D Desai.

Mato alleged that Desai's relative had been harassing him for the past several months by forcing him to sell off his shop. "They first build a Paan shop outside my shop and are now forcing me to sell off my shop at a meager price of Rs 1.5 lakh," Mato said.

Threatening to kill himself, Mato poured kerosene on his body. But before he could immolate himself, officers from the Shahpur police station rushed to the spot and apprehended him.

'We have arrested Mato and charged him with attempt to suicide," Shahpur police Inspector, M B Joshi, said.
